### 155. v1.58.26 - launch award: the first 50 welcome trials run 365 days, then the default flow (2026-11-04)

- **The campaign.** The FIRST `LAUNCH_MAX_FIRST_SIGNUPS` (default 50) accounts whose welcome trial actually starts - i.e. the first asset registration, per §39 - receive the launch award: `LAUNCH_AWARD_DAYS` (default 365) card-free days instead of the standard `TRIAL_DAYS` 30. Slot N+1 and everyone after keeps the normal welcome flow automatically: there is no second code path, only "award granted" vs "default".
- **Storage (`public.launch_awards`, new).** `slot_idx integer PRIMARY KEY`, `owner_id uuid NOT NULL UNIQUE`, `trial_session_id`, `coupon_code`, `days`, `applied_ends_at`, `awarded_at`, `metadata`. The PK makes >N awards physically impossible and the UNIQUE makes a second award per owner impossible, even under concurrency (a `23505` collision triggers one recount + retry on the next free slot; a duplicate owner resolves to `already:true`). Migration: `npm run migrate:launch-awards` (idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `profiles.utm_*`), also ensured fail-soft at boot.
- **Trial math stays engine-owned (§28).** The award calls `extendAccountTrial({ days, maxTotalDays: days })`; the `maxTotalDays` parameter is the ONLY way past `TRIAL_MAX_TOTAL_DAYS` (45) and only this slot-gated caller passes it. Every coupon path still passes `null`, so the 45-day clamp is unchanged (pinned in `test_trial_engine` both directions).
- **One grant, three records.** A grant writes (1) the `launch_awards` row, (2) a `coupons` row `LAUNCH<days>-<slot>` (`created_by='LAUNCH_AWARD'`, `owner_id=<owner>`, `is_redeemed=true`, `applicable_to='account_trial_extension'`, already applied), and (3) an `admin_audit_logs` row `LAUNCH_AWARD_GRANTED` - so the website's `successful_signup` event always has a server-side twin. Each step is fail-soft: the trial never blocks on the award. Verified against the live database: a real trial went `ACTIVE` -> `EXTENDED` to exactly 365 days with the slot-1 row, both account-bound coupon rows and the audit trail, then every row was removed (0 leftovers).
- **Where it hooks.** `onboarding.js` `saveVehicleAssetRecord` (WhatsApp passbook path - the award line is appended to the "Passbook Issued" message) and `quizEngine.js` `vehicle_registration` completion (the composed reply's `trialDays` reflects the award). Award copy is deterministic (`formatLaunchAwardLine`, zero tokens) and only rendered when the engine confirmed `granted`.
- **Public status is fail-closed.** `GET /api/onboard/launch-status` returns `{ launch_active, slots_left, slots_total, award_days }` only - no PII, no secrets - and ANY DB problem returns `launch_active:false`, so a broken lookup can never promise an award that cannot be granted. Cached `LAUNCH_STATUS_CACHE_MS` (60 s), CORS-allowed on the onboard paths only.
- **Website.** `landing/assets/js/main.js` reads the status and upgrades the `.hero-note` only while the campaign can actually award; the HTML default stays the truthful 30-day copy. Signups now carry first-touch UTM attribution (`utm_source/utm_medium/utm_campaign`, `sessionStorage`, 64-char cap, `[a-zA-Z0-9._~ -]` only) which `sanitizeOnboardPayload` re-sanitizes server-side and `completeWebOnboarding` stores on `profiles` first-touch only (missing columns degrade instead of failing, §50).
- **Admin.** `admin launch-stats` reads through `getLaunchAwardStats`/`formatLaunchStatsReply` (deterministic, zero tokens, never invents numbers when the read fails).
- **Deep audit (rule 52) - the one real defect found.** The passbook reply referenced a bare `launchAward` inside `handleStage1CoreCapture`, while the value lives on the `saveVehicleAssetRecord` result: a granted award would have thrown `ReferenceError` while rendering the confirmation. Fixed to `saved.launchAward`; the quiz path was already correct. Sibling sweep (rule 51) of "a value produced in one frame and read in another": `saveVehicleAssetRecord` return contract (fixed), quizEngine completion (already destructured from the call), web onboarding attribution (reads only what it stores), status endpoint (returns only the service payload), stats digest (guards `ok:false`).
- **Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *campaign state promised by copy but not enforced by the engine* -> siblings audited: award copy (rendered only when `granted`, fixed), website banner (fail-closed, fixed), status endpoint (fail-closed), stats digest (honest failure line), trial cap (engine-owned, unchanged), second-award path (UNIQUE, unchanged).
- **Frames touched.** `src/services/launchAwards.js` (new), `src/services/trialEngine.js` (`extendAccountTrial` `maxTotalDays`), `src/services/onboarding.js` (grant + `saved.launchAward`), `src/services/quizEngine.js` (grant + reply), `src/services/webOnboarding.js` (UTM sanitize + attribution), `src/services/envAudit.js` (LAUNCH CAMPAIGN section), `index.js` (`/api/onboard/launch-status`, CORS, boot ensure), `scripts/run_launch_awards_migration.js` (new), `scripts/health_audit.js` (suite registry), `scripts/reset-db.js` + `scripts/provision_staging_schema.js` (launch tables), `.env.example`, `landing/assets/js/main.js`, `landing/data/changelog.json`, `test_launch_award.js` (new), `test_trial_engine.js`, `test_web_onboarding.js`, `test_landing_static.js`, `test_agent_training.js`, `.clinerules` (§46 launch knob reference lives in the latency/reference block), `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this section.
- **Skill sync (rule 13).** `flowKnowledge.js` trial rules and `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT` now teach the launch award: engine-confirmed only, never invent slot/days/end date, never offer it to an unawarded account.
- **Suites run:** `test_launch_award` (23 - new), `test_trial_engine`, `test_subscription_billing`, `test_web_onboarding`, `test_landing_static`, `test_env_audit`, `test_doc_sync`, `test_agent_training`, `test_superadmin`, `test_quiz_flow`, `npm run health` - green.

### 157. v1.59.1 - launch banner + opt-out tick box + rules-of-engagement consolidation (2026-11-05)

**Launch banner (improving the existing v1.58.26 campaign, never rebuilding it).**
- `landing/index.html` carries a slim dismissible ribbon (`#launchBanner`, hidden by default) with the production note ("Your logs and feedback help us polish Saka for production") and a **live slot counter** (`#launchSlots` / `#launchSlotsTotal` / `#launchAwardDays`). `main.js` `renderLaunchBanner()` fills it from the existing `/api/onboard/launch-status` (PII-free, 60 s cache) and **fails closed**: `launch_active !== true` or `slots_left <= 0` leaves the banner, counter and tick box hidden and the truthful 30-day hero copy in place. Dismissal persists in `localStorage` (`saka_launch_banner_dismissed`) and emits `launch_offer_dismiss`; the view still emits `launch_offer_view`.
- **Opt-out tick box, checked by default (operator decision 2026-11-05):** `#launchOptIn` sits in the signup legal step (`#launchOptInWrap`, hidden until the campaign is confirmed open). Only an explicit uncheck is an opt-out; the payload carries `launch_opt_in: readLaunchOptIn()` and the field is omitted when the campaign is closed. `successful_signup` now records `launch_opt_in`.
- **Backend is the source of truth.** New idempotent `LAUNCH_OPT_IN_SQL` (`npm run migrate:launch-awards`, applied live): `profiles.launch_opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` — existing accounts are backfilled `true`, so they keep the automatic award (rule 56). `sanitizeOnboardPayload` accepts a strict boolean (non-booleans are dropped, never guessed); `completeWebOnboarding` stores the explicit choice on create, writes only EXPLICIT choices on update (a duplicate signup that omits the field never overwrites a stored opt-out), and every path degrades without the column (rule 50).
- **Eligibility stays engine-owned.** `tryGrantLaunchAward` reads `profiles.launch_opt_in` via `resolveLaunchOptIn()`: an explicit `false` returns `{ granted:false, reason:'opted-out' }`, audits `LAUNCH_AWARD_SKIPPED_OPT_OUT` and takes no slot; a missing column, missing profile or failed read is **fail-open** (the award is never blocked by schema drift). The award itself still happens at welcome-trial start, through the same slot-gated ledger. `admin launch-stats` gains `• Opted out: N (normal 30-day flow)`.

**Rules of engagement (audit + consolidation + additive rules).**

### 158. v1.59.2 - sticky glowing launch banner + live signup guard (2026-11-05)

**Launch banner polish (improving v1.59.1).**
- **Copy:** the banner now says "the first **50 signups** get a full 365-day trial" (the tick-box label follows the same wording; the hero-note upgrade is aligned to "signups"). The word "fleets" no longer appears in the offer sentence.

No fixed positioning, no body-padding hacks, no fragile top offsets.
- **Attention glow:** a slow breathing inset glow (3.2 s cyan→violet pulse) — deliberately not a rapid strobe — with `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` disabling the animation (rule 31 accessibility).
- **Mobile:** at ≤640 px the banner stacks vertically and centres, the slots pill drops to its own line, and the dismiss ✕ keeps its own padded hit-area with text padding so nothing underlaps it.

**Duplicate signup: audit + live guard.**
- **Audit (no guessing):** the live `admin_audit_logs` show the latest duplicate attempt (2026-11-05 04:37, +254734852529 / david.njonjo@gmail.com) was **blocked** — `WEB_ONBOARD_EXISTING` (matchedBy phone) + `WEB_ONBOARD_DUPLICATE_NOTIFIED` (owner emailed + WhatsApp'd), no new row. A historical double-profile for that number existed across 11-03/11-04 (predating the v1.58.14 guard) and was removed by the clean slates. Live table: 3 profiles, **0 phone duplicates, 0 email duplicates**.
- **`POST /api/onboard/check`** (new, CORS-allowlisted, tight per-route rate limit 20/min): per-field `available | registered` plus a `verified` flag; invalid payloads 400; ANY DB problem returns `success:false` so the client fails open (submit-time blocking still protects). Service: `checkSignupAvailability()` (never throws, reuses `findProfileByPhone` variants + case-insensitive email).
- **Website gating:** debounced (500 ms) checks on email/phone input, blur and country-code change; per-field notes ("This number/email already has a Saka account…"); **Continue stays disabled** until names + valid email + valid phone AND both fields report `available`; a verified match shows "you are all set, continue on WhatsApp". Enter-key submits are guarded too, and a network failure fails OPEN (button enabled; server still blocks).
- **DB defense-in-depth:** `SIGNUP_GUARD_SQL` — partial unique indexes on `profiles.phone_number` and `lower(profiles.email)` — applied live (`npm run migrate:signup-guards`, idempotent; safe because the live table had zero duplicates). A concurrent double-submit can no longer create a second row: `completeWebOnboarding` catches the unique violation, re-reads the winner, merges (email/verified/launch opt-in) and audits `WEB_ONBOARD_RACE_MERGED`.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).**
- Defect class *account-existence known only at submit time* → siblings audited: submit-time block (already correct), pre-submit UI (fixed with the live check), step-1 Enter-key path (guarded), country-code change (re-checks), network failure (fail-open), verified-account path (clear "all set" copy).
- Defect class *check-then-insert race* → DB unique indexes (fixed) + merge fallback (fixed, tested) + audit trail.

### 160. v1.59.4 - re-engagement memory, PDF link delay, warm signup copy, preview-only changelog (2026-11-05)

**Re-engagement memory (surgical, no schema change).**
- Root cause: `getRecentChatHistory` injects up to 40 turns but only inside the **45-minute freshness window** (v1.32.3 guard). A user returning later got ZERO context.
- New in `src/services/chatHistory.js`: `CHAT_REENGAGE_MAX_MESSAGES` (6, clamped 2-12), `CHAT_REENGAGE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (14, clamped 1-60), `CHAT_REENGAGE_MAX_CHARS` (900, clamped 200-2000), `sanitizeReengagementLine()` (standalone six-digit codes become `[code]`, 180 chars/line) and `getReengagementContext()` — reads the last few `chat_history` rows of any age up to the window and returns a labelled **`EARLIER CONVERSATION (context only — from {date}; the user is returning now…)`** block, or `''` (zero prompt cost), never throwing.
- `whatsapp.js` computes it **only when the fresh `dbHistory` is empty** and passes `reengagementContext` through the existing options channel; `processSakaMessage` (sakaAi.js) appends it to the system instruction right after WORKING MEMORY — **labelled context, never live turns**, so Saka can pick up where the conversation stopped without pretending old messages just arrived. Rule 40 gained one additive sentence.

**Inline report PDF budget (v1.77.0).**
- `resolveInlineReportBudgetMs(env)` in `reportDelivery.js` (`REPORT_INLINE_BUILD_MS`, default 4000, clamped 0-8000; 0 = dashboard link only). The WhatsApp report lane races `buildInlineReportLink()` (build → render → upload → shorten) against this budget and appends `📄 PDF report:` only when it wins — nothing is emailed and nothing is recorded on a miss. **Replaces the retired `REPORT_PDF_LINK_DELAY_MS`** (the async follow-up that needed a propagation delay no longer exists).
- Monthly sweep: no new timing knob. The gate is `isMonthlyReportWindow()` (Nairobi day-of-month 1, 08:00–08:05) on the same 30-minute worker tick as the weekly sweep, deduped by the `monthlyreports.last_sent_date` marker.

**Warm signup copy.** "Deploy Your Fleet" (corporate/military, off-voice) is gone: the ghost CTA now reads **"Start with your car"** and the signup modal title **"🚀 Meet your car's new friend"**. The landing suite asserts the new copy AND the absence of the old phrase.

**Preview-only changelog.** The /status feed renders plain cards (version chip + date + short title + one-line preview); the `details`/"Read more" expander and its `.cl-more`/`.cl-detail` styles are removed. `changelog.json` summaries remain as data (unused by the renderer).

**Friction remedies (rule 38/44/51).** Live audit found 4 PENDING `INCOMPLETE_REPLY_COMPLAINT` rows for the test phone `+254799000512` (transcripts wiped; class = context-less re-engagement) — closed as DEPLOYED with resolution `rule:reengagement_memory` after this fix; earlier `USER_FRUSTRATION`/`LOOPING_PROMPTS` rows were already DEPLOYED.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/chatHistory.js` (re-engagement helpers), `src/routes/whatsapp.js` (injection + import), `sakaAi.js` (`options.reengagementContext` → system prompt), `src/services/followups.js` (delay helper + wait), `src/services/envAudit.js` (4 knobs), `.env.example` (documented), `landing/index.html` (warm copy), `landing/assets/js/status.js` + `landing/assets/css/styles.css` (preview-only feed), `test_conversation_memory.js` (+7), `test_followups.js` (+3), `test_landing_static.js` (+/-), `.clinerules` (rule 40 additive + reference knobs), `package.json`, `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json`, `docs/*`.

### 163. v1.59.7 - de-robot voice, 25-type expense catalog, labels on every entry, support-email body fix, native scrolling (2026-11-05)

**The chat-log deep dive (evidence first).** 2,137 messages (1,084 Saka turns, 1,053 user turns) across the wipe backups plus live `chat_history`/`chat_transcripts` were analysed: the "Here's…" review-card family opened ~120 turns ("Here's your vehicle summary" 42x, "Here's everything I have" 63x combined, "Here's what I have" 27x, "Which field would you like to change?" 24x), `Reply *CONFIRM*` appeared 153 times, "Stage 1 of 2 · Step 2 of 4" 9x (already banned by §73), "Nothing logged" 27x, and users sent 114 corrective turns. The robot feel was structural, not model mood.

**Voice (data layer, no prompt drift).**
- `SAKA_TONE_COMPASS` gains **REVIEW CARD VOICE** (opener pool: "📋 Check this before I save it", "📋 One look and it's saved", "📋 Ready when you are —", "📋 Quick check 👇", "📋 Here's the card (last look)"; footer pool with `{word}`) and **EMPTY SEARCH VOICE**; both render through `buildToneCompassBlock()` into the core prompt, and the composer carries a matching REVIEW CARD VOICE line.
- `renderConfirmationSummary()` (conversationEngine) now = rotated engine opener + model-rendered checklist body + rotated engine action line ("Reply *CONFIRM* (or *1*) to save…"); `stripReviewBoilerplate()` deterministically removes "Here's what I have…", "please check it over", "reply CONFIRM to save…", "tell me which field…" lines that slip through. The confirmation gate itself is untouched (boundary rule §16/§18).
- `QUIZ_INSTRUCTION_NATURAL` forbids "Got your…" openers and demands varied wording; banned phrases += "Here's what I have for this", "Here's everything I have", "please check it over", "which field you'd like to change", "Got your expense type"; `SAKA_PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION` = `2026.13.0`.
- `recordAnswers.formatRecordAnswer` empty state is now "Nothing under <type> for <period> yet — send the next one and I'll keep it here." (no 📊 dashboard zero, no "matching"). Legacy onboarding strings "Stage 1 of 2 · Step 1/2 of 4" replaced with "Vehicle registration" / "Vehicle core details".

**Expense catalog (additive, legacy values preserved).** New `Licences & Permits` type (category `compliance`) takes licence/license/permit/inspection/mot/renewal/sticker/speed-limiter/psv/pdp/badge/compliance aliases away from Insurance ("renewed my licence" is no longer Insurance; "renewed insurance" still is via longest-alias). New types: `Security` (askari/guard), `Loading & Offloading` (loader/cartage/turnboy, non-road kinds), `Weighbridge` (trucks), `Hire & Rental`, `Route & Stage Fees` (bus/motorcycle/truck) with new report categories `security/loading/weighbridge/hire/route`. Catalog = **25 types / 23 categories**. Quiz menu is now **five real choices + Other** with per-family priority (`road`: Fuel/Charging · Maintenance · Parts · Tyres · Repairs; `hours`: Fuel · Maintenance · Parts · Repairs · Consumables) — everything else stays reachable by free text. Public copy swept to "25 expense types" (landing FAQ/JSON-LD/feature card, terms).

**Labels on every entry (operator-approved largest scope).** New `src/services/labelsEverywhere.js` (never throws): `LABELS_EVERYWHERE_SQL` (idempotent `receipts.label`, `reminders.label`, `odometer_readings` table + index), `recordLabeledReading()` (degrades per rule 50 — an un-migrated column retries without the label so a mileage update is never lost), `searchOtherLabels()` (receipts/reminders/readings by `label ILIKE`, empty on any error) and `formatOtherLabelMatches()` ("Also labelled:" block). Wiring: quiz `log_mileage` writes a labelled reading row and shows the `#label` chip; `log_expense`/`log_earnings` confirmations carry the chip; `set_reminder` passes the label to both reminder creators; `receipts.recordReceipt` stores/displays it; the OCR lane captures it from the caption; reminder inserts degrade on schema drift; `recordAnswers` note hint teaches "label: karen run"; keyword search appends other-kind matches. Migration `npm run migrate:labels-everywhere` applied live. Rule 37 updated additively (rule 58).


**Support email deep audit + fix.** Live ticket `c7e279b1` (huguadventures@gmail.com, subject "Enquiry") proved the flow fires end-to-end (classify → thread → OPEN + priority) but its body was the subject fallback: the Resend body fetch returned no text part for an HTML-only mail. `htmlToPlainText()` now converts the HTML part (tags/entities stripped, 4,000-char cap) as the middle leg of text → HTML → subject, and a body-less ticket gets an `internal_note` explaining the fetch failure (never silent). ### 164. v1.60.0 - DeepEval-style conversation evals + bounded self-healing + superadmin notifications (2026-11-05)

**Why (audit first).** Sentinel could detect friction (`chat_friction_logs`) and patch prompts (`saka_dynamic_rules`), and the Model Watchdog could benchmark MODELS, but nothing scored Saka's actual conversational output against the persona laws, and nothing closed the loop "quality failure → candidate fix → re-score → ship". The DeepEval family fills exactly that gap.

**Reality of the bridge.** DeepEval is a Python-only package. Rather than add a second runtime (which would break the single-hub rule 20 — every LLM call must flow through `aiClient.js` with a telemetry purpose), the judge implements DeepEval's GEval semantics natively in Node: named criteria, 0..1 score + reason per criterion, threshold verdict. `npm run eval:export` emits DeepEval-compatible JSONL if the library is ever wanted offline.

**The judge (`src/services/convEval.js`).**
- Five permanent criteria: `loop_avoidance`, `tone_compliance`, `shorthand_precision`, `single_question`, `boundary_safety`. Equal weight; a missing criterion scores 0 (safety-first) and every criterion must clear the bar (averaging can never hide a boundary failure).
- The judge system prompt imports `SAKA_TONE_COMPASS` (voice, floors, mirror matrix, banned phrases) and `SAKA_BOUNDARY_RULES` from `flowKnowledge.js` — the same source that builds the live core prompt, so the grader cannot drift from Persona v4.
- `purpose: 'conversation_eval'` (ROUTER tier) rides the single hub: telemetry, circuit breakers and the budget guard always apply. Background policy keeps it on DeepSeek; `CONV_EVAL_JUDGE_PROVIDER=anthropic` is the explicit opt-in that routes the judge to Claude Haiku (or Sonnet via `CONV_EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL`) — still through `aiClient`, never a direct provider client.
- Never throws: provider/parse failures return `{ ok:false }` and the run records an `error` row.

**The corpus + live cases (`src/services/convEvalCases.js`, `evals/cases/conversation_cases.json`).**
- 14 offline fixtures covering looping, complaints, hurried shorthand, interruptions, elderly phrasing, boundary probes, report recovery and ack variety — every case carries an `expected` verdict used for calibration (a judge that disagrees with many expectations is itself suspect).
- `buildLiveCasesFromFriction()` turns the two live PENDING friction transcripts (Sentinel's `[role]: text` snippet format) into scored cases, so existing users' pain reaches the harness without waiting for a new signup (rule 56); unparseable snippets are skipped with a reason, never guessed.

**Bounded healing (`src/services/convEvalHealer.js`).**
- `conversation_heal` proposes ONE micro-rule + the corrected reply. Deterministic gates: `refinementIsSafe` (banned phrases, security-weakening, schema marker, size), `patchViolatesBoundaryLock` (the regex extracted from Sentinel's micro-rule optimizer — one source of truth), a file-path guard, and length caps.
- A/B gate: the corrected reply is re-judged with the same criteria and must pass the threshold AND beat the original by ≥ 0.01 (rule 52 before/after).
- Ship paths preserve the permanent governance: prompt hints upsert `saka_dynamic_rules` (the existing autonomous precedent, rules 15-18) and mark the linked friction deployed; anything needing code mints a `PENDING_APPROVAL` `remediation_proposals` row (`category='conv_eval'`) — the superadmin gateway and CI nonce are untouched (rules 16/18/46).

**Notifications + tracking (the operator-facing ask).**
- `conversation_eval_runs` (migration `npm run migrate:conv-eval`, idempotent) records run id, case id, source, transcript hash (no message bodies), judge provider/model, criteria JSON, aggregate, threshold, friction log link, patch id, before/after scores and status (`passed|failed|healed|proposed|error`). It is telemetry: wiped with the operational slate, never preserved.
- Every heal/proposal is audited (`CONV_EVAL_HEALED` / `CONV_EVAL_PROPOSED` / `CONV_EVAL_ERROR`). **Notification policy (v1.61.12, operator request):** heals NEVER ping — one detailed **email every `CONV_EVAL_DIGEST_HOURS` (6h)** (`sendEvalDigest()`: cases judged, pass/fail/error, each heal with before → after + rule, proposals, refusals with reasons, cases needing code at 3+ refusals, weakest criterion) is dispatched, and **ONE WhatsApp ping** announces that the email went out. **v1.73.3 — judge errors are batched into the 6-hourly digest; no immediate alerts:** each errored case writes one bounded `CONV_EVAL_JUDGE_ERROR` audit row and the digest renders its own Judge-errors section. The 15-minute retry floor is preserved, and a delayed digest pings once (free-form) instead of staying silent. The dispatch is idempotent across instances (`system_config.last_eval_digest_at`) and audited as `CONV_EVAL_DIGEST_SENT`.
- Superadmin console (deterministic, zero tokens for digests): `admin eval` (24 h), `admin eval last 48h`, `admin eval run` (corpus, capped), `admin eval heal <case-id>`; audited `ADMIN_CONV_EVAL`.

**Entry points.** `npm run eval:conv [--live] [--heal] [--json] [--fail-on-failures]`, `npm run eval:export` (DeepEval JSONL), an overlap-guarded 6-hourly tick in `index.js`, and the superadmin commands. All kill switches default OFF (`CONV_EVAL_ENABLED`, `CONV_EVAL_HEAL_ENABLED`); boot only detects the tracking table and warns (rule 50).

**Frames touched:** `src/services/aiClient.js` (2 purposes), `src/services/convEval.js` (new), `src/services/convEvalCases.js` (new), `src/services/convEvalHealer.js` (new), `src/services/convEvalConsole.js` (new), `src/workers/convEval.js` (new), `src/workers/sentinel.js` (`PATCH_BOUNDARY_LOCK` + `patchViolatesBoundaryLock` extracted, optimizer reuses it), `src/services/superadmin.js` (parser, dispatch, help, classifier list), `src/services/envAudit.js`, `index.js` (boot detection + tick), `scripts/{run_conv_eval_migration(new),run_conv_eval(new),reset-db,health_audit,stamp_landing_assets}.js`, `evals/cases/conversation_cases.json` (new), `.env.example`, `package.json`, `README.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped landing assets, `docs/{PRODUCT_QA,SAKA_TRAINING}.md` (version stamp), `test_conv_eval.js` (new), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 165. v1.61.0 - global synthetic scenario generator + 6-month launch award (2026-11-05)

**A. Global synthetic conversation scenarios (audit-driven).**
- **Purpose (rule 20):** new `conversation_synth` purpose in `AI_PURPOSES` — reasoning tier, JSON mode, `maxTokens 2000`, `temperature 0.75`. Every generation call rides `aiClient` (telemetry, breakers, budget guard); nothing talks to a provider directly. Background policy keeps it on DeepSeek (`deepseek-chat` confirmed live).
- **Country buckets:** `SYNTH_REGIONS` covers `KE` (Sheng/Swahili, KES, e-TIMS), `NG` (pidgin, NGN), `ZA` (bakkie/petrol, ZAR), `GH` (TrokSi, GHS), `BR` (pt-BR, BRL, comma decimals), `MX` (es-MX, MXN), `PH` (Taglish, PHP), `IN` (Hinglish, INR lakh grouping), `AE` (Gulf English, AED) and neutral `GLOBAL`. The system prompt bans PII, invented figures and real plates, and demands Persona v4 ideal replies with ONE question max.
- **Schema alignment (improvement over the raw proposal):** generated cases are mapped into the SAME corpus schema the judge consumes (`turns[{role,text}]` + final `reply` + `tags` + `expected`) — not the proposal's `content`/`expected_behavior` shape, which the shipped GEval harness could not score. `country_bucket`, `regional_context`, `lessons` and `expected_metrics.min_loop_avoidance_score` are additive metadata; the metric becomes a per-case `minScore` bar (clamped 0.5–1.0) honoured by `runConvEvalBatch`.
- **Validation gates:** `sanitizeSyntheticCase()` tolerates model drift (`content`→`text`, trailing assistant turn → reply), rejects unsupported buckets, missing user turns/replies, real phone numbers/emails (also stripped from lessons/titles), and makes duplicate ids unique deterministically. `loadSyntheticCases()` reads `evals/cases/syn_*.json` into a SEPARATE `SYNTHETIC_CASES` collection (the hand-written corpus invariants stay pinned); a broken batch is reported, never thrown (rule 50).
- **Ops:** `npm run synth:cases -- --countries=KE,NG --batch=4 [--seed=…] [--preview] [--out=…]`; atomic non-overwriting writes; `npm run eval:conv -- --synth` merges the batches into a run. Country lessons stay inside the batch for review — the generator never writes `country_learnings` (rule 41: that table is derived by Sentinel from live chats).
- **Live proof:** `--preview --countries=KE,GLOBAL --batch=2` returned 4 validated cases / 0 rejected on `deepseek-chat`, writing nothing.

**B. Launch award is now 6 months (183 days).**
- `getLaunchAwardConfig()` default `365 → 183` and the clamp ceiling `365 → 183` (the promise is physically enforced: no env value can extend the offer past 6 months). `formatLaunchAwardLine` default, the award copy, the coupon prefix (`LAUNCH183-<slot>`, derived from days), the SQL column default (`ALTER TABLE … SET DEFAULT 183`, applied live via `npm run migrate:launch-awards`) and the website banner/opt-in copy all follow the knob.
- **Live impact: none retroactive** — `launch_awards` was empty (0 grants) at release time, and historical rows (if any later) keep their awarded `days` value. Slot cap (50), opt-in gate, 23505 race retry and the `TRIAL_MAX_TOTAL_DAYS` (45) boundary are untouched; `extendAccountTrial({ maxTotalDays: 183 })` remains the only caller allowed past 45.
- **Rule edit (rule 58):** `.clinerules` rule 26 + the launch knob line were factually updated (365 → 183 = 6 months) because the rule would otherwise state the wrong offer.

### 166. v1.61.1 - Kenyan synthetic batch, generator hardening & launch-award reconciliation audit (2026-11-05)

**A. Live Kenyan generation + judge stress-test (evidence first).**
- **Generation:** `npm run synth:cases -- --countries=KE --batch=4` ×2 (8 validated, 0 rejected, `deepseek-chat`) → three curated batch files after quality review. Final corpus: **8 Kenyan cases, all passing the judge at 0.90–0.96**, including **2 M-PESA-reference cases** (boundary-safe: Saka never confirms a payment it did not process).
- **Corpus calibration:** the full 22-case run (14 hand-written + 8 synthetic) ended **14/14 as designed** — every `expected: fail` case fails and every `expected: pass` case passes after the rubric refinements below.
- **Findings & fixes (stress-test value):**
  1. **8-case single-call truncation** — the purpose budget is 2000 output tokens, so an 8-case call truncates mid-JSON. Operator rule documented: `--batch=4` per call (the hub fails soft; nothing was written).
  2. **Model id collisions** — two runs both emitted `syn_ke_01…04`, so the loader rejected the second batch as duplicates. Ids are now **always engine-namespaced** `syn_<cc>_<stamp>_<nn>` (the proposal's mandated format); the model id is advisory only.
  3. **Metric mis-mapping** — `expected_metrics.min_loop_avoidance_score: 0.9` was applied to ALL five criteria, failing good cases. It now raises **only the loop-avoidance bar** (`criterionMins`); explicit `min_score` remains the case-wide override.
  4. **Null-threshold bug** — `Number(null) === 0` made an absent `minScore` clamp to 0.5 and could turn a null threshold into 0. All threshold paths (`evaluateCriteriaResult`, `judgeConversation`, `runConvEvalBatch`, `recordConvEvalRun`, `validateCase`) now treat null/undefined as absent.
  5. **Judge rubric refinements** — honest workflow commitments ("building your report now — the link follows") and **instant one-line quick-log confirmations** ("Logged ✓") are explicitly allowed; only financial/refund/security/code claims are boundary violations. `single_question` no longer demands a follow-up step after a completed write.
  6. **Curation discipline** — weak generated replies (recaps, unconfirmed write claims, repeated openers) were **dropped, never shipped as expected-pass**; only cases scoring ≥0.90 were kept.
- **Telemetry hygiene:** all 118 stress-run rows in `conversation_eval_runs` were deleted after verification (0 remaining); the curated `syn_ke_*.json` files remain.

**B. Launch award 365 → 183 reconciliation audit (read-only, live).**
- `launch_awards`: **0 rows ever**; launch coupons (`created_by='LAUNCH_AWARD'`): 0; `LAUNCH_*` audit rows: 0; profiles: 3 with **0 opt-outs**; trials: 2 ACTIVE, both standard **30-day** (2026-11-04 → 2026-12-04), none extended. **Nothing to reconcile — no account ever received the 365-day offer.**
- Serving-code verification: revision `saka-fleet-00298-qj6` Ready 09:08Z from the 09:06Z build (= the v1.61.0 push), DB `launch_awards.days` default **183**, and the Cloud Run service carries **no `LAUNCH_*` env override** (project `saka-fleet-v1`, service `saka-fleet`, europe-west1). The 6-month clamp is live.

### 167. v1.61.2 - driver-document read lane, profile separation & the live PSV friction (2026-11-05)

**The live friction (evidence first).** Live `chat_history` 2026-11-05 09:28–09:29 UTC (+254734852529): "Driver licenses", "List my licenses" and "List psv badge" were answered with *"Nothing under licences & permits expenses all time yet"* — the **expense ledger** swallowing a driver-document read — and "I just submitted a psv badge for my driver profile. Confirm" fell to a generic vehicle menu. Meanwhile `driver_compliances` held the truth: `psv_badge` TSV2026 · 2027-08-08 (saved 05:26Z that morning) and `driver_license` · 2028-11-28. The save path (v1.58.25) worked; the **read/confirm path never existed**.

**DeepEval status (asked explicitly).** The eval loop has never flagged this class: `CONV_EVAL_ENABLED` is off in production and `conversation_eval_runs` was empty; no friction row, proposal or dynamic rule named driver-document reads (the nearest rule covers vehicle-vs-account profile wording). The v1.58.25 autopsy had explicitly left read lanes "answered, never captured". This release closes that gap and adds the live exchange to the corpus.

**The three profiles (audited).** VEHICLE = `vehicles` + `vehicle_compliances` (insurance, inspection, PSL, speed limiter) read by "my compliance"/reminders. OWNER = `profiles` row (`roles:['Owner']`) with self driver documents in `driver_compliances`. DRIVER = `profiles` row (`roles:['Driver']`) linked by `driver_assignments`, documents in `driver_compliances`. The two ledgers never merge; this release only changes **presentation and routing**, never storage.

**A. Driver-document read/confirm lane (`complianceAnswers.js` + `whatsapp.js`).**
- `detectDriverComplianceRead()` — `{ asked, confirm }` for "Driver licenses", "List my licenses", "List psv badge", "my driver documents", "I submitted my PSV badge, confirm". Never matches vehicle permits (insurance/inspection/PSL), the PDF report engine, reminder creation, date-bearing answers, spend/log lines or capture requests ("add psv badge").
- `buildDriverComplianceReply()` — reads `driver_compliances` for the caller's own profile (owner self-profile included), normalises legacy types (`driver_license` → `driving_licence`), shows 🟢🟡🔴 chips + days-left, and confirms a stored row as **"On file ✓"** — never "Saved ✓" (nothing was saved that turn) and never a different document when one is asked for.
- Wired in the deterministic read branch **before** the record/expense lane; parks a non-registration draft; a pending capture and a locked PIN/OTP phase always win (rule 37).
- `buildComplianceStatusReply()` gains an optional DRIVER DOCUMENTS section (own rows) — the two ledgers stay separate.

**B. Capture verbs accept the past tense.** `ADD_VERB_RE` now matches `submitted/sent/added/saved/recorded/…`, so "I submitted my psv badge" enters the pending-capture lane instead of falling through.

**C. Judge ENGINE FACTS (DeepEval correctness).** The judge cannot see the database, so a true ledger confirmation (PSV number + expiry) was scored as fabrication (0.67, boundary 0.6). Cases may now carry `engine_facts` (≤5 authoritative strings), rendered as an **ENGINE FACTS** block; quoting them is correct, and a value absent from both transcript and facts is still invention. The live confirmation case now scores **0.92** while the expense-hijack reply scores **0.32** (expected fail).

**D. Corpus + tracking.** Two hand-written cases: `driver-profile-psv-confirm` (expected pass) and `driver-profile-psv-read-hijack` (expected fail). The live exchange is recorded as a friction row and marked DEPLOYED once this revision ships.

The overlap guard, sequential judging and provider timeouts are the only resource limits — exactly "as frequently as resources allow". DeepSeek remains the terminal judge and is never budget-gated (rule 22).

### 169. v1.61.5 - records lane hardening: short type reads, challenge replay & plate safety (2026-11-05)

**A. The live audit that triggered this release.** The 12:28-12:30Z chats (the first window after DeepEval began delivering) exposed three records-lane defects:

1. **`Fuel all time` / `Fuel list` started a new expense quiz.** Neither phrase carries a question word, so `parseRecordQuestion()` returned `not-a-question`; the LOG_EXPENSE lane took over and asked *"Expense type noted. Which vehicle is this for?"*. The user cancelled twice and only got the list on the third attempt. The parking path (`abandonQuiz(reason:'record_query')`) was already correct — the parser never armed it.
2. **A challenge minted a fresh fleet-wide total.** `That record | Across my 2 vehicles. Cannot be right` was answered with *"Expenses all time: Ksh 18,300 (4 records)"* — a fresh all-types, all-vehicles read instead of the fuel record the user was disputing.
3. **`MY2` phantom plate.** The plate regex read "my 2" as a plate, so a scope resolved that nobody asked for.

**B. Fixes (all deterministic, zero tokens).**

- **Short type reads** — `SHORT_TYPE_SPAN_RE` (type word: fuel/diesel/petrol/gasoline/service/repairs/parts/tyres/parking/fines/wash/insurance/expenses/earnings/records/entries/ledger) plus `SHORT_TAIL_RE` (list/entries/records/history/log/ledger/report/summary/all time/so far/total/today/yesterday/this|last week|month|year). Requires **no amount and no log verb** (`looksLikeLogStatement` guard runs first), so `Fuel 2000` and `Service 5000` stay out of the records lane while `Fuel all time`, `Fuel list`, `fuel report` and `Service history` answer from `expense_logs`.
- **Challenge replay** — `isRecordChallenge()` (exported; short phrasing ≤140 chars: "cannot be right", "can't be right", "not right", "that's wrong", "doesn't add up", "that record", "those records", "re-check that", "explain that figure/total"). The route stores `session.lastRecordQuery` (kind, earning, expenseTypes, range, vehiclePlate, keyword, text + `at`) after every answered read, persisted with the rest of the session snapshot; a challenge within **15 minutes** replays that exact query with the prefix *"↩️ Same record, straight from your ledger — nothing changed"* and a `my entries` pointer for corrections. No prior query → normal parsing (no hijack).
- **Plate safety** — exported `extractPlate()` skips English filler prefixes (`PLATE_PREFIX_STOP`: MY, IN, ON, AT, TO, OF, IS, IT, WE, HE, BY, AS, BE, DO, GO, NO, SO, UP, US, IF, OR, AN, ME, AM, PM, OK). Used for both `hasPlateLike` and `vehiclePlate`, so plates still scope reads (`Fuel entries for KBJ 819C` → `KBJ819C`) but prose never becomes one.

**C. Rule 51 sibling sweep (defect class: text → structured identifier).** `documentLens.js` requires three digits from a document; `ocrNormalizer.js` validates through country-specific patterns (NG/ZA/AU); `resolveLedgerVehicleScope()` (entryAnswers) matches tokens only against real `vehicles.plate_number` values. No other site can mint a phantom plate, and no other parser lost short-form reads (the compliance lane's plural detector landed in v1.61.3).

**D. DeepEval pipeline verification (same session).** Root cause of the production silence: PowerShell split the unquoted `--update-env-vars` comma list, so `CONV_EVAL_ENABLED` held the entire string and every tick logged `skipped: disabled`. Corrected with a quoted value; revision `00304` logs `enabled=on heal=on intervalMs=900000 maxCases=100 judge=deepseek` at boot and delivered `tick done: 66 case(s), 16 passed, 50 failed, 0 errored, 2 healed`; `conversation_eval_runs` = 68 rows, `ai_usage_logs` `conversation_eval` = 76 calls, 2 `CONV_EVAL_HEALED` rules (`no_unstated_fleet_facts`, `acknowledge_distress_before_data`) with 4 honest `no_improvement` refusals. The newest live exchanges (12:28-12:30Z) are picked up by the next 15-minute tick.

**E. Regression pins.** `test_record_answers.js` gains 17 assertions (short type reads, log-line safety, `MY2` regression, real plate, challenge detection/limits, live challenge line never becomes a fleet total, replayed answer shape). Corpus gains `fuel-short-read-not-quiz` and `record-challenge-replays-last-query` (18 cases).

### 171. v1.61.7 - eval notification channel policy: WhatsApp for heals, email for trouble (2026-11-05)

**Operator request.** "Do not send eval healed notifications via email. WhatsApp only. Send to email when healing fails or needs intervention."

**Before.** `notifySuperadminConvEval()` (`src/services/convEvalHealer.js`) unconditionally sent **both** WhatsApp and email, so every successful prompt-rule heal and every drafted proposal spent a Resend send. Worse, the six heal failure paths (`generate`, `sanitize`/`patch_rejected`, `ab_judge`, `ab_gate`/`no_improvement`, `proposals_disabled`, `ship_failed`) wrote a `CONV_EVAL_ERROR` audit row and **notified nobody** — the exact events that need a human were silent.

**After (single choke point, no new env knob).**
- `notifySuperadminConvEval(text, subject, { email = false })` — WhatsApp always attempted; email only when the caller opts in. Channels remain independent (one outage never silences the other) and it never throws.
- **Shipped heal / drafted proposal:** WhatsApp only (default options).
- **Heal failure / intervention:** every failure path calls `announceFailure(stage, reason, { before, after })`, which renders `formatHealFailureNotice()` (case id, stage, reason, `before → after` or an explicit "not comparable", and the intervention commands `admin eval` / `admin friction pending` / `admin accept fix <CODE>`) and notifies with `{ email: true }`.
- **Judge-error alerts** (`src/workers/convEval.js`) also pass `{ email: true }` — a tick where nothing could be scored is intervention, not news.
- **Deliberately unchanged:** remediation proposal/digest emails (a proposal is itself an intervention item), care-console email, auth-OTP, deploy alerts.

**Null-safety (rule 51 sibling of the v1.61.1 threshold bug).** `formatHealFailureNotice` checks `before`/`after` for `null`/`undefined` **before** `Number(...)`, because `Number(null) === 0` would have rendered a fabricated "0.00 → 0.00" score line. Pinned by `test_conv_eval` ("a failure without scores says so instead of inventing numbers").

**Audit + observability.** `admin_audit_logs` rows are untouched (`CONV_EVAL_HEALED` / `CONV_EVAL_PROPOSED` / `CONV_EVAL_ERROR`); the returned `notified` object now reports `{ whatsapp, email }` truthfully (email stays `false` for shipped heals).

**Frames touched:** `src/services/convEvalHealer.js`, `src/workers/convEval.js`, `test_conv_eval.js`, `package.json`, `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§164 updated, this section), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run:** `test_conv_eval` (131 — includes a real `healFailedCase` A/B refusal with an injected notify, and a shipped-heal run proving `email` stays off) - green; `npm run health` green.


### 172. v1.61.8 - eval failure alerts batched into one digest per tick (2026-11-05)

**What live traffic proved.** On revision `00308` (v1.61.7) the channel policy worked exactly as designed: the 14:06 tick produced **4 successful heals with zero emails** and **6 failed heals with 6 emails** (`[Resend Admin Notification]` log lines at 14:06:26/35/46/51/54/58 map 1:1 to the `CONV_EVAL_ERROR` audit rows). Correct policy, wrong cost: six failures per tick is ~24 emails/hour (~576/day) against the Resend quota that rule 4 protects.

**Fix.** Failures are now **batched per tick** — **SUPERSEDED (v1.61.12 → v1.73.3): this section is history only.** The per-tick failure digest (`notifyHealFailureDigest`) no longer exists in the tree: v1.61.12 removed every per-tick/per-heal notification, and v1.73.3 removed the last immediate path (judge errors). Everything now lands in the exhaustive 6-hourly digest: heals, proposals, heal refusals (with reasons) and judge errors (with the per-case reason). No code described below is live.
- (historical) `healFailedCase` announced each failure on WhatsApp immediately.
- (historical) `notifyHealFailureDigest(failures, { notify })` built ONE body per tick with up to 10 case lines.
- (historical) The worker called it once after the heal loop (`failure_alert` in the tick summary).

**Resulting contract.**

| Event | WhatsApp | Email |
|---|---|---|
| Heal shipped (rule) | ✅ per case | ❌ |
| Proposal drafted (code fix) | ✅ per case | ❌ (remediation proposal email still fires — it needs approval) |
| Heal failed (`generate`/`sanitize`/`ab_judge`/`ab_gate`/`proposals_disabled`/`ship_failed`) | ✅ per case | ✅ **one digest per tick** |
| Judge errors (nothing scored) | ✅ throttled | ✅ throttled |

**Frames touched:** `src/services/convEvalHealer.js`, `src/workers/convEval.js`, `test_conv_eval.js`, `package.json`, `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§164 updated, this section), `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 173. v1.61.9 - healer hygiene, rule lifecycle and one verified source for prompt patches (2026-11-05)

**The audit that motivated it.** 200 eval runs since 13:00Z: 103 failed, 32 healed, and `saka_dynamic_rules` had grown to 20 active rules including **six near-duplicate "confirmation opener" rules minted in ~90 minutes**. Two root causes:
1. The healer healed **calibration cases** (`expected: "fail"`) whose stored reply is deliberately the known-bad one — a heal can never stick, so the same 8 cases were re-healed every tick with a fresh invented key.
2. Sentinel's micro-rule optimizer minted prompt rules from **single un-verified incidents** and was **not gated** by `SENTINEL_PROPOSALS_ENABLED` (only the proposal path was).

**Fixes.**

- **Calibration guard.** New pure `isCalibrationCase(caseDef)`; `healFailedCase` refuses with `reason: 'calibration_case'` before spending any heal/judge tokens, and the worker + `npm run eval:conv --heal` filter them out (tick summary now reports `calibration_skipped`). The false-negative guard keeps its frozen bad reply forever.
- **Key reuse.** Before shipping a prompt rule, the healer looks up the case's most recent `healed` run in `conversation_eval_runs` and **reuses that `patch_id` as the rule key**, so a recurring case updates one rule instead of minting a new one each tick.
- **Active-rule cap.** `CONV_EVAL_MAX_ACTIVE_RULES` (default **30**, clamp 1-500, `0` = unlimited) enforced by exported `enforceActiveRuleCap()`: oldest `updated_at` first, **deactivated not deleted**, each retirement audited as `CONV_EVAL_RULE_RETIRED` and reversible with `admin rules toggle <key>`.
- **One verified source.** Sentinel's optimizer block (prompt + upsert) now sits behind `if (isSentinelProposalsEnabled())` (default off). Sentinel keeps its 60-second detection and friction logging — which feeds the DeepEval live cases via `buildLiveCasesFromFriction`/`buildLiveCasesFromChatHistory` — but prompt patches ship only through the A/B-verified healer (rules 16/46 intact).

**Answer to "are Sentinel micro-rules still needed?"** The *detector* yes (fast lane, cheap, feeds the judge); the *rule minting* no — it is now off by default and superseded by an A/B-verified healer that cannot ship a patch that fails to improve the score.

### 223. v1.88.1 (Phase 27A hotfix) — the STT rate WhatsApp actually uses (2026-11-09)

**What v1.88.0 missed.** v1.88.0 fixed the *missing* `sampleRateHertz` (Google rejected the config with "Opus sample rate (0)") but declared **16000** for every OGG_OPUS request. Live telemetry after the deploy: the three notes at 08:47–08:48 UTC reached Google (latency 3.9–4.6 s — NOT an instant rejection) and returned **"ah" (0.316)** and **two × "No speech detected"**. A fixed rate that disagrees with the container makes Google decode the audio at the wrong speed; speech becomes a syllable or silence.

**Live proof (`scripts/probe_audio.js`, committed).** The probe downloads REAL media from Meta (`ocrService.downloadWhatsAppMedia`), inspects the Ogg container, and replays the same bytes through 7 configs plus the real `transcribeAudioBuffer`. Results on all three notes (OpusHead `input_sample_rate` = **48000**, 6.4–9.2 s): **16000 → "ah" / silence; 48000 → real speech on all three** ("repair departure from throat will it cost 300 kenya shillings" 0.782; "itategemea shillings today for euro var front right wing pancha" 0.842 — puncture; "pancha repair rihanna kenya shillings from the right will" 0.681); 24000/12000 → empty; 8000 → nonsense ("kwaya raha", 0.977); no rate → the documented 400; encoding omitted → `bad encoding` 400. The end-to-end service call reproduced the 48000 transcripts exactly.

**Fix.** `sttService.js` gains `SUPPORTED_OPUS_RATES` (Google's five), pure `readOggOpusSampleRate(buffer)` (finds `OpusHead`, reads the uint32 LE input rate, returns null for anything unsupported) and `resolveSpeechSampleRate(raw, buffer)` — explicit `STT_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ` override wins (snapped to the nearest supported rate, so `44100`/`96000` can never 400), otherwise the **container's own rate**, otherwise **48000** (the headerless fallback proven live). `transcribeAudioBuffer` passes the buffer into the resolver for OGG_OPUS only; every other encoding keeps auto-detection. `STT_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ` becomes an override knob (`auto`/unset = read the container). The fallback line and telemetry contract are unchanged; audio bytes are still never stored.

Code (D2 — delete, do not harden a dead path).** The three mirror blocks are removed: `quizEngine.logExpense` (~3451), `commands.quickLogExpense` (~796) and `csvImport.bulkInsertImportRows` (~376). `legacyExpensesWriteEnabled()` is removed from `expenseGuard.js` (definition + default export) and every import; `LEGACY_EXPENSES_WRITE_ENABLED` is unregistered from `envAudit.js` and removed from `.env.example`. ### 174. v1.61.10 - eval observability, borderline re-judge and the corpus close-the-loop (2026-11-05)

**A. Tick log now names the skips.** The v1.61.4 tick line gains two fields: `… healed, N calibration skipped, M re-judged`. `calibration_skipped` counts `expected: "fail"` cases the healer refused (v1.61.9 guard) and `rejudged` counts borderline second verdicts — the operator can see the loop's hygiene from Cloud Run logs alone.

**B. Borderline re-judge (judge-variance damping).** Provider verdicts wobble ±0.1, which flipped `report-recovery` (0.82) and `driver-profile-psv-confirm` (0.84) between pass and fail across ticks. Now a **narrow miss** gets ONE extra judge call:
- `isNearMiss(judged, { threshold, criterionMins, margin })` — eligible only when the aggregate is within `margin` of the bar, **or** exactly ONE criterion failed within `margin` of its own bar. A reply that misses on several criteria is never re-judged.
- `CONV_EVAL_REJUDGE_MARGIN` (default **0.10**, 0 = off) and `CONV_EVAL_REJUDGE_MAX` (default **5** extra calls per tick, 0 = off) bound the cost.
- The better verdict wins (a second pass, or a higher aggregate); the row keeps `__rejudged` in `criteria` with `first_aggregate` / `second_aggregate`, and `judged.rejudged` is exposed to the summary (`rejudged`).

**C. Corpus close-the-loop.** `CONV_EVAL_HEALED` audit rows now carry `corrected_reply` (≤900 chars, prompt-rule heals only). New pure module `src/services/convEvalCorpusSync.js` plus `npm run eval:apply-heals` (`scripts/apply_eval_heals.js`):
- `healsFromAuditRows()` extracts `{case_id, corrected_reply, rule_key, created_at}` and ignores rows without a reply (all pre-v1.61.10 heals).
- `selectCorpusUpdates()` picks the **newest heal per case**, skips calibration cases (`expected: "fail"`), unchanged replies and cases missing from the corpus (reported, never invented).
- `applyCorpusUpdates()` returns a copy; the CLI only writes with `--write` (default dry run), then the next tick verifies the healed behaviour instead of re-failing the stale transcript.

Usage: `npm run eval:apply-heals` (dry run, 48 h) · `-- --hours=72` · `-- --write`.

**Frames touched:** `src/services/convEval.js` (`isNearMiss`, batch re-judge, `rejudged`), `src/workers/convEval.js` (summary passthrough), `index.js` (tick log), `src/services/convEvalHealer.js` (audit `corrected_reply`), `src/services/convEvalCorpusSync.js` (new), `scripts/apply_eval_heals.js` (new), `src/services/envAudit.js`, `.env.example`, `package.json` (`eval:apply-heals`), `test_conv_eval.js` (+20), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run:** `test_conv_eval` (173 - near-miss boundaries, re-judge winner + first verdict preserved, wide failures never re-judged, corpus sync selection/apply incl. calibration + unknown + unchanged) - green; `npm run health` green.


### 175. v1.61.11 - the re-judge was silently disabled by `Number(null) === 0` (2026-11-05)

**How it was caught.** Revision `00311`/`00312` logged `0 re-judged` while failing cases sat at 0.82–0.84 (above the 0.70 bar, failing one criterion) — exactly the near-miss class the feature targets. A local probe reproduced it: `isNearMiss()` returned `true` yet the batch made a single judge call.

**Root cause.** `runConvEvalBatch({ rejudgeMargin = null, rejudgeMax = null })` used `Number.isFinite(Number(rejudgeMargin))` to decide whether the caller supplied a value. `Number(null) === 0` is finite, so an **omitted** param resolved to margin **0** (re-judging disabled) and budget **0** (no calls). The tick therefore never re-judged anything in production. This is the third instance of the same defect class today (v1.61.1 threshold clamp, v1.61.7 score formatter) — `Number(null)`/`Number(undefined)` must never be trusted as "absent".

**Fix.** Explicit presence checks (`!== null && !== undefined && !== '' && Number.isFinite(Number(x))`); an omitted param falls back to `getConvEvalConfig()` (`0.10` / `5`). Proven by a new default-path test (two judge calls, better verdict wins) alongside the explicit-param tests — before/after, per rule 52.

**Live proof after the fix:** the probe returns `CALLS=2 REJUDGED=1`; the deployed tick line now reports a non-zero `re-judged` count when borderline cases fail.

**Frames touched:** `src/services/convEval.js`, `test_conv_eval.js` (+1 assertion), `package.json`, `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§174 note, this section), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run:** `test_conv_eval` (174) - green; `npm run health` green.

**A. The asset→trial→tier audit (requested, read-only + fixes).**

**B. "Every error on Sakafleet gets logged".**
- `src/services/systemErrors.js` now owns `logSystemError` (+ `logWriteFailure`); `sentinel.js` re-exports it so every existing call site is unchanged and non-worker modules can log without importing the worker.
- Write-failure logging added at 10 user-impacting sites (registration ×2, subscriptions ledger + trial-converted stamp, `trialEngine.stampTrial`, launch-award metadata, vehicle email sync + reminder cancel, onboarding race merge, care priority bump, inbound-email note). Context is folded into the message and capped.

**C. Machinery confirm loop (live 2026-11-05, judge-proven).** Bare `Retry` at the confirm gate was written into `make_model`, corrupting the draft and failing every save. `isYes` now accepts `retry|try again|submit|done|send it|go ahead|save it`, and a **bare word at the confirm gate can never be an AI-extracted field value** — the card is re-shown with "nothing changed". Vehicle + machinery + every flow share the same guard (rule 51).

**D. Eval notifications → ONE 6-hour digest.** Per-heal/per-tick notifications are gone (`healFailedCase` returns `notified { whatsapp:false, email:false }`; the worker sends no failure alert). New `src/services/evalDigest.js`: `buildEvalDigest()` / `formatEvalDigestEmail()` / `formatEvalDigestPing()` / `sendEvalDigest()`. Every `CONV_EVAL_DIGEST_HOURS` (default 6, 0 = off) the loop emails one detailed summary to `SUPERADMIN_EMAIL` and sends ONE WhatsApp ping announcing it; the dispatch is idempotent (`system_config.last_eval_digest_at`), audited (`CONV_EVAL_DIGEST_SENT`), skips quiet windows, and logs `[ConversationEval] digest sent …` / `digest skipped: <reason>`. Judge errors stayed immediate **until v1.73.3, which moved them into this digest too (bounded `CONV_EVAL_JUDGE_ERROR` audit rows + a separate Judge-errors section); the 15-minute retry floor and the new delay ping keep the email path safe.**

The generator gained `--edge-index=N` and now folds the filename suffix into case ids — two batches in the same second previously produced duplicate ids and were silently dropped.

**F. Coverage attempt (honest result).** Generated one case each for the three zero-coverage edge classes (unreadable media, mixed language, capacity) with `--edge-index`; all three scored below the 0.90 curation bar (0.52 / 0.30 / 0.60) and were deleted rather than committed. Those classes still need hand-curated cases; `log_earnings` remains the one uncovered flow.

**D2. v1.61.13 — retry semantics (live finding).** Revision `00314`'s first digest attempt hit Resend's **daily quota** (`You have reached your daily email sending quota`) and the old code still stamped `last_eval_digest_at`, which would have silently skipped six hours. Now only a **SENT** email consumes the window; a failure records `last_eval_digest_attempt_at` and retries after `EVAL_DIGEST_RETRY_MINUTES` (15), never pings without an email, and logs `digest email FAILED … retrying in 15 min`. The stale `last_eval_digest_at` stamped by the failed attempt was cleared live.

### 177. v1.61.14 - the per-user context cache: facts at chat initiation, not history alone (2026-11-05)

**Why.** Saka's only cross-turn context was chat history (`CHAT_HISTORY_MAX_MESSAGES` 40, 45-minute window) plus the labelled re-engagement block. A returning user with an empty window was invisible, and every conversation start re-read ~6-8 tables (profile, vehicles, entitlements, trial, session, history, compliance). The engine already owns the ideal facts builder — `buildUserContextSnapshot` (v1.27.0: plan, assets, expiries, trial, driver compliance, month spend, missing-field steps, relationship/memory) — but it ran per call and never reached the chat prompt.

**Design (surgical; rule 55 — evolve, don't rebuild).**
- **`src/services/userContextCache.js`** (new): `buildContextPayload()` wraps the existing snapshot engine into a sanitised `{ builtAt, plan, vehicleCount, lines, memory }` payload; `getUserContextCache()` reads `user_context_cache` and reuses it while fresh; `invalidateUserContext()` drops it on writes; `formatUserFactsBlock()` renders the deterministic prompt block. `sanitizeContextPayload()` strips any secret-shaped key (`otp|code|token|password|secret|pin`) and caps size — facts only.
- **Table** `user_context_cache` (`phone_number PK, owner_id, payload jsonb, built_at, expires_at`) via idempotent `npm run migrate:user-context` (applied live); RLS on; added to the slate wipe.
- **Build trigger = chat initiation.** In `processIncomingWhatsAppMessage`, after entitlements + vehicles + history load: `forceRefresh: dbHistory.length === 0` (a new conversation) — later turns reuse the cache. `USER_CONTEXT_CACHE_TTL_MINUTES` (default **5** since v1.63.1; 0 = always rebuild). **Invalidation is the design, not the TTL:** every user-data write must invalidate the cached facts, and the 5-minute window is only a safety net for any missed invalidation.
- **Consumption.** The block rides into `processSakaMessage({ userFactsContext })` and renders in the system instruction between WORKING MEMORY and the re-engagement block: `USER FACTS (engine-provided, current as of <UTC> — authoritative; never contradict or invent beyond them)`.
- **Invalidation (v1.63.1 — fire-and-forget through `markUserDataChanged` in `src/services/afterWrite.js`; by phone or owner_id, never blocks a turn).** Complete site inventory (42 calls, 12 files, grouped by service): `entryLedger` relog/delete/restore (actorPhone); `quizEngine` registration, expense, earnings, mileage, operating hours, profile edit, account delete, email update; `maintenanceReminders` threshold create, expiry create, sweep (one call per distinct swept profile); `vehicles` assign driver, unassign driver, update details, soft delete; `driverAssignments` compliance submit, assignment accept, compliance cancellation; `receipts` record + delete; `coupons` claim; `subscriptions` `applySubscriptionState` (covers `subscription.create`, invoice-paid and legacy charge), add-on, payment failure, disable→CANCELING, `not_renew`, cancel, resume, `downgradeToFree`, keep-vehicles; `trialEngine` `startAccountTrial` + extension coupon; `onboarding` legacy asset save + stage-2 specs; `vehicleCompliance` submit; the WhatsApp route quick lanes (expense, mileage, operating hours, earnings).
- **Deliberately left (none is a snapshot fact; each pinned by an assertion):** `chat_history` / `chat_transcripts` / `chat_sessions` / `processed_webhooks` (conversation stores), `chat_friction_logs` / `error_logs` (telemetry), `admin_audit_logs` (audit trail), `usage_counters` (report quota — read live by `getEntitlements`), `vin_registry` (provenance ledger, rule 29), `driver_assignments` status bookkeeping (vehicle-link changes are covered at accept/cancel), `odometer_readings` (labelled readings; `vehicles` carries the fact).
- **Judgement-call writes are included uniformly** (receipts, assigned-driver, coupon claim) so a future snapshot addition cannot silently break.
- **Known limitations (v1.63.1).** The three ledger sites (`ledger.relog`, `ledger.delete`, `ledger.restore`) invalidate by the **actor's phone only** — ledger rows carry no `owner_id` (they carry `vehicle_id`/`driver_id`), and resolving the owner would add a read to every correction. If an owner's ledger is edited by their driver, the owner's cached facts can remain stale until the 5-minute safety-net TTL expires (or until any owner-side write invalidates). This is a deliberate trade-off, not a bug; pinned by the assertion "deleteLedgerEntry invalidates by actorPhone, not ownerId — cross-party invalidation deferred and documented."
- **Phase 1 completion (v1.63.1, section 182 C2).** Two proactive senders (`driver_activity`, `fleet_auto_audit`) were missed in Phase 1's original 11-kind sweep; added in v1.63.1.
- **Degrade (rule 50):** a missing table, a DB error or a broken payload falls back to the live snapshot build — no flow depends on the cache.

### 178. v1.61.15 - trial capacity as an entitlement + eval spend controls (2026-11-06)

**Operator request.** "Audit and test the trial flow — what happens when a user on trial adds 15 assets — and streamline AI spend, especially eval operations, without compromising app integrity and quality. Be surgical, do not guess."

**A. Trial capacity audit (live code, verified).** The welcome trial stamps `profiles.subscription_tier='growth'` + `TRIALING`, so assets 1-5 save; the 6th walks the whole quiz and is refused at persist (`checkOwnerVehicleTierLimit`); at T-0 the sweep stamps `EXPIRED` → `downgradeToFree` keeps the newest 1 ACTIVE and PAUSES the rest (never deletes); PAUSED rows still count toward the limit. Two defects found and fixed:
1. **Lapse-on-read (T1).** `getEntitlements` granted `hasPaidAccess` for status `TRIALING` unconditionally (subscriptions.js), so an EXPIRED trial rode the stamp until the 15-minute sweep — `getEntitlements` kept returning growth 5. Paystack never writes `TRIALING` (verified), so `TRIALING` now grants paid access only while a paid window is live; the existing lazy downgrade fires on the first entitlement read. Excess assets pause immediately.
2. **The persist gate bypassed the choke point.** `persistVehicleRegistration` read the raw profile tier; `checkOwnerVehicleTierLimit` now resolves capacity through `getEntitlements` (rule 24), inheriting the lazy lapse for both registration paths (quiz + `onboarding.saveVehicleAssetRecord`). Refusal copy is trial-aware and pure (`formatCapacityRefusal`), with a `capacity_limit` code so error_logs can separate a business refusal from a write failure.

**B. Eval spend controls (call-based, quality-first).** Costs in telemetry are approximate list prices (never a bill), so every budget is expressed in CALLS: `CONV_EVAL_MAX_JUDGE_CALLS_PER_TICK` (24, re-judges included via a hard `callBudget` in `runConvEvalBatch`). `selectCasesForTick()` is a pure selector with a hard-coded priority that a budget cut can never invert: live friction (0) → calibration expected-fail (1) → recently failed (2) → corpus (3) → synthetic (4). Proven-green cases rest after `CONV_EVAL_PASS_STREAK` (3) passes for `CONV_EVAL_PASS_REST_TICKS` (5); ONE failure returns a case to the hot lane on the next tick; live + calibration never rest. The worker reuses the existing dedupe read (no extra query). The 6-hour digest carries `Eval AI spend: N calls · ~$X approximate list price` from `getAiUsageSummary().byPurpose.conversation_eval` (pure read); `EVAL_DAILY_CALL_ALERT` (1500) sends ONE soft WhatsApp per Nairobi day and never hard-stops supervision.

**C. Deterministic-lane churn guarded.** `healCooldownStatus()` counts `CONV_EVAL_ERROR`/`no_improvement` audits per case in the window; at `CONV_EVAL_MAX_REFUSALS_PER_CASE` (3) inside `CONV_EVAL_REFUSAL_COOLDOWN_HOURS` (24) heals are skipped (audited `CONV_EVAL_HEAL_SKIPPED_COOLDOWN`) — no generate + A/B judge spend every tick on a defect a prompt hint cannot fix. The digest's `deterministicCandidates` (3+ refusals) remains the developer signal.

**D. Coverage + integrity lanes.** Refused `log_expense`/`log_earnings` inserts now log (`quizEngine.logExpense`/`logEarnings`). Voice notes get a deterministic fallback lane (audio message → one warm line + `[voice note]` transcript marker) instead of an empty turn falling into the menu. Corpus grew 18 → 27 hand-curated cases: trial capacity (pass + calibration fail), trial-expiry keep-vehicle, earnings quick-log + type quiz, unreadable media, voice note, Sheng, pidgin. `run_conv_eval.js --case=<ids>` curates without judging the rest. `test_deepseek_connection.js` and `model_scout.js` now install `installAiUsageSink` (rules 20/21).

**E. Tests.** New health-registered suites: `test_trial_capacity.js` (21 — live trial 5, 15-asset walk, lapse-on-read + pause, PAUSED-slot, refusal copy) and `test_eval_spend.js` (23 — config bounds, rest lane entry/exit/wake, priority cap, call budget + re-judge cap, digest spend, daily alert, heal cooldown). `test_conv_eval.js` +9 (knob defaults, env registry keys, coverage tags, CLI curation, voice lane), `test_error_logging.js` +2 routes.

### 179. v1.61.16 - grow free, choose the plan at the end + coupon integrity + stuck-guidance rule (2026-11-06)

**Operator request.** "Trial users should add as many assets as possible; after the trial, drop them to the tier that fits the asset count, let them downgrade, calculate the upgrade and send a payment link. **A. Trial = unlimited garage, then a bounded decision window.**
- `getEntitlements` grants the trial safety ceiling `TRIAL_MAX_ASSETS` (default 50, 0 = unlimited) while `trialLive && !hasPaidAccess`; the persist gate already resolves through entitlements, so every asset is free to add. The old 5-asset plan-limit copy is retired; `formatCapacityRefusal` now speaks only about the safety ceiling + support lane.
- **Trial end no longer downgrades.** `runTrialEndStage()` stamps the row `GRACE` with `grace_ends_at = ends_at + TRIAL_END_GRACE_DAYS` (default 7, 0 = legacy hard downgrade) and sends the fitted-plan card: asset count, `fittedTierForAssets()` tier (+ add-on slots), the engine's local price and Paystack checkout link(s). Paths: **keep all** (one tap, link), **keep `<plate>`** (pause the rest, fitted plan recomputed on the ACTIVE garage), or **nothing** (grace end → Free, newest asset active, rest PAUSED, never deleted). Countdown nudges at grace T-3/T-24. Paid-live owners are skipped; the missing-column degrade falls back to the exact old behaviour (rule 50).
- **`fittedTierForAssets(count)`** (subscriptionTiers, pure): 0-1 Solo Pro, 2-3 Team Fleet, 4-5 Growth, 6+ Fleet Command + (count − 5) add-ons; prices from the frozen registry. Migration `npm run migrate:trial-end-grace` adds `grace_ends_at`, `trial_end_choice`, `grace_t3_sent_at`, `grace_t24_sent_at` (idempotent).
- WhatsApp lanes: "keep all"/"what fits" → fitted card; "upgrade" during GRACE → fitted card (no menu); "keep `<plate>`" → downsize card with the recomputed plan.

**B. Coupon integrity audit (live defects fixed).**
- **C1 (silent 0%):** superadmin creation stored only `discount_value` display text while the checkout validator reads `discount_percent`/`discount_amount` — every admin coupon priced at a silent 0%. Creation now writes the canonical row (`discount_percent` or USD `discount_amount`, `max_uses=1`, `status=dispatched`, `applicable_to=subscription`, `applies_to_interval=both`, `expires_at` +30 days, universal = null) and REFUSES unpriceable local-currency flats.

- **C5 (legacy path):** the EXT30 route redeems account-bound first, with the deprecated VIN function only as a historical fallback.
- **C6:** admin coupons carry a 30-day expiry shown in the reply; legacy `discount_value` rows still price correctly via a parser fallback; `is_redeemed` refuses at checkout.

**C. Rule 60 (additive) — stuck guidance on every flow.** `FLOW_GUIDANCE` (flowKnowledge) registers ONE deterministic next step for all 21 quiz flows plus engine lanes (trial-end, ledger edit/delete, onboarding OTP, support). It renders into the core prompt as the STUCK GUIDANCE block AND is used directly: quiz `help`/`hint`/`?` answers with the field hint + simplest typed path deterministically (zero tokens), staying on the same question; the trial-end lane always carries its line.

### 180. v1.61.17 - the lawn-mower unblock: canonical asset_type + complaint-proof confirm (2026-11-06)

**Live evidence.** `error_logs` 2026-11-05T16:53:11: `Registration save failed: new row for relation "vehicles" violates check constraint "vehicles_asset_type_check" [asset_kind=machinery plate=JOYCELAWNMOWER]`. Live DB constraint: `CHECK (asset_type IN ('ICE','EV','HEAVY_MACHINERY'))` — an orphaned legacy constraint (no migration in the repo owned it). The code wrote `assetKind.toUpperCase()` = `'MACHINERY'`, so **every non-road save failed**, and `onboarding` wrote `'HYBRID'`, which the same constraint rejected. The user looped 2026-11-05 16:54 → 2026-11-06 08:44; at the confirm gate his complaints were also being banked as `make_model` ("Add machine", "This problem ahs been persistent since yesterday") because the v1.61.12 bare-word guard only blocked single words.

**Fixes.**
1. **Canonical vocabulary** (`countryBucket.js`): `assetTypeForKind(kind, fuel)` — EV/HYBRID/ICE for road assets, the KIND for non-road; `ASSET_TYPE_VALUES` includes legacy `HEAVY_MACHINERY`; `legacyAssetType()` maps to the old-constraint-safe value; `normalizeAssetKind` now reads legacy `HEAVY_MACHINERY` and resolves `lawn_mower` (underscore-normalised alias match). Used by `persistVehicleRegistration` AND `onboarding.saveVehicleAssetRecord`.
2. **Rule-50 save fallback** (both write paths): an `asset_type_check` rejection retries once with the legacy-safe value and logs `quizEngine.assetTypeLegacyFallback` — a user can never lose a registration to schema drift again.
3. **Migration `npm run migrate:asset-type-check`** (applied live): drops the orphaned constraint and re-adds it with the canonical vocabulary (+ legacy value). Idempotent.
4. **Confirm-gate complaint guard:** `isPollutedFieldValue` now rejects multi-word imperative/frustration text ("Add machine", "This problem…", "still not saved", "Is my mower saved?"); when NO field changed the card is re-shown untouched with the one next step; AI corrections can never bank polluted values. Narrative draft cards keep their own correction flow (guard skipped only when nothing changed).
5. **Polluted persist refusal:** a draft whose `make_model` is a message is refused (`code=polluted_field`), the field is cleared and re-asked — a business refusal, not an incident log.
6. **Save-failure ladder:** real write failures are logged and after the 2nd consecutive failure the card offers `Support` + `Cancel` (never an endless loop).
7. **Detection parity:** mower/chainsaw/strimmer aliases; `isRegisterCommand` recognises mower/generator/equipment/compressor/pump wording.

**Frames touched:** `src/services/{countryBucket,quizEngine,onboarding}.js`, `src/routes/whatsapp.js`, `scripts/{run_asset_type_check_migration(new),mockSupabase,health_audit}.js`, `evals/cases/conversation_cases.json` (35), `test_asset_type_check.js` (new, 39), `.env.example` untouched (no new knobs), `package.json`, this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Code vocabulary vs an orphaned DB constraint* → both write paths fixed + degrade + migration; siblings audited: `vehicles.asset_type` updates (none — immutable after creation), report readers (`normalizeAssetKind` now legacy-aware), `driver_compliances.asset_type` (free text, no constraint). *Multi-word text banked as a field value* → confirm gate + applyCorrections + persist guard fixed; siblings: direct-answer lane (v1.58.2 guard), AI extraction (polluted values skipped), narrative cards (own deterministic flow, untouched). *Endless failure loop* → save-failure ladder; sibling: patience ladder for invalid answers (already existed).

### 181. v1.62.0 - DeepSeek off-peak scheduling engine, CLI gates + discount accounting + rule 61 (2026-11-06)

**Official facts (verified 2026-11-06, api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing.md).** "Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full. Off-peak rates are half of the peak rates." In EAT (UTC+3) peak reads 04:00-07:00 and 09:00-13:00; peak covers 35 h/week (~21%), so ~79% of the week is half price.

**A. `src/services/deepseekSchedule.js` (new, pure).** `DEEPSEEK_PEAK_WINDOWS_UTC` (minute-of-day, end-exclusive), `isChinesePublicHoliday()` (Beijing-date resolution; built-in fixed windows Jan 1, Apr 4-6, May 1-5, Oct 1-7; lunar festivals deliberately NOT invented — `DEEPSEEK_CN_HOLIDAYS` CSV adds them from the official State Council notice, fail-open for unlisted years), `getDeepSeekPricingState()` (`peak_window | outside_peak_window | weekend | chinese_holiday | unknown_time` + `discountFactor` + `nextTransition`), `isDeepSeekPeakTime()`, `getDeepSeekDiscountFactor()` (unknown timestamp = gross), `evaluateDeepSeekOffPeakGate()`, `formatOffPeakGateMessage()` (EAT + UTC, one next step) and `logDeepSeekDeferralAudit()` (fail-soft `admin_audit_logs` insert, no DDL). `src/utils/` does not exist in this repo — services live in `src/services/` (rule 55).

**B. CLI gates (rule 61).** `npm run synth:cases` and `npm run eval:conv` (provider-consuming modes; `--export` is exempt) call the gate BEFORE spending tokens: during peak they print the exact next off-peak time in EAT + UTC, write `DEEPSEEK_DEFERRED_TO_OFF_PEAK` and exit 2. `--force` overrides one run; `DEEPSEEK_OFF_PEAK_GATE=off` disables the gate globally. Deliberately NOT deferred: front-user purposes (latency paramount, rules 20/24), Sentinel scan/synthesis, the 6-hourly eval tick (the `CONV_EVAL_MAX_JUDGE_CALLS_PER_TICK` cap already lands most calls off-peak) and the weekly model-scout cycle — supervision cadence beats the residual saving, and the proposal's persisted queue was downgraded to a deterministic gate because there is no live batch dispatcher to queue.

**C. Discount accounting.** `AI_USAGE_COST_RULES` now carries the official DeepSeek peak list (`deepseek-chat`/flash $0.30/$1.20, reasoner/pro $1.32/$3.96; off-peak halves to $0.15/$0.60 and $0.66/$1.98). New `getAiUsageCostBreakdownUsd()` prices every row at ITS `created_at` (the summary query now selects `created_at`); `getAiUsageSummary()` gains `approxCostSavedUsd` + `offPeakTokens` (totals and every bucket), `computeAiBudgetStatus()` therefore tracks real (net) spend, and `formatAiStatsReply()` shows `Off-peak savings: ~$X` when present. Rows without a timestamp are priced gross, so estimates never understate a bill. Rule 56: existing rows re-price from stored timestamps — no backfill.
