### 182. v1.63.0 - proactive template registry: business-initiated messages survive the 24-hour window (2026-11-06)

**Why (P0-1).** Meta accepts a business-initiated free-form message and then silently drops it outside the 24-hour customer-service window (section 87.3 is the deploy-alert post-mortem: a valid `wamid`, no delivery). The product core promise is reminders, so every proactive family now has an approved Meta template slot.

**A. Pure registry (new `src/services/proactiveTemplates.js`).** One frozen registry of 11 kinds: `service_reminder, expiry_reminder, trial_ending, trial_grace, dunning, re_engagement, driver_unassigned, winback, deploy_live, eval_digest_ping, care_escalation`. Each kind declares `{ env, variables[], audience }`. `templateNameForKind()` reads `META_TPL_<KIND>` (default unset). `templateVariablesForKind()` returns the ordered body parameters and returns null when any required variable is missing or blank. `resolveProactiveMode()` is the single routing decision: template (name + variables) or text. No fetch, no DB, no transport lives in this module - tests never hit Meta.

**B. One transport, every sender.** `sendWhatsAppTemplateMessage()` (`src/workers/sentinel.js`) is the shared template POST (deliveryGuard respected). `sendProactiveWhatsApp(toPhone, text, kind, templateVars)` and `index.js sendMetaWhatsAppMessage(toPhone, body, kind, templateVars)` route through `resolveProactiveMode`; a failed template attempt falls through to the text path. Kinds wired: reminder sweep (`service_reminder` thresholds, `expiry_reminder` ladder), trial lifecycle sweep (`trial_ending` T-14/T-3/T-24 + extension offers + abandoned checkout; `trial_grace` fitted-plan card + grace countdowns + hard expiry; `dunning`; `winback` WINBACK40 + renewal benefits; `re_engagement`), follow-ups (`driver_unassigned`), eval digest (`eval_digest_ping`), customer care (`care_escalation`), boot LIVE alert (`deploy_live`).

**C. Deliberately left free-form.** In-window replies; Paystack/payment confirmations (the user just paid, the window is open); trial activation reward + T+7 nudge (fresh activity); superadmin budget/remediation pings (ops, two-way traffic); the existing `web_signup_welcome` template (unchanged).

**C2. v1.63.1 (2B) - Phase 1 completion (rule-51 correction).** Two owner-facing proactive senders were missed in the original 11-kind sweep and are now kinds 12-13: `driver_activity` (the pending-owner-notifications worker delivering the Driver Activity Summary to the owner) and `fleet_auto_audit` (the daily Fleet Auto-Audit report announcement cron). Both pass their kind through `sendMetaWhatsAppMessage`; with the knobs unset the free-form text is byte-identical to v1.63.0, and `docs/TEMPLATES.md` carries both bodies.

**D. No-canned-replies exemption (explicit).** The ratchet applies to FALLBACK TEXT only. Template BODIES live in Meta Business Manager (`docs/TEMPLATES.md` is the approval contract); code carries names and variable contracts, never prose. A template can only fire after the operator sets its knob, so the codebase stays free of canned conversational replies.

**E. Degrade and rollback (rule 50).** Unset knob = today free-form text, byte-identical (asserted). Missing variable = text. Meta template failure = text fallback. No schema, no migration; rollback is unsetting the knobs.

**F. Operator path.** `docs/TEMPLATES.md` carries the 11 bodies, variable specs, the Meta submission workflow and the exact `gcloud run services update --update-env-vars=META_TPL_<KIND>=<name>` commands. `npm run env:audit` proves parity; all 11 knobs are registered in `ENV_SECTIONS` (META WHATSAPP).

**G. Env knobs (13 since v1.63.1; all default unset).** META_TPL_SERVICE_REMINDER, META_TPL_EXPIRY_REMINDER, META_TPL_TRIAL_ENDING, META_TPL_TRIAL_GRACE, META_TPL_DUNNING, META_TPL_RE_ENGAGEMENT, META_TPL_DRIVER_UNASSIGNED, META_TPL_WINBACK, META_TPL_DEPLOY_LIVE, META_TPL_EVAL_DIGEST_PING, META_TPL_CARE_ESCALATION, META_TPL_DRIVER_ACTIVITY, META_TPL_FLEET_AUTO_AUDIT. Registered in `ENV_SECTIONS` and documented in `.env.example`; unset means the free-form fallback above.

**Tests.** New health-registered `test_proactive_templates.js` (39 assertions: completeness, uniqueness, name resolution, blank/missing degrade, ordered variables, routing, purity, wiring reachability). Kind + byte-identical assertions extended in test_sentinel_policy (30), test_maintenance_reminders (47), test_expiry_reminders (47), test_trial_engine (89), test_trial_capacity (43), test_followups (16), test_conv_eval (203), test_phase3_resilience (73), test_subscription_billing (86), test_notifications (19) and test_doc_sync.

### 184. v1.63.2 - record-challenge lane: acknowledge before data + scope reconciliation; eval gate is now calibration-aware (2026-11-06)

**A. The tone fix.** The v1.61.5 record-challenge replay shipped with the opener "↩️ Same record, straight from your ledger — nothing changed:" — the eval judge scored tone_compliance 0.6 (*"defensive and slightly robotic; no contractions, template-like card"*) while every other criterion passed (aggregate 0.78, above the 0.70 bar). The rule the lane needed — acknowledge distress before data — was already Persona v4 law (and the v1.61.5 heal `acknowledge_distress_before_data`); the lane simply never applied it. The opener is now `↩️ Fair check — here's the same record, unchanged:` — a short human acknowledgement with no banned-family phrasing (the judge rejects the "Let's keep moving" family; an earlier draft "Let's check that together" scored tone 0.4 for exactly that reason) — and it leads with the concern before the data. Final judged verdict: **aggregate 0.88, tone_compliance 0.8**.

**A2. The scope reconciliation.** After the tone fix the case still failed — on loop_avoidance 0.6: *"re-presents a ledger summary rather than addressing the 'across my 2 vehicles' challenge"*. The replay was contract-correct (last answered query, unchanged) but it never reconciled the user's stated scope with the replayed one-vehicle record. New pure helper `buildRecordChallengeScopeLine()` (`src/services/recordAnswers.js`): when the challenge text names a fleet scope (across/both/all/every/my N vehicles|cars|assets) AND the replayed query is vehicle-scoped (`lastRecordQuery.spec.vehiclePlate` set) AND the account holds 2+ vehicles, append: *"You mentioned N vehicles — this is the <plate> record. For a fleet-wide view, reply *<type> all time*."* The pointed phrase is a VERIFIED fleet-wide read (`fuel all time` / `expenses all time` / `earnings all time` all parse with `vehiclePlate:null`; bare "all vehicles" does NOT parse and is never offered). Scope-silent challenges, fleet-wide replays and single-vehicle accounts get no line (guards noise and `single_question`). When the scope line fires it REPLACES the `my entries` pointer — exactly ONE next step (two prompts read as a menu wall and fail `single_question`; the pointer remains the fallback when no scope line fires). The challenge text is the current turn's `commandText` — no session schema change was needed. `session.lastAssistantPrompt` storage is untouched (reply text only, normal path).

**B. The measurement filter.** `scripts/run_conv_eval.js --exclude-calibration`: all cases are still judged and persisted to `conversation_eval_runs` (calibration history preserved), but the headline and `--fail-on-failures` gate are computed over the signal cases only — printing "N cases (calibration excluded) · threshold X", "Real-fail rate: X%" and "Calibration hold: Y%". Section 164 documents the recommended gate.

**Frames touched:** `src/routes/whatsapp.js` (one-line reply), `scripts/run_conv_eval.js` (flag + gate), `evals/cases/conversation_cases.json` (case reply updated; historical rows not backfilled), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (section 164 line, 183 baseline note, this section), `CHANGELOG.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json` (+stamped assets), `docs/{PRODUCT_QA,SAKA_TRAINING}.md` (generated), `package.json`.

**Suites run:** `test_record_answers` (75, no prefix assertions), `test_conv_eval`, `test_doc_sync`, `test_no_canned_replies`; `npm run eval:conv -- --exclude-calibration` (23/23 signal pass, 12/12 calibration hold); `npm run eval:conv` (full aggregate recorded, below 0.70 by design); `npm run health` green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51) — two defect classes.** (i) *A lane that ships an ack rule and does not apply it* — the tone opener; sibling sweep across every deterministic reply lane with a canned prefix (`grep -rn "Same record" src/` = one hit; the `↩️` opener = the same single hit; receipt-delete, reminder and ledger lanes open with a direct answer) — no sibling carries a defensive variant. (ii) *A replay that satisfies the case contract but not the user's actual question* — the scope mismatch; sibling sweep = every lane that replays a prior answer (`grep -rn "lastRecordQuery" src/` = the record lane only; `lastAssistantPrompt` read paths feed repeat detection, not replay) — the scope-reconciliation helper now covers the record lane; no other lane replays prior answers today, so none needed the same guard.

**Baseline correction.** Pre-fix (fe29b00): 1 real fail / 23 = 4.3%. Post-fix (v1.63.2): 0 real fail / 23 = 100% pass, 12/12 calibration hold. This is the Phase 3 baseline.

### 185. v1.63.3 — Read Command Registry (Phase 3): one ordered registry for every deterministic read (2026-11-06)

**Why.** The deterministic read lanes in `src/routes/whatsapp.js` were an implicit if/else chain of ~560 lines (old lines 1677-2234). Nineteen detectors ran in a hand-maintained order, and DETECTION order differed from DISPATCH order (receipts was detected first but dispatched near-last; help menu and product Q&A were detected last but dispatched first). Adding a lane required finding the exact insertion point, and a catch-all parser could silently hijack an intent lane — the section 152 defect class.

**A. The registry (`src/services/readCommands.js`, new).** A frozen `READ_COMMANDS` array in the OLD DISPATCH precedence: help_menu → product_qa → country_knowledge → vehicle_summary → upload_menu → garage_empty → all_documents_expiry → document_number_search → driver_documents → compliance_correction → compliance_expiry → compliance_status → maintenance_schedule → reminders_list → ledger_turn → odometer_read → driver_profile_read → records_query → receipts_list. Each lane carries `{ id, parksQuiz, skipWhenLocked, skipWhenPendingCapture?, detect(text, ctx), render(hit, ctx) }`. `resolveReadCommand(text, ctx)` walks the array, honours the gates (PIN/OTP locked phase; `session.pendingComplianceCapture`) and returns an augmented lane `{ id, hit, parksNow, abandonReason, render(ctx) }` — or null. `render()` returns the COMPLETE aiResult; a claimed turn never shows the message to a second lane.

**B. Parking is reproduced, not re-invented.** `computeParking()` mirrors the old preamble (1515-1568): the first matching parking detector wins the recorded abandon reason in the old order — compliance family → ledger → records → odometer → driver profile — regardless of which lane answers, only when a fast quiz turn exists and no phase is locked. This preserves quirks such as "what is the current mileage?" recording `record_query` while the odometer lane answers, and "what can you do" parking a draft while the help lane answers.

**C. Kept inline in the route (by design).** The `ocrPaused` guard, the country command (a profile WRITE), `delete receipt N` (a WRITE, rule 37), the fast quiz turn and the AI fallback. Both post-hoc overrides are byte-identical: `looksLikeReportRequest` (old 2271) and the `looks-like-log` intent fix, which now reads the SAME `readCtx.recordSpec` the registry used.

**D. Golden capture (before any edit).** `test_read_registry.js` carries a FROZEN re-implementation of the old chain (`oldResolve` + `oldParking`, with verbatim inline regexes). The capture ran first: 41 fixtures, 0 mismatches. It exposed two live quirks now pinned as declarations: "how much did I spend on fuel last week?" and "what documents can I send?" are claimed by product Q&A ahead of the records/upload lanes (old precedence). Fixing them would be a behaviour change and is out of Phase 3 scope.

**E. Equivalence harness.** After the refactor: 121 assertions — every fixture resolves to the same lane id as the frozen old chain; first-claim precedence matches on 14 declared cross-lane overlap fixtures; parking reasons match on every fixture; kept-inline branches resolve to null; negatives (log lines, capture verbs, reminder creation, date-bearing corrections, report words, why-questions, a bare PIN) stay null; locked-phase and pending-capture gates match.

**F. Blast radius.** `whatsapp.js` −707/+85 lines (the chain + 59 orphaned imports). The route builds ONE `readCtx` snapshot and dispatches through `resolveReadCommand`; `isVehicleSummaryCommand()` keeps the feature-notice suppression (`summaryCommand`) working without a duplicated regex.

**Frames touched:** `src/services/readCommands.js` (new), `src/routes/whatsapp.js`, `test_read_registry.js` (new), `test_driver_compliance_answers.js`, `test_labels_everywhere.js`, `test_feature_notice.js`, `package.json`, `landing/data/changelog.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this file.

**Suites run:** test_read_registry (121), test_driver_compliance_answers (64), test_vehicle_compliance (67), test_odometer_answer (11), test_product_qa (152), test_record_answers (80), test_entry_ledger (all), test_labels_everywhere (22), test_feature_notice (25), test_no_canned_replies (2), test_quiz_flow (153), test_edit_delete (all), test_agent_training (180), test_web_onboarding (64), test_meta_signature (16), test_doc_sync — green; `npm run health` green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Defect class: a catch-all parser hijacks an intent lane* → sibling sweep = all 19 registry lanes + the 5 kept-inline branches + both post-hoc overrides. The harness pins first-claim precedence on every fixture and declares the 14 legitimate overlaps, so an undeclared double-claim fails CI. Deliberately left: the two product-Q&A shadowing quirks above (documented; a future behaviour change must update the declared table). Rule 13: `flowKnowledge.js` / `sakaAi.js` untouched — pure structural refactor, no flow/intent/copy change (test_agent_training 180 green).

### 186. v1.64.0 — Unified session.pending (Phase 4): one state machine, one resolver (2026-11-06)

**Why.** A chat session carried 13 independent pending* interaction fields (`pendingEntryAction`, `pendingSupportEscalation`, `pendingComplianceCapture`, `narrativeBatch`, `pendingAssignmentOtp`, `pendingTransferBuyerOtp`, `pendingCancelSubscription`, `pendingClearChat`, `pendingDeleteVehicle`, `pendingDriverAssignment`, `pendingEmailUpdate`, `pendingAccountDeletion`, `transferFlow`). Each owned its own TTL (15 min inline compares, 10 min OTP compares, or none at all), its own "fresh log outranks pending" rule and its own if/else branch in `whatsapp.js` — the section 152 / 169 defect class ("a pending support intake swallowed a quiz", "a draft correction became a saved edit"). Phase 4 is a PURE STRUCTURAL refactor: one state object, one registry, one resolver, zero behaviour change.

**A. The registry (`src/services/pendingState.js`, new).** `PENDING_KINDS` is frozen and declares, per kind: `ttlMs`, `priority` (today's route claim order), `freshLog` (`drops | yields | yields+clears | swallows | N/A`), `parksQuiz`, `blockedByQuizLock` (read-registry `skipWhenLocked`), `blockedByQuiz` (the `!session.quiz` guards on the ACTIVE chain), `otp`, `slot`, `boolean`, `legacyField`. 16 kinds are registered: 13 own the slot; three are documented out-of-slot members of the family — `record-challenge` (a replay memory on `session.lastRecordQuery`; migrating it would evict real pendings), `quiz-otp` (`session.quiz.phase` + `state.otp`/`otpDispatch`) and `onboarding-otp` (`onboardingStore.pending_otp`).

| Kind | TTL | Priority | freshLog | Quiz gates | Slot | Legacy field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| clear-chat | — | 100 | yields+clears | — | yes | pendingClearChat |
| support-intake | — | 95 | swallows | — | yes | pendingSupportEscalation |
| entry-edit | 15 min | 80 | drops (edit mode) | lock | yes | pendingEntryAction |
| record-challenge | 15 min | 75 | N/A | lock | no (memory) | lastRecordQuery |
| transfer-release-otp | 10 min | 70 | swallows | — | yes | transferFlow |
| assignment-otp | 10 min | 65 | yields (shape-gated) | — | yes | pendingAssignmentOtp |
| transfer-buyer-otp | 10 min | 60 | swallows | — | yes | pendingTransferBuyerOtp |
| cancel-subscription | — | 55 | swallows | blocked | yes | pendingCancelSubscription |
| compliance-capture | 15 min | 50 | yields | blocked | yes | pendingComplianceCapture |
| narrative-batch | 15 min | 45 | yields | — | yes | narrativeBatch |
| delete-vehicle | — | 40 | swallows | blocked | yes | pendingDeleteVehicle |
| driver-assignment | — | 35 | swallows (cancel → reprompt, PROP-02) | blocked | yes | pendingDriverAssignment |
| account-deletion-otp | 10 min | 30 | swallows | blocked | yes | pendingAccountDeletion |
| email-update-otp | 10 min | 25 | swallows | blocked | yes | pendingEmailUpdate |
| onboarding-otp | 10 min | 20 | swallows | — | no (onboardingStore) | — |
| quiz-otp | 10 min | gate | swallows | lock | no (session.quiz) | — |

**B. The resolver.** `resolvePendingTurn(session, text, ctx)` returns `{ kind, consumed, nextAction }` or `null`. `ctx = { now, quizPhaseLocked, hasQuiz }`. `consumed:true` means the pending owns the turn and `nextAction` names its handler (`confirm`, `cancel`, `apply-edit`, `select`, `delete-confirm`, `command`, `capture-issue`, `capture-answer`, `release-otp`, `otp-verify`, `resend`, `save-all`, `edit-row`, `annual`, `capture-phone`, `reprompt`, `quiz-otp-turn`). `consumed:false` means the message proceeds and the action says what happened to the pending: `drop-fresh-log` (entry-edit), `yield` (yields kinds and the quiz gates), `clear-and-continue` (clear-chat), `ttl-expired`. Precedence is the registry, not the caller: an expired slot is cleared first; `blockedByQuizLock` kinds (read-registry lanes) skip a locked PIN/account-OTP phase; `blockedByQuiz` kinds (ACTIVE chain) skip while any draft is open; then the kind's parser decides.

**C. Migration-on-read shim.** `hydrateSessionPending(session)` runs for EVERY message at `whatsapp.js` (line 987, before any branch): it validates an existing slot, TTL-cleans it, otherwise migrates the highest-priority live legacy field into `{ kind, data, at }` (collisions follow the table; expired fields are dropped), deletes the legacy own properties and re-exposes each legacy name as a NON-ENUMERABLE accessor over the slot. Consequences: (1) old snapshots in `chat_sessions.state` keep their pending state; (2) old branch code (`session.pendingEntryAction = …`, `session.transferFlow.step = …`) keeps working byte-identically; (3) a persisted snapshot now carries ONE `pending` value and no legacy keys. Writes follow the priority rule — a lower-priority legacy write cannot evict a higher-priority pending (the single intentional semantic of the one-slot model). `otpDispatch`/`state.otp` stay inside `session.quiz` and `onboarding-otp` stays in `onboardingStore` (security state is never folded into the slot; both are documented out-of-slot registry rows).

**D. Wiring and blast radius.** `whatsapp.js` adds ONE import and ONE hydration call; every branch body is untouched. The stateless 6-digit buyer-OTP sink (`session.pendingTransferBuyerOtp || (messageText.match(/^\d{6}$/) && …)`) is deliberately NOT a pending — it is a kept-inline route lane, still in place and pinned by a source assertion (Phase 5 must keep its position). No DDL: the slot rides the existing `chat_sessions.state` jsonb and the existing 24-hour snapshot age guard.

**E. Equivalence harness (`test_pending_state.js`, new, 434 assertions).** **A** — the fresh-log truth table per kind, derived from the declared `freshLog` and the observed outcome (13 kinds; support-intake swallows and clears, compliance/narrative survive, entry-edit drops, clear-chat clears-and-continues), plus the entry-edit delete-mode nuance and the driver-assignment missing-cancel bug. **B** — OTP/locked precedence: all 6-digit codes consumed, `looksLikeFreshLogLine('123456') === false`, a locked phase outranks `entry-edit` (skipWhenLocked) without destroying it, and the two no-quiz-guard quirks (`transferFlow`, `pendingAssignmentOtp`, buyer) still claim; an open quiz gates the ACTIVE-chain kinds. **C** — corrupt double-set priority equals the old claim order (entry-edit > compliance, assignment > cancel, delete > driver-assignment, transfer > assignment, clear > support; expired high-priority dropped). **D** — per-kind TTL expiry (15 min / 10 min families) and the deliberate no-TTL gates (30-day-old pendings still resolve). **E** — differential replay: **300 turns** (13 kinds × 12 texts + 6 quiz-gated/6 transparent kinds × 12 texts with an open draft) against a FROZEN re-implementation of the v1.63.3 claim order; both sides agree on every turn. The capture surfaced exactly one model mismatch — today a bare 6-digit message falls into the stateless buyer-OTP sink even while another pending is set; the sink is not a pending, so it stays a kept-inline lane and is pinned by a source assertion instead (no production behaviour change). **F** — the migration-on-read shim: legacy `pendingEntryAction → entry-edit`, legacy `pendingSupportEscalation → support-intake`, `otpDispatch` intact inside `session.quiz` and never migrated; JSON round-trip stores only `pending`; the accessor bridge write-through, clearing and priority rule. **G** — every pending kind has a `FLOW_GUIDANCE` line (rule 60).

**F. PROPs minted (deferred work, no code change implied by this release).** `PROP-2026-11-06-01` — make the fresh-log override UNIFORM across all non-OTP pendings (today's per-kind truth table is preserved here; generalising it changes behaviour for delete-vehicle, cancel-subscription, support-intake and driver-assignment). `PROP-2026-11-06-02` — `pendingDriverAssignment` does not honour "cancel" (it re-prompts); preserved for Phase 4 with a source TODO at the missing-cancel site and a dedicated assertion.

**Frames touched:** `src/services/pendingState.js` (new), `src/routes/whatsapp.js` (import + hydration + the PROP-02 TODO comment), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js` (16 pending-kind `FLOW_GUIDANCE` lines), `test_pending_state.js` (new), `scripts/health_audit.js` (suite registered), `package.json`, `landing/data/changelog.json`, `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (section 186, version + history), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run:** test_pending_state (434), test_read_registry (121), test_entry_ledger (all), test_narrative_draft (122), test_compliance_capture (30), test_driver_assignment_gate (54), test_quiz_flow (153), test_agent_training (180), test_conv_eval (203), test_first_message_flow (57), test_doc_sync — green; `npm run health` green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Defect class: a pending interaction that swallows or yields the wrong turn because its TTL/fresh-log/priority lives in its own branch* → sibling sweep = all 13 slot kinds + the 3 documented out-of-slot kinds; every quirk preserved and pinned (driver-assignment cancel, no-TTL confirm gates, transfer/assignment no-quiz guards, entry-edit delete-mode yielding, the stateless buyer sink). Deliberately left: the uniform fresh-log override (PROP-2026-11-06-01) and the driver-assignment cancel escape (PROP-2026-11-06-02) — both are behaviour changes and belong to their own releases. Rule 13: `flowKnowledge.js` gained one `FLOW_GUIDANCE` line per kind (rendered into the core prompt by the existing block); `sakaAi.js` and `conversationEngine.js` are unchanged — pure state-layer refactor, no intent/flow/copy change (test_agent_training 180 green).

### 187. v1.65.0 (5A/3) — whatsapp.js split: webhook + messages + barrel + shim (2026-11-06)

**Why.** `src/routes/whatsapp.js` was a 5,111-line monolith: the Meta handshake, HMAC, wamid dedupe, enqueue and the entire message processor in one file. Phase 5 splits it in three releases; **5A is a pure file move — not one behaviour line changes.**

**A. Layout (5A).**

```
src/routes/
├── whatsapp.js            <- temporary one-line shim: export * from './whatsapp/index.js';
└── whatsapp/
    ├── webhook.js         <- GET verification, POST HMAC, wamid dedupe, 200 ACK, enqueue
    ├── messages.js        <- the message processor + the 14 public helpers
    └── index.js           <- barrel: export * from './webhook.js'; export * from './messages.js';
```

- `webhook.js` (272 lines): `handleWhatsAppWebhookVerification` (moved verbatim from `index.js`), `META_APP_SECRET_PLACEHOLDER`, `verifyMetaWebhookSignature`, `processedWebhooksCache`, `DEDUPLICATION_TTL_MS`, `isMessageProcessed`, `markMessageProcessed`, `checkAndRecordWamid`, `handleWhatsAppWebhook`, plus the module-level resilient Supabase client.
- `messages.js` (4,876 lines): `onboardingStore`, `chatSessions`, the 12 helper exports and `processIncomingWhatsAppMessage`.
- `index.js` (barrel, 11 lines) and the one-line `whatsapp.js` shim every existing importer keeps using until 5C. Root `index.js` imports both webhook handlers straight from `./src/routes/whatsapp/webhook.js`; the three GET routes wrap it with `fastify`.

**B. Dependency graph — acyclic.** `webhook.js -> messages.js` (static `import { processIncomingWhatsAppMessage } from './messages.js'`, dereferenced only inside the queued task). `messages.js` imports only services, never the webhook. Reverse direction verified: the processor uses none of the dedupe/signature symbols, and the webhook never touches `chatSessions`/`onboardingStore`. No lazy `import()` anywhere.

**C. Verbatim proof.** Every moved line was compared byte-for-byte against `HEAD:src/routes/whatsapp.js`: processor 4,415 lines, helpers 300, webhook handler 122, dedupe 55, signature 55, session maps 2 and the client declaration 1 — all OK. UTF-8 bytes preserved (emoji round-trip check). The barrel resolves exactly 23 public symbols (22 original + the relocated GET verifier).

**D. Plus `src/services/deepAudit.js` (ledger-lint lookup, finding description, files array) and `src/services/conversationDiagnosis.js` (routing-map label + fallback file).

### 190. v1.68.0 (5B-3/4) — whatsapp split: reads + pending + quiz extracted (turn-owners separated; boundary contract formalized) (2026-11-07)

**Why.** Phase 5B-2 (section 189) thinned the processor down to its real job. Phase 5B-3 extracts the three remaining turn-owner families so the future orchestrator (5B-4) works against a processor that only decides WHO owns each message: the **read dispatch** (`src/routes/whatsapp/reads.js`), the **pending turn handlers** (`src/routes/whatsapp/pending.js`) and the **quiz orchestration** (`src/routes/whatsapp/quiz.js`). Not one behaviour line changes.

**A. The read dispatch (reads.js, 41 lines).** `dispatchReadTurn({ commandText, readCtx, quizForFastPath, quizPhaseLocked, session })` is the one call site of the Phase 3 registry: `resolveReadCommand(commandText, readCtx)`; on a match it runs the park (`abandonQuiz(session, { reason: readLane.abandonReason })`) BEFORE `readLane.render(readCtx)` exactly as inline (the lane's render ctx carries the session, so the abandoned draft must be gone first), and returns the complete `aiResult` or null. The processor keeps the `readCtx` build (one shared parse incl. `recordSpec`), the post-hoc `looks-like-log`/report fixes, the receipt-delete write lane, the fast-quiz regex lane and the AI fallback.

**B. The pending handlers (pending.js, 1,250 lines, 12 lanes).** Every per-kind handler returns data and mutates the passed session in place; the processor performs every send, every `chatSessions.set` and every `return { status }`. Lanes: `startClearChatTurn` + `resolveClearChatTurn` (confirm/CLEAR/cancel/clear-and-continue), `resolveSupportIntakeTurn` (the v1.58.22 lock that owns the NEXT turn), `handleTransferFlowTurn` (passbook release steps 2/3, `sendWhatsApp` passed in), `handleAssignmentOtpTurn` (shape-gated; returns null without Supabase so the branch behaves exactly as before), `handleBuyerOtpTurn` (the pinned stateless 6-digit sink guard stays in the processor), `handleSubscriptionTurn` + `maybeHandleSubscriptionTurn` (the engine-owned deterministic billing turn, now exported), `handleComplianceCaptureTurn` + `persistCapturedCompliance` (exported back for the in-processor direct-doc lane), `handleNarrativeBatchTurn` (SAVE ALL / edit N / cancel as `{ handled, reply, suppressQuiz, forcedFlow, aiExtracted }`), `handleDeleteVehicleTurn`, `handleDriverAssignmentTurn`, `handleAccountDeletionOtpTurn`, `handleEmailUpdateOtpTurn` + `handleEmailUpdateStartTurn`. `classifyPendingLane()` exposes the tested `resolvePendingTurn()` for the future single-point adoption; the LIVE dispatch stays positional.

**C. The quiz orchestration (quiz.js, 379 lines).** `arbitrateQuizTurn(...)` covers the switch-command abandon, the statement park, the pause ladder (`buildPausedQuizReply`), the flow switch, the logbook prefill and the default/engine turn, returning `{ quizTurn, earlyHandled, earlyReply, activeQuiz }`. `finalizeQuizOutcome(...)` covers the confirm-gate consumption (`quizTurn.handled`), the gate notice, the driver-onboarding flag, the vehicle-registration transition + owner driver-profile chain, the once-only contact-save nudge (its `historyLength` is threaded from the processor) and the delete-account teardown, returning `{ handled, reply }` or null. `renderRoleActions` moved here and is imported back — messages.js re-exports it, so the public surface is unchanged.

**D. Boundary contract + separation (permanent).** All three are leaf route modules: they may import from src/services/* and from ./helpers.js (a leaf that imports no route modules), but NEVER from ./messages.js. State in, data out. The **global circuit breaker** (loop detection + SOFT/HARD trip, messages.js final-reply stage) deliberately STAYS in the processor — it is a quiz-agnostic guard; quiz.js owns ONLY the quiz pause ladder. quiz.js -> pending.js has NO edge today: composite flows receive pending decisions as arguments, and a future one-way import is reserved.


**E. The interface contract (verbatim answers).**
- **(a) Who wins first?** Precedence is positional and preserved exactly: care/superadmin intercepts -> early pending gates (clear-chat -> support-intake -> stop/pause -> breaker reset/HARD gate) -> **read dispatch (inside the classification stage, before the remaining pending chains)** -> support family -> transferFlow -> accept/decline -> assignment-OTP -> buyer-OTP -> coupon -> subscription/cancel-subscription -> compliance-capture -> narrative-batch -> **quiz arbitration + turn** -> legacy onboarding -> ACTIVE-chain pendings (delete-vehicle -> driver-assignment -> ... -> account-deletion -> email-update) -> final-reply stage (breaker, upload hints, nudges). A read lane can still match and render before a later pending overwrites the visible reply — that is today's behaviour and did not change.
- **(b) Read match parks the quiz?** Yes — the park (`abandonQuiz`) lives INSIDE reads.js, BEFORE render, exactly as inline. The processor never calls pending.abandon on a read, and a read match never touches `session.pending`.
- **(c) Pending match abandons the quiz?** No pending chain abandons a quiz today: pendings rely on positional unreachability, `!session.quiz` guards and `quizPhaseLocked`. pending.js therefore never calls quiz.abandon(); the processor keeps ownership of every `abandonQuiz` call (`switch_command`, `statement_not_answer`, park reasons).
- **(d) Quiz completion consumes pending state?** No. Completing a quiz step never touches `session.pending` (quiz-otp lives inside `session.quiz`; narrative-batch is independent). Any future need is passed IN as an argument by the processor, which applies the returned mutation itself.

**F. Import graph (zero cycles).**
```
messages.js ──► reads.js    ──► services/readCommands.js, services/quizEngine.js (abandonQuiz)
messages.js ──► pending.js  ──► services/pendingState.js + the per-lane service handlers
                                 (chatHistory, customerCare, transfers, driverAssignments, vehicles,
                                  subscriptions, trialEngine, subscriptionTiers, linkShortener,
                                  complianceCatalog, vehicleCompliance, complianceCapture,
                                  globalization, conversationEngine, narrativeDraft, quizEngine,
                                  mailer) + ./helpers.js (leaf)
messages.js ──► quiz.js     ──► services/quizEngine.js, conversationEngine.js,
                                 conversationMemory.js, productQa.js, contactNudge.js + ./helpers.js
quiz.js    ──► pending.js   : NO edge today (reserved, one-way only, if ever needed)
pending.js ──► nothing in routes (helpers.js only)
reads.js   ──► nothing in routes
```


**G. Proof + what stays.** Byte-verbatim proof: 899 moved statement lines vs `HEAD:messages.js` — 794 exact (88%), 63 sanctioned renames (`customReply` -> `reply`, `isSpecialFlowHandled` -> `handled`, `sendWhatsAppReply` -> `sendWhatsApp` argument), 42 structural deltas each named in the CHANGELOG. Stays in the processor by design: the `readCtx` build + post-hoc record fix + receipt-delete/fast-quiz/AI fallback chain, the support-escalation trigger + its dead pending branch (`ticketCreated` pin), the coupon lane, the direct driver-document lane (imports `persistCapturedCompliance` back), the vehicle-doc prompt, the registration email gate, the driver gate, the narrative intake triggers, the global circuit breaker + OCR recovery ladder + upload hints, the duplicate-receipt quiz-null, the slow-ack timer, the session maps (`chatSessions`, `onboardingStore`), and every `customReply =` assignment of the call wrappers.

### 192. v1.70.0 — per-purpose AI tier optimization: mechanical renders on Haiku, complaint_recovery remapped to its own Tier-2 purpose (intent_classify's ~64% saving parked behind the A1 eval gate) (2026-11-07)

**Why.** Per §153 (v1.58.24) paid/trial plans ran EVERY front purpose on Sonnet ($2/$10 per MTok) — including mechanical renders: cached quiz questions, rare stall nudges, one-line small talk. The live 7-day `ai_usage_logs` window confirmed the margin risk: paid `intent_classify` rows averaged ~45,460 prompt tokens/call (~$0.092/call on Sonnet), `question_render` ~2,816 prompt tokens (~$0.0062/call), `prose_render` ~$0.0061/call. Phase 6 adds a per-purpose override registry so mechanical renders ride Tier-1 Haiku ($0.10/$0.50) while quality-critical purposes keep the plan tier.

**A. Routing matrix (mode='all', premium on, paid/trial maxTier>=2).**

| Purpose | Registry tier | Before v1.70.0 | v1.70.0 shipped | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `question_render` | 1 | 2 Sonnet (plan floor) | **1 Haiku (capped)** | MECHANICAL |
| `stall_nudge` | 1 | 2 Sonnet | **1 Haiku (capped)** | MECHANICAL |
| `small_talk` | 1 | 2 Sonnet | **1 Haiku (capped)** | MECHANICAL |
| `intent_classify` | 2 | 2 Sonnet | 2 Sonnet (cap parked by A1) | MECHANICAL (parked) |
| `prose_render` | 2 | 2 Sonnet | 2 Sonnet | QUALITY-CRITICAL |
| `extraction` | 1 | 2 Sonnet (plan floor) | 2 Sonnet | QUALITY-CRITICAL |
| `complaint_recovery` | 2 | 2 Sonnet via the question_render remap | **2 Sonnet via its own purpose** | QUALITY-CRITICAL |
| `admin_parse` | 1 | 2 Sonnet | 2 Sonnet (deliberately uncapped) | low volume |
| background (`*_synthesis`, `sentinel_diagnosis`, `prompt_refinement`, `friction_patch`, `conversation_*`, `model_*`) | 1/3 | unchanged | unchanged | BACKGROUND |

**B. The registry (as shipped).** `PURPOSE_TIER_OVERRIDES = { question_render: ROUTER, stall_nudge: ROUTER, small_talk: ROUTER }` plus `PURPOSE_TIER_OVERRIDE_HONORS_FORCED = new Set(['intent_classify'])`. Applied inside the existing plan-driven branch of `resolveTier()` (after the v1.58.24 floor raise, before the premium kill switch): a capped purpose is set back to Tier 1 unless it honors a caller-forced CONVERSATIONAL tier above the cap. Free accounts (`maxTier=1`), `PREMIUM_MODEL_MODE=escalate` and `PREMIUM_MODEL_ENABLED=off` never see the caps.

**C. Canary-honored `intent_classify` (parked by the A1 gate).** The honor-forced plumbing exists so `classifyIntentTier()`'s CONVERSATIONAL verdict (frustration, handshake, booking, multi-fact, long/complex) always outranks a mechanical cap — simple/short turns would ride Haiku while high-stakes turns stayed on Sonnet. The first gated run with the 4th override landed at 22/23 signal (see G), so the registry entry was parked before pushing; re-enabling is a one-line addition once a clean gate proves it invisible.

**D. Coupling fix (latent bug).** "Cleanup — conversationEngine.js:75 remapped compose purpose 'complaint_recovery' from 'question_render' to its own AI purpose (which existed since v1.12.0 but had zero callers). Without this, the question_render tier downgrade would silently degrade the most sensitive reply lane." `complaint_recovery` also joins `USER_FACING_PURPOSES` so a Tier-1 clamp (free plan / kill switch) routes to the front Haiku provider instead of the background DeepSeek leg.

**E. Escalate-mode delta (documented).** "escalate mode + paid → complaints rise from Haiku to Sonnet (restores the pre-1.58.24 intent). Operator-only mode; no production user hit this path." The old mapping routed complaints through question_render, which the legacy canary keeps at Tier 1; the purpose's own Tier-2 default is the original v1.12.0 §36.1 design.

**F. Cost projection (live 7-day telemetry + a modeled Solo Pro at 500 turns/mo).** Measured per-call on the paid Anthropic legs: Sonnet `question_render` ~$0.0062 → Haiku ~$0.0003 (−95%); `stall_nudge` / `small_talk` are near-zero volume (2 calls / 0 calls in the window). Modeled heavy paid seat: baseline ≈ $28.8/mo (300 classify × $0.092 + 125 prose × $0.0061 + 60 question renders × $0.0062 + 15 small/stall) → the shipped 3-override registry saves ≈ $0.4/mo (~1.4%). The parked `intent_classify` override is the real lever: ~210 of 300 classify calls are canary-tier-1, worth ≈ $18.4/mo (~64%). Live volume note: the window carried only 7 paid question_render calls, so today's absolute saving is small — the structure is what ships.

**G. Eval gate (A1).** First gated run (4 overrides): 22/23 signal (4.3% real-fail — `trial-end-downsize-choice` 0.83 `boundary_safety`), calibration 12/12, exit 0. A1 rule → `intent_classify` removed from the registry; re-run with 3 overrides: **23/23 signal (0/23 real-fail), calibration 12/12, exit 0** (the same case re-ran 0.88 PASS; eval cases are static `caseDef.reply` fixtures judged offline, so the 0.83 reading was the documented judge variance — the rollback still shipped per A1). Shipped 3 overrides.

**H. Frames touched.** `src/services/aiClient.js` (USER_FACING_PURPOSES + PURPOSE_TIER_OVERRIDES + PURPOSE_TIER_OVERRIDE_HONORS_FORCED + the resolveTier plan-driven branch), `src/services/conversationEngine.js` (ROUTER_PURPOSE_BY_COMPOSE remap + exported `routerPurposeForCompose`), `test_subscription_billing.js` (Test 5 superseded: mechanical inversions + parked-intent_classify pin), `test_phase6_purpose_tiers.js` (new, 52 assertions), `scripts/health_audit.js` (suite registry), `.env.example` (PREMIUM_MODEL_MODE comment), `README.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamped assets), `docs/` (generated), `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this file.

#### 192.1 v1.70.1 (Phase 6.5) — eval measurement robustness + intent_classify re-enabled (2026-11-07)

**Why.** The v1.70.0 A1 rollback parked `intent_classify` on a 22/23 signal run whose single miss (`trial-end-downsize-choice`, 0.83 `boundary_safety`) re-ran 0.88 PASS immediately after — the third flip-flop of the same case across v1.66.0 / v1.68.0 / v1.70.0. The trigger was judge noise, and the ~64% cost reduction was parked because the measurement could not make a reliable shipping decision. Phase 6.5 fixes the measurement.

**A. Flags (`scripts/run_conv_eval.js` → pure `parseConvEvalArgs` in `convEval.js`).** `--repeat N` (default 1, clamped 1..10) runs the corpus N times; `--min-pass-rate 0..1` (default 1.0, clamped) gates on the aggregated signal pool. Both forms (`--flag value`, `--flag=value`) parse; both work with `--exclude-calibration`. Example: `npm run eval:conv -- --exclude-calibration --repeat 3 --min-pass-rate 0.95` — a case failing 1 of 3 runs (68/69 = 98.6%) passes.

**B. Exit-code contract (fixed).** Old: `errored > 0 → exit 1` short-circuited BEFORE the gate line, so one unparseable judge answer blocked a valid run. New: `evalGateExitCode(aggregate)` — signal pass rate below `--min-pass-rate` → **1** (the actual gate); gate passed but judge errors present → **2** (visible warning; errored cases leave the denominator, so a flaky judge can never block a refactor); clean → **0**. Calibration expected-fails are HELD, never counted as signal failures (the plain path no longer double-counts them under `--fail-on-failures`). Healing runs on the first repeat only. The off-peak deferral already exits 2 — both mean "no verdict" (documented in the usage header).

**C. A1 re-evaluation (`intent_classify` temporarily re-enabled, then shipped).** `--exclude-calibration --repeat 3 --min-pass-rate 0.95`:
- Run 1: 13/13 judged signal pass · 10/10 calibration held · 10 signal + 2 calibration judge errors.
- Run 2: 3/3 judged signal pass · 6/6 calibration held · 26 judge errors.
- Run 3: 7/7 judged signal pass · 4/4 calibration held · 24 judge errors.
- **Aggregate: 23/23 judged signal = 100.0% (bar 95%), 20/20 calibration held, 62 judge errors → exit 2 by design.** The flagged `trial-end-downsize-choice` PASSED at 0.83 in its judged run (previously 0.83 FAIL / 0.88 PASS — the flip-flop is judge variance; eval replies are static fixtures, so routing cannot influence the score at all).
- **Decision: PASS → `intent_classify` ships enabled.** `PURPOSE_TIER_OVERRIDES` = `question_render`, `stall_nudge`, `small_talk`, `intent_classify` (all ROUTER); `PURPOSE_TIER_OVERRIDE_HONORS_FORCED = {intent_classify}` — the canary's forced CONVERSATIONAL verdict (frustration/handshake/booking/multi-fact) still wins. Modeled heavy paid seat: ~$0.4/mo mechanical + ~$18.4/mo parked classify saving → **~64% total AI-cost reduction** (~$28.8 → ~$10.4).

**D. Frames touched.** `src/services/convEval.js` (CONV_EVAL_REPEAT_MAX, clampRepeat, clampMinPassRate, parseConvEvalArgs, aggregateEvalRuns, evalGateExitCode), `scripts/run_conv_eval.js` (import + repeat loop + aggregate gate + usage/exit header), `src/services/aiClient.js` (intent_classify registry entry + jsdoc), `test_conv_eval.js` (+14 gate assertions), `test_phase6_purpose_tiers.js` (4-override pins), `test_subscription_billing.js` (cap restored), `README.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamped assets), `docs/` (generated), `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this file.

**E. Suites run.** test_conv_eval (216), test_phase6_purpose_tiers (51), test_subscription_billing (100), test_model_router (79), test_phase1_canary (37), test_phase2_analytics (59), test_phase3_resilience (73), test_agent_training (180), test_env_audit (44), test_conversation_compliance (29), test_doc_sync (30) — green; `npm run health` green.

**F. Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *judge noise treated as a quality signal by the CLI exit contract* -> siblings audited and closed: the `errored > 0` short-circuit (removed, exit 2), plain-path calibration counting under `--fail-on-failures` (signal-pool gate), heal-on-every-repeat (first run only), deferral/error both exiting 2 (documented), typo-weakened flags (clamped). Rule 13: no `flowKnowledge.js` / `sakaAi.js` change.

### 193. v1.71.0 (Phase 7) — fitted-plan card at T-3: tier-snapshot dedupe, T-0 becomes the grace reminder, PAST_DUE skip extended to T-24 (2026-11-07)

**Operator request.** "Move the fitted-plan card to three days before the trial ends so the user has a full week to decide; T-0 keeps the grace card as the final urgency nudge." Locked decisions from the approved plan: the card rides the existing T-3 digest (one message), the unchanged T-0 card carries no tier/price/link, the skip guard covers T-3 AND T-24, and the GRACE countdown repetition is deliberately left (§D4 below).

**A. The T-3 card (one message).** The T-3 stage of `runTrialLifecycleSweep` keeps the value digest (vehicles / expenses / reminders / reports / AI answers / ≈hours saved) and appends the fitted-plan card: `buildTrialEndOffer()` (reused as-is) → `fittedTierForAssets()` tier (+ add-on slots), the engine's local price and the shortened Paystack checkout link(s) (`metadata.trial_end_fit=true`). `t3DigestText()` renders the fitted block when an offer is supplied and the pre-v1.71.0 line otherwise (the T-14 midpoint recap is unchanged). The extension-coupon offer (`dispatchDueAccountTrialCoupons`) stays its own scheduled message — the T-3 day now carries up to three messages (digest + coupon + card, see §12.2).

**B. The dedupe rule (tier snapshot).** The T-3 stamp writes `nudge_t3_sent_at` AND `t3_fitted_plan` (`fittedPlanKey(fitted)` = `team_fleet` / `fleet_command+2`) atomically. At T-0 `runTrialEndStage()` compares the freshly computed key with the snapshot: different or null → the full `trialEndChoiceText()` card (today's behaviour — covers added/removed assets, trials shorter than 3 days and late-migrated rows); equal → the new `graceChoiceText()` — the decision, the grace deadline and the `keep <plate>` path with **no tier name, no price and no checkout link**, pointing back to "the payment link I sent you 3 days ago still works". `extendAccountTrial()` re-arms `t3_fitted_plan` with the nudge ladder. Known limit (documented): a price/currency change with an unchanged tier does not trigger a re-send — registry prices are frozen and the profile currency rarely changes mid-window.

**C. The skip guard (T-3 + T-24).** `isPaidLiveNow(owner, nowMs) || skipsTrialEndNudge(owner)` — the helper matches `PAST_DUE`, `CANCELED`, `CANCELLED`, `CANCELING` case-insensitively. Skipped rows are NOT stamped (a recovered account can still receive the card later). At T-0 the same guard retires the row to `EXPIRED` without a message (capacity lapses on read); the GRACE branch is deliberately untouched so an open window can never be stranded.

**D. Schema (migration `npm run migrate:trial-end-grace`, idempotent).** `trial_sessions.t3_fitted_plan text` joins `TRIAL_END_GRACE_SQL` and the boot `CREATE TABLE` mirror. Rule 50: the T-3 stamp is two-step (`setTrialFields` with both fields → on error `stampTrial` with `nudge_t3_sent_at` only) and the digest degrades to pre-v1.71.0 copy; T-0 with a missing snapshot always sends the full card.


**E. Addition A1 — the abandoned-checkout ladder is armed by the T-3 link.** `checkoutForTier` stamps `checkout_started_at`, so the T-3 card gives up to 3 recovery nudges (`T+30 min`, `T+24 h`, coupon `T-2 d`), capped by `CHECKOUT_REMINDER_MAX` and stopped at the GRACE transition (the ladder only targets ACTIVE/EXTENDED rows). Bonus — the T-3 card arms the abandoned-checkout ladder. Up to 3 recovery nudges; cap enforced by `CHECKOUT_REMINDER_MAX`; stopped at GRACE transition.

**D4 (deliberate) — GRACE countdowns keep their repetition.** `graceCountdownText()` (GRACE T-3/T-24) still repeats the fitted plan line, price and checkout link: it is an in-window urgency re-nudge whose link IS the action, the window is bounded (≤ `TRIAL_END_GRACE_DAYS`, 2 nudges), and the dedupe rule governs the T-3 → T-0 boundary only. Documented here so nobody "fixes" it into silence.

**F. Testability + a pre-existing date-bomb (fixed).** `runTrialLifecycleSweep` gained optional `checkoutFn`/`addonCheckoutFn` (mirrors `runTrialEndStage`); `scripts/mockSupabase.js` gained an optional `beforeUpdate` rejection hook (mirrors `beforeInsert`) to simulate the un-migrated column. Baseline `npm run health` was RED before any Phase 7 edit: `test_eval_spend` pinned its audit fixtures to a frozen `now = 2026-11-06T10:00Z` while `healCooldownStatus()`/`healFailedCase()` read the wall clock, so from 2026-11-07 the 24 h window excluded them (product code correct — reproduced green with a live clock). `healFailedCase()` now accepts an injectable `now` (defaulted) and the suite passes its frozen clock — deterministic forever.

**G. Rule 51 sibling sweep.**
| Defect class | Sibling | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| (i) Pricing card re-sent without change detection | `t24Text` pre-end urgency | Left — generic, carries no fitted pricing. |
| (i) | `graceCountdownText` (GRACE T-3/T-24) | **Deliberately left (D4)** — in-window urgency re-nudge, link is the action, window bounded. |
| (i) | Abandoned-checkout ladder | Verified compatible: arms from the T-3 link, cap 3, stops at GRACE. |
| (ii) End-of-trial nudges to accounts that can't convert | T-3 digest | Fixed (skip guard, no stamp). |
| (ii) | T-24 urgency | **Fixed alongside** (same guard). |
| (ii) | Activation reward / midpoint recap | Left — engagement copy, no conversion pricing. |
| (ii) | T-0 / GRACE branches | T-0 fixed (EXPIRED, no message); GRACE left on purpose (the window must close). |
| (clock vs fixture) | `healCooldownStatus` + `healFailedCase` call sites | Both clock-aware; the suite injects its frozen `now`. |

**H. Frames touched.** `src/services/trialEngine.js` (t3DigestText, graceChoiceText, fittedPlanKey, skipsTrialEndNudge, extendAccountTrial re-arm, T-0 comparison + guard, sweep signature/stats/T-3/T-24, exports), `src/services/trialSchema.js`, `src/db/subscriptionSchema.js`, `src/services/convEvalHealer.js` (injectable `now`), `scripts/run_trial_end_grace_migration.js`, `scripts/mockSupabase.js` (`beforeUpdate`), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js` (playbook + FLOW_GUIDANCE), `sakaAi.js` (trial law), `test_trial_engine.js` (+24), `test_trial_capacity.js` (+5), `test_subscription_billing.js` (+1), `test_eval_spend.js` (clock fix), `docs/` (generated), `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamped assets), `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this file.

**I. Suites run.** test_trial_engine (114), test_trial_capacity (48), test_subscription_billing (101), test_recovery_ladders (30), test_eval_spend (23), test_agent_training (180), test_doc_sync (30), test_proactive_templates (47), test_conv_eval (216), `npm run health` — green. `npm run eval:conv -- --exclude-calibration`: signal 22/23 (95.7%) — the single miss is the documented `trial-end-downsize-choice` judge variance (0.83 `boundary_safety`; eval replies are static fixtures and no routing/AI path changed in this release), calibration 11/11 held, 1 unparseable judge output (warning only).

**J. Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect classes *pricing card re-sent without change detection* and *end-of-trial nudges to accounts that can't convert* → siblings audited in the table above; fixed = T-3 card dedupe (snapshot), T-3/T-24 skip guard, T-0 EXPIRED retirement; deliberately left = GRACE countdown repetition (D4), activation/midpoint engagement copy, T-24 generic copy. Two test-suite clock defects (frozen fixture vs wall clock) closed by injectable `now`. Rule 13: `flowKnowledge.js` playbook + `FLOW_GUIDANCE.subscription_trial_end` and the `sakaAi.js` trial law updated in the same commit; `test_agent_training` green.

### 194. v1.72.x (Phase 8) — ledger hygiene (dual-write flag, superadmin double-count fix, dead export removal) + config namespacing (SYSTEM_CONFIG_KEYS registry, dual-window) (2026-11-07)

**Scope.** Three hygiene items from the Phase 7 backlog: P2-5 (dead `applyEntryUpdate` export), P2-3 (`expenses` vs `expense_logs` dual-write retirement behind a flag, with the three critical reads migrated) and P2-6 (`system_config` key namespacing behind a one-release dual-read/dual-write window). Release split approved by the operator: **v1.72.0/v1.72.1 prepare → v1.73.0 flips**.

**8A (v1.71.1) — P2-5 map: the dead export.**
- **Definition:** `entryLedger.js:221-259` — `applyEntryUpdate(supabase, { entry, patch, actorPhone, vehicleIds })`: scope check → `sanitizeEntryUpdate` → kind-aware column remap (earnings `amount`→`revenue_amount`) → in-place `.update()` on `LEDGER_TABLES[kind]` → `LEDGER_ENTRY_UPDATED` audit → returns `{ ok, entry, patch, rejected }`.
- **Superseded:** v1.37.0 (D1) replaced in-place edits with `relogLedgerEntry` (delete & re-log: hard-delete + full-row snapshot audit + fresh row keeps the original `created_at`, DELETE audit marked consumed so `restore` can never duplicate). The v1.63.0 route switch (`readCommands.js` edit-apply branch) was the last live reference.
- **Importers:** ZERO — proven by grep across `src/` and every `test_*.js` (only the definition + historical CHANGELOG/architecture mentions remained; the v1.63.0 recurrence autopsy had already flagged it as a Phase 9 P2-5 cleanup).
- **Action:** export deleted; `test_entry_ledger` pins `!('applyEntryUpdate' in entryLedger)` and that `relogLedgerEntry` still exports. All symbols the function used (`sanitizeEntryUpdate`, `writeAudit`, `LEDGER_TABLES`, `LEDGER_AUDIT_ACTIONS.UPDATED`) remain live via relog/delete/restore — no orphans.

**8B (v1.72.0) — P2-3 map: `expenses` vs `expense_logs`, and the PRI-1 live double-count fix.**
- **Writes.** Canonical `expense_logs` at `commands.js:607/611` (quick path) and `quizEngine.js:3258/3262` (`log_expense`); the legacy `expenses` mirror at `commands.js:616-622` (no `created_at`, no label/notes/fill_type/currency/driver linkage) and `quizEngine.js:3285-3292` (carries the retro `created_at`). Both mirror writes now sit behind `LEGACY_EXPENSES_WRITE_ENABLED` (default `true` = today's behaviour; `false` stops the mirror). The switch lives in `expenseGuard.js` (`legacyExpensesWriteEnabled()`), the module both writers already import.
- **Reads (4 audited).** `expenseGuard.isDuplicateExpense` — the only write-time dedupe — migrated to the canonical `expense_logs` by `vehicle_id` (both writers pass the vehicle they already hold; a plate-only caller resolves the vehicle first); `superadmin.handleAdminReportCommand` migrated to `expense_logs` only (**PRI-1**); `superadmin.handleAdminAuditCommand` vehicle passbook migrated to `expense_logs` by `vehicle_id`; `analytics.calculateFuelConsumption` legacy fallback **deliberately left** (archival read, dropped in v1.73.0).
- **PRI-1 — live bug fixed.** `totalExpenses` summed `expenses` + `expense_logs`, so every dual-written expense had been counted **twice** since the dual-write began. The report now reads `expense_logs` only; fleet totals match reality. Pinned in `test_superadmin.js`: a mock where the legacy table holds 999,999 and the ledger holds 150 asserts `total_expenses === 150` and that `handleAdminReportCommand` never queries `expenses`.
- **Schema divergence (documented).** `expenses` = `id, plate, expense_type, amount, liters, odometer_reading, created_at`; `expense_logs` is the canonical superset keyed by `vehicle_id` (+ `driver_id, category, cost, currency, fuel_liters, fill_type, notes, logged_at`, and `label` since v1.59.0). The mirror loses label, notes, fill type, currency and the driver/vehicle linkage by design.
- **No backfill.** `expenses` shares no reliable join key with the ledger and dual-write kept it in sync, so backfilling would risk minting duplicate ledger rows. It stays a **read-only archival table**; wipe/cleanup paths (`profileWipe`, `testCleanup`, `reset-db`, seed) keep deleting from it.
- **Teardown plan.** v1.73.0 flips `LEGACY_EXPENSES_WRITE_ENABLED=false`, drops the `analytics` archival fallback and removes the flag code — only after the three migrated reads are proven in production.
- **Frames touched (8B).** `src/services/expenseGuard.js` (flag + `vehicle_id` read + plate resolver), `src/routes/whatsapp/commands.js` (vehicleId + flag), `src/services/quizEngine.js` (vehicleId + flag), `src/services/superadmin.js` (report + passbook reads), `test_quiz_flow.js` (+4), `test_superadmin.js` (+3), `test_expense_guard.js` (new, 24), `.env.example`.

**8C (v1.72.1) — P2-6 map: `system_config` namespacing with a one-release dual window.**
- **Key inventory (9 fixed + the dynamic budget-alert family).** `prompt.saka_core_prompt` (owner sentinel, boot-critical, no default) · `deploy.last_deployed_revision` (deployLiveAlert, boot-critical) · `remediation.digest_frequency` (remediation, default `twice_daily`) · `remediation.digest_last_sent` · `remediation.urgent_last_sent` · `eval.digest_last_at` · `eval.digest_attempt_at` (evalDigest) · `eval.call_alert_date` (convEval) · `admin.wipe_pending` (superadmin; the 10-min OTP wipe gate). Dynamic family: `budget.alert.<pct>_<YYYY-MM-DD>` ← legacy `ai_budget_alert_<pct>_<date>` (superadmin, once per threshold per Nairobi day).
- **Registry + choke point.** `src/services/systemConfigKeys.js` (frozen registry: namespaced name → `{ legacyKey, owner, default, bootCritical, kind }`, the dynamic family, `describeConfigKey()` and the pure idempotent `planSystemConfigCopies()`); `src/services/systemConfigService.js` (`readConfig`, `writeConfig`, `readConfigMany`). Every raw `.from('system_config')` in `src/` is gone — pinned by `test_system_config_keys` Test 7.
- **Dual window (one release).** Reads: ONE atomic `.in('key', [namespaced, legacy])` query, namespaced value preferred, legacy fallback, then the registry default. Writes: upsert BOTH rows (so a mixed-version rolling deploy can never double-fire a marker). `SYSTEM_CONFIG_KEY_MODE` = `dual` (default) | `new` (stops legacy traffic; v1.73.0). Fail-soft: a DB error returns the default and a refused write is logged with its reason (rule 50).
- **Migration — COPY-then-DELETE, never a rename.** `npm run migrate:system-config-keys [-- --dry-run] [-- --drop-legacy]` copies every legacy row to its namespaced name and KEEPS the legacy row in release A. A rename would open a moment where neither key holds the value — exactly the window a booting instance must never see, because the deploy LIVE alert dedupes on `deploy.last_deployed_revision` and digests/cooldowns dedupe on their markers. `--drop-legacy` is the v1.73.0 teardown. Idempotent (re-runs copy nothing twice), audited as `SYSTEM_CONFIG_KEY_MIGRATED`, unknown keys are reported and never touched.
- **Live run (2026-11-07).** 12 rows read → 10 copies: deploy marker, 3 remediation, 3 eval, 3 legacy budget alerts; re-run: 22 rows, 0 copies (idempotent). `saka_core_prompt` had no legacy row (retired in v1.59.0, when the folded Persona-v4 prompt made the refinement obsolete) — and the live Sentinel suite then proved the new dual-write materialises BOTH `prompt.saka_core_prompt` and `saka_core_prompt` (`updated_by=sentinel_worker`).
- **Risk & mitigation.** (1) *Mid-boot rename → duplicate LIVE alert:* copy-only migration removes the gap; the atomic `.in()` read takes one consistent snapshot; dual-write guarantees the value exists under both names for any instance mix; worst case is one duplicate WhatsApp announcement (never blocks traffic). (2) *Split-brain Sentinel refinement:* dual-write covers rolling deploys both ways; the refinement remains version-gated and fail-soft. (3) *Marker double-fire across versions:* dual-write is what stops an old instance (writing legacy) and a new instance (writing namespaced) from missing each other.
- **Frames touched (8C).** New: `src/services/systemConfigKeys.js`, `src/services/systemConfigService.js`, `scripts/run_system_config_keys_migration.js`, `test_system_config_keys.js`. Migrated seven modules: `sakaAi.js` (prompt READ path only — see rule 13 below), `src/services/deployLiveAlert.js`, `src/workers/sentinel.js`, `src/workers/remediation.js`, `src/services/evalDigest.js`, `src/services/convEval.js` + `src/workers/convEval.js`, `src/services/superadmin.js`. Test mocks updated for the atomic `.in()` window: `test_notifications.js`, `test_agent_training.js`, `test_phase3_resilience.js`, `test_profile_wipe.js`. `package.json` (+`migrate:system-config-keys`), `.env.example`, docs/landing/changelog.

**Release split (approved).** v1.72.0/v1.72.1 PREPARE (flag + registry + dual window + reads migrated + live migration); v1.73.0 FLIPS (`LEGACY_EXPENSES_WRITE_ENABLED=false`, drop the analytics archival fallback, `SYSTEM_CONFIG_KEY_MODE=new`, `migrate:system-config-keys --drop-legacy`, drop the dual code paths).

**Rule 13 (v1.72.x).** `sakaAi.js` IS touched — but only its `system_config` READ path (`getSakaCorePrompt` now resolves the namespaced key with a legacy fallback). The prompt CONTENT is unchanged: `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT`, `SAKA_TONE_COMPASS`, `SAKA_FLOW_PLAYBOOK` and `flowKnowledge.js` were not edited (no intent, flow, field or copy change), so the training regression suite still asserts the same 180 behaviours.

**Suites run (Phase 8).** test_entry_ledger, test_expense_guard (24), test_quiz_flow, test_ocr_flow, test_superadmin (PRI-1 verified live), test_env_audit, test_system_config_keys (37), test_notifications, test_agent_training (180), test_phase3_resilience, test_conv_eval, test_profile_wipe, test_sentinel (live dual-write proof), `npm run health` green after each sub-commit.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51, consolidated).** *Class A — a superseded write path left behind:* `applyEntryUpdate` removed; every remaining `entryLedger.js` export has a live importer. *Class B — reads drifting from the canonical table:* all quoted `'expenses'` references classified (2 writes flagged, 3 production reads migrated, 1 archival fallback documented, 4 cleanup deletes kept); both dedupe callers pass `vehicleId`; both superadmin aggregates fixed. *Class C — key access outside a single choke point:* the drift test now pins that ONLY `systemConfigService.js` may touch `system_config`; all 22 live keys are either registry members or the registered dynamic family; unknown keys are surfaced, never silently migrated.

### 195. v1.72.2 (Phase 9) — trial-status deterministic aliases (read-registry lane shadowing product_qa) + earnings-invention calibration case (2026-11-07)

**Operator request.** Two small Phase 9 backlog items: P3-6 (deterministic trial-status aliases — "trial status", "my trial" and "trial" should route to the existing engine-owned summary without an AI call) and P2-7 (one `log_earnings` calibration expected-fail case representing the earnings-invention defect). Locked decisions: **D1** — the calibration tag is `fabrication` (consistency with the four existing calibration cases; never split the tag family with "invention"). **D2** — the read-registry lane is the PRIMARY fix, with the exact-phrase regex mirrored in the three existing subscription sites for quiz fast-path and provider-outage coverage.

**Audit correction 1 (rule 44/52).** The backlog premise "these phrases fall to the AI intent lane" was wrong at HEAD 9c3d1a4: for an idle registered owner the READ REGISTRY runs before the AI turn, and `matchProductQa('trial status')` returns the marketing `trial` QA entry (topics `\b(trial|free trial|…)\b`, and `STRONG_PRODUCT_RE` carries `\btrial\b`), so all three phrases were already zero-AI but answered with the generic "first 30 days are on us" card — the wrong answer. Second finding: extending only the three existing subscription regexes could never remove the AI call for idle messages, because the provider classification (`messages.js` AI turn) precedes branch 4b. Hence the new pre-AI lane.

**Audit correction 2.** The corpus held **3** earnings pass cases (`earning-quick-log`, `earning-type-quiz`, `mixed-language-pidgin-earnings`) and zero earnings calibration cases — not 4 pass cases as the backlog stated; the synthetic batches carry no earnings cases either.

**A. The `subscription_status` lane (readCommands.js).** New lane in `READ_COMMANDS` ordered IMMEDIATELY BEFORE `product_qa` (so it wins the claim and shadows the marketing card): `parksQuiz: false`, `skipWhenLocked: true`, `detect: /^(?:my\s+)?trial(?:\s+status)?[.!?]*$/i` on the trimmed text, `render: async (hit, ctx) => ctx.profile?.id ? { intent: 'VIEW_SUBSCRIPTION', extracted_data: {}, reply_message: null } : result(buildProductQaReply(matchProductQa('trial')), 'GENERAL_CHAT')`. The render adds ZERO reply logic: the existing processor gate (branch 4b) already accepts the VIEW_SUBSCRIPTION intent and `maybeHandleSubscriptionTurn`'s `wantsView` renders `formatSubscriptionSummary` ("🎁 Free trial — N day(s) left (ends <date>)"). Ownerless sessions keep today's marketing trial card, so a null reply is impossible.

**B. The `$` anchor is the safety law.** The existing subscription patterns are start-anchored with a trailing `\b`; applying that shape to `trial` would hijack "my trial ended, I have 6 trucks, what now?" (the trial-end decision window's fixture) and "trial extension" (EXTEND_TRIAL). The new alternative is whole-phrase (`^…[.!?]*$`), so only the exact status phrases (`trial`, `trial status`, `my trial`, `my trial status`) match. Six negative fixtures pin the non-hijack (trial-end sentence, extend my trial, trial extension, my trial is ending soon, trial ended yesterday, keep all), plus the locked-phase and ownerless behaviours.

**C. Mirrored regex anchors (identical alternative, defense-in-depth).** `sakaAi.js` `classifyIntentWithRegex` VIEW_SUBSCRIPTION rule (quiz fast path + provider-outage fallback; the EXTEND_TRIAL rules above it still win "extend my trial"/"trial extension"); `pending.js` `wantsView`; `messages.js` branch-4b gate (added as a separate `^…$` test — the gate's trailing `\b` alternation cannot express an end anchor and would break on trailing punctuation).

**D. The calibration case (P2-7).** `earning-invented-amount-calibration` appended to `evals/cases/conversation_cases.json`: turn "I made some money today" (no amount, no type, no plate), reply "Nice! Logged ✓ 5,000 KES daily takings for KDA 123B today. Want a report?" — inventing amount, type AND vehicle. `expected: "fail"`, tags `log_earnings, earnings, calibration, fabrication`. Loader-validated (slug id, 8–1600-char reply, PII guard clean); `selectCasesForTick` classifies it calibration (priority 1, never rests); the scheduled worker judges it when sampled (same as the other 12), the CLI judges it every run, and `--exclude-calibration` keeps it out of the headline while the hold count moves 12 → 13.

**E. Rule 13 sync.** `sakaAi.js` §7c VIEW_SUBSCRIPTION examples gain "trial status / my trial / trial"; `flowKnowledge.js` VIEW_SUBSCRIPTION behaviour gains the deterministic alias note (renders into the core prompt + docs); `docs/` regenerated via `npm run docs:gen`; no new intent or flow (registry unchanged at 39 intents / 21 flows), so `test_agent_training` still asserts the same 180 behaviours.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/readCommands.js` (lane + order note), `src/routes/whatsapp/messages.js` (gate), `src/routes/whatsapp/pending.js` (wantsView), `sakaAi.js` (§7c + classifier), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `evals/cases/conversation_cases.json` (+1), `test_read_registry.js` (+17), `test_subscription_billing.js` (+3), `test_conv_eval.js` (+1), `package.json`, `docs/` (generated), `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamped assets), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_read_registry (121 → 138), test_subscription_billing (101 → 104), test_conv_eval (216 → 217), test_product_qa (152), test_agent_training (180), test_first_message_flow (57), test_doc_sync (30), `npm run eval:conv -- --exclude-calibration` (signal 23/23, calibration 13/13), `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Defect class — a phrase claimed by the wrong deterministic lane:* every trial-family phrase was swept against all registry lanes; the fix moves the claim order (declared overlap `subscription_status` → `product_qa`), keeps exact-phrase only, and pins six negatives + the locked-phase and ownerless behaviours. Siblings audited: EXTEND_TRIAL (classifier + wantsExtend + coupon branch — left untouched, verified non-overlapping), the trial-end decision window (wantsFit/keep — left untouched, negative-pinned), record/odometer/QA lanes (no trial rule; QA shadowing deliberately moved behind the new lane). *Defect class — a flow family with no expected-fail calibration:* the earnings family now has one (`earning-invented-amount-calibration`); sibling families (fuel shorthand, coupon, trial-end, machinery) already had theirs.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/45 (consult-first), 10/11 (targeted stateless suites), 12 (auto commit/push), 13 (prompt+docs+training sync), 32/33 (fetch-first, version+history+CHANGELOG in the same commit), 44/51/52 (audit before acting, recurrence autopsy, deep-audit + extensive tests), 56 (existing users get the fix — the lane serves every verified owner), 58 (this report). No rule was edited or added.

### 196. v1.73.0 (Phase 10) — pagination, user ticket status, weekly report opt-in (2026-11-07)

**Headline.** Three UX features ship together, closing the whatsapp.js split program and the 11-phase remediation roadmap: (P3-1) paginated `my entries` / `receipts` via a session cursor and a view-only `more` turn; (P3-3) a user-side `my ticket` / `ticket status` read over the caller's OWN support tickets; (P3-4) a `weekly report on|off` opt-in with a Monday 08:00 EAT text-only fleet-summary sweep that never consumes the report quota. Five design decisions (D1–D5) and two additions (A1–A2) are locked below.

**P3-1 map (final).** Entry list: `entryAnswers.formatLedgerList` (page 1 = `ENTRY_LIST_LIMIT` 6) over `entryLedger.listLedgerEntries` (merge of `expense_logs` + `private_earnings`, driver/owner scoped, per-table fetch `cap*3+offset`, merged newest-first, `slice(start, start+cap)`), invoked by the `ledger_turn` lane. Receipts: `receipts.formatReceiptsReply` (page 1 = 5) over `listReceipts` (page 1 unchanged, client-side vehicle filter intact) plus the new `pageReceipts` (DB-side `range()` + `.in('vehicle_id', …)` + limit+1 `hasMore`) for pages 2+. `delete receipt N` stays a write lane anchored to the newest 5; `edit N`/`delete N` stay anchored to the newest 6. **D1 — `session.paginationCursor`, not `session.pending`.** Shape `{ at, listType: 'entries'|'receipts', offset, maxOffset, scope: { ownerId, driverId, vehicleIds } }`, 15-minute TTL (`paginationCursorActive`, explicitly NOT a TTL-free value), rewritten on every fresh list render, cleared when the newest window is the whole list. Rationale: the Phase 4 pending machine is a claim-order state machine with eviction + fresh-log policies and frozen truth-table tests — a page cursor is memory, not an interaction; `lastRecordQuery` is the precedent. **D2 — page 2+ is VIEW-ONLY** (headline "Older entries"/"Older receipts"; footer names `more` and the way back, never `edit N`/`delete N`). **D3 — 5-page cap** (entries 30 rows, receipts 25) then an honest redirect to `search <keyword>` or a report. **A1 — `pagination_more` negative fixture:** the lane is LAST in `READ_COMMANDS` and claims ONLY with a fresh cursor; `more`/`next`/`next page`/`older`/`show me more` with no (or expired) cursor fall through to the AI. `show me more` used to be claimed by `records_query` as a degenerate ledger read — `inspectRecordQuestion()` now short-circuits every list-continuation phrase (documented deviation, negative-pinned).

New `my_ticket` lane sits after `subscription_status` and before `product_qa` (exact-phrase `^(?:my\s+tickets?|ticket\s+status)$`), `parksQuiz: true`, `skipWhenLocked: true`, profile-gated. **OWN DATA only:** `customerCare.listUserTickets` filters `.eq('whatsapp_number', callerPhone)` — email-source tickets store a sender email in that column and can never match; another phone's rows are impossible by construction (pinned with a two-ticket mock). `formatUserTicketsReply` prints the last 3 with a short ref (`#` + first 6 alphanumerics), subject (≤60 chars), status chip (🔵🟡🟢⚪), ❗ high, localized last-update date. **A2 — empty-state idempotency:** zero tickets always yields the same honest empty state and never the support-intake prompt; the lane (read dispatch) always wins the turn before the support family. Rule 50: a pre-care-console table (`column "status" … does not exist`) degrades to the slim select in one retry. No reply/edit/close surface — rule 49 unchanged.


**P3-4 map (final).** `profiles.weekly_report_opt_in` did NOT exist — new idempotent migration `npm run migrate:weekly-report-optin` (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS weekly_report_opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`) + the column in `BOOTSTRAP_SQL`; opt-in by design (no backfill needed, rule 56). The toggle is a PRE-READ write lane beside the country command (`commands.resolveWeeklyReportToggle`, invoked in `messages.js` right after `resolveCountryCommand` and before the ack guards / read dispatch / AI turn) because the read registry's contract keeps writes out (section 190): grammar `^weekly\s+reports?\s+(on|off|enable|disable|yes|no)$` plus the bare `^weekly\s+reports?$` **state-read** — without it "weekly report" could be classified as `REQUEST_REPORT` and consume the monthly quota (**D4**, source-pinned: `weeklyReportToggleResult` precedes `await dispatchReadTurn(`). A failed write says so and never claims success (rule 50). The sweep (`src/workers/weeklyReports.js`, 30-minute gated tick from `index.js`, boot `setTimeout`): Monday 08:00 Africa/Nairobi via `formatNairobiDate` + `(getUTCHours()+3)%24` + minute ≤ 5; day marker `weeklyreports.last_sent_date` (registered in `SYSTEM_CONFIG_KEYS`, count 9 → 10; letters-only domain per the registry law) read/written ONLY through `systemConfigService`. **D5 — claim-first:** the marker is written BEFORE the owner scan; a re-tick (or a second instance) sees it and skips; a hard failure writes `''` back so the next tick retries (at-least-once — a missed week is worse than a rare duplicate). Per owner: `.eq('weekly_report_opt_in', true)` + active + not deleted, ≥1 ACTIVE vehicle (empty garages skipped silently), `buildFleetReport({ type: 'fleet' })` → `report.text` sent as ONE text message tagged kind `weekly_report` (template knob unset ⇒ free-form, byte-identical). **INVARIANTS (pinned, not assumed):** zero `usage_counters` writes (`recordReportUsage` never called/imported), zero `recordActivationEvent` calls (activation stays the strictly-three events of rule 26), no PDF path, no follow-up queue.
