### 198. v1.73.2 / v1.73.3 / v1.73.4 (Phase 12A/12C/12B) — driver-compliance reminder hygiene + quiet eval notifications + template button replies (2026-11-08)

#### 198A. v1.73.2 (Phase 12A) — the ladder resets only on a real date change, one ladder per document, edge cases skipped

**Why (audit first, rule 44/52).** The brief assumed only driver licences got expiry reminders; the live tree already ran `syncDriverComplianceReminders()` (v1.9.1, commit `7319980`) beside `syncDriverLicenseReminders()` inside `runReminderSweep` every 30 minutes. The audit instead found two real defects that no test covered: **(A1)** `createExpiryReminder()` rewrote every `notified_*` flag to `false` on EVERY upsert, so the 30-minute sync reset the ladder before each evaluation and the most urgent tier re-fired on every sweep — driver-linked alerts repeated every 30 minutes; **(A2)** a minimal licence is written to BOTH `driver_compliances` and `profiles.driver_license_expiry` (`driverAssignments.submitDriverCompliance`), so two parallel ladders existed for the same document.

**A. Merged sync (fix A2 + real coverage).** `syncDriverLicenseReminders()` + `syncDriverComplianceReminders()` became **`syncAllDriverComplianceReminders({ supabase, limit, now })`**:
- iterates EVERY `driver_compliances` row with an expiry (licence, PSV badge, PDP, CPC, operator card, medical — every catalog type) and upserts a driver-linked reminder per document TYPE;
- dedupe key: **`(subject_id, subject_type, category, linked_column)`** — one ladder per document TYPE. Category alone is NOT a key: `psv_badge`, `pdp` and `operator_cert` all map to `'permit'`, and collapsing them would lose per-document expiry tracking;
- a synced `driver_compliances:<licence type>` row supersedes the legacy `profiles.driver_license_expiry` reminder: the mirror is retired via **`retireLegacyDriverLicenceReminder()`** (`status='cancelled'`, the same retire value `deleteVehicle` uses);
- legacy-only drivers (no compliance row) keep their profile reminder (rule 56 — existing users never lose coverage);
- skipped at sync time: `lifetime === true`, a missing `number`, an invalid date, and rows **already expired** (D1 narrow reading; existing active reminders still fire their overdue tier in `evaluateExpiryReminders()`, so §28.5's missed-window contract is intact);
- `runReminderSweep()` now returns `{ …, driverRemindersSynced, driverRemindersRetired, driverRemindersSkipped }`.

**B. Date-change guard (fix A1).** `createExpiryReminder()` reads the stored `due_date` beside the id and compares it with the incoming date: an UNCHANGED date updates everything except the five tier flags (the ladder is preserved — no re-alert every 30 minutes); a CHANGED date (or a new/linkless row) resets the full ladder exactly as §28.4 always specified. The return gains `dateChanged` + `ladderReset` for testability. **Behaviour change (approved):** drivers stop receiving duplicate alerts every 30 minutes; the first post-deploy sweep is quieter. The same guard applies to every linked upsert (vehicle compliance edits included): re-saving an unchanged date no longer re-fires a consumed tier.

**C. Sibling sweep (rule 51).** `submitDriverCompliance()` (`driverAssignments.js`) mints reminders at write time; it now calls `retireLegacyDriverLicenceReminder()` whenever the saved item's category is `driver_license`, so the profile-mirror duplicate is retired at submission, not only at the next sweep. `createThresholdReminder()` deliberately left untouched — it INSERTS a new row per reminder and never resets flags.

**D. Suites run.** Baseline before edits: test_expiry_reminders (48), test_maintenance_reminders (50), test_driver_assignment_gate (54), test_user_context_cache (136), `npm run health` — green. After: **test_expiry_reminders (62 — +14 new assertions)**, test_maintenance_reminders (50), test_driver_assignment_gate (54), test_user_context_cache (136), `npm run health` — green. No behavioural assertion was edited; the only pre-existing test change is the renamed import/call.

**E. Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *an idempotent re-upsert that mutates notification state* -> siblings audited: vehicle-linked upserts (registration / `edit_vehicle` / `vehicleCompliance`) all route through the same `createExpiryReminder` guard (fixed); `submitDriverCompliance` fixed as above; `createThresholdReminder` left with reason. Defect class *two write paths owning the same document* -> the profile mirror now defers to the canonical compliance row in BOTH the sweep and the submission lane. Rule 13: no intent/flow/copy change — `flowKnowledge.js` / `sakaAi.js` untouched; `test_agent_training` stays green.

**F. Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/45 (consult-first), 8 (VIN untouched), 10/11 (targeted stateless suites), 12/33 (version + history + CHANGELOG + generated docs in the same commit), 13 (docs sync; prompt files untouched by design — no flow/copy change), 44 (the brief's premise corrected against the live tree), 50 (no schema change), 51 (sibling sweep + autopsy), 52 (before/after assertions; +14 new), 56 (legacy-only drivers keep coverage), 58 (this report). No rule was edited or added.

#### 198C. v1.73.3 (Phase 12C) — quiet eval notifications: judge errors land in the exhaustive digest, and the digest never goes silent

**Operator request.** No immediate alert for judge errors; every error, heal, proposal and failure lands in the next 6-hourly digest, and the digest becomes exhaustive.

**Audit first (rule 44).** The v1.61.8 per-tick failure digest (`notifyHealFailureDigest`) was already dead (removed in v1.61.12) and `healFailedCase` already returns `notified { whatsapp:false, email:false }`; only ONE immediate path remained — the throttled both-channel judge-error alert in `src/workers/convEval.js` (in-memory `lastErrorAlertAt`, `CONV_EVAL_ALERT_COOLDOWN_HOURS`, up to one alert per instance per window). Judge errors were also invisible to the digest beyond a count: errored run rows store no error text and no audit row was written.

**A. The immediate alert is gone.** `lastErrorAlertAt`, `resetConvEvalAlertThrottle()` and the both-channel judge-error alert block were deleted; `notified` stays `{ whatsapp:false, email:false }`. The retired `CONV_EVAL_ALERT_COOLDOWN_HOURS` knob was removed from `getConvEvalConfig()`, the env registry and `.env.example` (grep-proven single consumer).

**B. Judge errors become digest evidence.** New pure `buildJudgeErrorAuditRows(results, { phone, limit = 10 })` (exported from the worker) turns every errored result into ONE bounded `admin_audit_logs` row: `action='CONV_EVAL_JUDGE_ERROR'`, `details { case_id, reason ≤ 200 chars }`. The tick writes up to 10 rows (best-effort, never throws). `buildEvalDigest()` reads them into `judgeErrors` (max 10) + `judgeErrorCount`, rendered by `formatEvalDigestEmail()` as its OWN section — separate from the heal-refusal section so judge noise can never pollute the 3+-refusal code-fix candidates. `sendEvalDigest()` includes the new action in its audit read.

**C. The digest never goes silent (D3).** The v1.61.13 retry floor is KEPT (only a SENT email consumes the 6-hour window; a failure stamps `eval.digest_attempt_at` and retries after 15 minutes). New: a failed email now sends ONE free-form WhatsApp ping — `⏳ Digest email delayed — retrying in 15 min … Judge errors and case details will land in the next successful digest.` — returned as `retryPinged`; the success ping remains the `eval_digest_ping` template. The daily call-budget heads-up is KEPT (D4 — spend telemetry, not an error; WhatsApp only, once per Nairobi day).

**D. Suites run.** Baseline: test_conv_eval (218), test_eval_spend (23), test_proactive_templates (47), test_env_audit (44), `npm run health` — green. After: **test_conv_eval (236 — +18 new assertions)**, test_eval_spend (23), test_proactive_templates (47), test_env_audit (44), `npm run health` — green. No behavioural assertion was edited: the existing failed-email test gained a capturing ping stub (additions only).

**E. Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *quality-signal noise delivered through an interruption channel* -> siblings audited: per-heal notice (already silent, v1.61.12), per-tick failure digest (already removed, §172 marked superseded), judge-error alert (removed here), daily call alert (deliberately kept, D4). Defect class *a digest section built from a count with no persisted evidence* -> errored runs now have audit evidence; the digest cap (10 lines + "…and N more") mirrors the v1.61.8 contract. Rule 13: no intent/flow/copy change — `flowKnowledge.js` / `sakaAi.js` untouched; `test_agent_training` stays green.

Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/45 (consult-first), 10/11 (targeted suites), 12/33 (version + history + CHANGELOG + generated docs same commit), 13 (docs sync; prompts untouched), 21 (env-template parity: the retired knob left registry AND template together), 44 (audit-before-acting: the brief's "per-tick digests also fire" was already stale), 50 (no schema change), 51 (sibling sweep), 52 (before/after assertions), 58 (this report). No rule was edited or added.

#### 198B. v1.73.4 (Phase 12B) — template button replies: defensive plumbing + interactive diagnostics

**Operator request.** Ship Phase 12B without waiting for confirmation that the Meta templates actually carry quick-reply buttons: if a user tapped a button, handle it; if the payload is unrecognised, log the raw shape to `error_logs` so it can be debugged. Two decisions were locked before execution — **D1**: `remind_me` maps to `reminders` (the due LIST the template body promises), never `remind me` (which starts the set_reminder quiz); **A1**: the diagnostic must capture ONLY the `interactive`/`button` sub-objects — never the full `messageObj` (no message body, media ids, phone or timestamps in the captured shape).

**Audit first (rule 44/52).** `button_reply` / `list_reply` returned ZERO hits in `src/` — the only interactive code was the v1.51.10 sender-side builder (`src/services/interactiveReply.js`, preview-only, never wired to the wire). A button tap therefore reached the processor as a message with no `text.body` and no media: `resolveMediaEnvelope` was inert, the voice-note lane could not fire, and an empty turn fell through to the generic help menu (the same deliberate degradation the v1.61.14 autopsy documented for sticker/reaction/location). `finalizeMediaOcr` (media.js L138) is the ONLY reader of `messageObj.text?.body`, so it was the single text-injection seam. **Meta shapes were verified live against the official Cloud API webhook reference (rule 54):** `interactive.type='button_reply'` → `button_reply {id,title}`; `interactive.type='list_reply'` → `list_reply {id,title,description}`; also `interactive.type='product'`; legacy button-template replies → `message.button {text,payload}`.

**A. New leaf module `src/routes/whatsapp/interactive.js`.** Pure, stateless, services-only imports (`resolveQuickEditButtonId` from the v1.51.10 builder), never sends, never throws, exported through the barrel (section 189 leaf contract). `parseInteractiveReply(messageObj)` → `{ text, payload, intent } | null`:
- `button_reply` → title as text, id as payload; `list_reply` → row title/id; legacy `button` → text/payload.
- **`BUTTON_PAYLOAD_PHRASES`** (frozen, mirrored in `docs/TEMPLATES.md` §5): `remind_me`→`reminders`, `reminders`→`reminders`, `subscription`, `keep_all`→`keep all`, `help`. The registered phrase wins over the title (D1); an unregistered payload falls back to the button's own title, so Saka can always answer what was tapped.
- Quick-edit ids resolve through the existing resolver → the live operator (`my entries`, `edit vehicle`, …) with `intent='quick_edit'`; locked ids (`*:vin`, `entry_date`) return null there and fall through to the title — **the VIN can never be produced or resolved (rule 8)**.
- Unknown shapes (`product`, `nfm_reply`, missing reply object, empty id+title) → `null`; the processor diagnoses them instead of guessing.

### 199. v1.74.0 / v1.74.1 / v1.74.2 (Phase 13A/13B/13C) — the web dashboard foundation: auth + WhatsApp lane + overview card (2026-11-08)

**Program context.** The dashboard program (Phases 13–16) replaces the PDF-only report model with a web dashboard as the PRIMARY data surface, keeping the PDF as an export. Phase 13 ships the auth foundation and ONE page — the overview card — proving the entire trigger → link → OTP → session → render pipeline end to end. No vehicle detail, records, compliance, reports, settings, driver or superadmin views, no charts, no search, no PDF export from the dashboard (those are Phases 14–16).

#### 199A. v1.74.0 (Phase 13A) — magic link + email OTP + hashed HttpOnly session behind `DASHBOARD_ENABLED`

**Why this shape (rule 52 audit).** The repo had NO session/cookie infrastructure, NO authenticated route, and NO static file server. Everything needed an existing sibling pattern: `web_onboard_otps` (token-keyed OTP rows), `chat_sessions` (idempotent boot-ensured DDL + prune), `linkShortener` (`PUBLIC_APP_URL` base + flag read), `mailer.js` (Resend), `shortLinkNotFoundHtml` (inline HTML responses), and the `/api/onboard/check` per-route rate limit. The audit chose to evolve those (rule 55) rather than add any dependency: the dashboard is plain HTML/CSS from `renderPageShell()` and a scoped `@fastify/formbody` parser inside the dashboard plugin (the package was already a dependency but unregistered).

**Security contract (A3 — locked in 13A).**
- **sha256 at rest for everything secret**: the magic-link token, the 6-digit OTP and the 30-day session token exist raw ONLY in the email / the cookie. The row stores `token_hash`, `otp_hash` and `session_token_hash` (all `UNIQUE`; the session column is null until verification). `hashToken()` is `createHash('sha256')`.
- **OTP comparison is constant-time**: `safeCompareHex()` compares the stored hash against `hashToken(input)` with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, after an explicit empty/length check (timingSafeEqual throws on a length mismatch — the guard keeps the failure path signal-free). Codes come from `crypto.randomInt` (never Math.random).
- **Single-use link, single session**: a successful verify stamps `verified`, burns `otp_hash` (set null), writes one `session_token_hash` and never re-opens the link (`getLinkState`/`verifyDashboardOtp` both refuse with `already_used`).
- **Attempts cap 5**: each wrong code increments `attempts`; the 5th wrong answer returns `locked`, audits `DASHBOARD_OTP_LOCKED`, and the correct code is refused afterwards too.
- **60-second resend cooldown** (mirrors the web-onboarding resend gate): a fresh request within the window answers `cooldown` and inserts nothing (the raw code cannot be re-sent — only its hash exists).
- **Email failure leaves no orphaned live token**: the row is deleted when Resend returns false, so a user can never hold a link they did not receive.

**Schema (`public.dashboard_sessions`, `npm run migrate:dashboard`, idempotent + boot ensure).** `id uuid PK`, `token_hash text UNIQUE NOT NULL`, `session_token_hash text UNIQUE`, `owner_id uuid NOT NULL` (no FK — wipe order stays simple, matching `chat_sessions`), `email text`, `otp_hash text`, `attempts int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `verified boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, `link_expires_at` (15 min), `otp_expires_at` (10 min), `session_expires_at` (30 days), `created_at`. RLS enabled; indexes on `owner_id` and `link_expires_at`. Wiped by the slate reset (`RESET_TABLES` + the global TRUNCATE + the targeted-phone cascade by `owner_id`), staging DDL added to `provision_staging_schema.js`, and `test_db_reset_scope` pins all three.

**Service API (`src/services/dashboard.js`).** `isDashboardEnabled()` (`DASHBOARD_ENABLED` ∈ on|true|1, read at call time), `ensureDashboardTable`, `requestDashboardAccess({ supabase, ownerId, profile, entitlements, sendEmail })` → `{ ok, link?, reason? }` (eligibility: `email_verified` AND `entitlements.isTrial || entitlements.isPaid`; reason codes `flag_off | db_error | no_email | email_unverified | not_entitled | cooldown | email_failed`), `getLinkState`, `verifyDashboardOtp` → `{ ok, sessionToken, ownerId }` (reason codes `invalid_link | already_used | link_expired | otp_expired | locked | otp_mismatch | db_error`), `getSessionByToken`, `clearDashboardSession`, `pruneExpiredDashboardSessions` (unverified rows die 1 day past link expiry; verified rows die with their session — a live 30-day session is NEVER swept), plus the cookie contract and renderers. Every path returns a reason instead of throwing (rule 50).

**Routes (`src/routes/dashboard.js`, registered from index.js with one call).** `GET /d`, `GET /d/:token`, `POST /d/verify` (per-route rate limit 10 / 5 min), `GET /d/logout`. The form parser is registered inside the module's own encapsulated Fastify scope, so the rest of the app keeps its JSON/text parsers. **A1:** while `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` is off every route answers Fastify's own 404 payload (`Route GET:/d not found`, `statusCode 404`) — byte-identical to an unregistered route, so the dashboard's existence is never revealed. **Cookie contract:** `saka_dash=<raw token>; Path=/d; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=2592000; Secure` (`Secure` omitted only on localhost). Boot: `ensureDashboardTable`; housekeeping: prune at boot + every 15 minutes.

**Email (D2).** `sendDashboardMagicLinkEmail()` sends ONE email carrying BOTH the magic link and the 6-digit code (never-throw, returns false). **The code NEVER travels over WhatsApp** — the chat carries the link, the inbox carries the code; a leaked chat transcript can never open a dashboard.

**Files.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (new), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (new), `scripts/run_dashboard_migration.js` (new), `test_dashboard.js` (new, stateless — in-memory mock only), `index.js` (import + register + boot ensure + prune interval), `src/services/mailer.js` (`sendDashboardMagicLinkEmail`), `src/services/envAudit.js` (SERVER + `DASHBOARD_ENABLED`), `.env.example` + `.env`, `scripts/provision_staging_schema.js`, `scripts/reset-db.js`, `test_db_reset_scope.js`, `scripts/health_audit.js` (suite registered), `package.json` (1.74.0 + `migrate:dashboard`), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** Baseline: test_db_reset_scope (88), test_env_audit (44), test_read_registry (181), test_agent_training (187), test_doc_sync (30), `npm run health` — green. After: **test_dashboard (new, 78 assertions: flag 404s, eligibility, hashed storage, TTLs, cooldown, email-failure cleanup, single-use link, 30-day session, attempts cap, timing-safe compare, cookie contract, prune safety)**, test_db_reset_scope (90 — +2), test_env_audit (44), test_read_registry (181), test_agent_training (187), test_doc_sync (30), `npm run health` — green. Zero behavioural assertions edited (additions only). Migration applied live: `public.dashboard_sessions` created cleanly.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/45 (consult-first), 10/11/33 (targeted suites, version + history + CHANGELOG same commit), 13 (docs sync; no intent/flow change in 13A), 21 (env registry + `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` in SERVER + `.env.example` parity), 32 (origin synced first), 42 (open proposals checked — none), 50 (table missing / email failed both degrade to reasons, never throw), 52 (deep audit + before/after assertions), 54 (live migration + health verified), 55 (evolved existing patterns; zero new dependencies), 56 (wipe scope + staging DDL so old and new environments both work), 58 (this report). No rule was edited or added.

#### 199B. v1.74.1 (Phase 13B) — the WhatsApp lane: one trigger, one email, the code never in chat

**The lane (locked).** `READ_COMMANDS` gains one entry, `id: 'dashboard'`, placed AFTER `my_ticket` and BEFORE `product_qa` (the user-state read family). Detector (verbatim):

```js
const DASHBOARD_RE = /^(?:(?:open|show|see|view)\s+(?:me\s+)?(?:my\s+|the\s+)?|(?:my\s+|the\s+)?)(?:web\s+|online\s+)?dashboard[.!?]*$/i;
```

The `$` anchor is the grammar: `dashboard`, `my dashboard`, `open my dashboard`, `show me the dashboard`, `web dashboard` are claimed; `dashboard ideas`, `i can't see the dashboard`, `dashboard not loading for my fleet` fall through to the AI (pinned by negative fixtures). `parksQuiz: true` (it IS a read) and `skipWhenLocked: true` (a PIN/OTP phase always outranks it).

**The three reply paths (deterministic, zero AI tokens).**
1. **Flag OFF (A2):** verbatim `That's not something I can do yet — reply *help* to see what I can do.` — the dashboard is never named, and no token row, no email and no DB write happens.
2. **Flag ON and eligible** (`email_verified` AND `entitlements.isTrial || isPaid`): the service mints the row and emails the link+code, and the chat replies with the LINK only: `🖥️ Your dashboard link is on its way … I emailed a private link to a***a@example.com — it works for 15 minutes. The 6-digit code is in that same email; I will never ask for it here. <link> …`. **D2 is enforced by construction and pinned by tests:** no 6-digit sequence may appear in the WhatsApp reply (after stripping the "N minutes" phrasing) and the model playbook forbids repeating or accepting a dashboard code in chat.
3. **Flag ON, not eligible:** `email_unverified`/`no_email` → the website sign-up line (`https://sakafleet.com`); `not_entitled` → `Your dashboard opens on a trial or a paid plan — you are on Free right now. Reply *pricing* to see the plans.`; `cooldown` → `I just sent it — check your inbox (and spam)…`; `email_failed` → one honest retry line; `db_error`/any thrown error → `Something went wrong on my side — try again in a minute.` (the lane catches everything, rule 50 — a dashboard request can never crash a turn).

**Test transport (no real email in suites).** The lane reads `ctx.dashboardRequestAccess` / `ctx.dashboardEntitlements` when present (mirrors the `buildReport = buildFleetReport` injection pattern); production never sets them, so every copy branch is provable offline while the real service path stays exercised by the foundation suite.

**Flow/prompt sync (rule 13 + rule 60).** `flowKnowledge.js`: `FLOW_GUIDANCE.dashboard` (one stuck-guidance line) + new `SAKA_WEB_DASHBOARD_PLAYBOOK` (link/code TTLs, code by email only, trial-or-paid gate, overview-only scope) injected by `buildFlowPlaybook()`; `sakaAi.js` `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT` gains one `WEB DASHBOARD (v1.74.0)` line beside WEB SIGNUPS. `test_agent_training` +4 assertions (playbook block, email-only rule, guidance line rendered, core-prompt line).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/readCommands.js` (imports + DASHBOARD_RE + lane + header order), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js` (guidance line + playbook block + export + buildFlowPlaybook), `sakaAi.js` (core-prompt line), `test_read_registry.js` (+20 dashboard-lane assertions), `test_dashboard.js` (+10 lane-integration assertions), `test_agent_training.js` (+4), `docs/` (generated), `package.json` (1.74.1), `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamp), this file (§199B + version/history), `CHANGELOG.md`.

#### 199C. v1.74.2 (Phase 13C) — the four pages, the overview card and D3

**D1 — inline HTML, shared shell.** `src/services/dashboard.js` owns `DASHBOARD_CSS`, `renderPageShell(title, body, { headerRight })` (dark Saka palette, `noindex`, viewport-safe) and every page renderer; `src/routes/dashboard.js` is now only flag gate → service call → `text/html` response. No static server, no CDN, no new dependency. `theme` code is escaped through `escapeHtml` everywhere a user value or a phone/plate/date is interpolated.

**The four renderers.**
- `renderOtpPage({ token, emailMasked, error })` — masked destination, hidden token field, `pattern="[0-9]{6}"` input, error slot, "code works for 10 minutes / never share it, Saka will never ask in WhatsApp".
- `renderOverviewPage({ data, emailMasked })` — `Your fleet at a glance`, `updated <Nairobi date>`, the KPI grid (**Spend / Earnings / Net / Active vehicles N of M**), **Coming up** (six cards max: plate • category • date • `in N d` chip, `due` styling inside 7 days), **Recent activity** (five rows with date chips), the logout link and the footer line "Your PDF reports are still one message away in WhatsApp". Empty sections render warm honest states ("Nothing due in the coming weeks — nicely kept." / "No activity yet — log your first entry in WhatsApp…"), never a bare zero.
- `renderLogoutPage()` — confirms the browser lost access and teaches the way back (*dashboard*).
- `renderErrorPage(status, message)` — 400/401/404/410/500/503 titles; a failed card renders ONE honest explanation (no `undefined` leak, pinned).

**D3 — `upcomingExpiryItems(supabase, ownerId, limit = 6)`** exported from `fleetReports.js`: reuses `loadFleetData` + the unified `collectExpiryItems` (reminders take precedence, canonical vehicle columns fill gaps), filters `daysLeft >= 0`, sorts soonest-first, caps at the limit (1–50), returns exactly `{ plate, category, dueDate, daysLeft, status }`. Never throws (returns `[]`).

**`buildOverviewCard({ supabase, ownerId, profile, countryInfo })`** — calls `buildFleetReport({ type: 'fleet' })` + `upcomingExpiryItems` and shapes `{ ok, generatedAt, currency, locale, timeZone, kpis: { spend, earnings, net, activeVehicles, totalVehicles }, upcoming (≤6), recent (≤5) }`. Money is always the owner currency from `buildGlobalContext` (no hard-coded KES). Both builders are injectable for suites; production uses the real ones. A failed report returns `{ ok:false }` and the page answers a 503 explanation.

**Routes (final).** `GET /d/:token` → OTP page (or 400/410 error page for invalid/expired/used links). `POST /d/verify` → 303 `/d` + cookie, or 401 re-render with reason copy, or an error page when the link itself died. `GET /d` → cookie → session → slim-degrading profile load (rule 50) → overview card → page; **no cookie/invalid cookie → 401 page with the WhatsApp instruction** (a redirect to `/d/<new token>` is impossible: tokens are only minted from an eligible WhatsApp turn — redirecting to a token that does not exist would be a lie). An invalid cookie is also cleared. `GET /d/logout` → delete the session row + `Max-Age=0` cookie + logged-out page.

**Cookie contract (verbatim).** `saka_dash=<raw token>; Path=/d; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=2592000; Secure` — `Secure` is appended on every real host and omitted only for `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` development.

**Flag state.** `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` stays **OFF** in `.env.example` and `.env`; the operator flips it in Cloud Run only after the live walk-through (WhatsApp trigger → email → code → overview → logout). While off, all four routes remain a byte-identical generic 404 and the lane answers A2.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (overview card + 4 renderers + CSS), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (page wiring, profile degrade, logout), `src/services/fleetReports.js` (`upcomingExpiryItems` + default export), `test_dashboard.js` (+49: D3 shape/sort/filter/limit, card shaping, real-builder zeros, Fastify end-to-end pages incl. cookie attributes + 401/404 paths + logout row deletion, pure renderers), `package.json` (1.74.2), `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamp), this file (§199C + version/history), `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 200. v1.75.0 (Phase 14A) — the vehicle pages: list + one page per vehicle, owner-scoped, in the owner's currency (2026-11-08)

**Program context.** Phase 13 proved the pipeline with ONE page. Phase 14 owns the full dashboard (vehicles, records, compliance, reports, settings, charts, search, PDF export); 14A ships the surface an owner opens first — the fleet list and a page per vehicle — and nothing else. Still flag-gated: `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` stays **OFF** in `.env`/`.env.example` until the operator walk-through.

**D1 — data lives in `fleetReports.js`, pages live in `dashboard.js`.** Two new exports reuse the report engine end to end: `buildVehicleDirectory({ supabase, ownerId, countryInfo, profile, now })` and `buildVehicleDetail({ supabase, ownerId, vehicleId, countryInfo, profile, now, recordLimit = 8 })`. Both call the same `loadFleetData` + `collectExpiryItems` the four PDF/WhatsApp reports use, and the detail page's records are mapped through `reportLedger.expenseToLedgerRow` / `earningToLedgerRow`, so a dashboard row and a PDF row can never disagree on date, description or amount. Month money uses the same UTC month window (`monthStartMs`) and the same timestamp precedence as the ledger. `dashboard.js` only adds `buildVehiclesIndex` / `buildVehiclePage` (injectable, never-throw wrappers) plus the renderers.

**D2 — ownership is structural, not a filter.** `buildVehicleDetail` loads the OWNER-scoped dataset and looks the id up inside it; another owner's vehicle id is simply absent and answers `{ ok:false, reason:'not_found' }` (the `my_ticket` OWN-DATA pattern). The route turns `not_found` into a warm 404 page ("That vehicle is not on your fleet…"), never a 403 that would confirm existence. Pinned by `another owner's vehicle id answers not_found`.

**D3 — what each page shows (and what it does not).**
- `/d/vehicles`: one row per vehicle — plate (linked) + make/model, Active/Paused/Inactive chip, odometer in the display unit, driver name (or "No driver assigned"), this-month spend, an `N overdue` chip when anything lapsed and the soonest document's due chip. Sorted active-first, then plate.
- `/d/vehicles/:id`: plate + status, make/model • driver • updated line, three KPI tiles (odometer, spend this month, earnings this month), every document with its due date and chip (expired first, then soonest), and the latest 8 merged ledger rows with amount + date.
- Nav on every signed-in page: `Overview · Vehicles · Log out`; the overview gains one line — "See your vehicles →" (rule 31: one next step, no menu wall).
- **No VIN** (rule 8: the immutable asset identifier is not needed on screen), no charts, no search, no exports, no settings — later phases.

**D4 — the 13C country regression, fixed (rule 51 sibling sweep).** 13C rendered the real overview through `buildOverviewCard({ supabase, ownerId, profile })` with NO `countryInfo`, so `buildGlobalContext(null, profile)` fell back to GLOBAL/USD/en-US for every owner: a Kenyan fleet read "USD" on the live page while every WhatsApp report read KES. The routes now resolve `countryInfo` from the profile's phone number (`detectCountryFromPhone`, rule 7 phone-primary lock) and pass it to all three builders. Sibling audit of the defect class *"a builder called without country context silently defaults to GLOBAL"*: `buildOverviewCard` (fixed here), `buildVehicleDirectory` / `buildVehicleDetail` (born with the parameter, route passes it), the WhatsApp report path (`messages.js` already builds `countryInfo` from the number), the PDF path (same report builders with `countryInfo`), `upcomingExpiryItems` (no money/units), admin digests (deterministic text, no owner currency). One targeted assertion per sibling: the KE route test asserts KES on the list and the overview, the imperial test asserts miles.

**D5 — routes and the session gate.** New `GET /d/vehicles` and `GET /d/vehicles/:id`, both flag-gated first (A1 generic 404 while OFF) and registered BEFORE `/d/:token` so a token can never swallow them. The repeated cookie → session → profile sequence moved into one `requireOwnerSession()` helper (GET `/d` uses it too, same 401 copy and same cookie clearing). Rule 50: a failed profile load degrades to the slim column set; a failed directory/detail renders ONE honest 503 explanation (never a `undefined` leak).

**Skill sync (rule 13 + rule 60).** `SAKA_WEB_DASHBOARD_PLAYBOOK` now states the shipped scope ("also lists the owner's vehicles and opens one page per vehicle with its documents and its most recent records") and names the unshipped pages as off-limits; `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT`'s WEB DASHBOARD line matches. `test_agent_training` +3 assertions (playbook vehicle pages, "have NOT shipped", core-prompt scope), 191 → 194.

Zero behavioural assertions edited (additions only; the two renderer currency assertions were authored as `/(KES|Ksh)/` because `en-KE` renders "Ksh", not "KES").

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *"a page builder invoked without country context silently defaults to the GLOBAL region"* → siblings audited and each pinned (D4). Second class *"a route can shadow another by registration order"* → `/d/vehicles` + `/d/vehicles/:id` registered before `/d/:token`, and the flag-OFF sweep now covers both URLs so a future reorder fails loudly. Deliberately left: `renderVehiclesPage` shows the owner's full email mask on the index (same identity line the overview already used) and the paused-vehicle chip keeps the raw status word lower-cased rather than inventing a label set.

### 201. v1.75.1 (Phase 14B) — the records surface: owner-vehicle scope, filters, pagination, CSV/PDF exports, receipt links (2026-11-08)

**Scope.** Phase 14B ships the records surface only: `GET /d/records` (filterable table, 20 rows/page), `GET /d/records.csv` and `GET /d/records.pdf` (the SAME filtered set), and `GET /d/receipt/:id` (a 5-minute signed link). Compliance, the reports builder, settings, charts and every driver/superadmin view stay in 14C–16. Still flag-gated: `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` remains **OFF** in `.env`/`.env.example`.

**FIX-1 — the records query is OWNER-VEHICLE scoped, never `queryRecordLedger`.** `recordQuery.js` filters `driver_id = ownerId`, which is correct for the per-caller WhatsApp lane but would show a fleet owner only the rows they personally typed (~10% of a real fleet's ledger). `queryOwnerRecords()` therefore scopes `vehicle_id IN (the owner's live vehicles)` and merges `expense_logs` + `private_earnings` through the canonical mappers (`expenseToLedgerRow` / `earningToLedgerRow`). `recordQuery.js` is **untouched** (pinned by `test_record_answers` staying green with zero edits) and the proof is a driver-logged row (`driver_id='d-1'`) appearing in the owner's set. `loadOwnerVehicles()` is the one owner-scope source (`owner_id` + `deleted_at IS NULL`, bounded 500, fail-soft).

**The filter set (verbatim URL params).** `?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&type=Fuel,Repairs&vehicle=<id>&label=karen&keyword=shell&page=N`.
- **Dates:** Nairobi calendar days, inclusive; default = the last **30** days; range capped at **366** days; `from > to` refused.
- **Type:** comma-split expense types (≤12); when present the set is expenses only (earnings carry no expense type).
- **Vehicle:** must be one of the owner's vehicles (an unknown id is refused, never silently widened).
- **Label / keyword:** ≤40 chars, whitespace-normalised, `% , ( ) *` stripped (PostgREST-safe); label → `label.ilike`, keyword → `.or(label.ilike,notes.ilike)` (OR, not AND).
- **Page:** 0-based, cap 250.
- `parseRecordsFilters()` is the ONLY filter parser; the table, the CSV and the PDF all call it (no export can bypass the table's filter). Export links carry the filter and never the page.

**Two-table paging (why `.range` per table is not enough).** Each table is fetched up to `offset + pageSize + 1` rows via `.range(0, n-1)`, the normalized rows are merged newest-first and the merged list is sliced — paging each table independently with `.range(offset, …)` would produce wrong pages because the tables interleave by date (the `listLedgerEntries` precedent). Totals come from two `count: 'exact', head: true` queries with the same filters.

**Business-date columns differ (found during the build).** Expenses are filed by `created_at`; earnings by `logged_at` (the same precedence `reportLedger` uses, because `private_earnings.logged_at` is the business date and `created_at` is insertion time). A single `created_at` filter silently dropped backdated earnings — pinned by a seed whose earning carries only `logged_at`.

**D2 — receipt links are unique-match only.** There is NO foreign key between `receipts` and `expense_logs` in either direction (audited in the 14B map: `receipt_id` exists only as an audit-log detail key). `matchReceiptForExpense()` therefore accepts a link only when **exactly one** receipt shares the vehicle, the Nairobi calendar day and the amount; two or more candidates answer `ambiguous` (the row says “Multiple match”, no link), zero answers none. A page shares one cache, so lookups collapse to one query per vehicle+day+amount. The durable FK (`expense_logs.receipt_id` + backfill) is minted as a tracked follow-up proposal **PROP-2026-11-08-01** (`PENDING_APPROVAL`, risk `medium`, audited `REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL_CREATED`) — it is **not** part of 14B because it needs a schema change. **Shipped in v1.81.0 (§210):** the durable FK landed — exact links win and this heuristic survives only as the legacy fallback for rows written before the backfill.

**D1 — signed receipt URLs, 300 s, per request.** `GET /d/receipt/:id` → session → receipt row → **owner-vehicle scope OR `receipts.owner_id = owner`** → `signReceiptUrl()` → `302` to `createSignedUrl(path, 300)`. A miss answers **404, never 403** (existence is never confirmed), and no signed URL is ever minted for a foreign row. The object path comes from `receiptStoragePaths()` (media id first), so signing survives once the bucket is private. **Operator prerequisite: the `receipts` Storage bucket must be CREATE-AS-PRIVATE (or flipped to private) in the Supabase console — verified live 2026-11-08 the bucket does not exist yet (`fleet-reports` is `public:true`), so `createSignedUrl` currently answers `sign_failed` and the receipt route degrades to an honest 404.** Meanwhile `uploadReceiptImage` has been returning null for every photo (no bucket), so `receipts.image_url` is null fleet-wide and `media_id` is the only path source — which is exactly what signing uses. Existing internal consumers (`profileWipe`, delete/prune, path derivation) are unaffected. Free-tier receipts (`image_url = null`, no media id) answer the same honest 404.

**D3 — vendor is NOT a 14B filter.** Vendor lives only on `receipts`, never on `expense_logs`/`private_earnings`, so a records-table vendor filter would need the same heuristic join. Deferred to a receipts view (Phase 15+). Label + keyword search covers the “find that entry” need today.

**D4 — test double extensions.** `scripts/mockSupabase.js` gains `.or()` (comma list = DISJUNCTION, multiple calls ANDed), `.range(from, to)` (inclusive end, like PostgREST) and `.ilike()` (case-insensitive `%` wildcard), all routed through one `matchOne()` evaluator shared with the AND filters. Purely additive: the whole pre-existing suite set stayed green before any new assertion was added.

**Exports.** `serializeRecordsCsv()` is the repo's only CSV serializer: UTF-8 BOM (Excel-safe), CRLF, RFC-4180 quoting, ISO-8601 dates (canonical storage), columns `Date,Kind,Plate,Type,Description,Odometer,Unit Cost,Amount,Currency,Label`. `buildRecordsPdf()` reuses `buildLedgerGroups` + `buildProReportPdf` and returns a **Buffer** — no Storage upload and no email; the route streams it with a dated `content-disposition`. A capped export (2,000 rows) says “Showing the newest N records — narrow the dates” instead of pretending to be complete. `useStandardFonts` is a suite-only passthrough (the branded fonts are subset-encoded, so drawn text is only readable in QA mode — the same contract `test_pdf_engine` uses).

**Security.** Every route: flag gate first (`A1` generic 404 while OFF) → `requireOwnerSession()` → owner-vehicle scope → country from the phone. The receipt route additionally carries a `60 / 5 min` rate limit. **Rule 51(iii):** a failed export can never look like an empty file — `{ ok:false }` answers a 500 explanation and logs the route (`/d/records/csv`, `/d/records/pdf`) with **no row, note, label or amount** in `error_logs`, pinned by test.

**Rule 51 sibling sweep (defect classes).**
| Class | Siblings audited | Result |
|---|---|---|
| a query that filters by type but not by owner | `queryOwnerRecords` (vehicle scope), `matchReceiptForExpense` (same vehicle as the row), receipt route (owner fleet or owner id), CSV/PDF (same `parseRecordsFilters`) | pinned per surface |
| a signed URL that leaks scope | TTL fixed at 300 s, minted per request only after the scope check, no pre-generation | pinned (ttl + no call for a foreign row) |
| a failed query that looks like success | table (503 vs 200), CSV export (500, not an empty file), PDF export (500) | pinned |
| a date filter on the wrong column | expenses `created_at`, earnings `logged_at` | pinned (backdated-earning seed) |

**Rule 52 deep audit — three real defects caught by the new tests before shipping.**
1. `Number(null) === 0` made the export `offset` always win, so `page` was ignored and every page returned page 0 (caught by the page-1 assertion). Fixed with an explicit `hasOffset` check.
2. `.or('a,b')` was first implemented as one AND-group; PostgREST treats the comma list as a disjunction (caught by the two-column keyword assertion). Fixed to one group per condition.
3. The earnings date filter used `created_at`, silently dropping rows whose business date is `logged_at` (caught by the merge-count assertion). Fixed with `recordTimeColumn()`.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (+§7: constants, `nairobiDateOf`, `parseRecordsFilters`, `cleanRecordsTerm`, `loadOwnerVehicles`, `queryOwnerRecords`, `matchReceiptForExpense`, `attachReceiptMatches`, `signReceiptUrl`, `serializeRecordsCsv`, `buildRecordsPdf`, `renderRecordsPage`, `renderReceiptPage`, `recordsQueryString`, nav + records CSS, default export), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (+4 routes, imports), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js` (playbook scope: records table + exports + unique-match rule), `sakaAi.js` (core prompt scope), `scripts/mockSupabase.js` (`.or`/`.range`/`.ilike` + `matchOne`), `test_dashboard.js` (+112 assertions: 187 → 299; four new flag-off URLs), `test_agent_training.js` (+2: 194 → 196), `package.json` (1.75.1), `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamp), `docs/` (regenerated), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§201 + version/history), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** Baseline before edits: test_dashboard (187), test_record_answers (80), test_entry_ledger, test_fleet_reports (42), test_report_builders (83), test_ocr_flow (129), `npm run health` — green. After: **test_dashboard (299 — +112)**, test_agent_training (196 — +2), test_record_answers (80 — unchanged, `queryRecordLedger` untouched), test_entry_ledger, test_fleet_reports (42), test_report_builders (83), test_ocr_flow (129), test_read_registry, test_no_canned_replies (14 — ratchet still 4), test_kb_docs, test_landing_static, test_doc_sync, `npm run health` — green. Zero pre-existing assertions edited.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *“a scope inherited from another lane”* → every new surface re-derives the owner-vehicle scope instead of reusing the caller-scoped query (FIX-1, receipt route, CSV/PDF); *“a failed read rendered as a legitimate empty result”* → exports refuse with 500 + a route-only log; *“a date filter on the insertion timestamp”* → business-date columns pinned per table.

### 202. v1.75.2 (Phase 14C) — the compliance surface: vehicle + driver board, read-only driver pages, filtered PDF (2026-11-08)

**Scope.** Phase 14C ships the compliance surface only: `GET /d/compliance` (the owner's vehicles AND assigned drivers with a tracking rollup and the All / Due soon / Expired filter), `GET /d/drivers/:id` (read-only driver profile + every `driver_compliances` row), and `GET /d/compliance.pdf?view=…` (the SAME view, streamed). No editing of dates, no document upload, no write path of any kind — those stay deferred. Still flag-gated: `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` remains **OFF** in `.env`/`.env.example`.

**Decisions locked.**
- **D1 — driver document numbers are UNMASKED for the owner.** The owner owns the fleet and must be able to verify a licence/PSV number; the driver's own WhatsApp Compliance Card keeps `maskNumber`. Pinned by `document numbers are unmasked for the owner (D1)`.
- **D2 — the suite is extended, not multiplied:** all 14C coverage lives in `test_dashboard.js` (one registered suite, health stays green).
- **D3 — nav:** `Overview · Vehicles · Records · Compliance · Log out` (Compliance sits between Records and Log out). The `.chip.bad` (red `#F85149`) chip is the only CSS addition; `.chip.due` (orange) and `.chip.ok` (green) were already there.

**The engine reuse (rule 55).** The board reads through `buildComplianceReport` — the same builder the WhatsApp/PDF compliance report uses — then narrows it with ONE pure `filterComplianceReport(reportData, view)`. That function re-derives **totals AND the category matrices** (`summarizeCategory`, now exported) with the report's own bucket math, so a filtered PDF can never print a KPI that contradicts its own table. `expiryStatus` is likewise exported and reused for every chip, and the chip vocabulary is one helper (`complianceChipHtml`: expired → red, any due bucket → orange, active/lifetime → green, unknown → grey). The driver section is the one place the report cannot help: `driverCompliance` rows in the report carry no `driver_id` (only a phone), so the board queries `driver_compliances` by the owner's `assigned_driver_id` set directly — bounded, owner-scoped by construction.

**The two-sources finding (recorded).** *On file* (a `driver_compliances` ledger row) and *tracked* (an item in the unified expiry collector, which is fed by driver-linked reminders) can disagree: a document saved without a number is skipped by `syncAllDriverComplianceReminders`, so it exists on file but has no reminder ladder. The driver page and the board's driver rollup report the ledger truth (`documentCount` + status chips) while the vehicle section reports the collector truth — both honest, never merged into a fake "total". The legacy `profiles.driver_license_expiry` mirror is deliberately NOT read (retired by v1.73.2; reading it would re-introduce a duplicate ladder).

**Filters and ordering.** `?view=all|due|expired` (aliases `due_soon`/`soon`/`overdue`), default `all`; `due` = `0 ≤ daysLeft ≤ 30` (all three due buckets), `expired` = `< 0`. An unknown value answers **400** with one plain sentence. Sorting is ascending `daysLeft`, so expired items pin to the top of every list; a subject with no dated document says "No dates on file" (never a fake zero). Under a filtered view, subjects with no matching item are hidden (and an empty view gets a warm "Nothing expired — nicely kept." / "Nothing due in the next 30 days.").

**Routes + security.** All three: flag gate first (A1 generic 404 while OFF) → `requireOwnerSession()` → country from the phone → registered **before** `/d/:token`. `GET /d/drivers/:id` resolves ownership **structurally**: the id must be an `assigned_driver_id` of one of the owner's live vehicles, otherwise `not_found` → **404** (never 403) and the 404 body carries no name, phone or number (rule 51(iv), pinned). The PDF route streams a Buffer (`complianceReportToPdf` → `buildProReportPdf`) with a dated `content-disposition`; no Storage, no email.

**Rule 51 sibling sweep (defect classes).**
| Class | Siblings audited | Result |
|---|---|---|
| a scope inherited from another lane | driver page re-derives `assigned_driver_id ∈ owner vehicles` (not `getDriverComplianceStatus`'s any-profile semantics); board driver ids come from the same vehicle set; receipt/record surfaces untouched | pinned: foreign driver → 404 |
| a filter the export bypasses | `filterComplianceReport` feeds the board AND the PDF; the page's totals and the PDF KPIs read the same filtered data | pinned: `pdfDue` KPIs == filtered totals; board `reportData` == direct filter |
| a status chip that lies | one `complianceChipHtml` for board + driver page; `expiryStatus` reused from the report engine | pinned: all six buckets (expired/due_30d/due_14d/due_7d/active/lifetime/unknown) |
| identity leak on a miss | 404 body asserted free of name, phone and document number | pinned (rule 51 iv) |

**Rule 52 deep audit — three real defects caught before shipping.**
1. `loadOwnerVehicles()` selected `id, plate_number, make_model, status, deleted_at` — **no `assigned_driver_id`**, so the driver section would have been silently empty for every owner. Fixed by adding the column to the one scope query (the vehicle pages ignore it).
2. The report's `driverCompliance` rows carry **no `driver_id`** (only a phone), so a board built from the report alone would have merged every driver's documents into one bucket. Fixed by querying `driver_compliances` by the owner's assigned driver ids and attributing per driver.
3. A naive filter would have left `insuranceStatusMatrix` / `inspectionAndPermits` **stale**, so a filtered PDF would print a category matrix contradicting its own KPIs. Fixed by re-deriving the summaries from the filtered items with `summarizeCategory`.

### 203. v1.75.3 (Phase 14D) — reports builder + settings + data export; the Owner Dashboard is complete (2026-11-08)

**Scope.** The final owner-dashboard sub-phase: `GET /d/reports` (builder form) → `GET /d/reports.pdf` (bespoke PDF), `GET /d/settings` + `POST /d/settings` (one writable preference), `GET /d/export.csv` (every record in one file). No report templates, no emailing a report from the dashboard, no email/unit changes from the dashboard (WhatsApp owns those), no charts, no driver/superadmin views. Flag-gated as always: `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` stays **OFF** until the operator flips it.

**Decisions locked.**
- **D1 — date ranges are additive.** `dateRangeBounds()` gained `last_30_days` and `buildCustomReport()` gained an optional `bounds = { from, to, label }` override (the public key stays `bounds`; the local binding is `boundsOverride`). When absent, every pre-existing preset behaves exactly as before — the WhatsApp lane passes no `bounds`, so its behaviour is unchanged (`test_report_metrics` 25 + `test_report_builders` 83 stayed green with zero edits; `test_fleet_reports` 42 green).
- **D2 — CSRF is tokenless by design.** The session cookie is HttpOnly + `SameSite=Strict`; CORS is registered only for `/api/onboard*`, `/healthz` and `/api/health`, never `/d`. On top of that, `POST /d/settings` refuses a write whose `Origin` is present and not the request host (**403**, checked before the session gate). A missing Origin (older browsers) falls back to the SameSite guarantee. No new dependency.
- **D3 — one CSV, six sections, `record_type` first.** No ZIP (no archiver dependency exists; adding one would break the zero-dep preference). `serializeAllDataCsv()` streams expenses, earnings, reminders, vehicle documents, driver documents and receipt metadata (never image URLs), each preceded by a `# section` comment row (A2), with a `[CAP]` row when a table hits the 2,000-row limit (A1) and an `[ERROR]` row when a table cannot be read (never a silent empty section).

**The builder reuses the engine (rule 55).** `buildDashboardCustomReport()` is a thin wrapper over `buildCustomReport()` with `access: { lane: 'owner' }` and the resolved window — the same engine the WhatsApp custom-report lane uses, so metrics, charts, ledger and PDF layout are identical by construction. `parseReportSpec()` validates one spec (range, ≤366-day custom window, owner-only vehicle ids, ≤8 metric ids from `CUSTOM_METRICS`, five owner-metric defaults when none are ticked) and that spec feeds BOTH the form state and the PDF — the export can never describe something the form did not select. **Dashboard reports are quota-free by construction:** `buildCustomReport()` has no `usage_counters` path at all (the WhatsApp lane remains the only quota caller).

**The one writable preference.** `profiles.weekly_report_opt_in` — the SAME column the WhatsApp `weekly report on|off` lane writes and the Monday 08:00 EAT worker reads. Last-write-wins across surfaces; no shadow copy. A failed update renders "nothing changed" and never the Saved chip. The form posts an explicit `action=save_weekly` marker, so a stray POST can never silently unsubscribe an owner. Everything else on the page is read-only: masked email/phone, language, units, country, currency, plan label (`getTierLabel`) and the session expiry.

**Rule 51 sibling sweep (defect classes).**
| Class | Siblings audited | Result |
|---|---|---|
| a scope inherited from another lane | `parseReportSpec` validates vehicle ids against the owner's live set; metrics against the registry | pinned: foreign vehicle → 400 |
| a filter the export bypasses | one spec feeds the form and the PDF route | pinned: custom-range PDF + 400 on a malformed one |
| a settings write that fakes success | `saveSettings` returns an error and the page renders it, never Saved | pinned |
| CSRF | SameSite=Strict + no `/d` CORS + Origin guard | pinned: cross-origin POST → 403, row unchanged |
| dual-write divergence | the dashboard writes the same `weekly_report_opt_in` column the worker reads | pinned: row updated + patch names the column |

**Rule 52 deep audit — findings.** (1) The brief placed `dateRangeBounds`/`buildCustomReport` in `fleetReports.js`; they live in `reportMetrics.js` — the extensions landed there, nothing was duplicated. (2) `buildCustomReport` scopes by `vehicleIds` with a fallback that includes everything when the resolved list is empty, so an unvalidated foreign id would widen the scope — which is exactly why `parseReportSpec` is the only feeder (validated, pinned). (3) The unchecked-checkbox POST would have written `false` on any stray form submission, so the `action=save_weekly` marker was added and pinned.

### 204. v1.76.0 (Phase 15) — driver + superadmin dashboard lanes (2026-11-08)

**Scope.** The dashboard stops being owner-only: `dashboard_sessions.session_role` (`owner` | `driver` | `admin`) decides which lane a session may open, `/d/:token` verification re-checks the role claim, `dashboard` in WhatsApp resolves the caller's lane and `dashboard admin` is the superadmin phrase. Additive only — the owner dashboard, every Phase 14 route and the flag behaviour are unchanged. `DASHBOARD_ENABLED` still gates every surface (all five new URLs answer the generic 404 while off).

**Decisions locked.**
- **D1 — driver eligibility is a live assignment at mint time.** `requestDashboardAccess({ role: 'driver' })` skips the plan gate (a driver is an employee, not a payer) and requires at least one live `vehicles.assigned_driver_id` row; nothing found answers `no_assignment` with exactly *"You need to be assigned to a vehicle to access the driver dashboard. Ask your fleet owner to assign you."* The same check runs again at verify, so a withdrawn assignment kills an already-minted token.
- **D2 — admin isolation is a 404.** `/d/admin*` answers **404** to any non-admin session (owner or driver), so the surface's existence is never confirmed; the owner lane answers **403** to driver/admin sessions and the driver lane answers **403** to everyone else. Refused attempts write no audit row (nothing was viewed). Anonymous requests are 401 before any role check.
- **D3 — the driver sees their OWN numbers.** `buildDriverComplianceCard({ mask: false })` is used only by the driver's own pages (home + compliance); the WhatsApp card, reports and the owner's driver page keep the mask (the owner page already shows unmasked numbers by Phase 14C's D1).

**Schema (additive, rule 56).** `dashboard_sessions.session_role text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'owner'` — old rows default to the owner lane with no backfill, and `getSessionByToken` normalises anything unknown to `owner`. `DASHBOARD_SQL` adds it with `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (so a pre-1.76.0 table is upgraded by the existing boot ensure), `scripts/provision_staging_schema.js` carries it in the CREATE + ALTER, and `npm run migrate:dashboard-role` (`scripts/run_dashboard_role_migration.js`) applies it idempotently.

**Identity single-sourcing (rule 55).** The env superadmin check moved to `src/services/superadminIdentity.js` (`isSuperadminPhone`, `isSuperadminEmail`, zero dependencies); `superadmin.js` re-exports both so every existing importer is untouched, and the dashboard imports the neutral module instead of pulling the Sentinel worker graph.

**Role resolution (one rule, owner-first).** `resolveDashboardRole()` mirrors `resolveReportAccess`: `admin > owner > driver`, proven by a single `vehicles` read over `owner_id` OR `assigned_driver_id` (live rows only). A dual-role profile lands in the OWNER lane, exactly like the WhatsApp `dashboard` lane. It never throws and degrades to `owner` on a database error.

**Driver lane.** `buildDriverHome` (assigned vehicle + own compliance summary + last 7 days), `buildDriverDaybookPageData` (the full `buildDriverDaybook` engine, 14 days) and `buildDriverSelfCompliancePage` (own documents, unmasked). Every input is `driverId = session.ownerId` — never a vehicle id — so cross-driver reads are structurally impossible; the daybook keeps its existing `driver_id` + own-vehicle-ids filter. Renderers: `renderDriverHomePage`, `renderDriverDaybookPage`, `renderDriverSelfCompliancePage`, driver nav `Overview · Daybook · Compliance · Log out`, no owner-only links.

**Superadmin lane.** `buildAdminOwnersList` lists every profile with ≥1 live vehicle (counts + active counts, phones masked, name/visible-digit search, deterministic sort) and `buildAdminFleetView` reuses `buildOverviewCard` + `buildVehiclesIndex` + `buildComplianceBoard` against the target owner id — read-only, no write path in the module. Every `/d/admin*` GET writes `ADMIN_DASHBOARD_VIEW` to `admin_audit_logs` via `logAdminAudit` (page `owners` with the search, or `fleet` with `ownerViewed` + `found`), including a not-found view.

**WhatsApp lane.** `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_RE` (`dashboard admin` / `open my dashboard admin`) is checked first and carries the marker `'admin'`; a non-superadmin gets the verbatim A2 line without the service being called (no row, no email, no hint). Otherwise `resolveDashboardRole` picks `driver` vs `owner`, the request passes `role`, and the reply names the lane (`Your dashboard link…` / `driver dashboard` / `admin dashboard`). `no_assignment` → the D1 copy; `not_admin` → the A2 line.

**Rule 51 sibling sweep.**
| Class | Siblings audited | Result |
|---|---|---|
| i — a role claim trusted without a second check | mint AND verify both re-check (admin phone, driver assignment) | pinned: revoked assignment → `no_assignment`; non-superadmin row → `not_admin`; nothing stamped |
| ii — a scope inherited from another lane | driver pages read `driverId = session.ownerId`; admin pages read the TARGET owner id | pinned: own documents only; foreign driver's `FX-999` absent |
| iii — a cross-tenant read without audit | both `/d/admin` routes (list + fleet, including not-found) | pinned: `ADMIN_DASHBOARD_VIEW` rows with `page`, `ownerViewed`, `found` |
| iv — surface existence leaked via error | `/d/admin*` → 404; refused attempts audited by nobody | pinned: owner/driver 404, body never says "owners" |
| v — session role drift | unknown role → `owner`; legacy rows → `owner`; admin never enters the owner lane | pinned: legacy session = owner lane, 403 on driver pages, `db_reset_scope` pins the schema |

**Rule 52 deep audit — findings.** (1) `buildDriverComplianceCard` had no mask switch — the additive `mask = true` parameter keeps every existing caller masked. (2) `requestDashboardAccess` gated on entitlements for every caller; the gate is now owner-only, which is what makes a Free-plan driver possible without weakening the owner paywall (pinned both ways). (3) `resolveDashboardRole` returns early on a stubbed client (`typeof supabase.from !== 'function'`) instead of throwing — fixtures stay quiet and a real DB error still degrades to `owner`. (4) `requireOwnerSession` was renamed to `requireRoleSession(role)` and all 15 owner call sites pass `'owner'` explicitly, so a future lane can never inherit the owner gate by accident.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (`DASHBOARD_SQL` + `DASHBOARD_ROLES`, `session_role` in mint/verify/session, `resolveDashboardRole`, `hasLiveDriverAssignment`, driver + admin builders §10, five renderers, navs), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (`requireRoleSession`, 15 owner call sites, 5 new routes, `logAdminAudit`), `src/services/driverReports.js` (`mask` parameter), `src/services/readCommands.js` (admin phrase + role resolution + `no_assignment`), `src/services/superadminIdentity.js` (new), `src/services/superadmin.js` (re-export), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `scripts/provision_staging_schema.js`, `scripts/run_dashboard_role_migration.js` (new), `package.json` (1.76.0 + `migrate:dashboard-role`), `test_dashboard.js` (+85: 504 → 589), `test_read_registry.js` (+11: 201 → 212), `test_db_reset_scope.js` (+4: 90 → 94), `landing/data/changelog.json`, `docs/`, this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** Baseline: test_dashboard (504), test_read_registry (201), test_db_reset_scope (90), test_agent_training (200) — green. After: **test_dashboard (589)**, **test_read_registry (212)**, **test_db_reset_scope (94)**, test_agent_training (200), test_doc_sync, `npm run health` — green. Zero pre-existing assertions edited.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Defect class "two surfaces resolve a role differently"* → one resolver (`resolveDashboardRole`) feeds the WhatsApp lane and its owner-first order matches `resolveReportAccess`; *"a token minted under one role reused under another"* → the role is stamped at mint AND re-checked at verify; *"a cross-tenant page reachable by URL"* → the admin lane 404s non-admins and audits every accepted view.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/45, 3/4, 7 (country from the phone via `detectCountryFromPhone`), 8 (no VIN/plate changes), 10/11 (stateless suites, targeted runs), 12/33, 13/60 (playbook + core prompt + training assertions), 18 (no autonomous path touched; one additive column, no other DDL), 31 (warm plain copy, one next step), 42 (PROP-2026-11-08-01 remains the only open proposal, unrelated), 50 (slim profile fallback in the admin fleet view, fail-soft audit), 51/52 (five pin classes + findings), 54 (real suite runs), 55 (reused the overview/vehicles/compliance/daybook/compliance-card engines; extracted one identity module instead of duplicating it), 56 (defaults keep existing sessions and rows working), 58 (this report). **No rule was edited or added.** Phase 15 is complete; Phase 16 is next.

### 205. v1.77.0 (Phase 16) — monthly PDF summary + dashboard-first reports (2026-11-08)

**Scope.** Two goals, one release: (1) an opt-in MONTHLY PDF summary emailed on the 1st of each month at 08:00 EAT; (2) the legacy WhatsApp PDF path leaned out — the "building your report…" ACK, the background `fleet_report` job and the on-demand report email are gone, replaced by an instant dashboard-first reply with an optional inline PDF.

**Decisions locked.**
- **D1 — the async report flow is retired.** `handleReportRequestTurn` answers instantly; `followUpAckText`, `queueReportFollowUp`, `runFleetReport`, `resolveReportPdfLinkDelayMs`, the `FLEET_REPORT` kind and its recovery copy are deleted. The follow-up LANE survives for `driver_unassigned` only (the table, the worker tick and `migrate:followups` are untouched).
- **D2 — inline fast PDF under a budget.** `REPORT_INLINE_BUILD_MS` (default 4000, clamped 0–8000; 0 = dashboard link only) races `buildInlineReportLink()` (build → render → upload → shorten). On success the reply carries `📄 *PDF report:* <link>` and quota + `REPORT_GENERATED` activation are recorded; on a miss the dashboard link is the complete answer and nothing is recorded. The retired knob was `REPORT_PDF_LINK_DELAY_MS`.
- **D3 — vehicle summary keeps its email.** `deliverReportPdf` is unchanged in behaviour (it now calls the extracted `renderReportPdfBuffer`), and `vehicleSummary`'s explicit "vehicle summary pdf" ask still emails.
- **D4 — the monthly gate.** `isMonthlyReportWindow()` = Nairobi day-of-month 1, 08:00–08:05, claim-first marker `monthlyreports.last_sent_date` (new `CONFIG_KEY_MONTHLY_REPORTS_LAST_SENT`, owner `monthlyReports`, not boot-critical). `runMonthlyReportsSweep()` batches 200 opted-in owners, requires an email and ≥1 ACTIVE vehicle, builds the previous Nairobi calendar month (`buildCustomReport` + `bounds`), renders a Buffer (`renderReportPdfBuffer`) and emails it. **No WhatsApp message, no quota, no activation** (weekly precedent, rule 26).
- **D5 — the opt-in column.** `profiles.monthly_report_opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` — migration `npm run migrate:monthly-reports` (idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) + the staging schema CREATE/ALTER. The dashboard Settings page gained a **Monthly PDF summary** toggle with its own `action=save_monthly` marker (each toggle writes ONLY its own column); rule 50 degrades honestly when the column is missing.
- **D6 — WhatsApp symmetry.** `monthly report on|off` + a bare `monthly report` state read mirror the weekly toggle (a pre-read write lane, zero tokens, anchored so a report request is never swallowed).
- **D7 — the email.** `sendMonthlyReportEmail()` in `mailer.js` — Resend attachment (native Buffer), `reports@reports.sakafleet.com`, filename `saka-monthly-<Month_Year>.pdf`, warm plain copy, never throws (`false` = honest failure).

**The monthly period is engine-owned.** `previousMonthBounds(now)` derives the previous Nairobi calendar month with `+03:00` ISO bounds and a fixed English label, then `buildCustomReport` runs with `bounds` (the Phase 14D override) and the six financial metrics (`total_spend, earnings, net_profit, fuel_spend, fuel_litres, distance`). The rendered PDF is re-titled `Monthly Financial Summary` with the month as `periodLabel` — the dashboard can never drift from the email because both ride the same engine.

















**Rule 51 sibling sweep.**
| Class | Siblings audited | Result |
|---|---|---|
| i — a phrase claimed by a report-request lane | `monthly report on|off` and bare `monthly report` are anchored BEFORE the intent; "send me the monthly report pdf" never matches | pinned |
| ii — a dead surface after a feature retires | `pending_followups` rows of the retired kind are failed honestly, never sent; the driver-unassigned lane still delivers | pinned |
| iii — a budget that silently drops the PDF | a budget miss answers the dashboard link and records NOTHING (no phantom quota, no phantom activation) | pinned |
| iv — a schema column nobody migrated | the sweep returns `column-missing`, RELEASES the marker (no month burned) and logs the exact `npm run migrate` line | pinned |
| v — a double-send window | claim-first marker + replay no-op + per-owner fail-soft | pinned (replay + event order) |

**Rule 52 deep audit — findings.** (1) `dashboardBaseUrl()` already ends in `/d`, so the lane builds `${dashboardBaseUrl()}/reports` (the first draft produced `/d/d/reports`; the new suite pins it). (2) `recordReportUsage` was referenced by the new lane but no longer imported — the pinned quota assertion caught it before ship. (3) The brief asked for the column in `DASHBOARD_SQL`; that DDL owns `dashboard_sessions`, so the profiles column lives in the profiles migration + provisioning (documented correction). (4) `reset-db.js` needed no change (`profiles` is already in the wipe scope); `test_db_reset_scope` now pins all three schema carriers instead.

### 206. v1.78.0 (Phase 17) — conversational superadmin, deploy-live activation, legacy profile backfill (2026-11-08)

**Scope.** Three operator-approved tasks in one release (D1/D2/D3 locked): (1) make the superadmin reachable in plain language through an engine-owned Admin AI Agent; (2) turn the deploy-live template finding into an executable operator runbook; (3) backfill the legacy profile context columns with a NULL-only, audited reconcile.

**D1 — deploy notifications.** The push-time "building" alert (`scripts/notify_git_push.js`, `deploy_notify.yml`) stays free-form by design. The boot LIVE alert was already template-wired (`index.js` boot → `announceRevisionLive` → `sendMetaWhatsAppMessage(..., 'deploy_live')` → `resolveProactiveMode` → `sendWhatsAppTemplateMessage`), but a live audit of Cloud Run (`gcloud run services describe saka-fleet --region=europe-west1`) found **zero `META_TPL_*` variables**, so it degraded to free-form text and Meta silently dropped it outside the 24h window (§87.3). `docs/TEMPLATES.md` §3.1 now carries the exact activation runbook: create `saka_deploy_live` (Utility, en, static body "Saka update is LIVE. The new revision is now answering WhatsApp conversations."), await APPROVED, then `gcloud run services update saka-fleet --region=europe-west1 --update-env-vars="META_TPL_DEPLOY_LIVE=saka_deploy_live"`, verify `npm run env:audit` + `npm run health`, rollback = unset the knob. No code change was required — the fix is operator-side and documented where the contract lives.

**D2 — the Admin AI Agent (`processAdminMessage`).** Previously `handleSuperadminFlow` claimed only explicit directives; everything else from the superadmin phone got the static role hub (`admin.js`), and admin-looking misses got `buildAdminClarifyReply`. Now a superadmin-phone message that parses to `UNKNOWN` (admin-looking or not) runs the same 30-minute session gate and then `processAdminMessage(supabase, phone, text, { generate, healthCheck })`:

1. `admin_tool_call` (new purpose, Tier 1, jsonMode, 256 tokens) chooses exactly ONE tool from the frozen `ADMIN_AGENT_TOOLS` registry — `get_system_health`, `get_ai_usage(hours 1-168)`, `get_open_proposals` — or `none`. The prompt is generated from the registry (a registry entry without a prompt line is impossible) and forbids answering the question itself.
2. The engine executes the tool with the existing deterministic handlers: `collectHealthFacts()` (extracted from `handleHealthCheckCommand`, now shared so "check health" and the agent can never drift), `handleAiStatsCommand()` (the zero-token digest), `handleAdminRemediationsList(supabase, 'pending')`.
3. `admin_synthesis` (new purpose, Tier 1, 700 tokens) words the reply from the FACTS block only — every number/status is copied verbatim (rule 28); the prompt forbids invention and action claims.

Degrades: no tool → the existing clarify; tool failure → its deterministic reply (`formatAiStatsReply` text, health fallback lines); synthesis failure → the same deterministic reply; provider failure → clarify. Audits: `ADMIN_AI_TOOL` (tool, ok, hours, error) + `ADMIN_AI_AGENT` (text slice, tool, reply_chars, fallback) per turn; the old `ADMIN_CLARIFY` action is superseded. Static commands are untouched and pinned as zero-token (`admin ai-stats` never calls the model). Inactive session → "type adminstart", zero tokens. Non-superadmin phone → `{ isSuperadmin: false }` before any of this. `handleSuperadminFlow` gained an optional 4th `options` argument (injectable `generate`/`healthCheck`) so the whole flow is testable offline; every existing 3-arg caller is untouched. New help line under Snapshots: "just ask" with the plain-English example.

**D3 — legacy profile backfill.** Live `information_schema.columns` + `count(*) FILTER (WHERE ... IS NULL)` (read-only, via the existing Management-API transport) on `public.profiles` (60 columns, 3 rows): `weekly_report_opt_in`, `monthly_report_opt_in`, `launch_opt_in`, `country_source`, `country`, `country_code`, `unit_system`, `preferred_language`, `email_verified`, `is_active`, `jurisdiction_confirmed` = 0 NULLs (Postgres backfills `NOT NULL DEFAULT` on ALTER); `timezone`, `timezone_confirmed_at`, `currency`, `locale` = 3/3 NULL; `trial_used_at` = 2/3 NULL (correct = never used a trial). New `scripts/reconcile_profiles.js` + `npm run reconcile:profiles [-- --dry-run] [-- --limit=N]`: `buildProfileContextPatch()` patches ONLY null columns, resolving defaults from `REGIONS` + `resolveTimezoneFromCountry` (the same data the app uses); an explicit `country_code` (possibly `country_source='user'`) wins over phone detection; `timezone_confirmed_at` and `trial_used_at` are never written (a backfilled zone is a default, not a confirmation); every change audits `PROFILE_CONTEXT_RECONCILED` with a masked phone and before/after (the before-snapshot is taken BEFORE the update). Idempotent: a second run patches nothing. No DDL was needed — every column already exists live.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/aiClient.js` (2 purposes + front set), `src/services/superadmin.js` (`collectHealthFacts` extraction, `ADMIN_AGENT_TOOLS`, `clampAdminAgentHours`, `buildAdminToolPrompt`, `classifyAdminToolRequest`, `buildAdminSynthesisPrompt`, `executeAdminAgentTool`, `processAdminMessage`, flow seam + `options`, help line, `AI_USAGE_MAX_WINDOW_HOURS` import), `scripts/reconcile_profiles.js` (new), `scripts/health_audit.js` (+2 suites), `docs/TEMPLATES.md` (§3.1), `package.json` (1.78.0 + `reconcile:profiles`), `test_admin_agent.js` (new, 40), `test_profile_backfill.js` (new, 26), `test_phase6_purpose_tiers.js` (+7: 50 → 57), `README.md`, this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 207. v1.78.1 (Phase 17.5 hotfix) — deploy_live template carries version + commit/revision (2026-11-08)

**Why.** Phase 18 (Voice Notes) stayed on hold for this hotfix. The operator updated the approved `saka_deploy_live` template in Meta to a two-variable body — `🚀 Saka is LIVE!`, then `{{1}}`, then `{{2}}`, then "The new revision is now answering WhatsApp conversations." — but the registry still declared `deploy_live` as a static body (`variables: []`), so the template could never carry the release identity the free-form text already shows.

**Change (one seam, no new machinery).** `PROACTIVE_TEMPLATE_KINDS.deploy_live.variables = ['version', 'commit']` (`src/services/proactiveTemplates.js`). `announceRevisionLive()` builds `templateVars = { version: 'v<version>', commit: <revision> }`, passes it as the SECOND argument to the injected `send(text, templateVars)` and returns it in the result object (`src/services/deployLiveAlert.js`). The `index.js` boot hook forwards it: `send: (text, templateVars) => sendMetaWhatsAppMessage(SUPERADMIN_PHONE, text, 'deploy_live', templateVars)`. Version still comes from `readReleaseVersion()` (the architecture file, D2); the commit is `K_REVISION || COMMIT_SHA || RENDER_GIT_COMMIT`, the same value that dedupes `deploy.last_deployed_revision`.

**Degrade (rule 50).** An `unknown` version (architecture-file read failed) passes `''`, so `templateVariablesForKind` returns null and `resolveProactiveMode` falls back to `{ mode: 'text' }` — the template never fires with a broken parameter. Knob unset = byte-identical free-form text (unchanged). A live template whose approved placeholder count still differs also fails the Meta send and falls through to the text path.

**Suites run.** `test_proactive_templates.js` (52), `test_notifications.js` (22), `test_doc_sync.js`, `npm run health` — green.
