### 208. v1.79.0 (Phase 18) — voice notes: Speech-to-Text, injected as typed text (2026-11-08)

**Why.** Since v1.61.15 a WhatsApp voice note got one deterministic line — *"🎙️ I can't listen to voice notes yet — type it in…"* — because `resolveMediaEnvelope` treated audio as `isVoiceNote` and returned before the pipeline. That protected the turn from an empty `messageText`, but it turned away the most natural input on WhatsApp: a driver speaking a fuel stop. Phase 18 transcribes the audio and injects the transcript where a typed message goes, so **every** existing lane works by voice with zero new intents.

**Verified against the live tree and Google's docs (rule 54).** Sync `speech:recognize` is limited by Google to **60 seconds / 10 MB** (cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/sync-recognize), so the "2 minutes" plan was corrected to a **55 s** cap — longer notes keep the deterministic fallback instead of a 400. Audio payload is base64 in `audio.content`; WhatsApp voice notes are OGG/OPUS.

**A. `src/services/sttService.js` (new, 208 lines).** `transcribeAudioBuffer({ buffer, countryCode, mimeType, apiKey })` posts to `GCP_SPEECH_ENDPOINT` (default `https://speech.googleapis.com/v1/speech:recognize`) with `?key=` (the same `GCP_VISION_API_KEY` project key, or `GCP_SPEECH_API_KEY`). Body: `config { encoding (OGG_OPUS for ogg, MP3, FLAC, WEBM_OPUS, LINEAR16, AMR…; omitted when unknown so the API auto-detects), languageCode, alternativeLanguageCodes, enableAutomaticPunctuation: true }`, `audio { content: <base64> }`. Multi-result transcripts are joined with a space; `confidence` (first finite) and the detected `languageCode` come back. Never throws; timeouts retry once (`STT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`), HTTP/credential errors never retry, an empty result returns the explicit `No speech detected in the voice note`, a paused switch returns `skipped: true` with no network call. Helpers: `resolveSpeechLanguage` (**KE → sw-KE + en-KE/en-US; everyone else → en-US + sw-KE** — D3), `resolveSpeechEncoding`, `estimateAudioDurationSeconds(bytes, bitrate)` and `isAudioWithinDurationLimit` (16 kbps opus estimate).

**B. `media.js` (leaf contract intact).** `VOICE_LISTENING_ACK` (*"🎙️ Listening to your voice note — one moment…"*, D5 — data only, the processor sends), `prepareVoiceAck` (null while STT is paused) and `startAudioTranscription` (M15): reuses `downloadWhatsAppMedia` (same 5 MB cap, `User-Agent: curl/8.0.0`, never throws), rejects notes over the estimated duration, calls the STT service, and writes exactly ONE `ocr_requests` row — `provider='google_speech'`, `document_kind='voice_note'`, status `read | low_confidence | failed | paused | too_long`, attempts + latency + error (D4; no DDL, the table already exists). Returns data; media.js still never sends.

**C. Processor wiring (`messages.js`, four seams, zero new lanes).** (1) `resolveMediaEnvelope` already exposed `audioObj`; the v1.61.15 early-return is replaced by the **unverified gate first** (`resolveMediaGate`, D2 — fail-closed, no download/STT spend for a non-user), status `unverified_gated_media`. (2) The deterministic **listening ack** sends before the work starts (same post-ACK pattern as OCR, v1.22.0). (3) `startAudioTranscription` runs inside the SAME `Promise.all` as `startMediaOcr` + `loadTurnSnapshot`, so a voice turn pays one round trip. (4) The transcript joins the existing seam: `const messageText = voiceTranscript || (interactiveReply ? interactiveReply.text : mediaTurnText)` — every downstream lane (admin gates, clear-chat, pending lanes, quiz, reads, AI) sees exactly what the user would have typed. **A voice answer to a quiz works by construction** (`handleQuizTurn({ messageText })` parses it like typed text; proven in `test_quiz_flow` Test 4d), and the instant/slow acks are suppressed on voice turns so the user never gets two progress lines.

**D. Degrade + privacy (rule 50).** Any failure — paused switch, missing key, oversize, over-duration, HTTP/timeout, silence — sends the SAME `VOICE_NOTE_REPLY` line with the SAME `voice_note_fallback` status and the `[voice note]` transcript marker (byte-identical to v1.61.15) and logs ONE rolled-up `logSystemError` under `/webhook/whatsapp/voice` carrying only the failure reason/status/attempts — never user content. Audio bytes are never stored; only the `ocr_requests` metadata row survives.

**E. Knobs (envAudit `OCR & VISION` + `.env.example`).**

| Env var | Purpose | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `STT_ENABLED` | Voice-note transcription kill switch (`off\|false\|0` pauses → fallback line) | `on` |
| `GCP_SPEECH_API_KEY` | Dedicated Speech key (optional; falls back to `GCP_VISION_API_KEY`) | — |
| `GCP_SPEECH_ENDPOINT` | Override the Speech endpoint | `https://speech.googleapis.com/v1/speech:recognize` |
| `STT_TIMEOUT_MS` | Speech request budget | `25000` |
| `STT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | Attempts; abort/timeout retried, HTTP errors never | `2` (clamped 1–3) |
| `STT_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` | Sync-API duration cap (Google caps at 60 s) | `55` (clamped 5–60) |
| `STT_ESTIMATED_BITRATE` | Opus bitrate for the size→duration estimate | `16000` |

**Operator prerequisite.** Enable **Cloud Speech-to-Text API** in the same GCP project as Vision and allow it on `GCP_VISION_API_KEY`'s API restrictions (or set `GCP_SPEECH_API_KEY`). Documented in `README.md` and `.env.example`. **Live probe (2026-11-08, rule 54):** the current `GCP_VISION_API_KEY` answers `403 API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED` (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, consumer `projects/377676898502`) for `speech.googleapis.com` — the key is restricted to Vision, so the feature is **dormant in production** until the operator unblocks the Speech API on that key or sets `GCP_SPEECH_API_KEY`. Meanwhile every voice note degrades honestly to the fallback line and logs a rolled-up reason — no crash, no dead turn.

**Rule 13 statement.** No new intent and no new flow: the transcript reuses the LIVE grammar, so `flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js` and the `conversationEngine.js` composer are unchanged and `test_agent_training` stays green untouched.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/sttService.js` (new, 208), `src/routes/whatsapp/media.js` (imports, `VOICE_LISTENING_ACK`, `prepareVoiceAck`, `startAudioTranscription` — 337 → 484 lines), `src/routes/whatsapp/messages.js` (voice gate, combined ack, 3-way `Promise.all`, transcript/fallback seam, ack-suppression guards), `src/services/envAudit.js` (+7 keys, +1 secret), `.env.example` (+STT block), `README.md` (operator note), `scripts/health_audit.js` (+1 stateless suite), `test_stt_service.js` (new, 26 assertions), `test_quiz_flow.js` (+3), `test_env_audit.js` (+15), `test_no_canned_replies.js` (+1), `package.json` (1.79.0), `landing/data/changelog.json` (+ stamped assets), `docs/` (regenerated), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 209. v1.80.0 (Phase 19) — Amina (autonomous care agent) + fleet analytics (2026-11-08)

**Program context.** Phase 19 ships two surfaces the business runs on. (1) **Customer care stops being a queue** and becomes an investigation: every inbound email at `support@reports.sakafleet.com` is triaged by **Amina** — she reads the customer's profile, vehicles, recent system errors, recent WhatsApp chat and billing mirror, then either answers correctly or hands a fully-investigated case to a human. (2) The Owner Dashboard gains **`/d/analytics`**: tyre wear from the latest Tyres expense odometer plus a six-month cost-per-km trend, and the superadmin gains **`/d/care`**, the escalated queue with Amina's investigation log and drafts. Decisions locked with the operator: D1 `CARE_AI_ENABLED` **off** by default, D2 escalation inbox `support@sakafleet.com`, D3 tyre lifespan 50,000 km / Replace Soon at 40,000 km (both env-tunable), D4 server-rendered inline SVG (zero new dependencies).

**A. Amina's pipeline (`src/services/careAi.js`, `processCareEmail`).** The hook fires inside `handleInboundEmail()` right after `openOrAppendEmailTicket()` returns — one choke point for every inbound email, injectable for the suites and defaulting to the real agent. Order of operations, all engine-owned:
1. **Kill switch / ownership gate.** `CARE_AI_ENABLED` off (default) → `{ action:'disabled' }` with ZERO model calls; an `ESCALATED`/human-owned ticket → `{ action:'skipped' }` (Amina never answers for a human).
2. **Zero-token pre-gate (`carePreGate`).** Money/dispute text (`refund`, `charged twice`, `paystack`, `invoice`, `billing`, `dispute`…), legal/account actions (`delete my account`, `gdpr`, `lawyer`, `hacked`…), `priority=high` and the existing `shouldEscalateCare` keywords go **straight to a human without spending a token** (rule 28). The escalation names `pre-gate: <reason>`.
3. **Investigation loop (`runCareInvestigation`).** Up to **3 tool rounds** (`CARE_AI_MAX_INVESTIGATION_LOOPS`). Each round calls `chatCompletion({ purpose:'care_investigation', jsonMode:true })`; the model replies with ONE JSON shape: `{ "tool","args" }`, `{ "action":"reply","reply","confidence","reason" }` or `{ "action":"escalate","reason","confidence" }`. The ENGINE executes the tool, appends `TOOL RESULT <tool>: <json>` and loops. An unparseable reply is re-asked once per round; an undecided loop escalates with `investigation loop limit reached` — never a guessed answer.
4. **Resolve.** Only when `action='reply'` AND `confidence >= CARE_AI_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR` (0.7): `sendCareReplyEmail` → thread message (`out`/`email`) → status `RESOLVED` + `ai_draft` + note → audit `CARE_TICKET_AI_RESOLVED`. A failed send escalates instead (`reply email could not be sent`) — the draft is never silently dropped.
5. **Escalate.** Status `ESCALATED`, priority `high`, `ai_draft` = best draft (labelled unsent), one `internal`/`ai` thread message PER investigation step (the audit trail `/d/care` renders), a forward via `sendCareEscalationEmail` whose subject starts with the `[SFC-<shortid>]` tag, and `escalateCareToSuperadmin` (WhatsApp + email). Audit `CARE_TICKET_AI_ESCALATED` with the tools, reason and forward/alert booleans.
6. **Failure.** A provider/mail/ping crash escalates with the failure reason (the human path), audits `CARE_TICKET_AI_ESCALATED`, and never throws into the webhook. The generic care-worker ping is **suppressed** when the ticket was resolved or escalated (no double alerts).

**Amina's system prompt (rendered by `buildCareInvestigationPrompt`, verbatim excerpt).**
> You are Amina, the autonomous customer-care agent for Saka Fleet. … Reply ONLY with JSON — exactly one of these shapes: `{ "tool": "<tool name>", "args": { ... } }` / `{ "action": "reply", "reply": …, "confidence": 0.0-1.0 }` / `{ "action": "escalate", "reason": …, "confidence": 0.0-1.0 }` … **INVESTIGATION DIRECTIVE (absolute)** — A first-instinct answer is NOT enough. If the email mentions a broken flow, a missing record, a wrong number, a stuck quiz or a failed action, you MUST investigate first … Before you escalate, you must be able to state: "I checked X, Y and Z; I am still stuck on C." … Escalate ONLY when: (a) the issue involves money, refunds, legal, safety or an account/data action; (b) after investigating, your confidence is below 0.7; or (c) the fix needs a human … Never invent numbers, dates, prices, refunds, tiers, ticket states or policy … Never ask for a PIN, OTP, password or card number … Sign as "Amina, Saka Care". … Remember: you are the last line before a human. Exhaust every tool before you escalate.

The prompt renders the deterministic **FAQ knowledge base** (`careKnowledge.js` — logging, drivers, dashboard, reminders, receipts, reports, subscription, support, voice; every line a shipped behaviour, rules 13/31) and the **newest 10 learned rules** (`formatCareLearnings`).

**B. The four investigation tools (engine-executed, read-only, never throw).** `get_profile_context(email)` → profile (`*` select — the rule-50 drift class), plan/trial, vehicles (plate/model/status/odometer); `get_recent_errors(phone)` → last 5 `error_logs` whose message mentions the number (`ilike %digits%`); `get_recent_chat(phone)` → last 10 `chat_history` rows, chronological, labelled user/saka; `get_payment_status(email)` → the local billing mirror (`subscriptions` + matching `paystack_webhook_events` + `profiles.subscription_*`) labelled `Read-only mirror. Refunds, reversals and disputes are human-owned.` Every tool returns an honest empty result rather than an invented one; an unknown tool name is refused back to the model.

**C. The learning loop (`src/services/careLearning.js`).** Human replies are the training data:
- `careTicketTag(id)` → `[SFC-<8-char prefix>]`; the escalation subject always carries it.
- `routeCareInternalReply()` recognises a tagged subject from the exact `sakafleet.com` domain (a subdomain like `reports.sakafleet.com` is NOT the human inbox), resolves the ticket, appends the reply as an `internal`/`email` message, sets `IN_PROGRESS` + `assigned_to`, audits `CARE_TICKET_HUMAN_REPLY`, and runs `extractCareLesson`.
- `extractCareLesson()` calls `chatCompletion({ purpose:'care_learning', jsonMode:true })` with `{customer_email, subject, customer_message, human_reply}` and the strict prompt: ONE reusable rule, **no names/phones/emails/card numbers/OTPs**, **no prices or refund outcomes** (billing stays human-owned), empty lesson when there is no rule. `sanitizeCareLesson` scrubs emails → `[email]`, `+\d{7,15}` → `[phone]`, long digit runs → `[number]`, collapses whitespace, caps at 500 chars. Stored in `care_learnings` (`ticket_id, trigger_context, lesson, created_at`) + audit `CARE_TICKET_LEARNED`.
- `getRecentCareLearnings(10)` feeds the next investigation prompt — a missing table degrades to `[]` (rule 50). Lessons are PROMPT text only: they can never change code, schema, prices or permissions (rules 16/18).

**D. Schema + migration (`npm run migrate:care-ai`, idempotent).** `ALTER TABLE support_tickets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ai_draft text;` (Amina's best draft survives an escalation) and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS care_learnings (id uuid PK, ticket_id uuid, trigger_context text, lesson text, created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now())` + `idx_care_learnings_created`. Statuses gain **`ESCALATED`** (`CARE_STATUS`); `updateCareTicket`'s whitelist gains `ai_draft`. Every write degrades without the migration: `updateTicketSafe` retries without `ai_draft`, and lesson reads return `[]`.

**E. Reopen + threading semantics (rule 51 sweep).** `findOpenTicketByThread` now matches OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/**ESCALATED**/**RESOLVED**/**CLOSED** inside `CARE_THREAD_WINDOW_HOURS` (168 h). `openOrAppendEmailTicket` returns `{ reopened, humanOwned }`: a follow-up on a RESOLVED/CLOSED ticket **reopens the SAME ticket** (`status='OPEN'`) instead of opening a duplicate; a follow-up on an ESCALATED ticket appends but stays human-owned (Amina never re-answers). `listCareTickets('open')`/`high` include ESCALATED, `care inbox escalated` filters precisely, `careStats` counts it, and `formatCareTicket` shows `🚨 ESCALATED` + Amina's draft. The webhook's legacy `handleInboundSupportEmail` self-relay is **skipped** when Amina handled the mail (`result.ai.handled`) or the mail was a human internal reply — nobody receives their own text back.

**F. `/d/care` (superadmin, audited) — `buildCareQueue` + `renderCareQueuePage`.** Loads the ESCALATED/OPEN/IN_PROGRESS tickets, their threads, the `internal`/`ai` investigation messages and the newest 10 lessons; renders KPI counts, each escalated ticket's **Investigation log**, Amina's **unsent draft**, the console reply hint, and the **Lessons learned** list. `requireRoleSession('admin')` (owner/driver → 404), every view audited as `ADMIN_DASHBOARD_VIEW { page:'care', escalated }`. Queried directly in `dashboard.js` (never through `careConsole.js`) to keep the Sentinel worker graph out of the dashboard — the Phase 15 `superadminIdentity` precedent.

**G. `/d/analytics` (owner) — tyre wear + cost-per-km.**
- **Tyre wear (`buildTyreWearRows`).** Per live vehicle: the newest `Tyres` expense (`isTyreExpenseType` accepts exactly Tyre/Tyres/tire/tires — a "tyre repair kit" never resets the clock) with `odometer_reading > 0`; `kmSince = (vehicles.current_mileage ?? odometer_reading) − lastTyreOdometer`; `remainingPct = clamp(1 − kmSince / TYRE_LIFESPAN_KM)`; **Replace Soon** at `kmSince >= TYRE_REPLACE_SOON_KM`. Honest states: no Tyres row → `no_data`; no current odometer → `kmSince:null`; a rollback → clamps to 0 with a note. Imperial owners see miles; the percentage is unit-independent. Spec example pinned: 120,000 − 95,000 = **25,000 km → 50% remaining** on a 50,000 km set.
- **Cost-per-km trend (`buildCostPerKmTrend`).** Six monthly buckets (UTC month windows, the reports' `monthStartMs`), spend = every `expense_logs` amount in the bucket, distance = the SAME **`distanceInWindow`** engine every report uses (`fleetReports.js`, now exported; `distanceThisMonth` delegates to it — zero formula drift). `costPerKm = spend ÷ distance` or **null** when a month had no odometer movement. Totals, six-month average and peak ride the result.
- **Rendering (D4).** `buildCostPerKmChart` computes pure SVG geometry; `renderAnalyticsPage` emits an inline `<svg>` (grid, polyline, points with `<title>` tooltips, month labels) plus tyre cards with progress bars. Zero JS, zero new dependencies; every label escaped; failed loads render one honest 503 explanation.

**H. Knobs (envAudit `EMAIL` / `ANALYTICS` + `.env.example`).**

| Env var | Purpose | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CARE_AI_ENABLED` | Amina kill switch (`on\|true\|1` enables; anything else keeps the human path byte-identical) | `off` |
| `CARE_ESCALATION_EMAIL` | The human inbox Amina forwards unresolvable tickets to | `support@sakafleet.com` |
| `CARE_AI_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR` | Minimum confidence before Amina replies herself (clamped 0–1) | `0.7` |
| `TYRE_LIFESPAN_KM` | Assumed tyre-set lifespan for the progress bar | `50000` |
| `TYRE_REPLACE_SOON_KM` | "Replace Soon" threshold (clamped to the lifespan) | `40000` |

**I. AI purposes (rule 20).** `care_triage`, `care_investigation` and `care_learning` join `AI_PURPOSES` as **background/system** purposes (Tier 1 router, JSON mode) — deliberately NOT in `USER_FACING_PURPOSES`, so they ride DeepSeek and can never be escalated to the front tier. The model only PICKS a tool or DRAFTS text; every fact, status write, send and audit is engine-owned.

## 210. Phase 20 — Operational tools (v1.81.0): durable receipt→expense link + CSV bulk import

**Scope.** The last phase of the original roadmap ships two operational tools and nothing else: (1) `expense_logs.receipt_id` — the durable link between an OCR receipt and the expense its confirmation quiz wrote (PROP-2026-11-08-01), and (2) `GET/POST /d/import` — a CSV bulk import for historical expenses. No new intent, no new quiz flow, no AI purpose, no new dependency.

### 210.1 Task 1 — the durable link (PROP-2026-11-08-01)

**Schema (`npm run migrate:receipt-links`, idempotent).** `ALTER TABLE public.expense_logs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS receipt_id uuid REFERENCES public.receipts(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;` plus `idx_expense_logs_receipt`. **`ON DELETE SET NULL` is mandatory**: users may remove a receipt at any time (`delete receipt N`, rule 48) and that must never orphan or block the ledger row. `scripts/provision_staging_schema.js` now also provisions `public.receipts` (it never did) so the FK has a target on a fresh target schema.

**Where the id used to be lost.** `resolveReceiptVault()` discarded `recordReceipt()`'s returned row (`media.js`: `await recordReceipt(...)`, no assignment) and returned only `{ duplicateReceipt, logbookPrefill }`. The engine-only `prefill` seam already existed (the logbook precedent), it was simply never populated for receipts.

**The thread (D2 — prefill carries the FK).** `recordReceipt()` → `{ receipt }` → `receiptPrefill = { receipt_id }` (receipt branches only, never logbooks/insurance) → `messages.js` destructures and passes `receiptPrefill` → `arbitrateQuizTurn({ receiptPrefill })` → `quiz.js` starts the quiz with `prefill: receiptPrefill` (only when `!session.quiz && receiptQuizStart === 'log_expense' && !forcedNarrativeFlow`) → `startQuiz()` seeds `answers` verbatim. `applyExtraction`/`applyTextExtraction` iterate `def.fields`, so `receipt_id` is never asked, never rendered and **never AI-injectable**; `restart` drops it (fresh draft, no stale link).

**The write + the ownership guard (sibling sweep class i).** `case 'log_expense'` calls `resolveReceiptLink(ctx, { receiptId, vehicleId })`: UUID-shape check → one `receipts` read → link only when `receipt.owner_id === profile.id || receipt.driver_id === profile.id || receipt.vehicle_id === vehicle.id`; otherwise `null`. Never throws (rule 50). The row carries `receipt_id: linkedReceiptId` (explicit null when absent). **Rule-50 degrade:** the existing label-missing retry is followed by a second retry that drops `receipt_id` too, so an un-migrated column still saves the expense.

**The dashboard (exact link wins; D1 fallback stays).** `attachReceiptMatches()` collects every `raw.receipt_id` on the page and resolves them with **ONE** `.in('id', …)` query → `receiptStatus: 'linked'`; rows without the FK keep the unchanged unique-match heuristic (`'unique' | 'ambiguous' | 'none'`). A linked id whose receipt vanished degrades to the fallback. `renderRecordsPage` shows the View link for `linked` and `unique` identically. After the backfill proves coverage the fallback can be removed in a future phase — deliberately kept until then.

**The backfill (D4 — dry-run by default).** `scripts/backfill_receipt_links.js` (`npm run backfill:receipt-links [-- --apply]`): probes the column (a pre-migration run is told to migrate, never "0 rows"), loads every already-linked receipt id (1:1 enforcement), snapshots unlinked rows (bounded page reads — a read/write interleave could loop forever on unlinkable rows), matches each through the SAME `matchReceiptForExpense()` + `nairobiDateOf()`, accepts unique-only matches whose receipt is still unused, updates individually, and audits one `admin_audit_logs` row `RECEIPT_LINK_BACKFILLED` per run (mode + counts). Idempotent: only `receipt_id IS NULL` rows are ever read.

### 210.2 Task 2 — CSV bulk import (`/d/import`)

**No new dependency (D3).** The upload path is a file picker + `FileReader` + the page's own form post; the server accepts either an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` `csv` field (raised body limit `CSV_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES + 64 KB`) or a raw `text/csv` body through a scoped `addContentTypeParser`. **No `@fastify/multipart`, no CSV package** (pinned by the suite).

**The engine (`src/services/csvImport.js`, pure + testable).**
- `parseCsv()` — hand-rolled RFC-4180-lite: BOM strip, CRLF/LF, quoted fields with embedded commas/newlines and `""` escapes, case-insensitive header aliases (`Date|logged date`, `Vehicle Plate|plate|vehicle_plate|vehicle`, `Type|expense_type|category`, `Amount|cost|total`, `Odometer|mileage|reading`, `Notes|description|details`), required-column report, byte/row caps, file line numbers on every row.
- `validateImportRows()` — plates resolve against the owner's live vehicles in memory (unknown plate = error, which also enforces owner scope and vehicle capacity by construction); types canonicalise through `resolveExpenseType()` (the single catalog); amounts positive ≤ 100 M; odometer optional whole number; dates through **`dateParser.parseFlexibleDate`** (country-aware, rule 7) stored at Nairobi noon as UTC; future dates refused; notes ≤ 500 chars; in-file duplicates and the **3-hour DB duplicate** (the existing pure `isSameExpenseCandidate`, so a different odometer reading is a separate fill) flagged. **Two DB reads total for the whole file** (vehicles + one recent-expenses slice), never one query per row.
- `bulkInsertImportRows()` — chunked `.insert` (≤ 200), row shape identical to the quiz write (`driver_id` = the acting owner profile, `fuel_liters: 0`, `fill_type: null`, `created_at` from the row date, **no receipt link invented**), legacy `expenses` mirror behind `LEGACY_EXPENSES_WRITE_ENABLED`, per-vehicle odometer advanced to the highest imported reading only, **`markUserDataChanged({ reason: 'dashboard.csvImport' })` ONCE**, audited `CSV_IMPORT`. Rule 26 (v1.77.0): **no activation API is imported or called — an import can never start or extend a trial** (source pin in the suite). No report quota is touched.

**The two-phase flow (never trusts the browser).** Phase A `POST /d/import` → parse + validate → preview page (valid count, highlighted invalid rows with engine copy, raw text re-embedded). Phase B `POST /d/import/confirm` → requires `action=confirm`, **re-runs the exact same parse + validation on the submitted text** (a tampered hidden field can only fail), refuses when zero rows are valid, inserts the valid rows, `303 /d/import?imported=N`. Cross-origin writes refused before anything else (the settings precedent), 10/5-min rate limit on both POSTs, owner role only, honest 502 with the exact count when a chunk is refused.

**Knobs (envAudit `SERVER` + `.env.example`).** `CSV_IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` (500, clamped 1–2000), `CSV_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` (1048576). Nav gains **Import**; `.row-error` CSS highlights invalid rows.

**Rule 13 statement.** `flowKnowledge.js` log_expense `writes` names the durable link; `SAKA_WEB_DASHBOARD_PLAYBOOK` documents the Import page (columns, validation, no trial activation) and the durable-link rule; `sakaAi.js` core prompt scope line names the CSV expense Import page; `test_agent_training` +3 (205 → 208). No new intent/flow key.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/csvImport.js` (new), `src/services/quizEngine.js` (`resolveReceiptLink` + the write path + default export), `src/services/dashboard.js` (linked attach, View rule, `renderImportPage`, nav, CSS, import), `src/routes/whatsapp/media.js` (`receiptPrefill`), `src/routes/whatsapp/messages.js` (threading), `src/routes/whatsapp/quiz.js` (prefill branch), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (parser + 3 routes), `src/services/envAudit.js`, `.env.example`, `scripts/run_receipt_links_migration.js` (new), `scripts/backfill_receipt_links.js` (new), `scripts/provision_staging_schema.js`, `scripts/health_audit.js` (+suite), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `test_csv_import.js` (new, 70), `test_quiz_flow.js` (160 → 165), `test_ocr_flow.js` (129 → 132), `test_dashboard.js` (644 → 672), `test_agent_training.js` (205 → 208), `package.json` (1.81.0 + `migrate:receipt-links` + `backfill:receipt-links`), `landing/data/changelog.json`, `docs/`, this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_csv_import (new, 70), test_quiz_flow (165), test_ocr_flow (132), test_dashboard (672), test_agent_training (208), test_entry_ledger, test_record_answers, test_expense_catalog, test_user_context_cache, test_error_logging, test_doc_sync, test_no_canned_replies, `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) a foreign receipt could link to an expense* → `resolveReceiptLink` ownership guard + a pinned foreign-receipt scenario. *(ii) a deleted receipt could orphan/crash an expense* → `ON DELETE SET NULL` (a `delete receipt N` hard delete leaves the ledger row intact; pinned by the FK definition + the receipt-delete suite unchanged). *(iii) a re-uploaded/duplicate CSV could double-log* → in-file duplicate key + the 3-hour `isSameExpenseCandidate` guard + row/byte caps that refuse rather than truncate. *(iv) an import could trigger trial activation* → the module imports no activation API (source pin) and the bulk path has no activation call site. *(v) cost-per-km drift* → already swept in Phase 19; import writes only `expense_logs`/`expenses`/odometer. Deliberately left: the WhatsApp quick-log lane has no receipt context by construction (media receipts always route through the quiz), so it needs no link code.

### 211. v1.82.0 (Phase 21) — new rules, the ghost-profile fix, and WhatsApp-native dashboard sign-in (2026-11-08)

#### 211A. Rules 62 + 63 (additive, rule 58)

`.clinerules` gains **rule 62** (default to full operator capability — use every available connection/tool/integration; execute pending operator actions autonomously) and **rule 63** (query pending remediations and proposals before every operation; audit the proposed change, then offer/execute). No existing rule was edited or removed (rule 58 additive policy). Both are cross-references to rules 42/54, not replacements.

#### 211B. The +254734852529 ghost — live audit, purge, and an accurate profiles report

**Live audit (read-only probes).** One live `profiles` row: id `a9f9f690-9cd2-48c6-a274-ca645c63d78b`, `phone_number '+254734852529'`, `deleted_at NULL`, `full_name NULL`, `email NULL`, `email_verified false`, created `2026-11-08T10:20:07Z` by a first-contact "Dashboard" message. Referencing rows: 4 `chat_history`, 4 `chat_transcripts`, 2 `processed_webhooks`, 1 `chat_sessions`, 0 `user_context_cache`/`usage_counters`/`web_onboard_otps`/`dashboard_sessions`, and **18** `conversation_analytics` synthesis blobs whose `insights` mention the number. **The earlier wipe never completed** — `admin_audit_logs` contains no `ADMIN_PROFILE_WIPED` row for the number, only `CONV_EVAL_HEALED` prompts (10:29–10:36Z) asking the superadmin to confirm.

**Purge (`scripts/purge_ghost_profile.js`, new).** Dry-run by default; `--apply` hard-deletes the shell profile and the chat-family rows by `phoneVariants()` (E.164 / bare / 9-digit tail), **redacts** the number inside `conversation_analytics.insights` instead of deleting 18 synthesis snapshots that also describe other conversations, audits `GHOST_PROFILE_PURGED` (before / removed / after / verified / errors) and re-counts every table. Run result: profiles 1→0, chat_history 4→0, chat_transcripts 4→0, processed_webhooks 2→0, chat_sessions 1→0, conversation_analytics mentions 18→0, every other table already 0 — **PURGE VERIFIED**.

**`handleProfilesReportCommand` (superadmin.js).** Registered = `email IS NOT NULL` OR the superadmin's own row (the superadmin profile legitimately has no email); shells = `email IS NULL AND full_name IS NULL` (and not the superadmin) rendered on their own `Unverified Shell Profiles` line; named rows without email (owner-created driver profiles) ride `details.named_no_email`; `signups_24h/7d` and Recent sign-ups count registered profiles only; a profiles read failure answers ONE honest line instead of fake zeros (rule 50). `test_superadmin` gains a mock block pinning all four definitions (ghost excluded from totals and Recent). Live after: **2 registered / 0 shells**, Recent = Brenda + Superadmin only.

**v1.96.4 — the registered-vs-owners gap is named (the 6 vs 2 briefing discrepancy).** The report now splits the registered total explicitly: `Owners with Vehicles` (registered profiles that appear as `owner_id` on ≥1 live vehicle) and `Registered Without Vehicles` (the rest), so the arithmetic is answered on the page. Recent sign-ups still list every registered profile and append `[no vehicle yet]` to any that owns no live vehicle (they are labelled, never dropped). `details` gains `owners_with_vehicles` / `without_vehicles`; the legacy `active_vehicle_owners` key is preserved for audit continuity. The same split is printed by `handleAdminReportCommand` (08:00 briefing) and `buildCommandCenterMetrics` — see §236.

#### 211C. WhatsApp-native dashboard sign-in (D1–D5)

**D1 — strict 15-minute session.** `DASHBOARD_SESSION_TTL_MS` 30 days → **15 min**, so `dashboardSessionMaxAgeSeconds()` = 900 and the cookie is `saka_dash=<64 hex>; Path=/d; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=900; Secure` (Secure omitted on localhost). No sliding renewal: one write per sign-in, the prune sweep owns expiry.

**D2 — the lanes ship a STATIC link.** `dashboard` / `my dashboard` / `open my dashboard` / `web dashboard` **and the new `records` / `my records` alias** reply with `https://app.sakafleet.com/d/login` plus a 3-line tutorial (open → enter the WhatsApp number → type the 6-digit code I send here; in for 15 minutes). No DB write, no email, zero tokens. `dashboard admin` (exact phrase + `SUPERADMIN_PHONE`) replies with `/d/admin/login`; anyone else gets the verbatim A2 line. The Phase 16 report lane keeps its instant-PDF answer and now **appends the same sign-in link + tutorial** (the `/d/reports` deep link needs the session). Lane order was proven: dashboard sits before `ledger_turn`/`records_query`, and their own turns ("my entries", keyword searches) are pinned un-hijacked.


**D3 — honest refusals.** The login page answers inline: no account → "No account found for this number — sign up first at sakafleet.com"; Free owner → the trial/paid + *pricing* line; cooldown → "I just sent a code"; a failed WhatsApp send → one honest retry line. Shell profiles (no email, no name) are refused before any OTP is minted (the ghost class can never sign in).

**D4 — the admin door is separate.** `GET/POST /d/admin/login` renders the superadmin entrance and only ever mints `session_role='admin'` for the `SUPERADMIN_PHONE` number (checked at mint AND re-checked at verify). `POST /d/login` resolves the lane server-side (`role:'auto'`, admin > owner > driver) but **refuses the admin number** (`use_admin_login`) — `/d/login` can never mint an admin session. `POST /d/verify` now redirects each role to ITS home (`/d/admin`, `/d/driver`, `/d`) — previously every session landed on `/d`, so an admin session immediately hit a 403.

**D5 — the email magic link is retired but not deleted.** `requestDashboardAccess` became **`requestDashboardOtp({ phone, role, profile, entitlements, sendOtp })`**: profile lookup by phone variants, ghost guard, admin-door-first check, owner entitlement gate (the `email_verified` gate is gone — the WhatsApp number is the verified channel), driver live-assignment gate, 60-second per-owner cooldown, then a `dashboard_sessions` row (unchanged table, nullable `email`, `session_role`, 15-min flow window, 10-min OTP) and ONE WhatsApp text carrying the code. A failed send deletes the row (`otp_send_failed`), exactly like the old `email_failed`. Audit `DASHBOARD_OTP_SENT`. `verifyDashboardOtp` keeps every mechanic (sha256 at rest, constant-time compare, attempts cap 5, single-use burn, role re-check at verify) and now returns the role. `sendDashboardMagicLinkEmail` stays in `mailer.js` **deprecated and uncalled**.

**One transport (rule 55).** `src/services/metaMessenger.js` (new) owns `sendWhatsAppText()` — the exact free-form path extracted from `sendProactiveWhatsApp` (env guard, recipient cleaning, delivery blocklist, never-throws). `sentinel.js` delegates its text leg to it (template routing untouched), so the worker and the sign-in OTP cannot drift.


**Routes.** `GET/POST /d/login` + `GET/POST /d/admin/login` (flag-gated like every `/d` route, rate-limited 10/5 min, cross-origin writes refused); `POST /d/verify` (role-aware 303, masked-phone OTP page); `GET /d/:token` stays for pre-1.82 links; `requireRoleSession` 401 copy no longer promises an email; `accountLabel()` renders the masked WhatsApp number on every signed-in page when the email is null (email is now optional). `registerDashboardRoutes` accepts an injectable `requestOtp` seam for suites (production uses the service).

**Renderers.** `renderLoginPage({ admin })` (phone entry → inline OTP step; never mentions email); `renderOtpPage` now says "Check your WhatsApp" with the masked number (accepts `emailMasked` for legacy callers); `renderLogoutPage` teaches the new door. `dashboardOtpReasonCopy` carries the new reasons (`otp_send_failed`, `no_account`, `bad_phone`, `use_admin_login`, `not_entitled`, `cooldown`).

**Skill sync (rule 13/60).** `SAKA_WEB_DASHBOARD_PLAYBOOK` rewritten (static link, WhatsApp code, 15-minute session, email link retired, owner/driver/admin doors); `FLOW_GUIDANCE.dashboard` updated; `sakaAi.js` `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT` WEB DASHBOARD line updated; `test_agent_training` 209 (five assertions rewritten, not deleted).

**Frames touched.** `.clinerules` (+62/63), `scripts/purge_ghost_profile.js` (new), `src/services/superadmin.js` (profiles report), `src/services/metaMessenger.js` (new), `src/workers/sentinel.js` (text leg delegates), `src/services/dashboard.js` (requestDashboardOtp, getLinkState, TTL, copy, renderLoginPage/renderOtpPage/renderLogoutPage, dashboardLoginUrl/AdminLoginUrl, maskPhone export), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (login doors, role-aware 303, 401 copy, accountLabel, requestOtp seam), `src/services/readCommands.js` (static-link lane + records alias + admin door), `src/routes/whatsapp/commands.js` (report lane appends the tutorial), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `test_dashboard.js` (696), `test_read_registry.js` (206), `test_superadmin.js` (+8 mock assertions), `test_agent_training.js` (209), `test_report_lane.js` (34, +2), `package.json` (1.82.0), `landing/data/changelog.json`, `docs/`, this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.


**Suites run.** test_dashboard (696), test_read_registry (206), test_superadmin (green, exit 0), test_agent_training (209), test_report_lane (34), test_sentinel_policy (30), test_no_canned_replies (15 — ratchet still 4), test_db_reset_scope, test_doc_sync, `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect classes swept: *(i) a count query blind to auto-provisioned shells* → registered/shell/named-no-email definitions + mock pins. *(ii) a wipe believed done but never audited* → the purge script audits `GHOST_PROFILE_PURGED` and re-counts every table. *(iii) an auth channel change leaving email promises behind* → 401 copies, logout page, OTP page, reason map, report lane and both prompt blocks swept; tests assert the sign-in page and lane copy never mention email. *(iv) an admin session landing on an owner page* → role-aware 303 pinned for all three roles. *(v) nullable email breaking "Signed in as"* → `accountLabel()` falls back to the masked number. *(vi) guard ordering* → the admin door is checked before the ghost guard (the test caught a non-admin receiving `no_account`). *(vii) a new alias hijacking neighbour lanes* → dashboard sits before `ledger_turn`/`records_query`; their turns are asserted un-hijacked. *(viii) helper collision* → dashboard already had a local `maskPhone`; the email-style import was dropped so exactly ONE masking function exists per module. Deliberately left: `index.js`'s reply sender keeps its own fetch path (documented sibling, unchanged blast radius), and the deprecated mailer function stays one deprecation cycle.

### 212. v1.83.0 (Phase 22) — premium dashboard branding, passbook transfer & subscription pages

Phase 22 finishes the dashboard's commercial surface: it looks like the brand, hands a passbook over without leaving the web, and sells/manages the plan with engine-owned figures only. Locked decisions: **D1** one allowlisted asset route (no base64, no new dependency), **D2** Sora attempted with a Barlow fallback (revised live — see below), **D3** the transfer machine's steps 1-3 on the web, buyer stays on WhatsApp, **D4** engine checkouts + an optional `callbackUrl` (default unchanged), **D5** Add Vehicle = a `wa.me` "add car" deep link.

#### 212.1 Branding (D1)

- **`GET /d/assets/:file`** (inside the dashboard plugin, flag-gated 404): a STRICT filename allowlist (`Sora-600/700.woff2`, `Manrope-400/500/700.woff2`, `logo-lockup.png`, `favicon.svg`, `favicon-32.png`) builds the filesystem path from the TABLE, never from the request — traversal is impossible by construction. Serves `font/woff2` / `image/png` / `image/svg+xml` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a 240/5-min rate limit. Every URL is stamped `?v=` `DASHBOARD_ASSET_VERSION` (`1.83.0`) so a release busts the CDN.
- **`DASHBOARD_CSS`** now declares the five `@font-face` blocks (Sora 600/700 display, Manrope 400/500/700 body) and the Monolith tokens: `--accent:#B8EF5C`, `--accent-dark:#65A30D`, `--accent-soft/-line`, `--font-display`, `--font-body` and one `--glow` token (`0 0 0 1px var(--accent-line), 0 0 18px rgba(184,239,92,.16)`). The orange `#FF7A00` accent is retired. Focused inputs, hovered/focused buttons and active/focus-within cards all take the glow ring; buttons are a lime gradient with near-black ink.
- **Phone-first CSS:** `@media (max-width: 640px)` wraps the header + nav, raises buttons to 48 px and secondary actions to 44 px, sets 16 px controls (no iOS zoom) and two-column KPIs; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables transitions. `renderPageShell` renders the real `logo-lockup.png` (intrinsic 9.86:1, 177x18) with `alt="Saka Fleet"`, the SVG/PNG favicons and `theme-color #0A0A0C`; `noindex` stays.

#### 212.2 PDF polish (D2, revised by the live audit)

- `SAKA_PDF_THEME.brand` is now the **text-safe lime `#65A30D`** (AA on white) with `lime:#B8EF5C` kept for decorative fills only; fleet/financial/deep-dive/portfolio/default accents follow the brand and `status.info` retires teal.
- **Sora via WOFF2 does not survive PDFKit.** A live probe registered `Sora-600.woff2` fine and rendered page 1, but the SECOND document in the same process threw `Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView` from fontkit's WOFF2 subsetting (caught by `test_dashboard` — a filtered records PDF 500'd). `registerReportFonts` therefore NEVER loads woff2: it tries a vendored **Sora TTF/OTF** first (`Sora-600.ttf`, `Sora-SemiBold.ttf`, `Sora-600.otf`) and otherwise keeps the vendored **Barlow SemiBold** — the guaranteed display face today. Manrope body + JetBrains Mono are unchanged.
- **`SAKA_PDF_GEOMETRY`** exports `{ pageWidth: 595.28, pageHeight: 841.89, margin: 48, contentWidth: 499.28 }` so the mobile-friendly A4 margins are a pinned contract, not a comment.

#### 212.3 Passbook transfer page (D3)

- **`/d/transfer`** (owner role, CSRF Origin guard, 10/5-min on the writes) renders: the owner's live vehicles, a start form (vehicle, buyer WhatsApp number, buyer email, OPTIONAL handover odometer), the in-flight transfers with plain-language status chips (buyer phone/email MASKED), cancel buttons, recent handovers and the 5-step explainer.
- **Steps 1-3 reuse `transfers.js` verbatim:** `POST /d/transfer/start` → `initiatePassbookTransfer({ fromPhone, vehicleCandidate })` (the existing in-flight guard + annual free-transfer quota + fee row all run) → `setBuyerDetailsAndSendReleaseOtp` (emails the 6-digit release PIN to the OWNER) → 303 `?started=1&pin=<id>`; `POST /d/transfer/verify` → `verifyOwnerReleaseOtpAndNotifyBuyer` (status + PIN + expiry checks; WhatsApps the BUYER "ACCEPT") → 303 `?verified=1`; `POST /d/transfer/cancel` → `status='CANCELLED'` (open statuses only, never a delete).
- **The buyer stays on WhatsApp (steps 4-5 untouched):** ACCEPT → `handleBuyerAcceptance` → buyer email OTP → `completePassbookTransfer`. The dashboard NEVER shows or accepts the buyer's code.
- **Honest gates:** a phone-only owner (no `profiles.email` and no `vehicles.owner_email`) sees "Add an email first" and BOTH the UI and the server refuse to start (never a stranded transfer — the PIN could not be delivered). Every transfer is ownership-checked before verify/cancel; a foreign id answers **404** (existence never confirmed). The optional odometer (≤ 10,000,000, positive) writes a labelled `odometer_readings` row via `recordLabeledReading` and never blocks the transfer.
- **`release_otp` / `buyer_otp` are never selected** by `loadOwnerTransfers` — pinned by the suite.

#### 212.4 Subscription page (D4 + D5)

- **`/d/subscription`** (owner role) renders from `getEntitlements` + `evaluateVehicleCapacity`: plan badge + status chip (ACTIVE / welcome trial / GRACE / CANCELING / PAST_DUE), billed interval, trial end + days left, current period end, a capacity bar (`currentCount of capacity`, add-ons included), report quota, Billing history (the owner-scoped `subscriptions` ledger + invoice events whose `payload.metadata.user_id` re-checks against the owner — a failed JSON-path read degrades to the ledger only) and the engine-fed next-tier prices.
- **Checkouts are engine-owned:** `POST /d/subscription/checkout` → `checkoutForTier({ targetTierKey, interval, currency, callbackUrl })`; `POST /d/subscription/addon` → `getEntitlements().addonEligible` gate → `checkoutForAddon({ addonQuantity, interval, currency, callbackUrl })`. Both 303 to the returned Paystack URL and REFUSE anything that is not `https://` (no open redirect). Currency resolves from the phone's country via `buildGlobalContext` (rule 7).
- **`callbackUrl` (the only engine change):** `initializePaystackCheckout` gained an optional `callbackUrl`; `callback_url` = `callbackUrl || PAYSTACK_CALLBACK_URL || https://sakafleet.com/payment-success`. Omitted callers (chat, dunning, trial nudges) behave byte-identically — pinned by `test_subscription_billing`. The dashboard passes `${PUBLIC_APP_URL}/d/subscription`; Paystack appends `reference`/`trxref`, and the page prints the reference with the honest "Paystack confirms payments in the background — this page updates the moment your plan does" line (never a fake success; rule 28).
- **Add Vehicle (D5):** at capacity the link is replaced by the upgrade form (next tier, monthly/annual engine prices) and/or the Fleet Command add-on form (engine unit price). Below capacity it is `https://wa.me/19404407252?text=add%20car` — registration stays in the WhatsApp quiz where `checkOwnerVehicleTierLimit` still gates the slot.
- **Nav** gains Transfer + Subscription on every owner page; the page states card changes / refunds / cancellations are chat-only.

#### 212.5 Skill sync, tests & audit (rules 13, 51, 52, 60)

- `SAKA_WEB_DASHBOARD_PLAYBOOK` is headed **v1.83.0** and states both new pages (owner steps 1-3, buyer consent on WhatsApp, PIN never shown, engine prices only, Add Vehicle = wa.me, no card/refund actions); `FLOW_GUIDANCE` gains `dashboard_transfer` + `dashboard_subscription`; `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT`'s WEB DASHBOARD line names both pages. `test_agent_training` 209 → **215** (two version pins rewritten, six new assertions). `docs:gen` regenerated the knowledge docs.
- **Seams (rule 55, offline suites):** `registerDashboardRoutes` accepts injectable `transferNotifier` (`sendReleaseOtp` / `verifyReleaseOtp`) and `checkoutEngine` (`tier` / `addon`); production defaults to the real email/WhatsApp senders and the real billing engine, so the suites never send an email or hit Paystack.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect classes swept: *(i) a "supported" font format that only fails on the second use* → woff2 banned from PDFs + a per-build assertion that no `.woff2` is ever registered; *(ii) a page heading rendering while its form is withheld* → the "Start a handover" heading now keys on `ownerEmailAvailable` (caught by test); *(iii) escaping vs raw copy in assertions* → every page copy assertion pins the escaped form (`&#39;`); *(iv) cross-owner id replay* → verify + cancel both ownership-check and 404; *(v) an engine URL used as a redirect* → HTTPS-only guard + pinned 502; *(vi) test fixtures that silently hit the network through FX* → the fixture uses a +1 number so `buildGlobalContext` resolves USD with zero fetch; *(vii) name collisions in the 2.4k-line suite* (`fleetMock`) → renamed `p22FleetMock`. ### 213. v1.84.0 (Phase 23) — document storage: the `documents` bucket, the `vehicle_documents` ledger, dashboard files & the delete lanes

Phase 23 closes the last document gap: compliance documents (logbook/registration certificate, insurance policy, inspection certificate, road licence/PSL) were OCR'd for their fields and then the FILE was thrown away, so an owner at a police stop or a buyer viewing the car had nothing to show. Now the original is kept in a PRIVATE `documents` bucket and listed everywhere the compliance ledger already is. Locked decisions: **D1** `media_id text UNIQUE` on the new table (receipts precedent — a re-upload or a Meta retry never mints a second copy), **D2** the Free tier stores a file-less row (`storage_path = null`, parsed data visible — the receipt-vault contract), **D3** driver documents stay OUT of scope (vehicle-only table, §40.2).

#### 213.1 Schema & bucket (D1, D2)

- **`public.vehicle_documents`** (`VEHICLE_DOCUMENTS_SQL` in `src/services/vehicleDocuments.js`, migration `npm run migrate:vehicle-documents`, boot ensure `ensureVehicleDocumentsTable`, both idempotent):
  `id uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, `vehicle_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.vehicles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `document_type text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'other'`, `storage_path text` (NULL on Free), `original_filename text`, `parsed_data jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb`, `compliance_id uuid` + guarded constraint `vehicle_documents_compliance_fk → public.vehicle_compliances(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, `media_id text UNIQUE`, `uploaded_by uuid`, `uploaded_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()`; indexes on `(vehicle_id, uploaded_at DESC)`, `(uploaded_by, uploaded_at DESC)` and `compliance_id`.
- **The link to compliance lives ON the document row** (`compliance_id`), exactly like `expense_logs.receipt_id`: one compliance row can be proven by many stored files across years, `vehicle_compliances` gains no `proof_url`, and deleting a file never mutates the ledger (`ON DELETE SET NULL`).
- **Bucket:** `DOCUMENTS_BUCKET` (default `documents`) is created **PRIVATE** by the operator (same prerequisite shape as `receipts`, v1.75.1). Object path `documents/<vehicle_id>/<uuid>.<ext>` (pdf/png/webp/heic/jpg); reads are always 300-second signed URLs, never public URLs.
- **Document types:** `logbook | insurance | inspection | ntsa_cert | pinkslip | road_license | other`, derived from the Document Lens family (`logbook→logbook`, `insurance→insurance`, `inspection→inspection`, `road_licence→road_license`). `COMPLIANCE_TYPE_BY_DOCUMENT_TYPE` maps a stored file to the ledger row it proves (`road_license→road_service_licence`, `pinkslip`/`ntsa_cert→inspection`, `logbook→registration`).

#### 213.2 The vault (`src/services/vehicleDocuments.js`)

- `vaultVehicleDocument({ supabase, vehicleId, profileId, buffer, mediaId, mimeType, originalFilename, parsedData, documentType, entitlements })` — dedupes on `media_id` first (and re-reads on a unique-violation race), uploads only when `entitlements.receiptVaultStorage !== false` (paid tiers + welcome trial), inserts the row, fires `markUserDataChanged`, and **never throws**. A row-insert failure removes the just-uploaded object (no orphan files).
- `listVehicleDocuments` (vehicle or fleet scope, newest first, capped), `deleteVehicleDocument` (row + bucket object + `VEHICLE_DOCUMENT_DELETED` audit; uploader OR fleet owner only), `linkDocumentToCompliance`, `findPendingDocument` (newest UNLINKED document that can prove a compliance type inside `DOCUMENT_LINK_WINDOW_HOURS`, default 24) and `linkSavedComplianceDocument` (explicit prefill id wins, deterministic vehicle+type match is the fallback, never throws).
- `formatVehicleDocumentsReply` is the deterministic `documents` list (📄 per row, plate + date, honest `parsed only (Free plan)` chip, `delete document N` footer) — zero AI tokens.

#### 213.3 Media intake (`src/routes/whatsapp/media.js`, leaf contract intact)

- `resolveReceiptVault()` gains the compliance-document branch: for the four vehicle families (never receipts, never driver licences) with downloaded bytes it vaults the original and returns `documentPrefill = { document_id, document_type }`. The bytes exist for images AND PDFs (`ocrWhatsAppMedia` already returns `buffer`), so no second download.
- `messages.js` remembers the id as `session.pendingVehicleDocument` (session memory) and passes `documentPrefill` through the SAME engine-only prefill seam as `receipt_id` (`arbitrateQuizTurn` → `quiz.js` → `startQuiz` answers) — never asked, never rendered, never AI-injectable.

#### 213.4 Compliance link at save time (rule 51 sweep — four sites)

Every `submitVehicleCompliance` caller now calls `linkSavedComplianceDocument` after a successful save: the paragraph path in `messages.js` (session prefill id), the pending-capture turn in `pending.js` (`documentId` threaded through `persistCapturedCompliance`), the typed correction in `complianceAnswers.js` (`applyComplianceCorrection` gained `documentId`), and the registration seeds in `quizEngine.js` (`a.document_id` from the prefill). Without an id, the newest matching UNLINKED file links; with no match nothing happens.

#### 213.5 Dashboard surface

- **`GET /d/vehicles/:id`** — `buildVehiclePage` attaches `storedDocuments` (best-effort, rule 50) and `renderVehiclePage` renders a **Stored files** section: 📄 label + original filename, upload date chip, `View` (`/d/documents/:id`) and a Delete button with a browser confirm; a Free row reads `parsed only (Free plan keeps the figures, not the file)`.
- **`GET /d/compliance`** — one `.in('vehicle_id', …)` count query adds `docCount`; the vehicle table gains a **Files** column linking to the vehicle page.
- **`GET /d/documents/:id`** — the receipt route copied exactly: owner session, the document's vehicle must be on the owner's fleet, `signDocumentUrl` (300 s) → 302 + `no-store`; foreign/missing/Free-without-file answer **404** and no signed URL is ever minted for a foreign row.
- **`POST /d/documents/:id/delete`** — Origin-guarded (same `isCrossOriginWrite` defence as `/d/settings`), ownership-checked through `deleteVehicleDocument`, audits `VEHICLE_DOCUMENT_DELETED`, 303 back to the vehicle page.
- `DASHBOARD_ASSET_VERSION` deliberately stays `1.83.0` (no CSS/asset change this release; the pinned Test 53 stamp keeps its meaning).

#### 213.6 WhatsApp lanes

- **`documents`** / **`my documents`** / **`vehicle documents`** / **`stored documents`** / **`document vault`** → the new `documents_list` read lane (registered AFTER `receipts_list`, `skipWhenLocked`, `skipWhenPendingCapture` — a pending compliance capture still owns the turn). `documents list`, `required documents`, `what documents can I send?` and `list all documents with expiry date` keep their existing lanes (pinned).
- **`delete document N`** (`1-5`, literal `DELETE` to confirm) → `parseDocumentDeleteCommand` + `handleDocumentDeleteTurn` in `commands.js`, dispatched inline exactly like `receipt_delete`; the confirm prompt shows the numbered list, the delete removes the file and keeps the compliance dates, and the audit is `VEHICLE_DOCUMENT_DELETED`.
- `FLOW_GUIDANCE.document_vault` (rule 60) is rendered into the core prompt AND available to the engine.

#### 213.7 Lifecycle carriers (rule 51/56)

`vehicle_documents` joined `RESET_TABLES` + the phone wipe SQL + the global TRUNCATE (`scripts/reset-db.js`), `testCleanup.js` (by vehicle AND uploader) and `wipeProfileForSignup` (`src/services/profileWipe.js` — rows + bucket objects, reported as `document_storage_objects`). The knobs (`DOCUMENTS_BUCKET`, `DOCUMENT_LINK_WINDOW_HOURS`) are documented in `.env.example`, and the boot ensure runs next to `ensureReceiptsTable`.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/vehicleDocuments.js` (new, 429 lines), `scripts/run_vehicle_documents_migration.js` (new), `src/routes/whatsapp/{media,messages,pending,quiz,commands}.js`, `src/services/{readCommands,complianceAnswers,quizEngine,dashboard,profileWipe,flowKnowledge,conversationEngine}.js`, `src/routes/dashboard.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `index.js`, `scripts/{reset-db,testCleanup,mockSupabase}.js`, `.env.example`, `package.json` (1.84.0 + `migrate:vehicle-documents`), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (new, 60), `test_dashboard.js` (816, +20), `test_ocr_flow.js` (138, +6), `test_read_registry.js` (224, +16), `test_profile_wipe.js` (15, +1), `test_db_reset_scope.js` (99, +1), `test_agent_training.js` (219, +4), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/`, this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

A third: *"a mock that cannot prove a storage delete"* → `mockSupabase` gained `storage.remove` (+ PostgREST `in.(a,b)` OR-group parsing), additive and pinned by the new suite.

### 214. v1.85.0 (Phase 24) — the final audit: asset-kind meter parity, global country fixes and the passbook fee in the buyer's currency

Phase 24 was a three-domain READ-ONLY audit (asset kinds × 6 flows, six lifecycles, 14 country buckets × 7 concerns) followed by ONE fix release. The audit found no P0 (no money leak, no data loss, no security hole); every gap below was verified against the live tree before it was fixed.

#### 214.1 What the audit found (the three matrices, condensed)

- **Asset kinds (8 × 6):** registration, PDF builders, the expense/reminder catalogs and the bespoke-report metric filter were kind-correct. The FAILs were all ONE defect class — *a hardcoded odometer on a surface that never asked the registry*: `fleetReports.vehicleDisplay()` returned `{odometer, distanceUnit}` for every kind, so `/d/vehicles` and `/d/vehicles/:id` printed "Odometer 0 km" for heavy equipment/machinery/generators/watercraft; `/d/analytics` showed tyre cards + cost-per-km for hours-led fleets; the driver handover/handback quiz asked for an odometer on a generator.
- **Lifecycles:** trial (1-event activation, T-3 fitted card, GRACE window, 45-day cap, launch 183d), subscription (PAST_DUE + 3-day grace, CANCELING to period end, Free downgrade pausing excess), driver (OTP gates, 1-to-1, compliance cancellation), account deletion (MFA OTP, soft delete, VIN ledger preserved) and the 15-minute dashboard session were structurally sound. Gaps: the passbook fee quoted a hardcoded KES for every buyer; `delete_account` left `chat_sessions` behind; non-road passbook messages printed "VIN: N/A".
- **Global (14 × 7):** currencies/timezones/compliance/language/units/STT/dates were correct for KE, TZ, UG, RW, NG, ZA, GB, US, AE, IN, AU and DEFAULT. **BE was missing from REGIONS entirely** (EUR/nl-BE/Europe/Brussels unreachable) and **CA was unreachable** (+1 resolves US; the KB, currency and timezone existed but nothing could select them). Driver onboarding also handed GB/CA/US/AE/IN/AU/BE an "operator card" instead of their real documents, and KE/DEFAULT insurance+inspection rules leaked onto generators/boats.


#### 214.2 The fixes (all in this release)

1. **Registry-driven meters everywhere.** `fleetReports.vehicleDisplay()` branches on `primaryMeterForAssetKind()` and returns `{meterLabel, meterId, meterValue, meterUnit}` (plus the legacy `odometer`/`distanceUnit` for road assets; `odometer: null` for hours-led). `vehicleSummary()` carries the meter, so `renderVehiclesPage`/`renderVehiclePage` render "Engine hours 1,240 h" and never "Odometer".
2. **Analytics is kind-aware.** `vehicleAnalytics.js` gains `parseHoursFromNotes` (the `Engine hours: N h` note written since v1.39.0), `hoursInWindow` (the `distanceInWindow` twin), `buildCostPerHourTrend`, `buildServiceIntervalRows` (active HOURS reminders with live readings) and `buildCostPerKmChart(trend, { valueKey })`. `buildTyreWearRows()` now filters hours-led assets OUT at the source. `buildAnalyticsPage()` splits road vs hours fleets (`hasRoad`/`hasHours`, reminders loaded best-effort for hours fleets) and `renderAnalyticsPage()` renders tyre wear + cost per km for road assets, service intervals + cost per operating hour for machines, and an honest empty state when neither exists.
3. **Passbook fee in the buyer's currency.** `formatTransferFeeLine({ currency, rate, locale })` (pure) renders "USD 3.00 (~NGN 4,500)" for local buyers and a clean "USD 3.00" for USD buyers; `handleBuyerAcceptance` resolves the buyer's country from their E.164 number via `detectCountryFromPhone` and the cached FX rate. No copy can hardcode KES again (pinned).
4. **Non-road passbook identity.** `transferIdentity()`/`identityText()` + `assetDisplayName()`: road assets show VIN, equipment shows Serial, and nothing prints "VIN: N/A". The welcome email's subject/rows follow the asset (`identityLabel`/`meterLabel`/`meterValue`/`meterUnit`) and say "Initial Engine Hours" for hours-led assets.
5. **Driver handover meter per kind.** `handoverMeterFields({ mode, ctx })` (quizEngine) swaps `odometer_at_assignment`/`odometer_at_release` for `hours_at_assignment`/`hours_at_release` when the selected asset is hours-led; `createDriverAssignment({ handoverHours })` stores `metadata.hours_at_assignment` on the vehicle and keeps `handover_odometer` null; the unassign completion writes `operating_hours` (+`hours_updated_at`) and NEVER `current_mileage`. The `/d/transfer` handover field is labelled "Handover reading (odometer or engine hours)" and routes hours-led values through `applyOperatingHours` (which also evaluates hours reminders).
6. **Canada + Belgium.** `globalization.js` gains `EXTRA_REGIONS` (CA: CAD, en-CA, metric; America/Toronto is already in `COUNTRY_TIMEZONES`) and `regionForCountryCode()`; BE (+32, EUR, nl-BE) joins REGIONS; `COUNTRY_TIMEZONES.BE = 'Europe/Brussels'`; `countryBucket.resolveCountryInput()` resolves "Canada"/"ca" through the extras (the +1 default stays US, rule 7: an explicit choice is stamped `country_source='user'`). `routes/dashboard.countryForProfile()` now prefers the stored `profiles.country_code`, `paystack.FALLBACK_EXCHANGE_RATES` gains CAD, `landing/data/countries.json` ships CA + BE (+CAD rate), the homepage bootstrap map knows both (plus Europe/Brussels and the Canadian timezones), and `vehicleCompliance` gains the Belgian catalog (version 2026.18.0).
7. **Country-correct driver documents.** `driverComplianceCatalog.js` gains `commercial_licence`, `driver_card`, `heavy_vehicle_permit`, `hrt_licence` and `white_card` with `PROFESSIONAL_DRIVER_ITEMS` (GB → CPC + driver card + operator card; BE → CPC + driver card; US/CA → commercial licence; AE/IN → heavy-vehicle permit; AU → HRT + white card; East Africa unchanged). `complianceCatalog.complianceCategory` maps the new types (licences vs permits).
8. **Road rules stay on roads.** COUNTRY_KB DEFAULT + KE `vehicle_insurance`/`vehicle_inspection` gained `assetKinds: [vehicle, motorcycle, truck, bus]`; hours-led assets get a lighter, optional `equipment_insurance` hint instead. (Other countries' insurance/inspection rules remain kind-unscoped — deferred, §214.6.)
9. **Records/import labels per kind.** `recordsMeterLabel(vehicles)` (Odometer / Engine hours / Reading), `attachMeterReadings(rows, vehicles)` (hours parsed from notes), `serializeRecordsCsv({ meterLabel })`, a dynamic import-preview label + help text, and `csvImport.bulkInsertImportRows` writes hours-led readings into the notes (`Engine hours: N h`), leaves `odometer_reading` null and advances `operating_hours` — never mileage.
10. **Account deletion clears the session snapshot.** `delete_account` now also deletes `chat_sessions` (no stale quiz/OTP state survives a closed account).

#### 214.3 Sibling sweeps (rule 51)

- *Class: hardcoded meter label.* Swept every dashboard/PDF/CSV surface: `vehicleDisplay` (fixed), vehicle list/detail KPI (fixed), analytics tyre cards + cost-per-km (fixed), records CSV header + import preview (fixed), the financial report per-vehicle `odometer` field and pdfEngine's ledger column (deliberately left — raw ledger data; the dashboard speaks the meter), fleet-status text lines "Distance this month"/"Operating hours logged" (left: both are shown, so neither is wrong — P3).
- *Class: hardcoded currency.* Swept transfers (fixed), trial cards (`ctx.currency` — already correct), the dashboard subscription page (engine currency — correct), monthly/weekly summaries (`data.currency` — correct), driver-compliance/public copy (no money). Only the transfer fee line was hardcoded.
- *Class: country missing from REGIONS.* Compared all 14 COUNTRY_KB bundles, the driver catalogs, `landing/data/countries.json` and REGIONS: BE added to REGIONS, CA to `EXTRA_REGIONS` (prefix collision) and both to the landing dataset + bootstrap map; every other bundle already resolved.

### 215. v1.86.0 (Phase 25 — FINAL FEATURE PHASE) — the PSV fix, meter-aware PDFs, a smart sign-in, the command center, document replacement and creative handover labels

Phase 25 was the last feature phase: nine items from the operator's brief, executed against the live tree with every root cause reproduced before the fix. Decisions locked up front: **D1** the KE PSV badge scopes TRUCK/HGV (Traffic Act Cap 403 defines a PSV as carrying passengers OR goods for hire), **D2** a renewed document soft-supersedes the previous one, **D3** the command center rides the existing 08:00 briefing (full on Mondays, no second scheduler), **D4** `GET /d/logout` becomes a 303 with a banner.

#### 215.1 The two bugs

1. **Trucks and buses were invisible to the compliance gate.** Both resolvers (`complianceCatalog.resolveBundledCatalog`, `vehicleCompliance.resolveVehicleComplianceCatalog`) filtered on a legacy token list, but every road asset stores `vehicles.asset_type` = ICE/EV/HYBRID — the canonical identity is `vehicles.asset_kind`. A Kenya truck or bus therefore never matched `PSV/BUS/MATATU/MINIBUS`, so the PSV badge was filtered out of the driver menu, out of `getDriverComplianceStatus` (the gate), and out of the quiz; the KE speed-limiter certificate was hidden on trucks for the same reason. **Fix:** ONE bridge in `countryBucket` — `COMPLIANCE_ASSET_TOKENS` (kind → the catalog's vocabulary), `complianceAssetTokens()` and `complianceAssetMatches()`; both resolvers accept `assetKind` and match through it (`includeAll` unchanged, legacy `{ assetType }` callers unchanged, cars deliberately NOT PSV-class). `assetKind` is now passed at every call site (`quizEngine` ×3, `driverAssignments` ×2, `routes/whatsapp/pending` ×2, `commands`, `messages` ×2, `complianceAnswers`, `getVehicleComplianceStatus`). Catalog content: `KE.psv_badge` gains `TRUCK`,`HGV`, `COMPLIANCE_CATALOG_VERSION` → **2026.10.2** (vehicle catalog stays 2026.18.0 — its content did not change).
2. **PDFs printed "Odometer" for hours-led assets.** `pdfEngine.LEDGER_COLUMNS*` hardcoded the label; `reportDelivery`'s vehicle snapshot and distance KPI assumed an odometer; the v1.85.0 admin fleet table was a missed sibling. **Fix:** `reportLedger.buildLedgerGroups({ meterLabel, meterId })` carries the meter; `fleetReports.ledgerMeterFor(vehicles)` decides it (single asset → its meter; all-hours → `Engine hours`; all-road → `Odometer`; mixed → the honest `Reading`) and the builders expose `meter`/`assignmentMeter`; `pdfEngine.buildLedgerColumns({ showVehicle, meterLabel })` renames the column; `reportDelivery` switches the KPI to **Operating hours** for an hours scope and the snapshot to the asset's own label; `renderAdminFleetPage` prints `meterLabel`/`meterValue`.

### 216. v1.87.0 (Phase 26A) — launch award copy: the live "30-day trial" bug (2026-11-09)

**The report.** A new sign-up said the product showed "a 30-day trial" while the launch campaign promises six months. The audit reproduced the flow against the live tree and the live database before changing anything (rule 44).

**Live evidence (rule 54).** `launch_awards` slot 1 = owner `9cfb5f77…` (+254734852529, david.njonjo@gmail.com), coupon `LAUNCH183-1`, days 183; its `trial_sessions` row is `EXTENDED` with `ends_at = 2027-05-11T03:14:36Z` — **the engine was correct**. The `chat_transcripts` rows showed the actual defect: the pre-confirm card said *"a 30-day trial ledger entry is created once per VIN for life"* and the post-save card read *"🎁 Free trial: 183 days, until 9 Dec 2026"* — a 183-day label with the **pre-award 30-day end date**. Hypotheses (a)-(f) from the brief were all disproven: `LAUNCH_AWARD_ENABLED` is unset (default on), 49 of 50 slots were free, `TRIAL_MAX_TOTAL_DAYS` never clamped the award (`extendAccountTrial({ maxTotalDays })` is the only path past 45 and it worked), and no `profiles.trial_ends_at` column exists (the UI reads `trial_sessions`).

**Root causes.** (1) `quizEngine.confirmationNotesBase('vehicle_registration')` carried a pre-v1.16.0 sentence that contradicts rule 29 — `vin_registry` has been a provenance ledger (`trial_granted=false`) since v1.16.0. (2) The completion reply passed `welcomeTrial.endsAt` (captured BEFORE `grantLaunchAwardForTrial` extends the trial) as `trialEndsAt` while `trialDays` already reflected the award — two contradictory facts in one card. (3) The T+7 activation nudge hardcoded "Your 30-day trial is running" for every account.

**The fix.** New pure helper `resolveTrialCompletionFacts({ welcomeTrial, award, liveTrialEndsAt })` in `launchAwards.js` is the ONE decision: an extension that just landed → the grant's end date + day count; a repeat grant → the live `trial_sessions.ends_at` the caller re-read; a grant with no readable live end → the grant's day count and **no date** (never a stale one); no grant, or a grant whose extension failed → the welcome-trial facts and **no award line**. `quizEngine` uses it, appends `formatLaunchAwardLine` only when the fact holds (`trialFacts.awardConfirmed`), and degrades per rule 50. `activationNudgeText(ownerName, tierLabel, trial)` computes the day label from `started_at`/`ends_at`. The confirm card now reads *"Your account gets one welcome trial — it starts with your first vehicle."* and the delete-confirm bullet drops the stale "trial ledger" wording.

**Rule 13 sync (same commit).** `productQa` pricing facts gain the launch line (the generated `docs/PRODUCT_QA.md` was regenerated), `careKnowledge` subscription KB names the 6-month launch award, `flowKnowledge` `subscription_upgrade.writes` and the `sakaAi` UPGRADE_SUBSCRIPTION rule speak the engine-owned welcome trial, `subscriptionSchema` comments corrected, and architecture §2.3 + §18.3 now describe `vin_registry` as a VIN provenance ledger (the asset-bound trial retired in v1.16.0).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/launchAwards.js` (`resolveTrialCompletionFacts` + export), `src/services/quizEngine.js` (import, confirm card, delete-confirm bullet, completion block), `src/services/trialEngine.js` (`activationNudgeText` + call site), `src/routes/whatsapp/messages.js` (delete-confirm copy), `src/services/productQa.js`, `src/services/careKnowledge.js`, `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `src/db/subscriptionSchema.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `docs/` (regenerated), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§2.3, §18.3, this section, history, version), `CHANGELOG.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `package.json` (1.87.0), `test_launch_award.js` (+6), `test_quiz_flow.js` (+4), `test_trial_engine.js` (+2).

One targeted assertion per sibling.


### 217. v1.87.1 (Phase 26B) — OTP + invite template routing (2026-11-09)

**Why.** Meta accepts a free-form business-initiated message outside the 24-hour customer-service window and silently drops it. `/d/login` minted its 6-digit code as a plain text (`sendWhatsAppText`), so a returning user could request a code, be told it was sent, and never receive it. The same exposure covered two invitations Saka sends to people who had often never messaged Saka: a newly assigned driver (ACCEPT) and a passbook buyer (ACCEPT/DECLINE).

**What shipped.** Three new kinds in `proactiveTemplates.js` — `auth_otp` (`META_TPL_AUTH_OTP`, the FIRST **Authentication**-category template, `{{1}}` = code), `driver_invite` (`META_TPL_DRIVER_INVITE`, `{{1}}` = plate) and `transfer_invite` (`META_TPL_TRANSFER_INVITE`, `{{1}}` = plate). `sendWhatsAppText(to, text, { kind, templateVars })` resolves them through `resolveProactiveMode` and sends the approved template; an unset knob, a missing variable or a Meta rejection falls back to the free-form text (byte-identical default, proven by every existing suite). Call sites: `requestDashboardOtp` (kind `auth_otp`, `{ code: otp }`), `verifyOwnerAssignmentOtp` (kind `driver_invite`, `{ plate }`), `verifyOwnerReleaseOtpAndNotifyBuyer` (kind `transfer_invite`, `{ plate }`).

**Audit correction (rule 44).** The Phase 26 brief assumed the passbook buyer's OTP travelled over WhatsApp. It does not: `handleBuyerAcceptance` generates the buyer code and `sendEmailOtp` emails it (`transfers.js`), so the only WhatsApp-carried passbook message is the ACCEPT invitation — which is why the third kind is `transfer_invite`, not a second OTP.

**One transport (rule 55).** `metaMessenger.js` now owns both message shapes behind ONE `postWhatsAppMessage` guard + ONE catch (text and template share the credentials check, the delivery blocklist and the never-throws contract). `sentinel.sendWhatsAppTemplateMessage` and `src/routes/whatsapp/replies.js sendWhatsAppReply` both delegate to it; the text payload is unchanged and the silent-catch ratchet stays at its pinned budget.

**Operator contract.** `docs/TEMPLATES.md` is now 16 templates, with templates 14-16 carrying the exact body, category, language and variable spec plus the submission workflow; suggested names `saka_otp` (Authentication), `saka_driver_invite`, `saka_transfer_invite`. After approval: `gcloud run services update saka-fleet --region=europe-west1 --update-env-vars="META_TPL_AUTH_OTP=saka_otp,META_TPL_DRIVER_INVITE=saka_driver_invite,META_TPL_TRANSFER_INVITE=saka_transfer_invite"`, then `npm run env:audit` + `npm run health`. Rollback = unset the knobs.

**Rule 13/60 sync.** `SAKA_WEB_DASHBOARD_PLAYBOOK` and the `sakaAi` WEB DASHBOARD rule state that the code arrives even after a long silence and that templates/Meta are never mentioned to a user; `envAudit` registers the three knobs (META WHATSAPP section); `.env.example` documents them; `docs:gen` regenerated the KB docs.

**Suites run.** `test_proactive_templates` (58, +7), `test_dashboard` (868, +1), `test_driver_assignment_gate` (64, +1), `test_sentinel_policy` (30 — the template/text fallback contract unchanged), `test_env_audit` (59), `test_no_canned_replies` (15 — ratchet still 4), `test_conversation_compliance` (29), `test_agent_training` (219), `test_kb_docs` (36), `test_doc_sync` (30), `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *"business-initiated message minted free-form outside the 24-hour window"* → siblings audited: dashboard sign-in OTP (fixed), driver ACCEPT invite (fixed), buyer ACCEPT invite (fixed), the assignment OWNER OTP (emailed — no Meta concern), the buyer verification OTP (emailed — documented in TEMPLATES.md #16), web signup OTP (emailed), deploy/eval/care pings (already template-wired since v1.63.0), the trial activation reward (deliberately free-form: it fires right after fresh activity), superadmin budget/remediation pings (two-way ops traffic). Each fixed sibling carries one targeted assertion; the deliberately-left ones are documented here.

### 218. v1.87.2 (Phase 26C) — Resend quota detection + superadmin alert (2026-11-09)

**Why.** Resend refuses a send with HTTP 429 once the daily quota is exhausted (observed live during the v1.85.0 release run). Every email path failed invisibly: the web-signup OTP, the dashboard OTP fallback, the assignment OTP, the transfer release PIN, the monthly summary, trial reminders and Amina's replies simply stopped, with nothing in `error_logs` and no human aware.

**What shipped.** ONE wrapper in `mailer.js` — `sendResendEmail(payload, testSeam)` — now carries all **14** existing senders (the file-wide `getResendClient().emails.send(` is gone; behaviour and the `{ data, error }` contract are unchanged). Detection: `isResendQuotaError()` accepts `statusCode/status === 429`, a `rate_limit*` error name, or a `quota | rate limit | too many requests` message, on BOTH a returned error and a thrown one (a thrown 429 is re-recorded then rethrown so callers keep their catch). Recording: `recordResendQuotaWarning()` is the only writer — `readConfig` → dedupe → `writeConfig` → `admin_audit_logs` (`RESEND_QUOTA_ALERT`) → ONE superadmin WhatsApp text (`RESEND_QUOTA_WARNING_TEXT`). `isResendQuotaWarnedAt(dateStr, now)` is the pure UTC-day test. There is deliberately **no email fallback**: the email channel is exactly what is exhausted (documented in the module header, not hidden).

**Config key (rule 21 law).** `systemConfigKeys` gains `mailer.resend_quota_warned_at` (owner `mailer`, `legacyKey: 'resend_quota_warned_at'`, not boot-critical), so dual mode writes BOTH rows — the operator finds the marker under the documented `system_config.resend_quota_warned_at` name while the registry stays `domain.namespaced`.

**Command center.** `buildCommandCenterMetrics` reads the marker and exposes `email: { quotaWarnedAt, quotaWarnedToday }`; when today's warning is active the deterministic digest carries an `EMAIL_QUOTA` alert and `renderAdminCommandPage` renders a red banner ("⚠️ Resend quota exhausted today — paused until midnight UTC"). A previous-day marker renders nothing, because the quota resets at midnight UTC and a stale warning must never read as today's outage.

### 219. v1.87.3 (Phase 26B hotfix) — the Authentication-template button (2026-11-09)

**Found by a live send (rule 54).** After the operator approved the three templates and the knobs were set on Cloud Run (`saka-fleet-00375-tfs`), a real `saka_otp` send to the test number returned Meta **`131008` — "buttons: Button at index 0 of type Url requires a parameter"**: the approved Authentication template carries a URL button whose parameter is the code, and our body-only payload omitted it. The same run proved `saka_driver_invite` and `saka_transfer_invite` send cleanly (wamids captured), so the defect was the component shape, not the transport.

**The fix (data-driven — rule 55).** `PROACTIVE_TEMPLATE_KINDS.auth_otp` now declares `buttons: [{ subType: 'url', index: 0, variable: 'code' }]`. New pure `templateButtonsForKind(kind, values)` builds the ordered button components and returns `null` when a declared button variable is missing (so a missing code degrades the whole send to text — a template can never fire with a broken button). `resolveProactiveMode` returns `{ mode: 'template', templateName, variables, buttons }`; `sendWhatsAppTemplate` emits the body component first and the buttons after it; `sendWhatsAppText` and `sentinel.sendWhatsAppTemplateMessage` pass `buttons` through. Button-less kinds keep the body-only payload exactly as before (pinned).

**Proof.** `test_proactive_templates` pins the button contract and the exact wire payload — body `654321` plus `{ type: 'button', sub_type: 'url', index: '0', parameters: [{ type: 'text', text: '654321' }] }` — now 64 assertions (+6), including "button-less kinds keep the body-only payload" and "a missing code degrades to text". The live re-send after deploy is the operator-visible confirmation.
