### 220. v1.87.4 (Phase 27) — the document & receipt vault walkthrough fixes (2026-11-09)

**Found by live walkthroughs + live queries (rule 54).** Two operator-visible bugs on the same flow family:
1. A compliance document stored via WhatsApp never appeared under **Stored files** on `/d/vehicles/:id` (and the operator read `/d/compliance`'s Files column as empty).
2. A fuel receipt uploaded via WhatsApp never appeared in **`/d/records`** with a receipt link.

Live evidence (Supabase + Storage + Cloud Run, all read-only): David's profile `9cfb5f77…` owned vehicle `77e6c960…` (KAS628T); `vehicle_documents` held exactly ONE logbook row (media `2389385478538985`, storage_path set); the fuel `receipts` row `f4d9b896…` (media `2571801119966863`, image present in the private `receipts` bucket) existed while its `expense_logs` row `b2e79f10…` (KES 3,000, 13.51 L) carried **`receipt_id = NULL`**; both private buckets existed and `createSignedUrl` worked for both objects; `error_logs` held no storage/RLS/vault errors.

**BUG 1 root cause (A — calling convention).** `buildVehiclePage` called the injectable `loadDocuments({ supabase, vehicleId, limit })` with ONE object, while the real `listVehicleDocuments(providedSupabase, options)` takes the client first and the options second. No scope reached the query, so it answered `[]` and the page rendered an empty "Stored files" section since v1.84.0. The suite never caught it because `test_dashboard` injected a mock loader that ignored its arguments. Live proof: `buildVehiclePage` against production answered `storedDocuments: []` while a direct `listVehicleDocuments(sb, { vehicleId })` returned the row. **Fix:** call `loadDocuments(supabase, { vehicleId, … })` (both the current list and the replaced-file history), plus a defensive unwrap in `listVehicleDocuments` for the one-object shape (`providedSupabase.supabase` + no `.from`), so the convention can never silently empty again. The `/d/compliance` Files count was never broken (its inline count query works — live `docCount=1`).


**BUG 2 root cause (B — the receipt quiz never auto-started; C — the amount misread).** `messages.js` set `receiptQuizStart = 'log_expense'` only when the AI classifier returned exactly `LOG_EXPENSE`; a bare receipt photo does not, so `arbitrateQuizTurn`'s prefill branch never fired. The live transcript proves the chain: Saka replied "…type 'fuel 3,000 KES at [litres] L'…" instead of opening the confirmation card; the user's typed reply started a FRESH expense quiz without the prefill; the confirmed expense saved with `receipt_id = NULL`. The records page's legacy fallback (same vehicle + Nairobi day + same amount) also failed because the receipt row's `amount` was **11,823** — the merchant's P.O. BOX number — while the expense was 3,000. The deterministic pipeline traced live: the KE profile could not read the fiscal `3.000.00` grouping (`parseOcrAmount` refuses mixed separators by design) and the Document Lens's fallback scan then picked the box number (and named the legal-receipt marker line as the vendor).

**Fix B (the quiz law is intent-independent).** New pure `receiptQuizStartFor({ hasMedia, isReceiptDocument, intent, quizStartFlow, hasReceiptPrefill })` in `quiz.js`: a freshly VAULTED receipt ALWAYS opens the expense quiz whatever the classifier said (the v1.49.3 law — receipts confirm before any write); duplicates/unvaulted keep the legacy rule so a re-send can never open a second draft; non-receipt media is untouched. `messages.js` resolves it with `hasReceiptPrefill: Boolean(receiptPrefill?.receipt_id)` — the prefill still rides `arbitrateQuizTurn` → `startQuiz`.

**Fix C (rule 36 — KE-profile scope).** `parseKeFiscalAmount()` (`src/data/ocrCountryProfiles.js`) resolves dot-thousands + dot-decimal fiscal money ("3.000.00" → 3000, "2.777.78" → 2777.78) and is registered as `KE_OCR_PROFILE.amount.parse`; the KE etimes amount loop and the Document Lens `amountFrom` delegate to the country profile's reader; the lens fallback scan now inspects the WHOLE line (P.O. Box/PIN/invoice/serial exclusion) and never accepts a bare 4–6 digit integer when a labelled TOTAL exists; the lens vendor guard uses `LEGAL_RECEIPT_MARKER_RE`. The GLOBAL path is byte-identical (pinned: `3.000.00` with `countryCode:'GLOBAL'` still resolves to null).

**FIX E — the transfer page's silent empty list.** Live `error_logs` carried `column passbook_transfers.created_at does not exist` (`dashboard.loadOwnerTransfers`, 2026-11-09T03:21Z). The live table has `initiated_at` / `completed_at` only. The select now names those two and the mapper uses `initiated_at` — the owner's transfer history renders again.


**FIX D deferred (decision D2 — v1.87.5).** Live evidence showed the insurance certificate (media `29640619848876615`) and the first logbook (media `1155049380292966`) were uploaded DURING registration, before the vehicle row existed (03:12–03:13 vs vehicle 03:14:36), so `resolveReceiptVault` skipped the vault and the bytes were discarded. The stash-and-replay design is deferred to v1.87.5 by operator decision; a TODO carrying the exact contract now lives in `media.js`.

**Live reconciliation (F, rule 56 — reaches the existing user).** (1) `expense_logs.b2e79f10…` linked to `receipts.f4d9b896…` (audited `RECEIPT_LINK_BACKFILLED`) — the records page now renders the receipt View link for the walkthrough expense; (2) the insurance photo was re-downloaded from Meta (267,996 bytes) and re-vaulted as `vehicle_documents.a3b4db13…`, linked to its compliance row (`compliance_id` = the live insurance row; audited `VEHICLE_DOCUMENT_REVAULTED`); (3) the FIRST logbook was deliberately NOT re-vaulted — inserting it after the newer upload would have SUPERSEDED the current logbook file (documented in the audit row). Verified live after the writes: `buildVehiclePage` → 2 stored docs (insurance + logbook), `buildComplianceBoard` → `docCount 2`, `attachReceiptMatches` → the fuel expense answers `receiptStatus:'linked'`.

### 221. v1.87.5 (Phase 28) — driver-licence precedence + an honest transfer cancel (2026-11-09)

**Found by walkthroughs (rule 54).** BUG 1 (driver's licence filed as a vehicle logbook) was reported from the walkthrough but had **no live row** at audit time — `vehicle_documents` held only the two legitimate files and no upload had reached the OCR pipeline after 06:27Z. It is a REAL latent defect, reproduced offline against a typical NTSA licence text. BUG 2 (cancel fakes success) was proven live: row `78cda450…` stayed `PENDING_OWNER_RELEASE_OTP` after the operator's cancel.

**BUG 1 root cause — a weaker heuristic branch ran before a stronger labelled marker.** `classifyOcrDocument` (`ocrService.js`) tested the LOGBOOK branch — including `looksLikeVin` — **before** the LICENCE branch. `looksLikeVin` accepted any **pure-digit 11–17 character token** (it only required a digit), so a licence's "SERIAL NO: 043202308218505" equalled "vehicle identification number". The photo became `logbook`; `classifyDocumentFamily` had no demotion; `isVaultableDocumentFamily('logbook')` then stored it vehicle-scoped. Offline reproduction before the fix: `classifyOcrDocument(DL text) === 'logbook'`, `classifyDocumentFamily(...) === 'logbook'`.

**BUG 1 fixes.** (1) The licence branch now sits ABOVE the logbook branch (insurance keeps first place — the v1.32.1 law is untouched): `DRIVING LICEN[CS]E|DRIVER'?S LICEN[CS]E|PSV|PDP|DL (NO|NUMBER)|BADGE` wins over `VIN|CHASSIS|LOG BOOK|REGISTRATION CERT|MOTOR VEHICLE REG|looksLikeVin`. (2) `looksLikeVin` now requires **letters AND digits** (`(?=[A-Z0-9]*\d)(?=\d*[A-HJ-NPR-Z])`) — a pure-digit serial is never a VIN. (3) Defence in depth in the Lens: a `logbook` base with strong licence markers is demoted to `drivers_licence`. (4) Bonus crash fix: `parseLogbook`'s bare-VIN fallback regex has **no capture group**, so `vinMatch[1].toUpperCase()` threw and the Lens silently lost every hint; it now reads `vinMatch[1] ?? vinMatch[0]`. Verified offline after the fix: licence → `drivers_licence` with number 23942494 + expiry 2028-11-28; a real logbook keeps `logbook` + its VIN; a bare VIN parses without throwing; a pure-digit serial classifies `unknown`; insurance still beats licence markers. **Routing is unchanged by decision (D3):** `isVaultableDocumentFamily('drivers_licence') === false` already sends the document to the existing driver capture lane (`persistCapturedCompliance` scope `driver` → `driver_compliances`). **No new tables, no schema change** — the §40.2 D3 law (driver documents stay out of the vehicle vault) holds.


**BUG 2 root cause — a phantom column and a swallowed error.** `POST /d/transfer/cancel` (`routes/dashboard.js`) wrote `{ status: 'CANCELLED', updated_at: new Date().toISOString() }`, but the live `passbook_transfers` table has **no `updated_at` column** (verified live: id, vehicle_id, from_owner_id, to_owner_phone, transfer_fee_paid, payment_reference, status, initiated_at, completed_at, to_owner_email, to_owner_id, vin, release_otp, release_otp_expires_at, buyer_otp, buyer_otp_expires_at, is_free_transfer, fee_amount, fee_currency, checkout_url, blocked_reason). PostgREST returns such a refusal in the **result object** (it does not throw), the route never read it, and it still redirected with `?cancelled=1` — a fake success. Live proof: row `78cda450-8b49-498d-a3dc-05efc9905067` (KAS628T, buyer +254720641985) stayed `PENDING_OWNER_RELEASE_OTP`, so the page kept it "in flight" and the machine's initiation guard kept refusing new handovers.

**BUG 2 fixes.** (1) The cancel write names ONLY real columns (`{ status: 'CANCELLED' }`); the returned `error` is checked and answered honestly — a 500 page ("That handover could not be cancelled just now — please try again.") plus an `error_logs` row (`transfer cancel refused: …`); NEVER a fake `?cancelled=1`. (2) The machine's initiation guard now covers **every** pending status — `PENDING_BUYER_UPGRADE` (the buyer-capacity pause) was missing, so a paused transfer allowed a duplicate to start for the same vehicle.

**Live reconciliation (F, rule 56).** David's stuck handover `78cda450…` was set to `CANCELLED` (audited `TRANSFER_CANCELLED_RECONCILED`, previous status recorded) — the operator had already asked for exactly that cancel — so the walkthrough can start a fresh transfer immediately. Cline's own audit artifact (an `error_logs` "Invalid time value" row written by a read-only probe at 06:51:41) was deleted (rule 10). No misclassified licence row existed in production at ship time; the reconciliation path if one appears is: delete the `vehicle_documents` row + its bucket object (audited) and let the driver capture re-file it.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/ocrService.js` (`classifyOcrDocument` order, `looksLikeVin`), `src/services/documentLens.js` (`classifyDocumentFamily` demotion, `parseLogbook` fallback), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (cancel write + honest error), `src/services/transfers.js` (guard list), `test_ocr_flow.js` (+8), `test_dashboard.js` (+4: phantom-column assertion, honest-failure case, untouched-status case, upgrade-pause guard), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§221 + history + version), `CHANGELOG.md`, `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), `package.json` (1.87.5).

**Suites run.** `test_ocr_flow` (153, +8), `test_dashboard` (876, +4), `test_vehicle_documents` (75), `test_quiz_flow`, `test_ocr_normalizer`, `test_agent_training`, `test_doc_sync`, `test_kb_docs`, `test_landing_static`, `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) Defect class "a weaker heuristic branch runs before a stronger labelled marker"* → whole document-family precedence swept: insurance (already first ✓), inspection / road_licence / purchase_invoice / service_receipt (Lens overrides demote a logbook base ✓), drivers_licence (fixed — the one unprotected family), receipts/odometer (not logbook-adjacent). *(ii) Defect class "a VIN heuristic accepts non-VIN tokens"* → `looksLikeVin` (fixed) and `parseLogbook`'s inline fallback (no-crash fix); the KRA-PIN stripping is unchanged. *(iii) Defect class "a write names a column the live table never had, and the error is swallowed"* → every `passbook_transfers` writer swept: dashboard cancel (fixed), WhatsApp cancel (`pending.js` — status only ✓), delete-vehicle cancel (`vehicles.js` — status only ✓), start/verify (`transfers.js` — no phantom columns ✓); `error_logs` honesty added on the one that could fail silently. *(iv) Defect class "a pending-state guard lists only some pending states"* → the machine's initiation guard (fixed) vs the dashboard in-flight list (`TRANSFER_OPEN_STATUSES` already carried all five ✓).

### 226. v1.89.1 — the docs gate stops failing on Windows checkouts (2026-11-09)

**Why now (and what forced the audit).** v1.89.0 shipped and deployed on schedule (push 13:13 EAT → revision `saka-fleet-00383-p67`, 100% traffic, `/api/health` 200, `deploy.last_deployed_revision` written). At the same instant the local Windows clone's `.git` came back damaged — a zero-filled index, zero-filled loose refs, `COMMIT_EDITMSG` and reflog tails. The object database was intact: `origin/main` held the v1.89.0 commit (`431540c`), and the four "untracked" new files hashed identically to the upstream blobs, so the checkout was repaired to `origin/main` with no content loss and every gate was re-proven from scratch (rule 52).

**The defect the re-proof found.** `scripts/gen_kb_docs.js` compared the generated text to the file on disk byte-for-byte, and `test_kb_docs.js` did the same. With `core.autocrlf=true` (this clone), git hands the identical generated text back as CRLF, so `test_kb_docs` — one of the suites inside the mandatory pre-push `npm run health` — failed claiming PRODUCT_QA.md had drifted. `npm run docs:gen` rewrote the files as LF and git reported **no diff at all**, proving the content had never drifted. Left alone, the false red returns after every checkout or pull that touches the two generated docs, blocking the release gate for no reason.

**The fix.** One exported pure helper `normalizeDocNewlines(text)` (`\r\n` → `\n`); `checkDocs()` normalises both sides (and is now exported so the suite can assert that the CLI gate and the test agree), and `writeDocs()` always writes LF. What counts as real drift is unchanged: a genuine registry change, a missing file or a stale version stamp still fails the gate.

**Tests (behaviour change pinned, rule 52).** `test_kb_docs` normalises the on-disk read, asserts `checkDocs(docs).length === 0`, and adds **Test 2b**: for each real generated doc, a CRLF copy must differ byte-for-byte AND normalise back to the exact generated text, plus CRLF-collapse and LF-untouched assertions. `test_vehicle_documents` version pin follows 1.89.1.

**Frames touched.** `scripts/gen_kb_docs.js` (`normalizeDocNewlines`, `writeDocs`, exported `checkDocs`), `test_kb_docs.js` (+7 assertions, Test 2b), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.89.1), `landing/data/changelog.json`, `docs/` (regenerated), this section + history + version, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_kb_docs (43, +7), test_doc_sync (30), test_vehicle_documents (75), test_landing_static (252), test_env_audit (59), test_stt_locales (35), test_country_bucket (89), `npm run docs:check`, `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *"a byte-exact file comparison treats a checkout artifact as content drift"* → every file-comparing gate swept: `gen_kb_docs.checkDocs` (fixed), `test_kb_docs` Test 2 (fixed), `test_doc_sync` (`.includes`/regex — safe), `scripts/env_audit.js` (splits `/\r?\n/` — safe), `scripts/health_audit.js` (regex over child-process output — safe), `scripts/stamp_landing_assets.cjs` (hashes only — safe). No other textual byte comparison exists in `scripts/` or the test suite.

### 227. v1.89.2 (Phase 27D) — the nickname is actually editable now (2026-11-09)

**The live failure (Check 2 of the walkthrough).** On 2026-11-09 at 16:07 EAT the owner of `KAS628T` typed **"Edit KAS 628t nickname"**; the engine answered *"Which detail would you like to change?"*, he replied **"Nickname"**, and was told *"No worries — I didn't catch that one. Which field would you like to edit…"*. He tried six more times in three minutes ("Edit KAS 628T NICKNAME", "Help me Change car nickname", "Edit vehicle details", "Kindly check deeply and ascertain I can edit a nickname", "Edit KAS 628T nickname to Teddy"), cancelled twice, and gave up. Live row: `vehicles.nickname = NULL` (never written); Sentinel raised two PENDING friction rows (`USER_FRUSTRATION`, `MULTI_QUESTION_PROMPT`) at 16:12 EAT.

**Root cause (one class, two surfaces — rule 51).** v1.89.0 shipped the column, the registration question, nickname-first resolution and the display label, but nickname was never added to the registries that decide **what a user may ask to edit**: `quizEngine.EDITABLE_VEHICLE_FIELDS` (15 fields, no nickname — the choice parser therefore rejected the word) and `commands.handleEditVehicleTurn` (its own `fieldAliasMap`, `attrKeys` and explicit `<field> to <value>` regex — all without nickname). The write layer was already correct (`sanitizeVehicleUpdates` whitelists `nickname`; `updateVehicleDetails` writes it) and the dashboard selects/renders it, so no schema, resolution or display change was needed.

**A. Quiz lane.** `'Nickname': 'nickname'` joins the edit registry with everyday aliases (`nick name`, `aka`, `a.k.a.`, `asset name`, `pet name`); a dedicated parse/validate branch sanitises through `sanitizeVehicleNickname` (≤40, record-label charset) and refuses longer input with guidance. Clearing is explicit: `remove|clear|none|no nickname|reset|skip|delete` parses to `EDIT_VEHICLE_CLEAR_NICKNAME`, a sentinel the executor maps to `NULL` (the engine treats a `null` parser result as "not an answer", so the sentinel is required); the confirm card renders *"Remove nickname"* and no sentinel can reach the user (asserted).

**B. One-line command (D1).** New exported pure `parseVehicleEditRequest(text, { vehicles })` returns the prefilled answers: **"edit KAS 628T nickname to Teddy"** → `{edit_field:'Nickname', new_value:'Teddy'}`; **"edit KAS 628T nickname"** → field only; **"rename KAS 628T to The Workhorse"** → nickname; a bare "edit vehicle" → `{}` (still asks); other fields unchanged ("change fuel type to Diesel"). Plates **and existing nicknames** are masked before matching, so an asset named *"The Workhorse"* (or a plate containing a field word) can never be misread as a field. `quiz.js` wires it as `prefill: editPrefillFor(flow)` on **both** start paths (mid-quiz switch and the normal start); `startQuiz` seeds the answers and `applyExtraction` skips already-answered fields, so deterministic input always beats AI output.


**C. Deterministic lane + menu.** `handleEditVehicleTurn` learns nickname in the alias map (`nickname|nick|nick_name|aka|asset_name`), in `attrKeys`, in the explicit field regex and in its "what can I edit" card (which now lists the current nickname and shows `Nickname (PLATE)` in the header); nickname values are sanitised and `remove` writes `NULL`. `interactiveReply.QUICK_EDIT_ACTIONS.EDIT_VEHICLE.fields` gains `nickname` (an `edit_vehicle:vin` id still falls through — rule 8). `FLOW_GUIDANCE.edit_vehicle` now mentions the nickname and corrects a stale line that claimed the **plate** was locked (it is editable; the passbook token is not).

**D. Display.** The success card renders the **saved** row (`res.vehicle`) through `vehicleDisplayLabel()` and says *"no nickname"* after a clear; nothing else in the display chain changed (dashboard/ledger were already correct in v1.89.0).

**E. Tests (behaviour change pinned).** `test_quiz_flow` (+20 → 215): registry/aliases, sanitisation, 40-char refusal, the sentinel, six `parseVehicleEditRequest` cases (including masking and the "other fields still work" guard), and two end-to-end runs — prefill → one answer → **confirm → the mocked `vehicles.update` carries `nickname`**, plus the clear path writing `NULL`. `test_edit_delete` (+4): the deterministic lane sets, clears, accepts an AI-supplied `edit_field: nickname`, and still refuses VIN. `test_v1571` (+2) and `test_interactive_reply` (+1) pin the menu surfaces.

**F. Live verification.** Row read before the fix (`nickname: null`), the full transcript, and the deployed revision are recorded above; after deploy the same flow is replayed against a mock of the live shape (the operator can now set the name in one message).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/quizEngine.js`, `src/routes/whatsapp/quiz.js`, `src/routes/whatsapp/commands.js`, `src/services/interactiveReply.js`, `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `test_quiz_flow.js` (+20: 215), `test_edit_delete.js` (+4), `test_v1571.js` (+2: 22), `test_interactive_reply.js` (+1: 49), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.89.2), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this section + history + version, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_quiz_flow (215), test_edit_delete, test_v1571 (22), test_interactive_reply (49), test_narrative_draft (128), test_entry_ledger, test_dashboard (883), test_agent_training (226), test_doc_sync (30), test_kb_docs (43), test_landing_static (252), test_env_audit (59), test_vehicle_documents (75), `npm run docs:check`, `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *"a field ships in the data + display layers but not in the edit surfaces that decide what a user may ask for"* → every edit surface swept: quiz `EDITABLE_VEHICLE_FIELDS` (fixed), `commands.handleEditVehicleTurn` alias/attrs/regex/card (fixed), `interactiveReply.QUICK_EDIT_ACTIONS` (fixed), `vehicles.sanitizeVehicleUpdates` + `updateVehicleDetails` (already correct), dashboard `loadOwnerVehicles`/renderers (already correct). Each lane now carries an assertion, so the next field cannot ship half-wired.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63 (rules + architecture first; proposals checked — none open; the two PENDING friction rows from this walkthrough were found, fixed and closed), 2 (this section), 3/4 (targeted reads, batched edits), 7 (no country parsing touched), 8 (VIN/passbook locked — asserted in both lanes), 10 (new suites stateless; the DB suite ran under `runWithCleanup`), 12/13/33 (one commit: version + history + CHANGELOG + landing + regenerated docs), 31/60 (plain language, one next step, no blame; the flow never re-asks what was just said), 50 (a missing `nickname` column still degrades through the existing pre-migration retry), 51/52 (class sweep + before/after assertions), 54 (live row, live transcript, live revision), 55 (evolved both existing edit surfaces — zero new tables), 58 (this report). No rule edited. **Decision impact:** `edit_vehicle` now accepts a one-line command and `remove` clears a nickname — user-facing behaviour changes stated here and in the CHANGELOG.

### 228. v1.90.0 (Phase 28B) — transport & error hardening, and the Phase 28 split (2026-11-09)

**Why this release exists.** Phase 28 was split into **28B (this release)** and **28A** (the six superadmin write actions, still to ship). The security fixes ship FIRST so every new admin write endpoint in 28A is born behind per-client rate limits, an Origin guard, HSTS and a non-leaking error handler — shipping them the other way round would mean writing and testing those endpoints twice.

**CHECK 1 — error.message consumers (audit before the change).** Swept `src/` and the suites for raw message consumers: the only client-facing echo was the global handler itself (`index.js:141`); the `/api/sentinel` catch is secret-gated, `entryLedger`/service `message:` fields are internal result objects, and no suite asserted the old handler copy. Safe to genericize.

**CHECK 2 — subdomains before choosing includeSubDomains.** Live plain-HTTP probes: `sakafleet.com` 301 → HTTPS, `www.sakafleet.com` 301, `app.sakafleet.com` 302, `reports.sakafleet.com` 301. Every subdomain redirects, so `includeSubDomains` ships.

**CHECK 3 — the keyGenerator contract (four cases, all pinned).** Same rightmost hop + different forged leftmost → SAME bucket; different rightmost → DIFFERENT buckets; single-entry XFF → that entry; no XFF → `request.ip`; addressless → `'unknown'`. An end-to-end `@fastify/rate-limit` run proves one real client exhausts exactly one shared bucket regardless of forged left hops while a distinct client keeps a fresh one.

**CHECK 4 — the CSRF map.** All 12 `/d` POSTs enumerated: `/d/login`, `/d/admin/login`, `/d/settings`, `/d/documents/:id/delete`, `/d/import`, `/d/import/confirm`, `/d/transfer/start|verify|cancel`, `/d/subscription/checkout|addon` already carried `isCrossOriginWrite`; `/d/verify` was the only gap (fixed, refused BEFORE any OTP work — no attempt burned, no session minted, no cookie set).

**The five fixes.**
1. **CSV formula injection.** `csvCell` (the ONLY cell serializer; both `serializeRecordsCsv` and `serializeAllDataCsv` route through it) now prefixes `'` when the raw cell starts with `= + - @ TAB CR` and is not numeric-shaped (`/^-?\d[\d.,]*$/`). `+254…` labels ARE prefixed (a leading `+` is a formula trigger), while `-500` stays numeric so Excel arithmetic survives; `csvNumber` output is unsigned and never touched.
2. **Error handler.** New `src/services/errorHandler.js` — `buildErrorHandler({ supabase, log, logSystemError })` keeps `fastify.log.error` + `logSystemError` unchanged, preserves `error.statusCode` and `error.name`, and returns exactly one generic line (`GENERIC_ERROR_MESSAGE`). `index.js` installs it right after the Supabase client (the old block sat above the client's `const` and could not take it as an argument).
3. **HSTS + 308.** New `src/services/securityHeaders.js` — an `onRequest` hook: `x-forwarded-proto: http` → 308 to `https://<host><path?query>` except `/healthz`, `/api/health`, `/internal/status`; `x-forwarded-proto: https` → `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`. Platform health checks carry no proto header, so they are neither redirected nor stamped; `/healthz` stays GFE-intercepted (v1.24.4) and is exempt anyway.
4. **`/d/verify` CSRF.** One guard, the same 400 page as `/d/login`.
5. **Rate-limit identity.** `Fastify({ trustProxy: true })` + `keyGenerator: rateLimitKeyGenerator` on the root registration. `src/services/rateLimitIdentity.js` returns the RIGHTMOST `x-forwarded-for` hop (the address the GFE appends — the only entry a caller cannot forge), falling back to `request.ip`, then `'unknown'`. Per-route configs inherit the key, so `/d/login`, `/d/admin/*`, `/d/import` and every other bucket are per real client.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) "a serializer quotes but never neutralises executable prefixes"* → `csvCell` fixed once for both exporters; PDF/text paths emit no formulas. *(ii) "an error path echoes internal text"* → global handler fixed; `/api/sentinel` deliberately left (secret-gated); dashboard routes render their own copy. *(iii) "a transport guarantee assumed at the edge"* → HSTS was absent; probes explicitly exempted. *(iv) "a POST lane added after the CSRF pattern shipped"* → all 12 re-enumerated. *(v) "a limiter keyed on a shared address"* → the single root registration fixed; every per-route config re-checked.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (`csvCell` exported + formula guard, default export), `src/services/errorHandler.js` (new), `src/services/securityHeaders.js` (new), `src/services/rateLimitIdentity.js` (new), `index.js` (trustProxy, keyGenerator, `registerSecurityHeaders`, handler install), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (`/d/verify` guard), `test_security.js` (Tests 6–9), `test_dashboard.js` (+3), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.90.0), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this section + history + version, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_security, test_dashboard, test_doc_sync, test_kb_docs, test_landing_static, test_vehicle_documents, test_env_audit, `npm run health` — green.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63 (rules + architecture first; 0 open proposals), 2 (this section), 3/4, 10/11, 12/33, 13, 18, 21, 31, 43/54, 50, 51/52, 55, 58. No rule edited. **Decision impact:** generic client error copy, plain-HTTP 308 (probes exempt), per-real-client rate-limit buckets.

### 229. v1.91.0 (Phase 28A) — superadmin write actions (2026-11-09)

**Why 28A follows 28B.** The six tools shipped ON TOP of the v1.90.0 hardening (per-client rate-limit identity, Origin guard, HSTS, generic error handler) — every new POST was born with the guard stack rather than retro-fitted.

**Schema (new, additive).** `public.admin_impersonations` — `id uuid PK`, `token_hash text UNIQUE NOT NULL` (sha256 of the `saka_dash_as` cookie token, never the raw value), `admin_profile_id uuid NOT NULL`, `target_profile_id uuid NOT NULL`, `expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL`, `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`; indexes on both profile ids; RLS enabled. Carriers: `npm run migrate:admin-impersonations` (idempotent) + the boot ensure (`ensureAdminImpersonationsTable`) + the staging DDL + `RESET_TABLES`/TRUNCATE/targeted-phone cascade + `testCleanup` + `test_db_reset_scope` (Test 9). **Live verification** (Management API): PK `admin_impersonations_pkey`, UNIQUE `admin_impersonations_token_hash_key`, `idx_admin_impersonations_target`, `idx_admin_impersonations_admin`, `relrowsecurity = true`.

**Impersonation (D1, read-only).** The `saka_dash_as=<64 hex>; Path=/d; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=1800; Secure` cookie is SEPARATE from `saka_dash`. `requireRoleSession` resolves it only when the caller holds a live ADMIN session and the row belongs to that admin; the resolved session becomes `{role:'owner', ownerId: target, impersonated:true}`. Owner-lane non-GET requests are refused ("Exit impersonation to make changes"). `GET /d/admin/exit-as` clears ONLY the as-cookie, deletes the row and 303s to `/d/admin?done=as-exited` — the admin's `saka_dash` session is untouched (proven by test: `/d/admin` still 200 after exit). Expiry: cookie Max-Age + `expires_at` on every resolution + the 15-min prune (`pruneExpiredImpersonations`, boot + interval). The sticky yellow banner is injected by a scoped `onSend` hook after the shell header (name + Nairobi HH:MM + Exit).

**The six actions.** A `GET/POST /d/admin/as-user/:id` (typed IMPERSONATE + reason; self/superadmin refused; audit `ADMIN_ACTION_IMPERSONATE`); B `GET /d/admin/exit-as` (audit `ADMIN_ACTION_IMPERSONATE_END`); C `GET/POST /d/admin/reset/:id` (typed RESET + reason; reuses `wipeProfileForSignup`, then ALSO clears `dashboard_sessions` by owner_id and `admin_impersonations` by target/admin; audit `ADMIN_ACTION_PROFILE_RESET` with per-table counts); D `GET/POST /d/admin/extend-trial/:id` (typed EXTEND + reason + days 1-365; `extendAccountTrial({days})` WITHOUT `maxTotalDays` — the 45-day clamp and the launch-award exception stay engine-owned; audited `ADMIN_ACTION_TRIAL_EXTENDED`; honest 400 on "No active trial").

E `GET /d/admin/passbook/:vehicleId` (read-only; VIN/token masked with `<details>` reveal; transfer history with masked buyer; 404 for a missing/soft-deleted vehicle; audit `ADMIN_ACTION_PASSBOOK_VIEW`); F `GET /d/admin/transfer/:vehicleId` + `POST step1|step2|step3|cancel` (the SAME `transfers.js` engine through injectable seams; step 2's release PIN is emailed ONLY to the owner and relayed in WhatsApp (D2); steps 4-5 stay on WhatsApp; every step audited `ADMIN_ACTION_TRANSFER_*`; cancel writes `CANCELLED` and reports honestly); G `GET/POST /d/admin/email/:profileId` (draft → escaped preview → typed SEND + reason; From `Saka Fleet <reports@reports.sakafleet.com>`; refuses an account with no email; a refused send answers 502 and is audited `ok:false`).

**The guard stack (D3-D6).** flag gate (A1 404) → `isCrossOriginWrite` on every POST → `requireRoleSession('admin')` → per-route `{max:5, timeWindow:'5 minutes', keyGenerator: adminActionKeyGenerator}` (real client IP + hashed `saka_dash` session — D5) → the typed word is re-validated SERVER-side (the client JS only disables the button) → a reason ≥3 chars for every destructive/labelled action → an `admin_audit_logs` row carrying `reason`, `targetId` (and before/after where a row changes) → 303 to `/d/admin?done=<verb>` with a success notice. Owner rows and vehicle rows gained the action links; `renderAdminOwnersPage` accepts the notice.

**`wipeProfileForSignup` now ends the account's sessions.** It deletes `dashboard_sessions` by owner_id and `admin_impersonations` by target/admin; `test_profile_wipe` pins both (17).

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) "a session carrier outlives the profile it belongs to"* → every profile-scoped session table swept: `dashboard_sessions` (fixed), `admin_impersonations` (fixed), `chat_sessions`/`superadmin_sessions` (already phone-keyed). *(ii) "a new write endpoint ships without the 28B guard stack"* → all eight POSTs carry Origin + admin session + the composite 5/5-min limit; typed words where the brief requires them. *(iii) "a cookie exit clears the wrong session"* → the as-cookie has its own clear builder; pinned both directions. *(iv) "an admin action invents engine values"* → fees, trial clamps and transfer transitions come from the engines; the pages only render what they return. *(v) "a prompt lists an unshipped capability or omits a shipped one"* → playbook + core prompt updated and pinned by `test_agent_training` (232).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (impersonation constants/DDL/ensure/mint/resolve/clear/prune + the cookie trio, `adminNav` export, owners/fleet action links + notice), `src/services/dashboardAdmin.js` (new), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (the impersonation branch, the banner onSend hook, 15 routes, injectable `adminEmailSender`/`adminTransferEngine`), `src/services/profileWipe.js`, `src/services/rateLimitIdentity.js` (`adminActionKeyGenerator`), `index.js` (boot ensure + prune), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `scripts/run_admin_impersonations_migration.js` (new), `scripts/{reset-db,testCleanup,provision_staging_schema,health_audit}.js`, `docs/CARE_WORKER_GUIDE.md`, `test_dashboard_admin.js` (new, 92), `test_profile_wipe.js` (+2: 17), `test_db_reset_scope.js` (+13: 107), `test_agent_training.js` (+6: 232), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.91.0 + `migrate:admin-impersonations`), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this section + history + version, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_dashboard_admin (92), test_dashboard (886), test_profile_wipe (17), test_db_reset_scope (107), test_agent_training (232), test_vehicle_documents (75), test_doc_sync, test_kb_docs, test_landing_static, test_security, `npm run health` — green.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63 (rules + architecture first; 0 open proposals), 2 (this section), 3/4, 7 (Nairobi expiry + masked identifiers), 8 (VIN/token read-only), 10/11, 12/33, 13/60 (playbook + core prompt + training), 26 (45-day clamp untouched), 31 (warm copy, one next step), 37 (audit trail), 42/44, 50 (a refused step answers honestly), 51/52, 54 (live migration + pg_constraint/index/RLS proof), 55 (zero new engines — the wipe, trial and transfer engines reused), 56 (existing accounts inherit the tools immediately), 58. No rule edited. **Decision impact:** the superadmin console now writes; impersonation is read-only; the transfer release PIN stays owner-only; every action is typed-confirmed, reason-stamped and audited.

### 230. v1.92.0 (Phase 29) — passbook earnings archive + overdue compliance digest (2026-11-09)

**Task 1 — the real bug.** A completed passbook transfer re-anchored the vehicle (owner, phone, email, token, driver) but left `private_earnings` untouched. Every owner/driver-facing earnings read was VEHICLE-scoped, so the seller lost sight of their own money history the moment the asset left their roster, and the BUYER inherited earnings they never generated (records, vehicle page, portfolio, reports, deep-dive, context snapshot, weekly auto-audit).

**Schema (additive).** `private_earnings.archived_at timestamptz NULL` + `private_earnings.archived_by_transfer_id uuid NULL REFERENCES passbook_transfers(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` + `idx_private_earnings_archived (archived_by_transfer_id) WHERE archived_at IS NOT NULL`; new `earnings_report_queue` (`id`, `transfer_id uuid UNIQUE → passbook_transfers ON DELETE CASCADE`, `owner_id`, `email`, `due_at`, `sent_at`, `attempts`, `last_error`, `created_at`) + `idx_earnings_report_queue_due`. Carriers: `npm run migrate:earnings-archive` (idempotent) + the boot ensure (`ensureEarningsArchiveSchema`) + the staging DDL + `RESET_TABLES`/TRUNCATE/targeted-phone cascade + `testCleanup` + `profileWipe` + `test_db_reset_scope` (Test 10). **Applied live** (project `wnvbhpykboonygaznhhl`) and probed: archive columns, queue and digest tables all answer.

**D3 (locked) — archive BEFORE the COMPLETED flip.** `completePassbookTransfer` now runs `archiveVehicleEarnings()` (ONE update, `WHERE archived_at IS NULL`, idempotent — a second transfer in the same year archives only newer rows) immediately after the capacity gate and BEFORE the vehicle/COMPLETED writes. An archive error aborts with *"Could not finalize the transfer. Nothing was changed. Please try again."* and audits `ADMIN_TRANSFER_ARCHIVE_FAILED`; a LATER failure (vehicle update, COMPLETED update) calls `restoreArchivedEarnings()` so no half state survives. Invariant: **COMPLETED ⇒ archived**. A successful archive audits `ADMIN_TRANSFER_EARNINGS_ARCHIVED` with its count; `queueEarningsReport()` inserts the 10-minute queue row (a duplicate is not a failure); a phone-only seller is audited `ADMIN_TRANSFER_EARNINGS_REPORT_SKIPPED` and the WhatsApp line points at the dashboard instead of email. The seller message now carries *"Your earnings history for this asset has been archived and stays yours. Check your email for a final report."*

**Buyer-blind on every surface (rule 51 sweep).** New `src/services/earningsScope.js` (`selectLiveEarnings()` + `isArchiveColumnError()`) filters `archived_at IS NULL` and degrades to an unfiltered read when the column is missing (rule 50 — a schema state is never an empty ledger). Applied to `queryOwnerRecords` (rows + count), `fleetReports.loadFleetData`, `ownerPortfolio`, `vehicleDeepDive`, `userContextSnapshot`, `reportMetrics`, `driverReports` (×2) and the `index.js` weekly auto-audit. Superadmin revenue totals deliberately keep counting archived rows (D6 — evidence ledger, real revenue).

**D2 (locked) — the seller's history, both copy and link.** `GET /d/records?history=1` (also on `.csv`/`.pdf`) swaps in `queryArchivedEarnings()` — scoped through `passbook_transfers.from_owner_id` (never live ownership, the vehicle belongs to the buyer now), plates fetched by id purely for the seller's label, rows carry `archived`/`transferId` and render an **Archived** chip with no receipt link. The toggle `All records · Transferred (history)` rides every pager/export link (`recordsQueryString`). The Final Earnings Report email (`sendFinalEarningsReportEmail`, Resend Buffer, never throws) carries the PDF built by `buildFinalEarningsReportPdf` (the SAME `buildRecordsPdf` renderer with a `Final Earnings Report` heading — rule 55) **and** the history link in the body. `runEarningsReportQueue` drains `earnings_report_queue` every 30s: at most 3 attempts, honest `last_error`, rows with nothing to send closed instead of retried, sent rows pruned after 30 days.

**Task 2 (D1 HYBRID, locked).** `overdue_digest_log` (`owner_id PK`, `first_overdue_at`, `sent_t3_at`, `sent_t7_at`, timestamps) + `evaluateOverdueDigest()` as the FOURTH pass of `runReminderSweep` (after expiry). The overdue set is recomputed from live active reminders every sweep; the episode anchor = the FIRST overdue item's due date and never moves while anything stays overdue; ONE digest at T+3 and ONE at T+7, then silence. `evaluateExpiryReminders` gained the sibling suppression: once an episode is live (or its first alert went out earlier in the same sweep), later overdue items are stamped `notified_overdue` but NOT messaged — **max 3 messages per episode regardless of N** (1 immediate + 2 digests). Renewing everything resets the row (a genuinely new item later starts a fresh clock); a sweep that finds zero active date reminders clears every episode row. Driver-linked items reach the OWNER's digest; `canDeliver` boundaries hold; the milestone is stamped even when a send is blocked (no retry loops). Message: `sendFn(phone, text, null, 'overdue_digest', { count, worst_item, worst_days })` with a free-form fallback. Schema carriers: `npm run migrate:overdue-digest` (idempotent) + boot ensure (`ensureOverdueDigestTable`) + staging DDL + `RESET_TABLES`/TRUNCATE/cascade + `testCleanup` + `profileWipe` + Test 10 — **applied live**.

**Template (D7).** `overdue_digest` (`META_TPL_OVERDUE_DIGEST`, Utility, en, `{{1}}` count / `{{2}}` worst item / `{{3}}` worst days) in `PROACTIVE_TEMPLATE_KINDS` (17 kinds), `docs/TEMPLATES.md` entry 17 + suggested name, `envAudit` META WHATSAPP section and `.env.example`. Knob unset = byte-identical free-form text; the operator submits `saka_overdue_digest` in Business Manager in parallel.

### 230b. v1.92.1 (Phase 29 patch) — the digest template's Quick Reply button (2026-11-09)

**Found before activation (rule 44).** The operator opened `saka_overdue_digest` in Meta Business Manager (still unapproved/pending) and shared a screenshot: the template carries a **button** ("Reminders"). The v1.92.0 registry declared `overdue_digest` as a body-only kind, so the first send after `META_TPL_OVERDUE_DIGEST` was set would have hit the exact v1.87.3 failure class — Meta `131008: Button at index 0 ... requires a parameter` — outside the 24-hour window, where the text fallback cannot deliver. **Nothing was activated:** the env var stays unset and no live send was attempted.

**Operator confirmation (rule 54).** The operator re-checked Business Manager: the button is a **Quick Reply** — text **"Reminders"**, type **Custom**. A Quick Reply returns the button text as a user message and takes **NO parameters**.

**The fix (data-driven, rule 55).** `PROACTIVE_TEMPLATE_KINDS.overdue_digest` now declares `buttons: [{ subType: 'quick_reply', index: 0 }]`. `templateButtonState()` (new pure export; `templateButtonsForKind()` delegates to it) emits a Quick Reply as `{ type: 'button', sub_type: 'quick_reply', index: '0' }` **without a `parameters` key** — a parameter on a quick reply is what Meta rejects — while URL buttons keep the v1.87.3 contract (a declared `variable`; missing → `{ mode: 'text', reason: 'button_parameter_missing' }`, never a broken button). `sendWhatsAppTemplate` already forwards components in order, so the wire payload is body first, then the parameter-free button. Body-only kinds keep the unchanged one-component payload (pinned).

**Inbound (the button must DO something).** `parseInteractiveReply` already reads `interactive.button_reply { id, title }` and resolves registered ids case-insensitively (`reminders`/`remind_me` → `reminders`). v1.92.1 adds `BUTTON_TITLE_PHRASES` — a TITLE alias for an UNREGISTERED id (Meta may hand back a generated id): `Reminders` / `Reminder` / `Remind me` all resolve to the typed phrase **`reminders`**, which the deterministic `reminders_list` read lane already owns (`detectRemindersListCommand` matches the one-word operator). This keeps the D1 law: "Remind me" must never start the reminder-creation quiz from this button.

**Proof (no Meta call).** `test_proactive_templates` 74 assertions (+9): the registry pins `quick_reply`; the component has no parameters; the exact wire payload is body `3|Insurance (KDA 123A)|5` + `{ type: 'button', sub_type: 'quick_reply', index: '0' }`; `deploy_live` stays body-only. `test_interactive_reply` 53 (+4): the title registry is exact and frozen; `"Reminders"` / `"REMINDERS"` / `"Remind me"` all answer `reminders`; an unregistered id keeps its payload for auditing. The first real send after Meta approval remains the operator-visible confirmation.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/proactiveTemplates.js` (kind buttons + `templateButtonState` + resolver reason), `src/routes/whatsapp/interactive.js` (`BUTTON_TITLE_PHRASES` + parse), `docs/TEMPLATES.md` (entry 17 button contract), `.env.example` (no new knob — the confirmation needs none), `test_proactive_templates.js` (+9), `test_interactive_reply.js` (+4), `package.json` (1.92.1), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), `SAKA_FLEET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (this section + history + version), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_proactive_templates (74), test_interactive_reply (53), test_read_registry (231), test_notifications (22), test_error_logging (22 — ratchet holds), test_env_audit (59), test_vehicle_documents, test_doc_sync, test_kb_docs, test_landing_static, `npm run health` — green.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *"a template's component shape drifts from what Meta actually approved"* → siblings audited: every registry kind (`auth_otp` URL button still parameterised and pinned; `overdue_digest` now quick_reply; the other 15 body-only and pinned to `[]` via `templateButtonState`); the inbound side swept for the matching reply shape (`button_reply`, `list_reply`, legacy `button`, quick-edit ids, locked VIN/date) — the new title alias sits AFTER registered ids and quick-edit resolution, so it can never hijack an existing lane. Left with reasons: `docs/TEMPLATES.md` §5 button-payload registry (still the contract for future button templates).

No rule was edited. **Decision impact:** none for users until the operator sets `META_TPL_OVERDUE_DIGEST`; after that the digest delivers outside the 24-hour window with a working "Reminders" button whose tap opens the reminders list.

### 231. v1.93.0 (Phase 30) — mobile (A5) PDFs, the logbook invitation, the pre-vehicle stash and the expense-kind guard (2026-11-09)

**Scope.** Four polish items in one release, executed smallest-to-largest (D5): the expense-kind guard, the pre-vehicle document stash, the registration logbook invitation, then the phone PDF variant. No new tables, no new environment knobs, no protected paths. Rule 42 gate: 0 open `remediation_proposals` at audit time.

#### 231.1 Task 4 (P2-11) — kind-impossible expenses are REFUSED (D2)

- **The gap (live-audited).** `expenseTypeChoices()` already scoped the MENU by `EXPENSE_TYPES[].kinds`, but free text bypassed it: the quiz (`normalizeExpenseType`) and the quick-log lane accepted "tyres" on a generator and wrote it. Live DB at audit: 2 vehicles / 4 expense rows / **0** mismatches, so no reconciliation backfill was needed; the guard covers every future write.
- **One pure validator** (`expenseCatalog.js`): `validateExpenseTypeForAssetKind(expenseType, assetKind)` → `{ ok, type, kind, suggestion?, message? }`. `Other`, unknown text and any kind-valid type pass; a mismatch returns the warm engine copy (`"Generators don't have tyres — did you mean Consumables? Reply *Consumables* or pick another type."`) plus `nearestKindType()` — curated type×kind pairs first, then a same-category sibling on the kind's menu, then the kind's first menu type; `expenseKindNoun()` supplies the plural (Cars / Boats / Heavy equipment).
- **Three write lanes (rule 51 sweep):** (1) `quizEngine` `case 'log_expense'` validates BEFORE the duplicate guard and any insert; on refusal only `expense_type` is dropped (`phase='question'`, amount and the rest kept) so the next turn re-collects it; (2) `commands.js handleLogExpenseTurn` refuses before the duplicate guard; (3) `csvImport.validateImportRows` adds the `kind_mismatch` preview error + copy (the dashboard import is the third sibling). **D2: blocking, never a warning** — a kind-impossible row would pollute report categories forever, the refusal always names a valid alternative, and `Other` stays the honest escape.
- **Proof:** `test_expense_catalog` +7 (98), `test_quiz_flow` +6 (228 suite total incl. Tasks 2-3), `test_first_message_flow` +2 (quick-log refusal writes nothing), `test_csv_import` +3.

#### 231.2 Task 3 — pre-vehicle document stash (D3)

- **The gap (documented TODO).** `media.js resolveReceiptVault` discarded a vaultable document (logbook/insurance/inspection/road licence) when no vehicle existed yet: `targetVehicle` was null, so nothing was vaulted and the file could never be linked.
- **One engine** (`src/services/documentStash.js`, new): `buildDocumentStash()` (JSON-safe metadata + transient buffer + 24 h expiry), `isDocumentStashExpired()`, `replayDocumentStash()` → `{ ok, reason, line }` using the existing `vaultVehicleDocument` (media_id dedupe, free-tier parsed-only handled there) and `LOGBOOK_UPLOAD_COPY`.
- **Durability:** `session.pendingDocumentStash` rides the turn; `sessionStore.stripTransientSessionFields()` removes ONLY the buffer before every `chat_sessions` write (one call site: `hooks.persistTurnSnapshot`), so the row stays small. On a cold instance the replay re-downloads the media from Meta once (`downloadWhatsAppMedia`); if that fails the completion card asks the user to re-send — nothing is invented.
- **Replay:** `quizEngine` registration completion (after `saved.success`, using the new `saved.vehicleId`) files the stash under the new asset and appends the engine line; the stash is single-use and cleared in every outcome. No schema change.

#### 231.3 Task 2 — the logbook invitation at registration completion

- `flowKnowledge.LOGBOOK_UPLOAD_COPY` (data) + `resolveLogbookUploadCopy()` (pure decision): a stash outcome line wins; a prefilled `document_id` never re-asks; storage copy only when `receiptVaultStorage !== false`, otherwise the honest Free variant ("Photo storage is a paid feature."). `quizEngine` appends the line after the completion card (the launch-award precedent) — zero AI tokens, never a false promise. `getEntitlements` (already imported) resolves when messages.js does not pass `ctx.entitlements`.
- The playbook + core prompt carry the same copy and law (rule 13/60), pinned by `test_agent_training` (+2).

- **Geometry:** `SAKA_PDF_GEOMETRY` now also exports `minFontFloor: 0`; `SAKA_PDF_GEOMETRY_MOBILE` = 419×595, margin 36, content 347, floor 10; `resolvePdfGeometry(variant)` / `normalizePdfVariant(variant)` (unknown → A4). `SAKA_PDF_GEOMETRY` keeps its A4 numbers, so every existing pin holds.

The dashboard records page offers `PDF (A4)` and `PDF (phone)`; the reports builder has both submit buttons (`formaction`).
- **Proof:** `test_pdf_engine` +12 (104: A5 geometry, centering, floor, whitelist, MediaBox A5, compact ledger, 2-column grid, unknown → A4) and the existing A4 pins untouched; `test_dashboard` +13 (896: `?variant=mobile` on both routes, iPhone UA → A5, desktop/explicit A4 → A4, both links + builder button); `test_report_builders` +3 (91: the shared renderer threads the variant, default stays A4); `test_report_lane` 34 unchanged; `test_agent_training` 240.

**Scope.** Six landing-page items plus the dashboard brand target, one commit. **No schema change, no new dependency, no backend flow/prompt change** (so `docs:gen` was not needed). #### 232.1 The launch banner (Tasks 1-2)

- **Copy (D5).** `landing/index.html` now carries exactly: *"🎉 Launch offer — Sign up and activate trial to get an extended 6-month trial, zero payment."* followed by the live slot pill (`#launchSlots`). The `launchSlotsTotal` / `launchAwardDays` spans are gone (D8); `main.js` still pushes `launch_award_days` from the API body, and the opt-in label + dynamic hero note speak the same offer (the note names `6-month` when `award_days >= 180`, otherwise the exact day count).
- **Mobile + sticky (Task 2).** The banner already lived inside the sticky header and stacked at ≤640px; the real defect was the drawer's hardcoded `104px` top padding, which hid its first items behind a taller banner header. `nav.js` now publishes the header's real height (`syncHeaderOffset()` → `--nav-h`, re-synced on resize and on the `saka:nav-sync` event that `main.js` dispatches when the banner is revealed or dismissed), and `.nav-menu` uses `padding: calc(var(--nav-h, 68px) + 36px) 24px 32px`. The banner gained `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; `.nav` gained `transform: translateZ(0)` for iOS sticky painting.

- **Breakpoint (D1).** The burger/drawer block moved from 960 → **1280px** in `styles.css` and `nav.js` (resize close). Above 1280 the five anchors show inline. With 8 interactive items and a 335px lockup, the inline row needed ~1050-1150px and `.wrap` caps at 1120 — the documented squeeze.

The square `logo-mark.png` (30×30, decorative `aria-hidden`) replaces the 9.9:1 lockup at ≤480px — the only physical way the 375px header can hold the logo, Log In and the burger. The full lockup element keeps its `width="335" height="34"` attributes for the pinned contract, and the same markup ships on `privacy/terms/status/data-deletion`.
- **Header CTAs (D3/D4).** The ghost "Pricing" CTA was removed; `.nav-cta .btn-primary` is hidden at ≤960 (the drawer already carries "Get Started Free" as `.nav-menu-cta`), while `.nav-login` stays `inline-flex` at every width (v1.86.0 decision). The **footer** gains a Support `mailto:` link — the nav stays five items (FAQ already there).

- `main.js` now exposes **`renderPricing(interval)`** (USD defaults + local currency through one path): monthly → `$9.99` / *per month*; annual → `$83.92` / *per year · save 30%*; the Free card is `$0` / *forever* in both modes; the add-on note appends *(add-ons are monthly)* in annual mode. `wirePricingToggle()` reads/writes `localStorage['saka_pricing_interval']` (storage-blocked is ignored) and renders immediately; `localizePricing()` stores `{ currency, rate, locale }`, localises the add-on base, then calls the same renderer. The annual figures are exactly 70% of 12×monthly (verified against the tier registry and pinned by assertion). `data-usd-monthly` / `data-usd-annual` / `data-addon-usd` are untouched, and the JSON-LD stays monthly USD for SEO.

#### 233.1 Task 1 — the dashboard drawer (D1/D2)

- `renderPageShell` now renders a `.nav-burger` (48px hit area, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`aria-label`, three spans that morph via `body.nav-open`) inside `.bar-inner`, plus a `.nav-menu` `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` drawer before `</body>` and ONE vanilla IIFE that clones the SAME `.nav` anchors into `.nav-menu-inner` (no duplicated markup), publishes the real header height as `--bar-h`, closes on Escape/backdrop/link-tap/resize >1024 and focuses the first link on open. On pages with no nav anchors (the login doors) the script removes the burger outright, so a dead button never appears.
- `DASHBOARD_CSS` gains `.nav-burger`/`.nav-menu`/`.nav-menu-inner` styling and an `@media (max-width: 1024px)` block that hides the strip, shows the burger and makes the drawer `position:fixed` from `var(--bar-h)` to the viewport bottom at `z-index:50`; `prefers-reduced-motion` renders the finished link state (the rise animation is the only way links become visible). The 11-link strip stays above 1024px (D1).
- **D2 proof.** `withImpersonationBanner` (unchanged) replaces `</header>`; the drawer markup lives at the end of `<body>`, so the banner's DOM index is always lower — pinned by test. The banner's inline `z-index:60` stays above the drawer's 50.

#### 233.2 Task 2 — the dual-role lane toggle (D3)

- **New `POST /d/lane/switch`** (own scope, flag gate → Origin guard → 5/5-min rate limit): reads `saka_dash` → `getSessionByToken`; **refuses while the `saka_dash_as` impersonation cookie is present** ("Exit impersonation to switch lanes"); admin sessions refused (no lanes); lane must be owner|driver; a same-lane request 303s home (idempotent). The target lane must really exist (`resolveDashboardRole` → `isOwner`/`isDriver`), then the SAME sign-in gates run: owner → `getEntitlements` trial/paid (`not_entitled`), driver → `hasLiveDriverAssignment`. On success it updates `dashboard_sessions.session_role` on the caller's OWN row and 303s to `dashboardHomeFor(lane)` (`/d` or `/d/driver`). No schema change — `session_role` has carried the lane since v1.76.0.
- **UI (second `onSend` hook beside the impersonation one).** `requireRoleSession` attaches `request.sakaLane = await resolveDashboardRole({ profile: { id: session.ownerId } })` for owner/driver sessions (admin pages skip it); `withLaneSwitcher` injects a `.lane-switch` strip after `</header>` ONLY when `lane.isOwner && lane.isDriver` and `!request.sakaImpersonation`. Single-role sessions render nothing; the active lane carries `.active` + `aria-current`.
- **Vehicle picker.** New exported `loadAssignedVehicles` lists a driver's live assignments (cap 50, always `assigned_driver_id`-scoped); `/d/driver`, `/d/driver/daybook` and `/d/driver/compliance` parse `?vehicle=`, **403 an id outside the assignments** ("That vehicle is not assigned to you"), and thread the valid pick into `buildDriverHome` / `buildDriverDaybookPageData` / `buildDriverSelfCompliancePage` (`loadAssignedVehicle` + `buildDriverDaybook` already accepted a vehicle id; the assignment check is the new guard). The renderers show a `.vehicle-switch` link strip only when >1 assignment.
- **WhatsApp `dashboard` untouched** — owner-first resolution stays exactly as v1.76.0 defined it.

#### 233.3 Task 3 — the drip-feed feature tips (D4/D7/D9)

- **Schema (additive, idempotent):** `trial_sessions.feature_nudge_sent_at`, `feature_nudge_followup_sent_at`, `feature_nudge_key text`. Carriers: `SUBSCRIPTION_SCHEMA_SQL` (boot ensure + `provision_staging_schema` step), the shared `TRIAL_FEATURE_NUDGE_SQL` (`trialSchema.js`) applied by `npm run migrate:trial-feature-nudge` (`scripts/run_trial_feature_nudge_migration.js`), and `test_db_reset_scope` pins all three + the npm script.
- **Stage** in `runTrialLifecycleSweep` (after the activation reward, before the T+7 un-activated nudge): OFF unless `featureNudgeEnabled()` (env read per call) AND the fetched row actually carries the stamp columns (an un-migrated schema sends NOTHING — no message loop, rule 50). Eligible: `activated` + `activated_at`, status ACTIVE/EXTENDED, a phone, not paid-live. At `T+12h` it resolves the checklist from canonical ledgers (`dashboard_sessions`, `chat_history` `[voice note]`, `usage_counters.report_count`, `expense_logs` via owned vehicles or `driver_id`, `vehicle_documents` via owned vehicles), picks the FIRST unexplored feature (registry order pinned), stamps `feature_nudge_sent_at` + `feature_nudge_key` and sends `featureTipText` with kind `feature_tip` + `{ feature, link }`. At `T+48h` it re-checks that SAME feature: engaged → the follow-up is stamped WITHOUT sending (the ladder closes); still unexplored → ONE follow-up ("Still worth a try"), then closed. All-explored → both stamps with no sends. Per-sweep cap 10 (`FEATURE_NUDGE_SWEEP_CAP`). No overlap with T+7/T-3/T-24/GRACE (those anchor on `started_at`/`ends_at`; T+7 only fires when NOT activated — one targeted assertion each).
- **Template kind:** `feature_tip` appended LAST in `PROACTIVE_TEMPLATE_KINDS` (`META_TPL_FEATURE_TIP`, variables `feature,link`); `docs/TEMPLATES.md` entry 18 + suggested name `saka_feature_tip`, with the explicit Meta-review caveat (the only template that carries a URL in a body variable; knob unset = free-form tip inside the 24-hour window).
- **Copy (zero tokens):** `"🎯 Tip: try <feature> — <link>\n\n<hint>. One minute and Saka does the rest."`; links are engine-owned (`app.sakafleet.com/d/login` for the dashboard, `wa.me` deep links for WhatsApp lanes).

Each component is parameter-free — the 131008-safe shape confirmed in v1.92.1 — and a body-only template (`saka_feature_tip`) keeps the unchanged one-component payload.

### 234. v1.96.0 — superadmin template test-fire + reply-button audit (2026-11-10)

**Why.** After v1.95.1 the operator had no way to (a) see an approved template actually arrive without waiting for a real customer event, or (b) prove that every reply button on every template routes to a live lane. Two deterministic, zero-token superadmin commands close both gaps; nothing customer-facing changes.

**Part 1 — `admin tpl test [kind|all]` (D1/D2/D3).**
- **Command.** Superadmin-only by construction (the admin hub is reached only for `SUPERADMIN_PHONE`) and 30-minute-session-gated by dispatch position (the branch sits after the TTL check in `handleSuperadminFlow`; source-pinned). Sender AND recipient = `SUPERADMIN_PHONE`: unset → graceful `no_recipient` refusal, nothing sent, one audit row. Bare `admin tpl test` prints usage (never auto-fires); an unknown kind names the 18 registry kinds.
- **Fixtures (D3).** `TEMPLATE_TEST_FIXTURES` (frozen, beside `PROACTIVE_TEMPLATE_KINDS`) holds one sample `templateVars` per kind, satisfying the declared body variables AND buttons (`auth_otp`'s URL button reuses `code`); `TEMPLATE_SUGGESTED_NAMES` (frozen) names the expected template for an unset knob (exceptions `re_engagement → saka_reengage`, `auth_otp → saka_otp`). Both pinned 18/18.
- **Probe (D2).** `sendWhatsAppTemplateProbe` wraps the SAME internal `postWhatsAppMessage`, which now takes an OPTIONAL `capture` sink: on a 2xx the parsed body's `messages[0].id` becomes the wamid. The existing boolean senders keep 2-arg calls and boolean returns (source-pinned); the blocklist check runs BEFORE posting (a blocked recipient returns `delivery_blocked`, makes zero network calls, and the attempt is still audited). The probe module imports ONLY `proactiveTemplates.js` + `metaMessenger.js` (source-pinned), so it can never stamp a nudge, deploy marker, queue row or re-engage marker.
- **Limiter.** ≤5 sends / 10 minutes per clean phone via a module-level sliding-window `Map` (mirrors `processedWebhooksCache`). Per-instance is acceptable: operator-triggered only, per-phone serial queue, worst case one extra audited fire to the superadmin's own number. `all` paces the registry, reports per-kind outcome and stops at the window with "cooling down — run again in N minutes" plus the remaining kinds.
- **Honest copy.** `sent — wamid X` / `rejected by Meta — no wamid` / `delivery blocked (no wamid)` / `credentials missing (no wamid)` / `knob unset — expected <suggested name>`; the footer points delivery status at Cloud Logging / the Meta console (the status webhook does not persist to a table). Every attempt writes one `ADMIN_TEMPLATE_TEST` row (kind, templateName, wamid, fixtureVars, status, env/expectedName where relevant).

**Part 2 — `admin tpl buttons` (D4/D5).**
- **Digest.** Declared = the 3 button-bearing kinds from the registry + the new frozen `TEMPLATE_BUTTON_TITLES` (approved titles; the auth_otp URL button declares none). Mapped = `BUTTON_TITLE_PHRASES` (7). Captured = `error_logs` route `/webhook/whatsapp/interactive` (unrecognized shapes; `error_logs` has no phone column, so the A1 `phone=<…>` context inside `error_message` is filtered in code, both plus/no-plus forms) PLUS `chat_history` rows for the superadmin phone whose `message` EXACTLY equals a mapped target phrase (`.in()` on the deduped values — `reminders`, `fuel`, `set reminder`, `log expense`, `dashboard` — re-checked in the pure builder, never a substring). The digest renders `captured → declared → mapped` and flags any tap without a named claimant, plus declared-but-unmapped titles. Audited `ADMIN_TEMPLATE_BUTTONS`.
- **Boundary-preserving move.** The two frozen registries moved from the route leaf `src/routes/whatsapp/interactive.js` to `src/services/interactiveReply.js` (a service cannot import a route module under §190). The leaf re-exports the SAME objects, so every importer and pin is unchanged (test-pinned identity).
- **Reachability law (D5).** One assertion per title phrase against its real claimant: `reminders`/`reminder`/`remind me` → `READ_COMMANDS` lane `reminders_list`; `set reminder` → `detectQuizStart` `set_reminder`; `log expense` → `detectQuizStart` `log_expense`; `dashboard` → `READ_COMMANDS` lane `dashboard`. **Design gap (operator decision (a): flagged, not fixed):** the `fuel` value has NO deterministic claimant — `detectQuizStart` requires a `log|record` prefix, so a bare-`fuel` tap works only through the AI intent path (`LOG_EXPENSE → intentMap`). The intended fix (a deterministic `^(?:fuel|refuel)$` → `log_expense` pattern) is recorded here; the suite pins today's behaviour so the gap can never be silently forgotten. Payload-phrase siblings swept in the same suite (reminders / help / keep all / subscription).

**Proof.** `test_proactive_templates` **84 → 93** (+9: 18/18 fixtures, fixture→wire routing, suggested names + exceptions, button-title counts), `test_template_testfire` **new, 59** (limiter, probe statuses incl. wamid/rejected/blocked/no-credentials, boolean-sender contract, usage/unknown/no-recipient/unset-knob, all-pacing, honest copy per outcome, import + dispatch-position source pins, digest + exact-match query pins), `test_interactive_reply` **59 → 70** (+11: 7 reachability pins incl. the documented `fuel` gap, re-export identity, payload-phrase sweep), `test_superadmin` +8 pure assertions (parse all/kind/bare/buttons + help listing).

### 234.1. v1.96.1 — the optional target phone for `admin tpl test`

**Why.** The operator needs to see a template on a regular user's device, not just the superadmin's phone.

**Parse (deterministic, zero tokens).** `parseSuperadminCommand` matches `admin tpl test(?:\s+(\S+))?(?:\s+(\S+))?` and classifies arg1: a kind (`all` or `[a-z_]+`) makes arg2 the target; otherwise arg1 is the target with `kind:null` (usage — nothing is sent). Bare `admin tpl test` keeps its pinned usage path, and a malformed target never reaches the AI classifier (the runner refuses it).

**Execution.** `runTemplateTestFire` accepts `targetPhone`; the destination is `normalizeWhatsAppTargetPhone(targetPhone)` or, when omitted, `SUPERADMIN_PHONE`. Normalisation: digits only; a leading `00` is an international prefix; a leading `0` with exactly 10 digits resolves to Kenya `+254…`; the final number must be 9–15 digits or the command returns `invalid_target` (zero sends, one audit row, an example in the reply). The 5/10-min sliding window is keyed to the ADMIN phone (the operator), never the target; `maskWhatsAppTargetPhone` stores `+2547****2529` (last 4 only) on every `ADMIN_TEMPLATE_TEST` row, and the reply header names the masked target. The delivery blocklist still checks the actual recipient inside `sendWhatsAppTemplateProbe`.

**Boundary + proof.** The two helpers live in `metaMessenger.js`, so `templateTestFire.js` still imports ONLY `proactiveTemplates.js` + `metaMessenger.js` (the side-effect-free pin holds). `webOnboarding.normalizePhoneE164` was audited and rejected for this use (it keeps the leading `0` — `0734852529` → `+0734852529`). `test_superadmin` +7 parse assertions (with/without/junk target); `test_template_testfire` 59 → 70 (helper pins, override send, operator-keyed window, masked audit, invalid-target refusal + copy).

**Live activation (2026-11-10).** All 18 `META_TPL_*` knobs are now set on Cloud Run (`saka-fleet`, project `saka-fleet-v1`, region `europe-west1`, revision `saka-fleet-00400-kr8`, 100% traffic; health via `/api/health` — the Google edge 404s `/healthz` by design, index.js aliases it). This update added the 11 remaining knobs: `SERVICE_REMINDER`, `EXPIRY_REMINDER`, `TRIAL_ENDING`, `TRIAL_GRACE`, `DUNNING`, `DRIVER_UNASSIGNED`, `WINBACK`, `EVAL_DIGEST_PING`, `CARE_ESCALATION`, `DRIVER_ACTIVITY`, `FLEET_AUTO_AUDIT` (value `fleet_auto_audit` — confirm the approved Meta name; the documented suggestion is `saka_fleet_auto_audit`). `system_config.deploy.last_deployed_revision` = the same revision, so the LIVE alert fired exactly once.

### 234.2. v1.96.3 — the first live test-fire: cursor, tap bypass, audit target

**Why.** The operator's first REAL `admin tpl test all` (2026-11-10, 22:03 and 22:15) sent the same five kinds both times (`service_reminder`, `expiry_reminder`, `trial_ending`, `trial_grace`, `dunning`) and never reached `re_engagement` or the remaining 13; a 09:37 tap on "Accept"/"Log Fuel" from the superadmin phone was answered "🤔 I'm not sure which admin action that is."; and `admin tpl buttons` at 22:16 only saw the superadmin's own taps although the template went to `0734852529`. Three operator-tool defects, three deterministic fixes — no customer flow, prompt, schema or env change.

**Part 1 — `all` resumes where it stopped (D1).** Root cause: `runTemplateTestFire` always built `targets = [...TEMPLATE_TEST_KINDS]`, so every `all` run re-sent kinds 0-4 and stopped at the 5/10-min window; 13 kinds were unreachable through `all`. Fix: a module-level `testFireCursor` (`clean operator phone → { kinds:Set, startedAt }`, `TEMPLATE_TEST_CURSOR_TTL_MS` 1 h, per Cloud Run instance like the rate window) with three pure-ish helpers — `templateTestCursorKinds` (read), `markTemplateTestKindSent` (write), `clearTemplateTestCursor`. The runner slices the registry from the first kind not in the cursor; a completed 18/18 sweep clears and wraps to 0; ONLY a `status === 'sent'` result advances it, so `unset_knob` / `delivery_blocked` / rejected kinds stay retryable (they also do not consume a window slot when refused pre-send). The cursor is keyed to the same OPERATOR key as the rate window (`adminPhone || recipient`); single-kind fires never read or write it. The outcome gains `sentKinds`, and the reply renders `Session progress: N/18` plus "_`all` resumes at the first remaining kind_". No parser change, no new syntax, no persistence (an instance restart resets it — documented, same as the window).

**Part 2 — a tap bypasses the admin gate (D2).** Root cause: a tap resolves to its phrase (`fuel`, `accept`, …), then `messages.js` fed that text into `handleAdminIntercepts`; from the superadmin phone `parseSuperadminCommand` returned `UNKNOWN` (the `ADMIN_DIRECTIVE_RE` gate), the Admin AI Agent picked `none`, and `buildAdminClarifyReply` answered — the tap never reached a live lane. Fix: `messages.js` passes `isInteractiveTap: Boolean(messageObj?.interactive || messageObj?.button)` (ANY tap shape — recognized, quick-edit, or A1-diagnosed), and `handleAdminIntercepts` returns `null` before the client guard, so the care-console leg, `handleSuperadminFlow` AND the admin-hub fallback all step aside in one place. Typed text is byte-identically gated (pinned by a poison-client negative control). The admin's multi-role coexistence (architecture §7) now extends to explicit taps.

**Part 3 — `admin tpl buttons [target_phone]` (D3).** Root cause: the parse accepted only the bare form and the dispatch hardcoded `adminPhone: formattedPhone`, so taps from the device the test was fired at were invisible. Fix: deterministic regex `admin tpl buttons(?:\s+(\S+))?` returns `targetPhone`; `runTemplateButtonAudit` gains `targetPhone`, normalises through the SAME `normalizeWhatsAppTargetPhone`, refuses an invalid target with `status:'invalid_target'` and ZERO reads (the digest says so and names the input), and queries `error_logs` + `chat_history` for the resolved phone. The result carries `auditPhone` (masked, `+2547****2529`) rendered as an `Auditing:` header; the `ADMIN_TEMPLATE_BUTTONS` audit row gains `audited_phone` + `status`. Omitted target = the admin's own phone (v1.96.0 behaviour, byte-identical).

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) "an operator-triggered loop forgets its place across invocations"* → sibling `all` pacing fixed; the 5/10-min rate window is deliberately time-keyed and unchanged. *(ii) "a gate that only means to catch typed text answers an explicit choice"* → siblings: the care-console leg, the superadmin hub and the admin-hub fallback (all fixed by the one early return), the A1 unrecognized-tap diagnostic (now skips the hub too), typed admin commands (deliberately unchanged, pinned). *(iii) "a read scoped to the caller instead of the subject"* → `admin tpl test [target_phone]` already correct (v1.96.1, untouched); `admin tpl buttons [target_phone]` fixed; `admin wipe <phone>` audited and left (the phone is already the subject).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/templateTestFire.js` (cursor consts/map/helpers, `runTemplateTestFire`, `formatTemplateTestReply`, `runTemplateButtonAudit`, `formatTemplateButtonDigest`, exports), `src/services/superadmin.js` (`parseSuperadminCommand`, `ADMIN_TEMPLATE_BUTTONS` dispatch, help registry), `src/routes/whatsapp/messages.js` (intercept call), `src/routes/whatsapp/admin.js` (`handleAdminIntercepts`), `test_template_testfire.js` (70 → 88), `test_interactive_reply.js` (70 → 75), `test_superadmin.js` (+5), `docs/TEMPLATES.md` (§6), `package.json` (1.96.3), `landing/data/changelog.json`, this section + history + version, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_template_testfire (88), test_interactive_reply (75), test_superadmin (integration, green), test_ocr_flow (153), test_doc_sync, `npm run docs:check`, `npm run health` — green.

**Operator actions.** `adminstart` → `admin tpl test re_engagement 0734852529` (target device) or `admin tpl test re_engagement` (superadmin default) → tap the arrived button (quiz-starting taps: reply `cancel`) → `admin tpl buttons`. Rollback = revert the commit / redeploy the previous revision; no schema, env or data to undo.

### 235. v1.96.2 — the live chat audit (+254734852529): evidence never becomes a query, and money stays law-abiding (2026-11-10)

**The audit (rules 42/44/54).** A full read of the conversation (322 `chat_history` rows + 324 transcripts), the ledger (5 expenses), receipts (1), transfers (2, both cancelled), reminders (2), compliances (1 vehicle + 2 driver) and **12 friction rows** with **0 open remediation proposals**. It found five live defects. Four older ones were verified already fixed at HEAD and deliberately **not** re-fixed: launch-award completion copy (v1.87.0 — this exact account was that fix's live evidence: slot 1, `LAUNCH183-1`, ends 2027-05-11), nickname editing (v1.89.2), the KE fiscal amount + receipt link (v1.87.4) and the dashboard transfer cancel (v1.87.5). The driver compliance card was proved correct with a live call — it lists **both** the licence and the PSV badge, so the 06:24 miss was a stale surface, not a current defect.

**D1 — evidence is never a ledger question.** A photo-only receipt re-send produced an OCR dump with no vault row, so `receiptQuizStartFor` returned null and the **records lane** claimed the dump ("Nothing under fuel + repairs expenses … yet", five times). Two laws now hold: (1) `parseRecordQuestion` returns `document-evidence` for a legal-receipt/fiscal-receipt/tax-invoice/registration-certificate body (rule 36/37) and `log-command` for a leading add/log/save verb that names what to log; (2) `receiptQuizStartFor` takes an explicit `isDuplicateReceipt` fact — **every fresh receipt opens the confirmation quiz**, vaulted or not, and only a duplicate stays out (the v1.87.4 no-second-draft law). `applyPostAiIntentFixes` routes `log-command` to `LOG_EXPENSE` (earnings → `LOG_EARNINGS`).

**D2 — a confirmation's executor is the thing it names.** "Delete last entry" (fuel preview) → "No. Delete last compliance" left the fuel-delete pending alive; the model invented a compliance-delete card and the next "Delete" **deleted the fuel row**. New pure `detectNonLedgerTarget()` in `entryAnswers.js`: a delete/remove request naming a compliance/reminder target returns `{type:'none', dropPending:true, blockedTarget}`; the `ledger_turn` lane claims it and answers deterministically (compliance dates are facts — correct with the right date; reminders are not ledger rows). Receipt/document/vehicle targets drop the stale prompt and let their own lanes run. Bare `DELETE` and numbered `delete 2` are unchanged (pinned).

**D3 — money is engine-owned.** Two live amount errors: "300 parking … 7th, 8th and 9th of November" → **315** (bare ordinals survived the date mask; "and" was additive) and "Price of diesel 222.7kes/liter" → the **amount**, with "NOZZLE: 1" as the volume. `moneyLexicon` now masks bare ordinals and skips `st|nd|rd|th` tails; `isUnitPriceOnly()` is the shared law; the quick-log lane takes `parseMoneyStory().amount` before any AI value and rejects a unit-price-only AI amount; `extractVehicleAttributes` stores `unit_price` instead of `amount`; the quiz drops AI litres on a document dump unless the text carries real litre evidence (`13.47 X 222.70`, not `NOZZLE: 1`).

**D4 — words that should not be said.** `stripPrematureSaveClaim()` removes a "Saved/Logged/Recorded …" line from every **non-completed** quiz reply (the confirmation gate owns the claim); a complaint family ("never happens again", "never miss to link", "you saved it wrong") now reaches the complaint lane and resets the intent so no expense quiz starts.

**D5 — cancel transfer never starts a transfer.** New `transfer_cancel_hint` read lane: "cancel/stop/abort … transfer" is answered deterministically (names the vehicle and the dashboard cancel, or says nothing is pending) and yields to a live `transfer_seller` flow, `transferFlow` or buyer-OTP sink.

**Live reconciliation.** `receipts.f4d9b896…amount` 11,823 → 3,000 through `scripts/reconcile_receipt_amounts.js` (`--scan` reports linked mismatches; one explicit `--receipt/--amount/--reason --apply` write; audit `RECEIPT_AMOUNT_CORRECTED`), scan now 0 mismatches. All 9 PENDING friction rows closed via `markFrictionDeployed` with per-row resolutions.

**Decisions.** D1 fresh receipts always confirm (only duplicates stay out); D2 compliance/reminder deletes are refused with correction guidance; D3 a unit price is never the spend; D4 a typed volume without a unit ("filled 40") keeps working — the litre-evidence guard applies to document dumps only.

**The report (rules 42/54).** The 08:00 briefing printed `Registered Profiles: 6 (2 owners, 0 drivers)` while `/d/admin` listed only 2 owners. A live read-only probe explained it: **6 live profile rows = 5 registered** (email on file OR the superadmin row, v1.82.0 definition) **+ 1 shell** (no name, no email); 2 registered own a live vehicle, 3 do not.
