### 237. v1.96.5 — the receipt that was filed as a logbook (live 2026-11-11, +254734852529 / KAS628T)

**The report (rules 42/54).** The operator's screenshot showed a `/d/records` row `KAS628T · Fuel · 13.47 L · Ksh 3,000 · Receipt: —`. A live read-only audit proved the whole chain: `expense_logs.863aed9a…` (created 2026-11-11T08:35:18Z) carried `receipt_id: NULL`; the ONLY `receipts` row for the owner was the 11-09 one (`f4d9b896…`); `ocr_requests` for 11-11 held exactly ONE row — media `987949260501656`, **`document_kind: 'logbook'`** — and the transcript showed the fuel quiz open at "How much did you spend?" when the photo arrived, the full e-TIMS OCR text answering the quiz, and the confirm card saving without a link. Worse, `vehicle_documents` held **six junk "logbook" rows that were the same Astrol receipt re-sent six times** (`a5053731`, `14fa83df`, `ca458a9e`, `0eef23d2`, `985dea35`, `12df7fc3`; all with `parsed_data.vin: "P051141264M"` — the station's PIN), and the genuine logbook `bca7003f` had been **superseded by a receipt photo** on 11-10. Offline reproduction against the live tree: `classifyOcrDocument(text) === 'logbook'`, `classifyDocumentFamily(text) === 'logbook'`, `parseDocumentFields(...).fields.vin === 'P051141264M'`.

**Root cause (the exact v1.87.5 defect class, on receipts).** `classifyOcrDocument` tested the LOGBOOK branch (via `looksLikeVin`) **before** the receipt branches; `looksLikeVin` stripped `PIN:`-labelled tokens and `P\d{9}[A-Z]` but not the bare KRA control-unit serial `KRACU0300578490` (15 chars, letters+digits, valid VIN charset) — so a fiscal fuel receipt became a logbook. Downstream, every link trusted that one decision: `resolveReceiptVault` skipped the receipt branch (no `receipts` row → no `receiptPrefill`) and took the document branch (`isVaultableDocumentFamily('logbook')` → vault + supersede), `messages.js` computed `isReceiptDocument = false`, and the quiz consumed the OCR dump via the AI extraction, saving `receipt_id = NULL`. A SECOND gap would have survived the classifier fix: `arbitrateQuizTurn` only carried `receiptPrefill` into a NEW quiz (`!session.quiz`), so a photo sent mid-draft never reached the open draft.

**The fixes.** (1) `ocrService.classifyOcrDocument`: a strong-fiscal guard ABOVE the logbook branch — `START/END OF LEGAL RECEIPT | FISCAL RECEIPT | TAX INVOICE | TOTAL TAX | TAXABLE | BUYER PIN` + fuel/litre evidence → `receipt_fuel` (generic markers only; no country profile leaks — rule 36); insurance stays first (v1.32.1), licence second (v1.87.5). (2) New exported `stripFiscalSerials()` (labelled PINs incl. BUYER/CLIENT, `CU:` serials, `P\d{9}[A-Z]`, bare `KRACU…` invoice numbers) shared by `looksLikeVin` and the Lens `parseLogbook` fallback — `vin: P051141264M` can never be minted again. (3) `documentLens.classifyDocumentFamily`: the missing receipt demotion beside the licence guard — a logbook base with fiscal markers returns `receipt_fuel` / `receipt_general`. (4) `media.js resolveReceiptVault`: `fiscalReceiptLike` (`isKenyaEtimesText` or `TAX INVOICE / TOTAL TAX / TAXABLE`) refuses the document vault AND the logbook prefill — a fiscal receipt can never be stored as a compliance document or supersede a genuine one. (5) `quiz.js injectReceiptLinkIntoDraft()`: an open `log_expense` draft receives the fresh `receipt_id` (engine-only; never asked/rendered/AI-injectable; `restart` drops it; `resolveReceiptLink` still re-verifies ownership). A registration/compliance draft is deliberately NOT hijacked (decision D5, operator-approved). (6) Two siblings caught while proving the fix: `amountFrom` read the tax token `E-8%` as **8** (now rejects percentage tokens, never trusts a tax-component line's next value, scans the fiscal-stripped text with date/time exclusions) and `detectCurrencyFromText` read `RM` (MYR) inside "SCU **INFORMATION**" (alphabetic symbols now require their own word; punctuation symbols like `R$` keep substring behaviour).


**Live reconciliation (rule 56).** The six junk logbook rows were deleted with their `documents` bucket objects (`VEHICLE_DOCUMENT_PURGED_MISCLASSIFIED`), the genuine logbook `bca7003f` restored as current (`VEHICLE_DOCUMENT_RESTORED`), and the 11-11 receipt re-downloaded from Meta (media `987949260501656`), vaulted as a `receipts` row (amount 3,000, 13.47 L, KAS628T) and linked to `expense_logs.863aed9a…` (`RECEIPT_LINK_BACKFILLED`). Verified after the writes: `attachReceiptMatches` → `receiptStatus: 'linked'` (the records page renders **View**), the vehicle page lists only the genuine logbook + insurance, and the compliance Files count is unchanged.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) "a weaker heuristic branch runs before a stronger labelled marker"* → classifier precedence (fixed); Lens family demotions (licence ✓ v1.87.5, receipts fixed); `looksLikeVin`/`parseLogbook` VIN heuristics (hardened via the shared strip); compliance-document intake (fixed — receipts can never enter `vehicle_documents`); mid-quiz prefill (fixed); compliance link at save (audited — four call sites mechanically correct, the pollution entered at intake); quick-log lane (deliberately left — text-only by construction, v1.81.0 D5); CSV import (no media path); dashboard render (audited — `—` was truthful, View for `linked`/`unique` unchanged). *(ii) "a number or symbol read from the wrong place"* → tax-token amount (fixed), fraction-in-word currency (fixed), PIN-as-VIN (fixed), nozzle-as-litre and unit-price-as-spend (already fixed v1.96.2 ✓).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/ocrService.js` (`classifyOcrDocument`, `stripFiscalSerials`, `looksLikeVin`), `src/services/documentLens.js` (`classifyDocumentFamily`, `parseLogbook`, `amountFrom`), `src/services/ocrNormalizer.js` (`detectCurrencyFromText`), `src/routes/whatsapp/media.js` (imports, `resolveReceiptVault`), `src/routes/whatsapp/quiz.js` (`injectReceiptLinkIntoDraft`, `arbitrateQuizTurn`), `test_ocr_flow.js` (145 → 164), `test_quiz_flow.js` (235 → 240), `test_dashboard.js` (934 → 936), `test_ocr_normalizer.js` (38 → 40), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.96.5), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 238. v1.96.6 — Enhanced Conversions on website signup (2026-11-12)

**What changed.** The OTP-verified signup push (`successful_signup`, v1.49.3, event name unchanged) now carries first-party data for GA4 attribution and Google Ads Enhanced Conversions: `user_data: { email, phone_number }` in the SAME dataLayer push as the event. This is the GTM pattern — the container's GA4 / Google Ads tags read a data layer variable named `user_data`; a standalone `gtag('set', 'user_data', …)` is impossible on this site because no raw gtag.js ships: **GTM-TGR68X2X is the single consent-gated hub (v1.49.0)** and adding a second Google tag would double-count conversions. Values ride **unhashed** (Google's documented option); the Google tag hashes with SHA-256 in the browser before transmission.

**Formats are guaranteed, not assumed.** Two pure normalisers in `main.js` re-check the form values at push time (defense in depth — the form already lowercases the email and builds the phone from the `+NNN` country-code select + digits):
- `enhancedEmail(value)` — `.trim().toLowerCase()`, and an address-shape test; anything else becomes `null`.
- `enhancedPhone(value)` — strips spaces/dashes/parens and accepts ONLY `^\+[1-9]\d{7,14}$` (E.164: leading `+`, country code, number — no spaces, no dashes). A national-format number (`0712345678`) or one without its leading `+` is omitted, never guessed.
Only valid values are attached (`userData.email` / `userData.phone_number`); the event still fires when neither exists, and both are read from `window.__onboard`, which is still populated at the `/api/onboard/verify` success branch.

**Consent scope v3 + disclosure (rules 7/56).** Passing hashed email/phone to Google for ad measurement is a material widening of what "Analytics & marketing" means, so `cookieConsent.js` VERSION 2 → 3 forces a fresh opt-in from returning visitors. GTM still loads only after `analytics === true`; the loader now also queues `{ event: 'consent_analytics_granted', analytics: true }` so the container can key Consent Mode (defaults granted are accurate — the container never exists without consent). No consent = no GTM = no transmission; the dataLayer message itself is memory-only. The "Analytics & marketing" settings sentence on ALL six pages, `privacy.html` §11 (new paragraph naming Enhanced Conversions, SHA-256 and E.164 plus the opt-out) and `llms.txt` disclose the consented hashed data; `landing/data/changelog.json` gains a plain-language customer entry.

**Tests (rule 52 — behavioural, not source-matching).** `test_landing_static` Test 23 (+24: 429 → 453) lifts both normalisers out of `main.js` and executes them in a `node:vm` sandbox: `"  Grace.W@Example.COM  "` → `grace.w@example.com`; `"+254 712-345-678"` → `+254712345678` (asserted against `/^\+254\d{9}$/` AND `/^\+[1-9]\d{7,14}$/`); `"0712345678"` and `"254712345678"` → omitted. Source assertions cover the combined push (`user_data: userData`, `userData.email`, `userData.phone_number`), consent v3 + the consent event, and the disclosure on every page/file.

**Operator next steps (GTM UI, not code — rules 54/55).** (1) GA4: `sign_up` tag on the custom event `successful_signup` with "Include user-provided data from your website" → data layer variable `user_data`. (2) Google Ads: conversion tag with Enhanced Conversions on the same variable. (3) Consent Mode: all-granted defaults (accurate — the container only exists after opt-in). Tag Assistant → `https://sakafleet.com` → accept all → test signup; then GA4 DebugView.

**Frames touched.** `landing/assets/js/main.js` (`enhancedEmail`, `enhancedPhone`, `trackSignup`), `landing/assets/js/cookieConsent.js` (VERSION 3, `consent_analytics_granted`, header), `landing/{index,privacy,terms,status,data-deletion,404}.html` (analytics settings copy), `landing/privacy.html` §11, `landing/llms.txt`, `landing/data/changelog.json`, stamped landing assets (`?v=1.96.6`), `test_landing_static.js`, `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.96.6), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_landing_static (453), test_doc_sync (30), test_kb_docs, test_vehicle_documents, `npm run docs:check`, `npm run health` — green.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63 (rules + architecture first; **0 open proposals** verified live), 55 (evolved the existing push + GTM hub — no second Google tag, no new vendor), 56 (the consent-version bump reaches existing visitors; the signup payload applies to every future signup), 51/52 (all six consent-copy siblings swept; behavioural before/after assertions), 33/43 (one version commit; landing FTP deploy + backend deploy on push), 2/13/34 (architecture + CHANGELOG + site feed synced; `flowKnowledge.js` / core prompt intentionally untouched — no intent, flow, field or prompt changed, so rule 13's skill sync is not triggered), 7 (E.164 country-aware; the country-code list is global). No rule edited. **Impact:** consented signups now transmit a correctly formatted hashed email + E.164 phone for ad measurement; without consent nothing transmits; returning visitors must re-consent once.

### 239. v1.96.7 — web signup dead-end + plate escape hatch + single-question nudge law (2026-11-12)

**Why (live evidence, rule 54).** The 24 h ops audit found two friction points. (1) *The ghost signup*: `POST /api/onboard/check` ×4 at 08:57:02–18Z on 11-12, then no `POST /api/onboard`; zero `WEB_ONBOARD_*` audit rows in the window; `checkSignupAvailability` (webOnboarding.js:475) and the route (index.js:650) log nothing, so the typed values are unrecoverable — and the code showed a real dead-end either way: `refreshContinueGate` kept Continue disabled for EVERY `registered` verdict, including UNVERIFIED accounts that the submit path (`inspectExistingSignup` → `'unverified'` → fresh OTP) is built to serve, while `signedUpMessage` gave verified matches a text note with no link and unverified matches no next step at all. (2) *The stalled user* `+254728134729` (11-10, a fresh web signup verified 40 min earlier): "Nissan tiida" → "What type of vehicle are we registering?" → "Nissan tiida hatchback" → the plate question at 18:23:58 → silence; nudges at 18:41 and 19:01 asked for the plate AND offered Restart/Cancel in the same message (Sentinel flagged both as `MULTI_QUESTION_PROMPT`); never returned, 0 vehicles.

**A. Landing UI (landing/index.html, landing/assets/js/main.js).** A verified match keeps Continue disabled (rule 47 — never re-onboard a verified account) and now reveals `#registeredWhatsAppCta` — a live `wa.me/19404407252` button ("💬 Chat with Saka on WhatsApp →", prefilled "Hi Saka, I'm already signed up"). An UNVERIFIED match is allowed through the gate: the note says the verification code will be re-sent and the existing `/api/onboard` flow re-serves it (`inspectExistingSignup` state `'unverified'`). The verified flag rides `availability.verified` from the check response; a network failure still fails OPEN (server-side duplicate block unchanged). The submit-time belt-and-braces guard now blocks only a registered+VERIFIED match.

**B. PII-safe telemetry (index.js).** When `/api/onboard/check` returns `registered` for either field it writes `admin_audit_logs.action='WEB_ONBOARD_CHECK_REGISTERED'` with `{ emailRegistered, phoneRegistered, verified }` — NO typed value — audited via `auditWebOnboardEvent` (actor WEB_ONBOARD), fail-soft, wrapped so telemetry can never block the check. The next ghost signup is diagnosable; the anti-enumeration contract (20/min, per-field only) is untouched.

**C. Plate escape hatch (quizEngine.js).** `isPlateSkipText()` (exported) recognises a closed list of phrases — no plate (yet), no number plate, don't/dont have it/the plate/my plate/a plate, i don't know it/the plate, not with me, logbook not with me, no logbook, later, plate later, not now, not yet, skip, skip plate, i'll send it later, can't remember, forgot, no idea, not sure — normalised (lowercase, curly quotes, collapsed spaces, trailing punctuation) and ALWAYS overruled by `isPlateLike` so a real plate can never be read as a skip. On the `plate_number` field the turn parks a draft and returns the ONE engine-owned line `PLATE_DRAFT_PARKED_REPLY` ("No problem — I've saved your draft… send the plate whenever you're ready"). The draft is the `registration-draft` member of the unified pending family (pendingState.js): 24 h TTL, `freshLog: 'yields'` (a fresh log line is processed and the draft survives), `blockedByQuiz: true` (an open quiz always outranks it), resolver clears on cancel/discard and yields on everything else. `resumeRegistrationDraft()` restores the captured answers through `startQuiz({ prefill })` and feeds the plate through `handleQuizTurn`, so it answers the closed question exactly as if the flow never parked. `src/routes/whatsapp/quiz.js` calls it at the top of `arbitrateQuizTurn` when there is no quiz, a parked draft exists, and the message is plate-like. NO schema change (the approved plan): no vehicle row, no VIN, no trial exists until the plate arrives — rules 9/26 intact.

**D. Copy + nudge law (rule 13/31/60).** The plate question now reads "…(e.g. KDA 123A or the newer KDD 123D) — don't have it handy? Just say *no plate yet* and I'll save your draft.", and the invalid-format message repeats the escape. `FLOW_GUIDANCE.vehicle_registration` names the escape; `FLOW_GUIDANCE['registration-draft']` gives the parked draft its own one-line next step; the `vehicle_registration` playbook `rules` states the escape, resume, cancel and the single-question nudge law; `DEFAULT_SAKA_CORE_PROMPT` gains `PLATE STEP LAW (v1.96.7)`; `conversationEngine.PLATE_DRAFT_NOTE` mirrors it for the composer. The nudges themselves are LLM-composed (no hardcoded literal exists in routes/workers), so the law lives where the composer reads it — a plate-step nudge asks ONLY for the plate and Restart/Cancel follows on the next turn.

**Tests (rule 52).** `test_quiz_flow` (+11: 250) — skip phrases, real-plate/make-model immunity, park reply + `active:false`, pending slot shape, captured answers without a plate, resume on `KDD 123D`, pending consumed, fresh-log yield keeps the draft, `registration-draft` guidance, generator sibling pin (the escape never parks a serial asset), VIN/serial phrase immunity. `test_pending_state` (+7: 444) — 14 slot kinds, fixture, fresh-log `yields` + survival, cancel clears, quiz-gate precedence without destroying the draft, differential replay exempts the new kind with the reason documented (it postdates the frozen v1.63.3 chain). `test_agent_training` (+4: 245) — the core-prompt law, "no plate yet", the playbook nudge law, the guidance line renders. `test_landing_static` (+4 net: 455) — verified-never-advances vs unverified-continues, resend copy, CTA element + wa.me number + `refreshRegisteredCta`. `test_duplicate_signup` (21) unchanged.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Class A — a client-side gate that blocks a path the server supports:* siblings audited → verified match (fixed: CTA), unverified match (fixed: continue → OTP), network failure (already fails open, pinned), Enter-key submit (guard updated), country-code change (re-check preserved). *Class B — a required question with no escape:* siblings audited → serial step on non-road assets (deliberately left: its resume lane must key on the serial parser — a separate tested lane; pinned that the plate escape never leaks there), VIN step (deliberately left: the logbook-photo fallback is offered and VIN is the permanent identifier; pinned that `no vin yet` never triggers the plate escape), optional fields (already skip-able). One targeted assertion per sibling.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/quizEngine.js`, `src/services/pendingState.js`, `src/routes/whatsapp/quiz.js`, `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `src/services/conversationEngine.js`, `landing/index.html`, `landing/assets/js/main.js`, `index.js`, `test_quiz_flow.js`, `test_pending_state.js`, `test_agent_training.js`, `test_landing_static.js`, `package.json` (1.96.7), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 240. v1.96.8 — the mobile cookie banner: visible, tappable, above every overlay (2026-11-13)

**Why (mobile report).** A phone visitor could not submit the website signup. `legalSubmit` (`landing/assets/js/main.js`) correctly gates account creation on `window.__sakaCookies.chosen()` and re-opens the banner via `__sakaCookies.open()`. But the banner sat at `z-index: 90` while the onboarding modal backdrop (`.modal-backdrop`) is a fixed, full-viewport overlay at `z-index: 100`: the bar rendered UNDERNEATH the dimmed backdrop — visible only as a ghost and never clickable — so the form kept answering "accept or reject cookies" with nothing to tap. Two further mobile defects compounded it: `bottom: 14px` had no `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` (the bar hid behind the iOS home indicator / collapsed Safari toolbar) and the one-row `flex-wrap: nowrap` layout squeezed the copy to nothing on 375px phones. The gate's native `alert()` also blocked interaction and pointed nowhere.

**The fix (CSS + JS, no new dependency).**
- `.cookie-banner`: `z-index: 9999` (above `.modal-backdrop` 100, `.cookie-settings-backdrop` 110, `.nav` 60, `.nav-menu` 55, `.launch-banner` 1) and `bottom: calc(14px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`.
- `@media (max-width: 640px)`: the banner wraps, the copy unclamps onto its own row, `.cookie-actions` takes the full width and each button is ≥44px tall (rule 31).
- `cookieConsent.js`: `showBanner()` adds an `attention` class (removed by `hideBanner()` on any choice); `@keyframes cookie-pulse` gives three gentle lime beats and is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- `main.js` gate: `__sakaCookies.open()` + `document.activeElement.blur()` (closes the mobile keyboard) + an inline `#cookieGateErr` line ("One more step — choose cookies in the bar at the bottom of the screen.") shown in the legal step; the native `alert()` is gone and the line clears on the next passing submit.
- Sibling safe areas: `.modal-backdrop` and `.cookie-settings-backdrop` gain `padding-bottom: calc(20px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` so the signup/OTP/settings panels clear the home indicator too.

**Tests (rule 52).** `test_landing_static` Test 24 (+18: 455 → 473): the base banner rule is `position: fixed` with `z-index: 9999`; extracted z-indexes prove 9999 > nav 60, drawer 55, modal 100, settings 110, launch banner 1 (one assertion per sibling); the rule carries `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` inside a `calc()`; exactly one `.cookie-banner` rule sets `display: none` (the base) and `.show` reveals it, so no media query can hide it; the 640px block wraps the banner, makes the action row full-width and keeps 44px targets; `main.js` carries `cookieGateErr` + the keyboard blur and no longer carries the dead-end alert; `cookieConsent.js` marks `attention`; `@keyframes cookie-pulse` is wired and the reduced-motion media turns it off.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Defect class "consent UI layered beneath a full-viewport overlay"* → siblings audited: `.modal-backdrop` (safe-area padding added; deliberately stays below the banner — the consent layer is topmost), `.cookie-settings-backdrop` (safe-area padding added; the banner is hidden by JS while it opens), `.nav` / `.nav-menu` / `.launch-banner` (top-anchored — no safe-area need; z-order pinned), dashboard overlays (`src/services/dashboard.js` has no cookie banner — deliberately left). *Class "bottom-fixed UI without the iOS safe area"* → both backdrops fixed, banner fixed; one targeted assertion per sibling.

**Frames touched.** `landing/assets/css/styles.css` (`.cookie-banner`, `.cookie-banner.attention`, `@keyframes cookie-pulse`, reduced-motion media, 640px block, `.modal-backdrop`, `.cookie-settings-backdrop`), `landing/assets/js/cookieConsent.js` (`showBanner` / `hideBanner`), `landing/assets/js/main.js` (legalSubmit gate), `landing/index.html` (`#cookieGateErr`), stamped landing assets (`?v=1.96.8`), `landing/data/changelog.json`, `test_landing_static.js` (Test 24), `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.96.8), this file (`§91`, §240, history + version), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_landing_static (473), test_vehicle_documents (version pin), test_doc_sync, `npm run health` — green.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63 (rules + architecture first; **0 open proposals** verified live — 7 unrelated PENDING friction rows left for their own review), 3/4 (targeted reads, batched edits), 10/11 (stateless suites, no test rows created), 31 (warm, one next step, 44px tap targets), 33/43 (one version commit; deploy on push), 51/52 (sibling sweep + before/after assertions), 54 (live read-only operator check), 55/56 (evolved the existing banner/consent assets; every page re-stamped), 2/13 (architecture + CHANGELOG + landing feed in the same commit). No rule edited. **Impact:** a phone visitor can now see and tap the cookie choice above the signup form, safely above the iOS home indicator, and is told exactly where to look.

### 241. v1.96.9 — GTM delivered first-party from gtm.sakafleet.com (2026-11-13)

**Why.** Ad blockers filter the standard Google Tag Manager host, so consented analytics silently under-counted. The operator raised a first-party host (`gtm.sakafleet.com`) that proxies the same container.

**Live verification (rule 54, before any edit).** The earlier session correctly stopped when `curl -I` returned **404** (`{"message":"Route GET:/gtm.js not found"}` from a Cloud Run/Fastify service) and shipped nothing. After the operator fixed the route: `GET https://gtm.sakafleet.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-TGR68X2X` → **200**, `content-type: application/javascript; charset=UTF-8`, **642,911-byte** payload containing `GTM-TGR68X2X`. HEAD returns 400 (proxy quirk; browsers load scripts with GET, so this is irrelevant).

**The change (one line).** `landing/assets/js/cookieConsent.js` `loadGtm()`: `j.src = 'https://gtm.sakafleet.com/gtm.js?id=' + i + dl;` (was `https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js`). Consent untouched: `applyConsent()` calls `loadGtm()` only when `data.analytics === true`; the `gtmLoaded` one-shot guard, `GTM_ID = 'GTM-TGR68X2X'`, the `consent_analytics_granted` dataLayer push and the never-blocking `try/catch` all stay.

**No `<noscript>` iframe (deliberate).** The six HTML pages have never shipped the standard GTM noscript fallback, and this release explicitly does not add it: a `<noscript>` iframe cannot read the localStorage consent gate and would contact the GTM host for every no-JS visitor regardless of opt-in. Test 25 pins its absence.

**Tests (rule 52).** `test_landing_static` Test 9's domain pin now asserts `gtm.sakafleet.com`; new Test 25 (+11: 473 → 484): exact loader URL, `GTM-TGR68X2X` preserved (and no `GTM-TGR682X`), the `analytics === true` gate, a case-insensitive `walk(LANDING)` sweep proving zero `googletagmanager.com` anywhere under `landing/` (binaries skipped), per-page absence on all six HTML files, and the no-noscript consent guarantee.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *Class "a hard-coded third-party host duplicated across delivery paths"* → loader (fixed), HTML script/noscript paths (absent by design — per-page + noscript assertions), `main.js` dataLayer pushes (no host — fine), dashboard pages (no GTM — deliberately left), prose/docs (no URLs — the directory sweep proves it). One targeted assertion per sibling.

**Operator notes.** `gtm.sakafleet.com/gtm.js` must keep serving the GTM bootstrap as `application/javascript` (preserve path + `?id=` query); `GET https://gtm.sakafleet.com/healthy` is the readiness probe. If the proxy ever dies, `loadGtm()`'s `try/catch` means the page is unaffected and analytics simply stops — the browser network tab is the diagnosis point.

**Frames touched.** `landing/assets/js/cookieConsent.js` (header + `loadGtm`), `test_landing_static.js` (Test 9 + Test 25), stamped landing assets (`?v=1.96.9`), `landing/data/changelog.json`, `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.96.9), this file, `docs/` (regenerated), `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_landing_static (484), test_vehicle_documents (83), test_doc_sync (30), test_kb_docs (43), `npm run docs:check`, `npm run health` — green.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63 (rules + architecture first; **0 open proposals** verified live — 8 unrelated PENDING friction rows left for their own review), 3/4, 10/11, 13 (no intent/flow/field/prompt change), 31, 33/43, 51/52, 54 (live GET + payload verified before the edit; the earlier 404 stop was correct), 55/56, 2. No rule edited. **Impact:** consented analytics load from a first-party host; consent behaviour and the data collected are unchanged.

### 242. v1.97.0 — the superadmin User Management CRM (`/d/admin/profiles`)

**Why.** The v1.91.0 console carried six write tools but its list only showed owners WITH a vehicle, and there was no single page for an account: support could not see shells/drivers, search by email, correct an identity, apply an offline-payment plan, leave a note, or end stray sessions without WhatsApp commands.

**The Master List (`buildAdminProfilesList`, `renderAdminProfilesPage`).** Three fail-soft reads merged in JS: `profiles` where `deleted_at IS NULL` (full column set, slim retry on schema drift), live `vehicles` (counts + active), `trial_sessions` where `status='ACTIVE'` (latest `ends_at`). Status precedence: Superadmin (phone identity) → Past due → Paid · tier (ACTIVE/CANCELING) → Trial · N d left / ends today / Trial ended → Shell (no name AND no email, the v1.82.0 definition) → Free. Search covers name, email, masked phone and raw phone digits (≥3). Phones and emails are masked in the table; sort is status weight → active vehicles → name (deterministic). The legacy `/d/admin` owners list is unchanged (still the fleet reference; `test_dashboard` pins it).

**The detail page (`buildAdminProfileDetail`, `renderAdminProfileDetailPage`).** Profile (full select + slim retry), fleet (≤50), the last 3 `support_tickets` matched by `whatsapp_number` OR `sender_email`, the last 300 audit rows JS-filtered to `details.targetId` (notes separately), and the entitlements snapshot passed in by the route (`getEntitlements(..., useCache:false)`, caught → null). Every optional block degrades independently and the page names what failed (`degraded:` banner). The page renders: identity form, subscription block (engine view, Extend trial link, manual tier + force-verify forms), fleet table (passbook links), support, notes, audit history, security, impersonation + email-as-Saka links, and the danger zone. Each destructive form carries a `data-typed` word and a client-side disable (JS is never the gate).

**Guard stack (all six POSTs, identical to v1.91.0).** `isDashboardEnabled()` → generic 404; `isCrossOriginWrite` → 403; `requireRoleSession('admin')`; `ADMIN_WRITE_RATE` (5/5-min composite IP+session); server-side `typedExactly` (UPDATE / TIER / VERIFY / LOGOUT / WIPE); `adminReasonOk` (3–300 chars); field whitelist/engine validation; `logAdminAudit` with actor + `targetId` + `before`/`after`; 303 `?done=<verb>` banner. Notes are the one POST without a typed word (the note itself is the reason, 3–500 chars). Wipe/identity/tier refuse the superadmin target; force-logout refuses the caller's own session; wipe refuses self; every refusal is an honest 400.

**Identity law (operator instruction).** `applyAdminIdentityUpdate` is a pure whitelist: `full_name` (≤120), `email` (validated, lowercased, duplicate-refused), `country` (≤80, stamps `country_source='user'`), `unit_system` (metric|imperial). **A changed email defaults `email_verified=false`; ticking "Force Verify" in the same submit keeps it verified.** Phone, tier, trial, VIN/passbook and all subscription columns are structurally unreachable.
**Engine-owned tier override (`applyManualTierOverride`, subscriptions.js).** `isKnownTierKey` first (a typo is refused — `normalizeTierKey` would silently map it to Free), then profile tier/status/interval (`ACTIVE`, `cancel_at_period_end=false`), then an APPENDED `subscriptions` ledger line with `source='manual'` (the additive `subscriptions.source text` column: schema CREATE + idempotent ALTER + `npm run migrate:subscription-source`; an un-migrated table retries without the column and logs), `invalidateEntitlements` + `markUserDataChanged`. No price, period or payment outcome is invented (rule 28).

**Force-verify / force-logout / wipe.** Verify sets `email_verified=true` (before-snapshot captured BEFORE the write — a live row reference otherwise lies). Force logout deletes `dashboard_sessions` by owner + `admin_impersonations` by target and audits the cleared counts. Wipe reuses `wipeProfileForSignup` + session/impersonation cleanup, refuses self and the superadmin, and audits per-table counts.

**Latent defect fixed (rule 51).** `subscriptions.js` called `logWriteFailure` in two catch paths without importing it — a ReferenceError that could mask the billing failure it meant to record.

**Tests (rule 52).** `test_dashboard_admin` 100 → **162**: flag-off 404 ×8 URLs; cross-origin 403 ×6 POSTs; Test 13 list (shell/no-vehicle/driver included, masked outputs, email+phone search, audited view, failed-trials degrade); Test 14 detail (sections, ticket, links, danger zone, 404, failed-tickets degrade); Test 15 identity (typed word, reason, email unverified by default, Force Verify, country_source, whitelist, duplicate email, before/after audit); Test 16 tier (bogus tier, lowercase word, profile flip, `source='manual'`, audit, superadmin refusal); Test 17 logout (sessions cleared, counts audited, self refused); Test 18 wipe (typed word, erase, audit, superadmin refusal); Test 19 notes + verify. Siblings: `test_dashboard` (936), `test_agent_training` (247 — playbook `SUPERADMIN USER MANAGEMENT` line + core-prompt CRM sentence), `test_subscription_billing` (108), `test_trial_engine` (138), `test_profile_wipe` (17), `test_db_reset_scope` (128).

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** *(i) "a write reads its own before-state after mutating it"* → verify/tier snapshot before the write (mock live references exposed it); identity already synchronous. *(ii) "an unknown key is silently defaulted"* → `isKnownTierKey` guard. *(iii) "a schema carrier exists in only one place"* → `source` in the CREATE + ALTER + migration + boot ensure. *(iv) "a helper is used but never imported"* → `logWriteFailure` import. One targeted assertion per sibling.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboardAdmin.js` (CRM constants, `buildAdminProfilesList`, `loadAdminProfileRow`, `buildAdminProfileDetail`, `applyAdminIdentityUpdate`, six section renderers, both page renderers, `ADMIN_ACTION_WORDS`, select-field support, exports), `src/services/subscriptions.js` (`applyManualTierOverride`, `isKnownTierKey`, `logWriteFailure`), `src/db/subscriptionSchema.js` (`source`), `scripts/run_subscription_source_migration.js` (new), `src/routes/dashboard.js` (imports + 8 routes), `src/services/dashboard.js` (`adminNav`), `src/services/flowKnowledge.js`, `sakaAi.js`, `test_dashboard_admin.js`, `test_agent_training.js`, `test_user_context_cache.js` (43-site ratchet), `package.json` (1.97.0 + `migrate:subscription-source`), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 243. v1.97.1 — the unverified-signup dead-end (`kiddymoms01@gmail.com`, 2026-11-13)

**Live evidence (rule 54, before any edit).** The profile existed — `kiddymoms01@gmail.com`, `email_verified:false`, phone `+254720641983`, created 05:01:41Z; the first attempt DID create a `web_onboard_otps` row (05:01:41Z) that was never verified. On the 07:14–07:28Z return visit the check endpoint answered correctly (`{verified:false, emailRegistered:true, …}`) and the UI promised a resend, but the final `POST /api/onboard` (07:28:16Z, same email, a retyped phone `+254721111111`) wrote `WEB_ONBOARD_EXISTING` + `WEB_ONBOARD_DUPLICATE_NOTIFIED` and returned `already_verified:true` — no code re-sent, the OTP gate unreachable. GTM's `formSubmit` with `formCanceled:true` also proved the details form could cancel silently on the disabled Continue gate.

**Root cause A — two endpoints disagreed on one fact.** `inspectExistingSignup` returned `'email_exists'` for ANY email match without checking `email_verified` (the v1.40.0 duplicate rule), and `/api/onboard` treated `email_exists` as "already registered". The v1.96.7 fix had aligned the CHECK endpoint and the frontend gate only; the SUBMIT endpoint still lied to half-finished signups.

**Root cause B — a gate that returned silently.** `main.js` did `if ($('detailsContinue') && $('detailsContinue').disabled) return;` after `preventDefault()` — an Enter-key submit during a pending/failed availability check produced zero DOM change.

**The fix.**
- `inspectExistingSignup`: an email match is `'verified'` ONLY when `email_verified === true`; otherwise `'unverified'` (the `'email_exists'` state is retired — no producer remains).
- New `reissueWebOnboardCode({ supabase, email, phone, firstName, lastName, profile })`: reuses the open OTP row (same `onboard_token`, attempts reset) or creates one; carries the **STORED profile phone** so `verifyWebOnboardCode → completeWebOnboarding` flips the right profile (a retyped number can never mint a second row); never writes `profiles` (no phone overwrite, no tier/trial change); audits `WEB_ONBOARD_RESUMED`.
- `/api/onboard`: only `'verified'` takes the already-registered/notify branch; `'unverified' && matchedBy === 'email'` re-issues the code, sends it and returns `{ success:true, onboard_token, profile_created:false }` — the site advances to `#stepOtp`. The same-phone unverified path keeps the normal flow.
- `main.js`: the disabled gate now renders a visible outcome — "Still checking your details — one moment." + `runAvailabilityCheck()` while pending; the verified-match CTA; or "Please check your details — the Continue button is still locked." — plus a `console.warn`. `legalSubmit` prefers `out.body.message || out.body.error` for business refusals and logs malformed `/api/onboard` and `/api/onboard/check` bodies with `console.error('[onboard] …')`.
**Tests (rule 52).** `test_web_onboarding` 64 → **72**: unverified email-match states, and Test 6b (code+token issued, stored-phone carrier, profile untouched, `WEB_ONBOARD_RESUMED`, retry reuses the row + resets attempts, verified accounts refused). `test_duplicate_signup` 21 → **25**: the email-match expectation corrected to `verified`, the kiddymoms01 resume state, route-source pins for `reissueWebOnboardCode` and the removed `email_exists` branch. `test_landing_static` 484 → **489** (Test 26): no silent gate return, visible checking copy + re-check, locked-gate copy, server-message preference, malformed-response logging.

Live Cloud Run (`saka-fleet-00419-btm`) carries the superadmin keys, both inbound secret mounts and `META_TPL_CARE_ESCALATION=saka_care_escalation`; the `CARE_*` family is absent so production defaults to OFF. The operator flip is the documented `gcloud run services update … --update-env-vars=CARE_AI_ENABLED=on,CARE_ESCALATION_EMAIL=support@sakafleet.com,CARE_AI_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR=0.7` (never run silently by Cline).

### 246. v1.97.4 — care reply status writes, lookup flake and the `/d/care` thread

**Why (live audit, 2026-11-13).** `care reply 0fc5fb1e …` emailed the customer and threaded the `out` message, yet the ticket stayed ESCALATED (`updated_at` frozen at escalation time) and the KPI read `In progress: 0`; the first rapid attempt had answered "That ticket was not found." for a live ticket. Root causes: (1) the live `support_tickets_status_check` — inherited from the pre-v1.58.14 table — allowed only `OPEN/BOT_HANDLED/ESCALATED/CLOSED`, so every `IN_PROGRESS` (console reply, `[SFC-]` router) and `RESOLVED` (Amina) write was rejected by PostgREST, and `updateCareTicket` swallowed the error with no log; (2) `resolveCareTicketId` ignored the PostgREST `error` and mapped any transient failure to "not found"; (3) `/d/care` rendered only ESCALATED cards and only `internal/ai` messages, so human replies could never be seen; (4) `support_tickets.ai_draft` was missing live (`migrate:care-ai` had never been applied).

**The change.** `CARE_SQL` gains an idempotent constraint widening (`DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS` + `ADD` with the six canonical statuses; `BOT_HANDLED` kept for legacy rows — no code writes it). `updateCareTicket` logs every refusal via `logWriteFailure`, the reply/email branch appends an honest warning to the confirmation when the status write fails, and `routeCareInternalReply` returns `ok:false` with the reason while the lesson + audit still run. `resolveCareTicketId` destructures `error`, retries once after 300 ms and logs every transient failure; "not found" is reserved for a clean empty result. `renderCareQueuePage` lists every ticket from `buildCareQueue` (OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/ESCALATED) with a live status chip, the full Thread (customer/care/internal + channel + time), the internal note, the investigation log and Amina's draft; the KPI strip reads the same counts (In progress now reflects the DB).

**Live remediation (applied).** `npm run migrate:care-console` (constraint widened) and `npm run migrate:care-ai` (`ai_draft` + `care_learnings`) were applied to project `wnvbhpykboonygaznhhl`; ticket `0fc5fb1e-c8c1-492c-b4dd-eb4b64eeea19` was set to `IN_PROGRESS` after the constraint fix.

**Tests (rule 52).** `test_care_worker`: reply on an ESCALATED ticket → `IN_PROGRESS` + `out` message; a refused status write → honest copy + `error_logs` row while the customer reply is still sent; a transient lookup failure → retried + logged, never "not found". `test_dashboard`: an IN_PROGRESS ticket renders its chip, its outbound thread message and its internal note, with `counts.inProgress = 1`.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *a legacy CHECK constraint silently rejects a status the engine writes; PostgREST refusals are swallowed* → siblings swept: `RESOLVED` (careAi resolve path) unblocked by the same constraint; every `updateCareTicket` caller (reply/email/note/take/release/close/reopen/escalate/deescalate/`[SFC-]` router/careAi) audited; `resolveCareTicketId` callers audited; dashboard render gap closed; the mock-vs-prod divergence is pinned by the `beforeUpdate` test. Deliberately left: `BOT_HANDLED` stays allowed for legacy rows (no code references it).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/{careConsole,careLearning,dashboard}.js`, `test_care_worker.js`, `test_dashboard.js`, `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.97.4), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Suites run.** test_care_worker, test_dashboard, test_care_learning, test_inbound_email, test_doc_sync, test_kb_docs, test_vehicle_documents, test_landing_static, test_env_audit, `npm run env:audit`, `npm run health` — green.

**Rules shaped this work (rule 58).** 1/39/42/45/63, 3/4, 10/11, 12/33, 21, 44, 50/51/52, 54, 55, 56, 2. No rule edited. **Impact:** `care reply`/`care email`, the `[SFC-]` human-reply router and Amina's resolve path persist their statuses; `/d/care` shows live threads and KPIs; refused writes can never be silent again.



### 247. v1.97.5 — compact care queue UX + the honest `[SFC-]` lesson diagnosis

**Why (live audit, 2026-11-13).** The operator replied to an `[SFC-…]` escalation email from the Hostinger inbox yet `/d/care` still showed **Lessons: 0**. Rule-54 live read-only queries against project `wnvbhpykboonygaznhhl` (Supabase Management API) proved the chain end-to-end:
- `public.care_learnings` → **0 rows** (`newest: null`); the KPI was factually correct, not a renderer bug.
- `admin_audit_logs` → `CARE_TICKET_HUMAN_REPLY` at `2026-11-13 10:57:04 UTC` for ticket `0fc5fb1e-c8c1-492c-b4dd-eb4b64eeea19` with `{"learned":false,"lesson":null}` — **the router ran**; `EMAIL_INBOUND_SIGNING_SECRET` is valid (a bad signature returns 401 and writes nothing).
- `support_ticket_messages` → the stored "human reply" is only `👤 Human reply (support@sakafleet.com): Re: [SFC-0fc5fb1e] Re: How do I log fuel?` — the reply **body** never arrived. `fetchInboundEmailBody()` returned no text (silently), `handleInboundEmail` fell back to `text: bodyText || email.subject`, and `extractCareLesson` correctly refused to invent a rule from a subject line (`no-reusable-lesson`).
- The operator's real answer went out through the WhatsApp `care reply` console at `10:52` (`CARE_TICKET_REPLIED`, `channel: email`) — the console path never feeds the learning loop by design; only inbound `[SFC-]` replies do.
- Zero care/lesson-related `error_logs` rows existed, so the failure was invisible. (Rule 42: proposals verified live — 4 `DECLINED`, 8 `DEPLOYED`, **0 open**.)

**The change (renderer — `renderCareQueuePage`).**
- New local helper `careTitleHtml(ticket)`: strips every `[SFC-…]` tag and any leading `Re:`/`Fwd:` chain, collapses whitespace, and titles a subjectless ticket from its `message_body` cut at **60 chars + `...`** (subjects are shown whole). Output stays `escapeHtml`-ed.
- `statusChipHtml` emits dedicated classes: `chip care-escalated` (red `#F85149`, white), `chip care-progress` (amber `#F59E0B`, black `#0A0A0C`), `chip care-open` (blue `#2563EB`, white); `RESOLVED` keeps `chip ok`, unknown statuses keep the plain chip.
- Each card now renders `<details class="care-details">` for **💬 Thread** and **🔎 Investigation log**. The thread is `open` only when the ticket is `ESCALATED`; the investigation log starts closed everywhere (OPEN/IN_PROGRESS are fully compact). The internal note, investigation steps and Amina's draft live inside the investigation details; the console-reply hint stays visible below them.
- A ticket with no investigation steps shows one grey `chip care-pregate` badge — `⚙️ Pre-gate escalation` — replacing the old bulky paragraph.
- The empty-lessons copy now names the real requirement: a human reply to an `[SFC-…]` email teaches a rule **when the reply body reaches the inbox**.

**The change (pipeline — the silent fallback is dead, rule 50/51).**
- `handleInboundEmail` gains a `fetchBody` test seam and treats a failed **or empty** Resend body as an incident: `logWriteFailure(supabase, 'inboundEmail.fetchInboundEmailBody', Error('Resend body unavailable: <reason|empty>'), { emailId })` — an `error_logs` row every time.
- The internal-reply branch computes `bodyAvailable = Boolean(bodyText)`, passes it to the router, and returns it in the handler result.
- `routeCareInternalReply` accepts `bodyAvailable` (default `true` so direct/console callers stay unchanged), records `bodyAvailable` in the `CARE_TICKET_HUMAN_REPLY` audit details and returns it — a subject-only fallback can never masquerade as a real reply again.


**Tests (rule 52).** `test_dashboard` 944 → **958** (Test 51c): exactly 6 `<details>` blocks for 3 tickets, exactly one `open` and it wraps the escalated thread, the investigation log is never open by default, the three coloured chip classes, the pre-gate badge (and the paragraph gone), the 60-char subjectless-title truncation, tag/`Re:` stripping, and the four CSS rules. The previously vacuous hostile-subject check now injects into `data.tickets` (the renderer's real source since v1.97.4). `test_inbound_email` 42 → **48**: a failed `fetchBody` → `error_logs` row + `bodyAvailable:false` + subject-only honest fallback; an empty body is logged too; the real router's audit row carries `"bodyAvailable":false`.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *a verified webhook silently degrades to a subject-only "reply" when the provider body fetch fails, and the refusal is never logged* → siblings swept: the only `fetchInboundEmailBody` caller now logs both failure modes; every `routeCareInternalReply` caller carries `bodyAvailable`; the dashboard title path is the only place a ticket subject renders (escaped + stripped); the vacuous hostile-subject assertion was strengthened; and the new CSS comment leaked the words "care queue" into the inlined `DASHBOARD_CSS` of the owner-404 page (caught by the existing anti-leak assertion) — wording fixed to `/d/care`. Deliberately left: Amina's `processCareEmail` body degradation is unchanged (it records ticket message bodies, not lessons).

**Frames touched.** `src/services/dashboard.js` (`renderCareQueuePage`, `careTitleHtml`, `statusChipHtml`, `DASHBOARD_CSS`), `src/services/inboundEmail.js` (`handleInboundEmail` fetch seam + failure log + `bodyAvailable`), `src/services/careLearning.js` (`routeCareInternalReply` payload/audit/return), `test_dashboard.js`, `test_inbound_email.js`, `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.97.5), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.

### 248. v1.97.6 — the Resend receiving endpoint (why the Lesson was empty)

**Why (live investigation, rules 44/54).** `/d/care` read `Lessons: 0` after a real `[SFC-]` reply. The v1.97.5 audit proved `CARE_TICKET_HUMAN_REPLY {learned:false}` and a subject-only "human reply"; v1.97.6 found the exact failure point:
- `error_logs` (`route='inboundEmail.fetchInboundEmailBody'`) → **empty**. Correct: the 10:57 reply ran on `saka-fleet-00419/00420/00421` (v1.97.4 code, live 10:48→11:32); v1.97.5's logging deployed at ~19:04 (`saka-fleet-00426-264`), so the old silent path covered it.
- Resend API, our endpoint: `GET https://api.resend.com/emails/e5302c09-e6c4-417b-95dd-82dc644ddafb` → **`404 {"statusCode":404,"message":"Email not found","name":"not_found"}`**.
- Resend API, receiving endpoint: `GET https://api.resend.com/emails/receiving/e5302c09-…` → **`200`** with `html` **and** a clean `text` (`"For future reference: If a user asks how to log fuel, do not investigate. Just reply and tell them to open their WhatsApp and type 'Logged 40L diesel at 50,000km …"`). The body existed all along; the app was asking the SENT-email API.
- Cloud Run logs (Logging API, 10:55–11:05Z): `POST /webhook/email/inbound` → `200` (1.9 ms metadata, then `req-1c` `200` after ~1.8 s of processing). The webhook fired; the fetch 404'd inside it.
- Resend receiving list: the only `[SFC-]` reply received is `e5302c09-…` at 10:57:01Z. Nothing arrived ~11:30 (the 11:22/18:54 rows are outbound test escalations).
- No auth/plan issue: the receiving endpoint answered `200` with the same `RESEND_API_KEY`.

**The change.** `fetchInboundEmailBody` now retrieves `https://api.resend.com/emails/receiving/{id}` (was `/emails/{id}`). Extraction (`text`/`html`), the 8 s timeout, the v1.97.5 failure logging and the handler-level `htmlToPlainText` HTML-only fallback are unchanged — the existing HTML-only path (pinned since v1.59.7) now simply receives real `html` when `text` is absent.

**Tests.** `test_inbound_email` 48 → **52**: stubbed `globalThis.fetch` pins the URL to the receiving endpoint (the sent endpoint can never return), the real response shape yields `{ok:true,text,html}`, an HTML-only received email returns its `html`, and a `404` stays `{ok:false,reason:'http-404'}` feeding the v1.97.5 `error_logs` path (stub saved/restored, rule 52 isolation).

**Live reconciliation (rule 56, post-deploy).** The recovered 10:57 reply is replayed through `routeCareInternalReply` with its real body and `bodyAvailable:true`: the ticket thread gains the real answer, `CARE_TICKET_HUMAN_REPLY {bodyAvailable:true, learned:true}` + `CARE_TICKET_LEARNED` are audited and `care_learnings` gains its first row (Lessons KPI leaves 0). The outcome (lesson text + counts) is recorded in the release report.

**Recurrence autopsy (rule 51).** Defect class *a provider integration is wired to the sibling API namespace (sent vs received) and the refusal is treated as "no body"* → siblings swept: the only Resend fetch in the repo is `fetchInboundEmailBody` (mailers only POST to `/emails`); the body path logs every failure/empty response (v1.97.5); the HTML-only fallback is pinned at both fetch and handler level. Deliberately left: no retry — the 404 was deterministic, not transient.

**Frames touched.** `src/services/inboundEmail.js` (`fetchInboundEmailBody`), `test_inbound_email.js`, `test_vehicle_documents.js` (version pin), `package.json` (1.97.6), `landing/data/changelog.json` + stamped assets, `docs/` (regenerated), this file, `CHANGELOG.md`.
